# Matching (Match and Merge configuration) — study and implementation

Written 2026-09-21 on branch `feature/matching` (worktree `ebx-mdm-factory-matching`), completing
`docs/MASTER-ZONE.md`'s lots 4-5 ("Generating the matching configuration", "Matching run"): given a
GREENFIELD master zone that already exists for real on this instance (`Companies_Master`/`Master`,
tables `Company` 11 fields / 107 rows, `Contact` 17 fields / 89 rows — `PLAN.md`, lot 3), propose a
`MatchPlan` per promoted entity, translate an accepted one into a real Match and Merge configuration,
launch a scoped run, and keep `Xref.goldenKey` current.

**Revised 2026-09-21, same day, after coordinator review of commit `1cdb8bd`.** Two changes, both folded
into the sections below rather than kept as a separate addendum: (1) `matching/run` no longer POSTs to an
unverified REST endpoint with the agent account's credentials — it calls the add-on's own public Java API
in-process, with the caller's session, found by `javap` on `ebx-addons.jar` and read from that server's
on-disk Javadoc (§2.6, §4.4); (2) `ebx.MasterGenerator` now declares the MAME add-on on the master model
itself, closing the gap §2.2 found rather than leaving it as an open question for the product owner (§2.2, §5).

**Evidence tags**, the same convention `docs/MASTER-ZONE.md`/`docs/SOURCE-RELATIONS.md` already use, plus
two added this revision for the Java-side investigation:

- **READ `path:line`** — read directly in this worktree's Java source.
- **READ (live)** — a real, read-only MCP call against the running instance this session
  (`mcp__match-merge__matching_guide`/`matching_config_schema`/`get_matching_config`/
  `get_matching_activation_status`/`profile_table_for_matching`, `mcp__data-access__*`, and, this
  revision, `mcp__data-model__list_operations`/`get_data_model`/`get_publication`). Nothing was written,
  generated, patched, activated, or run.
- **READ (schema, not live)** — the JSON Schema of a *write* tool (`generate_matching_policy`,
  `generate_merge_policy`, `apply_matching_config`, `patch_matching_config`, `activate_matching`,
  `set_table_settings`, `set_trusted_sources`, `delete_matching_config`, and, this revision, `add_addon`/
  `list_addons`/`remove_addon` via `list_operations`), loaded via `ToolSearch` or `list_operations` to
  read its parameter shape and description text — **never called**. This is how §3's and §5's translation
  layers were designed without a single write against the live instance.
- **READ (javap)** — a real `javap -p` decompilation of a class file, this revision on
  `ebx-ps-fasttrack-server/lib/ebx-addons.jar` (the Match and Merge add-on's own Java classes) and
  `ebx-lib.jar` (`com.onwbp.adaptation.Request`). Ground truth for method signatures, exception types, and
  enum constants — never inferred from a name alone.
- **READ (on-disk Javadoc)** — the add-on's own published Java API documentation, on the same server, under
  `ebx-addon-mame/www/common/html/onHelp/advanced/Java_API/**` and the admin guide under
  `ebx-addon-mame/www/common/html/onHelp/simple/admin_guide/**`. Real prose and real code samples from the
  product itself, not reconstructed from decompiled signatures alone.
- **INFERRED** — a conclusion not directly read or measured; flagged as a design choice or a
  recommendation, not a fact.

Read first, in full, as instructed: `PLAN.md`, `docs/MASTER-ZONE.md`, the internal EBX MCP guide
§§6/8/9/10. The whole master-zone generator/loader/reset chain (`ebx.MasterGenerator`, `ebx.MasterLoader`,
`ebx.MasterReset`, `master.MasterModel`, `master.MasterTransferPlan`, `master.MembershipConsistencyCheck`,
`ebx.MemberEntitiesBackfill`) already exists, deployed, and was read in full before writing anything here —
every new class in this lot reuses its patterns (resumable `PipelineStep`, per-caller private `readEntities`/

## 2. Live investigation

### 2.1 `matching_guide` and `matching_config_schema` (READ (live), all three guide topics + the full schema)

Read in full; the concrete facts that shaped every design decision below:

- **Algorithm codes are prefixed and must be passed as-is**: `ebx-addon-mame@exact`, `@jarowinkler`,
  `@levenshtein`, `@beider-morse`, `@soundex`, `@range`, `@operator`, `@hybridFuzzy`, `@fuzzyFullText`,
  `@exactFullText`, `@phoneticFullText`. `MatchPlanRules`/`MatchingPolicyTranslator` only ever emit
  `@exact` and `@fuzzyFullText` — the two the real `Companies` policy itself uses on every field except
  `LegalEntityIdentifier`'s own exact match (§2.1 of `docs/MASTER-ZONE.md`).
- **Decision-node function parameter rules** (`matching_config_schema`, `decisionTree.function`
  description, quoted): *"All fields match: field minimumScore (defaults to 100 if omitted); ... Average:
  node minimumScore (required, no default), field weight (defaults to 1 if omitted)."* This is exactly
  why `MatchingPolicyTranslator` puts `minimumScore` as a **field-level** param on an exact tier but a
  **node-level** param on the `Average` tier, and `weight` as a **field-level** param only inside the
  `Average` node — getting this backwards would trip `MISSING_FUNCTION_PARAM`/`MISSING_ALGORITHM_PARAM`
  at `validate_matching_config` time.
- **A threshold must be 1-100** (`matching_guide`, threshold-tuning topic): 0 is rejected outright.
  `MatchPlanRules` never emits 0.
- **Running a match is not an MCP tool** (`matching_guide`, threshold-tuning topic, quoted in full):
  *"Running a match is not one of the MAME MCP tools -- it is the matching-execution REST endpoint,
  called with a recordPks list ... recordPks: [] (or omitted) runs the whole table. This is an
  authoritative, table-wide recompute: before a single pair is re-evaluated, it discards every existing
  match and suspect verdict already stored for that table -- across EVERY matching policy configured on
  the table, not only the one you are running."* This describes the plain REST endpoint specifically; the
  Java API's own `matchRecords(table, request, policyCode)` (§2.6, what `matching/run` actually calls
  since the coordinator's review) takes a `Request` instead of a `recordPks` list, but the same hazard
  applies to an unbounded/empty `Request` — which is exactly why `master.MatchingRunScope` refuses outright
  rather than build one, see §4.4.
- **Function chains are the only merge/record-selection shape** (`matching_config_schema`,
  `mergeChains`): a "single function" write is normalised into a one-entry array on read; the terminal
  function `constant` must be last and only the `survivor_field` chain offers it.

### 2.2 `get_matching_config`/`get_matching_activation_status` on `Companies_Master`/`Master`/`/root/Company` — `TABLE_NOT_FOUND` (READ (live), a real finding)

```
get_matching_config(table="/root/Company", dataModel="Companies_Master")  -> TABLE_NOT_FOUND
get_matching_config(table="/root/Company")                                -> TABLE_NOT_FOUND
get_matching_activation_status(table="/root/Company")                     -> TABLE_NOT_FOUND
matching_config_schema(table="/root/Company")                             -> TABLE_NOT_FOUND
```

The table genuinely exists (`data-access.list_tables(Companies_Master, Master)` lists `/root/Company`,
11 fields, and `profile_table_for_matching` — §2.3 — reads it live and correctly). `get_matching_config`'s
own error text: *"the table path does not resolve under the optional dataModel, or under any data model
registered with the MAME add-on"* — **not** the `CONFIG_NOT_FOUND` soft miss that would mean "the table
exists, nothing is configured on it yet" (the shape `docs/MASTER-ZONE.md` §4.2 originally expected for a
fresh table).

**Most likely explanation, read from the write tool's own precondition (READ (schema, not live),
`activate_matching`'s own description, quoted in full)**: *"The table's data model must declare the MAME
add-on (`<osd:addon>ebx-addon-mame</osd:addon>`) and be published ... A matching configuration must
already exist for the table (create one first with `generate_matching_policy`)."* `ebx.MasterGenerator`'s
`master.MasterModel.build` emits a plain `build_data_model` tree with no `osd:addon` anywhere (READ
`master/MasterModel.java` in full, confirmed no such property is ever written) — so `Companies_Master`
has never declared the addon, and MAME's own table registry genuinely has never heard of `/root/Company`.

**This reconciles with CLAUDE.md §8's own prior finding** ("a model packaged as a module XSD needs a
model reload before match-merge accepts it; a DMA publication does not") **only on its own narrow
precedent** — that finding was about *importing* an already-addon-tagged module XSD into the DMA
(`import_data_model_from_module`), not about a model *built from scratch* with `build_data_model`
(`MasterGenerator`'s own path, identical to `StagingGenerator`'s).

**Closed this revision, inside the factory, not left for the product owner (§5):** `ebx.MasterGenerator` now
declares the add-on on the master model itself — `master.only`, never landing/staging — via a new
`ensureMameAddon` step, called wherever the model is about to be published (fresh build) or republished
(regeneration), including the case that matters most concretely: **the real, already-published
`Companies_Master` generated before this fix existed.** `MasterGenerator.runRegeneration`'s own
`diff.isUpToDate()` short-circuit (previously: "the promoted entities already match the published tables
exactly, nothing to do, no republish") now also checks the add-on and republishes whenever it was just
declared, even with zero table/field changes — see §5.1/§5.2 for the exact mechanism and its own
uncertainties.

`MatchingConfigurator.configureOne` (§4) still treats a live `TABLE_NOT_FOUND` here as a clean, named
refusal rather than attempting a write chain doomed the same way — but the message now points at
`master/generate` ("declares and republishes the add-on additively, safe to re-run") instead of describing
an unowned gap, since closing it is now `MasterGenerator`'s own job.

### 2.2.1 `dataModel` is not the model's NAME — a second, real bug, measured live 2026-09-21, branch `fix/mame-datamodel-arg`

Twelve seconds after `master/generate` answered `"applied":["MAME add-on declared on Companies_Master ...
republished."]` (GENERATED, 21:21:03), `POST /projects/Companies/matching/configure` still refused with
`TABLE_NOT_FOUND` — reading exactly like §2.2's already-closed gap. It was not: the coordinator's own
direct calls to `match-merge`, same instant, showed

```
get_matching_config(table="/root/Company")                                   -> CONFIG_NOT_FOUND   (correct, ready)
get_matching_config(table="/root/Company", dataModel="Companies_Master")     -> TABLE_NOT_FOUND     (same table, same instant)
```

`Companies_Master` is the master model's own NAME — the exact string `MatchingConfigurator`/
`MatchPlanLlmSuggester` had been passing as `dataModel` on every call. The tool's own contract for that
argument (its description, quoted in full): *"the data model (publication) that owns the table, e.g. the
SchemaLocation string shown in a config's identity ... supply ONLY to disambiguate a table path
configured under more than one data model; omit it otherwise (the table is resolved automatically)."* A
plain publication name is never that `SchemaLocation` string, so passing one always broke resolution
instead of narrowing it — the add-on genuinely already knew the table with **no restart**, the moment it
was declared and republished; the factory's own code was the only thing standing in the way.

**Fixed on `fix/mame-datamodel-arg`:** every call in `MatchingConfigurator.configureOne` now omits
`dataModel` by default. A new pure helper, `master.MameDataModelResolution`, decides from the FIRST
`get_matching_config` answer (called without `dataModel`) whether to keep omitting it (`CONFIG_NOT_FOUND`
or a found config), thread through a resolved `AMBIGUOUS_TABLE` candidate for the rest of the pass (never
seen live — see that class' own Javadoc for the tolerant, best-effort parsing this needed and why it must
be re-verified at the first real occurrence), defer to a `TABLE_NOT_FOUND`-specific check, or refuse
outright on anything else. `MatchPlanLlmSuggester`'s own per-entity `matching_config_schema(table,
dataModel)` call (fieldCapabilities, §4.2.1) now resolves the same way, advisory-only: a failed resolution
there just omits `dataModel`, exactly like any other soft miss on that path.

The `TABLE_NOT_FOUND` refusal message is also now truthful instead of unconditional: it reuses
`MasterGenerator`'s own read-only `list_addons` parsing (`checkMameAddonDeclared`, extracted from
`ensureMameAddon` for this reuse, §5.2) to say which of the two real situations applies — the add-on
genuinely isn't declared yet (run `master/generate`, unchanged advice), or it IS declared and match-merge
still doesn't resolve the table (retry, or check the master dataset is actually built on this publication —
`master/generate` would not help in that case, and the message says so instead of pointing at it anyway).

### 2.2.2 `AMBIGUOUS_TABLE`'s real shape, and a THIRD bug it exposed — measured live 2026-09-23, branch `feature/simulation-preview-policy`

Deployed main `7605a78`, Proposal review → Contact (plan `PROPOSED`) → Simulate answered:

```
Simulation failed: Cannot prepare a preview matching policy for /root/Contact: get_matching_config answered
TABLE_NOT_FOUND - run master/generate first if the MAME add-on is not declared on the master model yet.
```

— reading exactly like §2.2/§2.2.1's already-closed gaps (the add-on not declared). It was not. The
coordinator's own direct calls, same session:

```
get_matching_config(table="/root/Contact")                                                    -> AMBIGUOUS_TABLE
  message: "declared by more than one data model: urn:ebx:module:EBX FastTrack - TIBCO EBX Presales
            environment:/WEB-INF/ebx/schemas/Companies.xsd, urn:ebx:publication:Companies_Master"
get_matching_config(table="/root/Contact", dataModel="urn:ebx:publication:Companies_Master")  -> CONFIG_NOT_FOUND (correct, ready)
```

`list_addons` on `Companies_Master` confirms the MAME add-on is activated on the whole model — `/root/Company`
never hit this because, in the FastTrack module's own model (`Companies.xsd`), only `Contact` is declared
there too (a genuine two-model ambiguity for `Contact` alone, not for `Company`).

**The real bug: `MameDataModelResolution`'s own text-scan fallback, not `MatchingPreviewPolicy`.**
`ebx.MatchingPreviewPolicy.ensure`'s first `get_matching_config(table)` call correctly carries NO `dataModel`
(unaffected by §2.2.1's fix), and correctly gets `AMBIGUOUS_TABLE` back. `master.MameDataModelResolution
.resolve(json, "Companies_Master")` is what then goes wrong: the `AMBIGUOUS_TABLE` answer has NO array field
of candidates (confirmed live, first time this shape has actually been observed — `master.MameDataModelResolution`'s
own class Javadoc had flagged this as unverified since 2026-09-21), so resolution fell to the text-scan
fallback. That fallback tokenized the message on every `:`/`/`/`.` (its own `IDENTIFIER` regex), which strips
the `urn:ebx:publication:` prefix clean off and keeps only the bare `Companies_Master` tail as the
"candidate" — `containsWholeToken` then matches it trivially (a bare string contains itself as a whole token),
and `Decision.dataModel` ends up being that BARE string. `ensureFresh`/`ensureRewrite` DO thread the resolved
`dataModel` through correctly on every subsequent call (verified by re-reading `MatchingPreviewPolicy.ensureFresh`
line by line — `putDataModel(generateMatchingArgs, pDataModel)` etc. are all present and correct) — but the
value they were handed was itself wrong: passing the bare `Companies_Master` back to `get_matching_config`
answers `TABLE_NOT_FOUND` (§2.2.1's own documented finding), reproducing the EXACT bug `MameDataModelResolution`
was built to eliminate, one level down.

**Fixed**: `MameDataModelResolution.extractCandidates` now tries a THIRD extraction strategy, ordered between
the array-field read and the old bare-token scan — every `urn:ebx:module:...`/`urn:ebx:publication:...` span
in the text, delimited by the next comma (the message's own list separator) or the end of the text, read as a
candidate WHOLE (`extractUrnCandidates`, a new `URN_CANDIDATE` pattern). `containsWholeToken` still finds
`Companies_Master` inside `urn:ebx:publication:Companies_Master` (only a `:` — not a word character — precedes
it), so the resolved `dataModel` is now the FULL urn string, exactly what the coordinator measured working
live. The old bare-token scan is kept as a last-resort fallback (for a hypothetical message format that never
wraps a candidate in a URN at all — never observed live either way) so `MameDataModelResolutionTest`'s own
pre-existing `ambiguousNoCandidatesArray_scansMessageText` (a hand-guessed, non-urn fixture) keeps passing
unchanged. New tests pin the EXACT live payload (`ambiguousLiveContactPayload_resolvesToTheFullUrn`) and a
trailing-punctuation edge case (`ambiguousUrnCandidateWithTrailingSentencePunctuation_stripped`).

This section originally ended here, unverified beyond re-reading the coordinator's own two measured calls -
see §2.2.3 immediately below for what the very next live retry actually found.

### 2.2.3 The SAME fix, deployed, still wrong — the two fields bleed into each other, measured live 2026-09-23 ~03:05

Minutes after §2.2.2's fix was deployed, the same Contact -> Simulate click answered a DIFFERENT refusal:

```
Could not tell which data model owns /root/Contact while preparing a preview policy: get_matching_config
answered AMBIGUOUS_TABLE and 2 candidate data models contain 'Companies_Master' as a whole token (expected
exactly one) - the table path is declared under several data models: [urn:ebx:module:EBX FastTrack - TIBCO EBX
Presales environment:/WEB-INF/ebx/schemas/Companies.xsd, urn:ebx:publication:Companies_Master Pass the
optional 'dataModel' to disambiguate; candidates: urn:ebx:module:EBX FastTrack - TIBCO EBX Presales
environment:/WEB-INF/ebx/schemas/Companies.xsd, urn:ebx:publication:Companies_Master]
```

The garbled second list entry ("...Companies_Master Pass the optional 'dataModel' to disambiguate;
candidates: urn:ebx:module:...") gave it away. The coordinator supplied the EXACT raw answer this time:

```json
{"code":"AMBIGUOUS_TABLE",
 "message":"Table /root/Contact is declared by more than one data model: urn:ebx:module:EBX FastTrack - TIBCO EBX Presales environment:/WEB-INF/ebx/schemas/Companies.xsd, urn:ebx:publication:Companies_Master",
 "nextStep":"Pass the optional 'dataModel' to disambiguate; candidates: urn:ebx:module:EBX FastTrack - TIBCO EBX Presales environment:/WEB-INF/ebx/schemas/Companies.xsd, urn:ebx:publication:Companies_Master",
 "success":false}
```

**The bug: §2.2.2's own fix scanned `message` and `nextStep` CONCATENATED, joined by a single space - not a
comma.** `message` ends with `...urn:ebx:publication:Companies_Master`; `nextStep` begins with `"Pass the
optional..."`. The extraction pattern of that fix (`urn:ebx:(?:module|publication):[^,]+` - "read up to the
next comma") does not stop at a plain space, so the span starting at `message`'s own trailing
`urn:ebx:publication:Companies_Master` ran straight across the message/nextStep boundary and did not stop
until the FIRST comma found INSIDE `nextStep`'s own candidate list — producing a mangled "candidate" reading
`"urn:ebx:publication:Companies_Master Pass the optional 'dataModel' to disambiguate; candidates:
urn:ebx:module:...xsd"`. That mangled string still CONTAINS `Companies_Master` as a whole token (nothing but a
space precedes it, nothing but more text follows — the whole-token check only looks at the immediate
neighbours), so it "matched" too — alongside the clean, correctly-bounded candidate extracted from
`nextStep`'s own tail. Two matches where there must be exactly one: `resolve` refused outright, verbatim as
quoted above.

**Fixed, two changes, both needed (either alone reproduces the bug on this exact payload):**

1. `extractCandidates` now calls `extractUrnCandidates(messageText, nextStepText)` with the two fields kept as
   TWO SEPARATE strings — never concatenated. A span extracted from `message` can no longer run into
   `nextStep`'s own text, and vice versa; each field's candidate list is scanned, deduplicated, and merged
   (`LinkedHashSet`, first-seen order: `message`'s own candidates first, then any NEW one `nextStep` adds).
2. `URN_CANDIDATE`'s own module alternative now stops at a plain comma, a semicolon, a closing bracket, a
   newline, or the literal sequence `" Pass "` (this tool's own "Pass the optional 'dataModel' to disambiguate"
   phrasing, guarded against by name, since a badly-bounded scan bleeding into exactly that sentence is what
   happened live) — not only "the next occurrence of `urn:ebx:`", which was §2.2.2's own (still too permissive)
   terminator. The `urn:ebx:publication:...` alternative was already tight (`[A-Za-z0-9_.\-]+`, no lookahead
   needed — a publication code never contains a space) and needed no change.

Parsed candidate list for the exact live payload above, BOTH fields scanned and deduplicated (verified by
`MameDataModelResolutionTest#ambiguousLiveContactPayloadWithNextStep_deduplicatesAcrossFields_resolvesToTheFullUrn`):

```
["urn:ebx:module:EBX FastTrack - TIBCO EBX Presales environment:/WEB-INF/ebx/schemas/Companies.xsd",
 "urn:ebx:publication:Companies_Master"]
```

— the SAME two candidates appear in `message` and in `nextStep`, collapsed by the dedup to one copy of each.
`containsWholeToken` matches only the second; `Decision.dataModel` resolves to `"urn:ebx:publication:Companies_Master"`,
which the coordinator confirmed live answers `CONFIG_NOT_FOUND` for `/root/Contact`.

Never re-verified live this session (task constraint) beyond re-reading the coordinator's own exact captured
JSON above — proved by `tools/test_local.sh` against that exact payload, not by a third live retry on Contact.
This is the SECOND live-deployment surprise on the same code path in the same session; a fourth is not ruled
out — the next symptom to watch for, if `message`/`nextStep` ever legitimately contain a comma INSIDE a
module's own trailing segment (a module name with a comma in it, never seen so far), would be the module
alternative stopping too early.

### 2.6 The Match and Merge add-on's public Java API (READ (javap) + READ (on-disk Javadoc), this revision)

Found by `javap -p` on `ebx-ps-fasttrack-server/lib/ebx-addons.jar` (server project, read-only) and read
from that same server's own Javadoc (`webapps/ebx-addon-mame/www/common/html/onHelp/advanced/Java_API/**`)
and admin guide (`.../simple/admin_guide/**`), 2026-09-21. This is what `ebx.MameMatchingApi` (§4.4) is
built from — no HTTP, no agent-account credentials, in-process with the caller's own session.

- **Entry point**: `OperationsFactory.getMatchingOperations(Session)` → `MatchingOperations`;
  `OperationsFactory.getProcessOperations(Session)` → `ProcessOperations`. Both are per-call, cheap to
  obtain — the Javadoc's own code sample calls them once per script/service invocation with whatever
  session the caller already has (a workflow's system-user session in the sample; a REST resource's own
  `SessionContext`-injected session, the same pattern every other write in this module already uses, for
  `ebx.MatchingConfigurator`).
- **Preconditions, quoted from `MatchingOperations`'s own class Javadoc**: *"All the matching operations
  are required to have an activated matching configuration for the table ... No dataspace lock is taken.
  The add-on only prevents a second add-on process from starting on the same table and operation while one
  is running, and that guard is local to the JVM - it does not protect a cluster."*
- **`matchRecord(table, primaryKey, policyCodeOrNull)` is SYNCHRONOUS** (one record); **`matchTable`/
  `matchRecords` are ASYNCHRONOUS**, both returning a `MatchingProcess` handle. `MameMatchingApi.launchScoped`
  uses the 3-arg `matchRecords(AdaptationTable, Request, String policyCodeOrNull)` — the `Request` carries
  the scope (`com.onwbp.adaptation.Request.setXPathFilter(String)`, confirmed by `javap` on `ebx-lib.jar`;
  `AdaptationTable.createRequest()` builds it). A 4-arg overload also exists
  (`matchRecords(table, request, policyCodeOrNull, query)`) that ANDs a second XPath string onto the same
  request (Javadoc: "Only the records selected by both the request and the query are matched") — not used
  here, since `master.MatchingRunScope` already builds the exact predicate needed.
- **Checked exceptions, quoted from the class Javadoc**: `InvalidParameterException` — "an argument is
  missing or unusable ... Fix the call; retrying as-is fails again." `InvalidStateException` — "the add-on
  cannot run the operation right now, for example matching is paused, the policy is inactive, or a process
  is already running on the table. The same call may succeed later on." Both carry a
  `getMessage(Locale)`. `MameMatchingApi` wraps both into a named `OperationException`, never swallowed.
- **No timeout on the blocking wait — a real hazard for a REST thread, deliberately not used.**
  `ProcessOperations.waitingForBackgroundProcessDone(AdaptationTable)` blocks the calling thread
  UNBOUNDED until the add-on's background process finishes (`throws InterruptedException` only — no
  timeout parameter at all, confirmed by `javap` and the Javadoc's own signature). `MameMatchingApi`
  never calls it; it polls `MatchingProcess.getMatchingStatus()` itself on a fixed 500ms interval up to an
  explicit, caller-supplied deadline (`matching/run`'s own `maxWaitMs` query parameter, default 30s) and
  returns whatever status it has when the deadline passes — `RUNNING`, not an error. `ProcessStatus`
  (READ (javap)): `INITIALIZING`, `RUNNING`, `DONE`, `FAILED`, `CANCELLING`, `CANCELLED`.
- **`simulateMatch(Adaptation, String policyCodeOrNull)` → `SimulationResult`** (`AutoCloseable`,
  `Iterable<MatchingEngineResult>`) — the Javadoc's own guarantee, quoted: *"When the simulate service is
  called, matching results are not persisted into the MatchResult table."* Each `MatchingEngineResult`
  (READ (javap)) exposes `getResult()` (`MatchingResultType`), `getTargetRecordPrimaryKey()`,
  `getPivotRecordPrimaryKey()`, `getTargetRecordAdaptation()`, `getPivotRecordAdaptation()` — fully
  readable, zero risk, exactly what `POST matching/simulate` reports (§4.5). Closed in a
  try-with-resources inside `MameMatchingApi.simulate`, never leaked to the caller.
- **The leaf-name question, refined**: `DecisionNode` (READ (javap)) has BOTH `getName()` (`String`, a
  free-text label — this is where the live `Companies` config's `"Same LEI"`/`"Match"`/`"Suspect"`/
  `"Not Match"` values come from, §2.5) AND `getMatchingResult()` (`MatchingResultType`, a real enum with
  exactly the constants `MATCHED`/`SUSPECTED`/`NOT_MATCHED` — confirmed by `javap`, not inferred). So the
  schema's documented write-side enum (`trueNode`/`falseNode`.`name` = `MATCHED`/`SUSPECTED`/
  `NOT_MATCHED`) and the live read-side display strings (`"Match"`/`"Suspect"`/`"Not Match"`) are plausibly
  two DIFFERENT properties of the same underlying node that the MCP tool's JSON happens to both call
  `name` — a write-time enum token vs. a read-time human label the tool renders for the same field key.
  **Still not proven by a live write-then-read round trip** (forbidden this session either way) — `docs/MATCHING.md`
  §3.3's own recommendation stands: re-check after the first real `generate_matching_policy` call.
- **`ConfigurationOperations` (READ (javap)) does NOT offer what `matching/configure` needs — this is why
  it still goes through the `match-merge` MCP server, not the Java API.** Its only three methods:
  `getTableConfiguration(AdaptationTable)` (read), `pauseMatchingTrigger`/`resumeMatchingTrigger` (pause
  only). No method creates a matching policy, a merge policy, links them, or activates matching — that
  surface simply does not exist in the Java API; the DMA UI (and the `match-merge` MCP server that wraps
  the same underlying configuration mechanism) is the only way to do it. **Justification for keeping MCP
  for `configure`**: it is not a style preference, it is the only surface that exists for this job.
- **`GroupOperations`/`MergeOperations`/`ChangeStateOperations` (READ (javap), not used this lot)**:
  `GroupOperations.getGroupsWithActionRequired`/`getGroup` (read suspect/merge groups),
  `MergeOperations.merge`/`mergeGroup`/`mergeRecords`/`mergeGroups`/`unmerge` (a full programmatic merge
  API, synchronous variants and a `mergeRecordsWithContext(ProcedureContext, ...)` overload for running
  inside an existing procedure), `ChangeStateOperations.updateState` (set a record's `State` —
  `UNSET`/`GOLDEN`/`MERGED`/`PENDING_APPROVAL`/`DELETED`, READ (javap)). None of this lot's routes need
  them — noted here because a future lot (a "confirm this suspect" or "undo this merge" route) would
  reach for these instead of the MCP server, the same way `matching/run`/`matching/simulate` now do.

## 3. Translating a `MatchPlan` into a real Match and Merge configuration

### 3.1 The ordered call chain (READ (schema, not live) for every write tool; READ (live) for the two read ones)

**`dataModel` on every row below is omitted by default, never the publication name** (§2.2.1, a real bug
fixed 2026-09-21) — resolved once, from row 1's answer, by `master.MameDataModelResolution`, and threaded
through unchanged for the rest of the pass; see §2.2.1 for the measured bug and the fix.

| # | Call | R/W | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `get_matching_config(table[, dataModel])` | **Read** | Run for real by `MatchingConfigurator.configureOne` before anything else — see §2.2's `TABLE_NOT_FOUND`/`CONFIG_NOT_FOUND` distinction, which this call must tell apart correctly, and §2.2.1 for the `dataModel` argument itself. |
| 2 | `generate_matching_policy(table, matchingPolicy[, dataModel])` | **Write** | *"Additively persist a matching policy ... creating the table's matching configuration if it has none ... Include a decisionTree, or the policy will not round-trip."* No `mergePolicyCode` on this first call — nothing to link to yet. |
| 3 | `generate_merge_policy(table, mergePolicy[, dataModel])` | **Write** | *"Additive: it adds a new merge policy without replacing or deleting existing ones."* Per CLAUDE.md §8, `relatedTables` is deliberately omitted — the tool adds every inverse-FK table itself, `MANUAL` by default; passing one explicitly would duplicate it. |
| 4 | `patch_matching_config(table, operations=[{op:"set_merge_policy_link", target:{policyCode}, value: mergePolicyCode}][, dataModel])` | **Write** | The schema's own `mergePolicyCode` field description says exactly this: *"generate_matching_policy writes one policy, so it can only link to a merge policy the table already stores ... Leave this out and wire the link with the set_merge_policy_link operation."* |
| 5 | `validate_matching_config(table[, dataModel])` | **Read** | `MatchingConfigurator` refuses (never calls `activate_matching`) when `valid == false`. |
| 6 | `activate_matching(table[, dataModel])` | **Write** | Its own precondition text is what explains §2.2's `TABLE_NOT_FOUND` — see there. `MatchingConfigurator` requires the re-read status to say `ENABLED` before declaring success. |
| 7 | not part of `configure` at all — a later, separate call, `matching/run`, via the add-on's Java API (§2.6/§4.4), never the plain REST endpoint this row originally named | **Write** | See §4.4 for why the REST endpoint was replaced. |

**Added 2026-09-21 (`fix/matching-policy-fields`), between row 1 and row 2**: `MatchingConfigurator.checkFieldCapabilities`
calls `matching_config_schema(table[, dataModel])` again (this time genuinely past `CONFIG_NOT_FOUND`, unlike
`MatchPlanLlmSuggester`'s own earlier per-entity call at §4.2.1, which has only ever soft-missed
`TABLE_NOT_FOUND`) and refuses BEFORE calling `generate_matching_policy` at all if the built policy declares
a field `fieldCapabilities` does not report as capable of pre-clustering. Never exercised live this session
either (a read call, but made from the same forbidden session) — if the schema call fails, soft-misses, or
carries no `fieldCapabilities` for this table, this step records "not verified" and proceeds, the same
discipline `MatchPlanLlmSuggester` already applies to the identical soft-miss.

### 3.2 `MatchPlan.requirements` — structured JSON, not the free-text the XSD comment suggests

`tools/build_xsd.py`'s own field comment reads *"What makes two records the same, in plain words; handed
to the Match and Merge policy generator."* Reading `generate_matching_policy`'s own parameter schema
(READ (schema, not live)) shows this is imprecise: **the tool takes a fully structured `matchingPolicy`
object** (fields, decision tree, algorithms, thresholds), never a plain-language sentence. `MatchPlan`
still needs *something* structured to hold and re-derive from, so `master.MatchPlanRules` writes
`requirements` as a compact (minified) JSON description, and
`master.MatchingPolicyTranslator` is the one place that turns it into the two real payloads. Shape (see
`MatchPlanRules`' own Javadoc for the full field-role rules):

```json
{
  "tiers": [
    {"outcome": "MATCH", "type": "EXACT", "fields": [{"field": "vatNo", "algorithm": "ebx-addon-mame@exact", "minimumScore": 100}]},
    {"outcome": "SUSPECTED", "type": "AVERAGE", "minimumScore": 90, "fields": [
      {"field": "name", "algorithm": "ebx-addon-mame@fuzzyFullText", "weight": 3, "bothNullValueHandling": "NOT_MATCH", "oneNullValueHandling": "NOT_MATCH"},
      {"field": "country", "algorithm": "ebx-addon-mame@exact", "weight": 1, "bothNullValueHandling": "DO_NOTHING", "oneNullValueHandling": "DO_NOTHING"},
      {"field": "city", "algorithm": "ebx-addon-mame@fuzzyFullText", "weight": 1, "bothNullValueHandling": "DO_NOTHING", "oneNullValueHandling": "DO_NOTHING"}
    ]}
  ],
  "clusteringFields": ["vatNo", "name", "country", "city"],
  "mergePolicy": {"mode": "ONLY_DUPLICATES", "recordSelection": "mostCompleted", "defaultFieldMerge": "longest"}
}
```

**Size of the field, and what a writer does when the JSON does not fit (2026-10-12, `fix/match-plan-requirements-length`).**
`MatchPlan.requirements`, `previousRequirements` and `evidence` are `text` fields of **100 000** characters (they were 4000, 4000 and 8000).
Measured live 2026-10-12 20:40 on Vol100kM: a 14-node Person plan written by "Propose another" was stored as exactly 4000 characters
ending in `...(truncated)`, because every writer cut its text with `TextLimits.truncate` - fine for a message a person reads, fatal for JSON
that is read back: `matching/configure` and the review tree could not parse it. Two rules now, both in `master.StoredJsonFit` (pure,
`StoredJsonFitTest`):

- a JSON that code parses back is **stored whole or not at all**. `MatchPlanLlmSuggester.write` and `MatchPlanSuggester` check requirements
  and evidence BEFORE touching the row; a plan that does not fit is not written, the pass answers, for that entity,
  `plan of N characters exceeds the field limit of M; the model proposed K nodes` (in the outcome's `refused` object, in the step's message,
  and, for "Propose another", through the §10.2 case (c) revert: the row goes back to PROPOSED with that reason and keeps its previous
  plan). A whole-project pass that refused some plans ends its job as an expected failure naming them, the other entities being written.
- `previousRequirements` copies the field it replaces, which always fits the same limit, so it is never cut either.

A 100-node tree is about 30 000 characters, so the limit leaves room for any realistic tree. Existing datasets need nothing: widening a
`maxLength` is a harmless evolution (EBX only checks values against it, no column is migrated); a plan stored cut by the old limit stays
cut (unparseable) until it is re-proposed - "Propose another" on it writes the whole plan.

**`bothNull` / `oneNull` in a stored plan are PLAN-level values, not always what is sent (2026-10-12, §55).** `DO_NOTHING` in
`requirements` means "abstain": a parent-confirmation (REFERENCE) field, a `contradiction: true` node, a field "not required" in an
AVERAGE node. `DecisionTreePlan`, `CrossSystemPathRule` and the candidate-filter reasoning read it that way and the stored JSON is never
rewritten. Whether the add-on takes it on a decision-tree field depends on its build: the build of 2026-09-27 did, the build 6.3.0.5-RC3 of
2026-10-10 refuses it, so the payload is translated when it is built (§55).

### 3.3 `MatchingPolicyTranslator` — the recursive tree build, and the leaf-name question

Each tier becomes one nested decision node (`function = "All fields match"` for an `EXACT` tier,
`"Average"` for the fuzzy one), `trueNode` the tier's own outcome leaf, `falseNode` the next tier — the
last tier's `falseNode` is a `NOT_MATCHED` leaf. This exactly mirrors the real `Companies` tree's own
nesting (§2.5, `docs/MASTER-ZONE.md` §1.1): three nested branches, innermost `Average` node, a `Not
Match`/`NOT_MATCHED` leaf at the bottom of every path. **`MatchingPolicyTranslator` writes the schema's
documented enum values (`MATCHED`/`SUSPECTED`/`NOT_MATCHED`), while the real, live `Companies`
configuration stores `"Match"`/`"Suspect"`/`"Not Match"` instead (§2.5).** §2.6's `javap` finding refines,
without fully closing, this: the add-on's own `DecisionNode` Java model carries a free-text `getName()`
label SEPARATELY from a real, strongly-typed `getMatchingResult()` (`MatchingResultType`, confirmed by
`javap` to have exactly the constants `MATCHED`/`SUSPECTED`/`NOT_MATCHED`) — so the schema's write-side
`name` enum and the live read-side display strings are plausibly two different properties the MCP tool's
JSON happens to key the same way, not a genuine round-trip inconsistency. This class still writes the
schema's documented enum values on that reasoning, but **the first real `matching/configure` run must
re-read the result with `get_matching_config` and check the leaf names it reports, adjusting
`MatchingPolicyTranslator` if the enum form is rejected or silently renamed** — a live write-then-read
round trip was forbidden this session either way, so this is a refined hypothesis, not a closed question.

### 3.3a The first real failure, 2026-09-21 22:16 — two bugs, both fixed (`fix/matching-policy-fields`)

The coordinator's first live `POST /projects/Companies/matching/configure` got past `get_matching_config`
(a genuine `CONFIG_NOT_FOUND`) and failed at `generate_matching_policy` itself:

```json
{"code":"INVALID_PARAMS","message":"Decision tree references a field not declared on the policy: name",
 "nextStep":"Add the field to matchingPolicy.fields, or reference an existing field path.","success":false}
```

The plan (`MatchPlan.requirements`) declared `clusteringFields: ["city","country"]`; its decision tree also
compared `name` — the EXACT identifier tier AND the `AVERAGE` tier's own fuzzy anchor. Nothing had ever
required a field used only for COMPARISON (never for blocking) to also appear in `clusteringFields`, so the
translator — which only ever built `matchingPolicy.fields` FROM `clusteringFields`, verbatim — never told the
add-on about `name` at all.

**Fix 1 — `matchingPolicy.fields` now declares the UNION of `clusteringFields` and every field the decision
tree compares**, order stable (`clusteringFields` first, then any additional tree field in first-appearance
order). A field's pre-clustering weight is its own highest weight across every tier it appears in (an
`AVERAGE`-tier field's own `weight`; an `EXACT`-tier field, which carries no `weight` of its own, defaults to
1), clamped to a minimum of 1 — never 0 (`matching_guide`: a threshold of 0 is rejected outright, and no
established meaning exists for a pre-clustering weight of 0 either). Null handling on a declared field
mirrors the tree's own value at that field's FIRST tier appearance, exactly as the live `PointOfSale`
configuration already does (§2.1/§2.5), rather than a hardcoded `DO_NOTHING`.

**A structural limit surfaced by this fix, not resolved by it**: this codebase has found no way to compare a
field in the tree WITHOUT also exposing it to pre-clustering — every tree field must now be declared in
`matchingPolicy.fields`, and every declared field carries a `weight` the schema itself calls a *pre-clustering*
weight. Whether `weight: 0` would opt a field out of pre-clustering while still letting it be compared is
UNKNOWN (CLAUDE.md/§2.1: never emit 0, and nothing in this session established what it does) — so, in effect,
`clusteringFields` today only orders/weights the pre-clustering gate rather than restricting membership in it.
`MatchPlanLlmPass`'s own `clusteringFields` tool-schema description was updated with one sentence saying so
(the schema's own JSON shape is unchanged).

**Fix 2 — every field path is record-relative WITH A LEADING SLASH**, found the same minute by re-reading
`matching_config_schema`'s own field descriptions (`fieldCapabilities` lists `/name`, `/city`, `/country`, ...;
"Field paths are record-relative, the same form `matchingPolicies[].fields[].field` takes") and the real, live,
already-running `PointOfSale` configuration, which stores `/Name`, `/Address/City`, `/Address/Country`,
`/Retailer` in BOTH `matchingPolicies[].fields[].field` and every `decisionTree...fields[].field`. This
codebase's own internal representation (`MatchPlanRules`/`MatchPlanLlmPass`'s `requirements` JSON,
`MatchPlanProfileReader`'s parsed `fieldCapabilities` map) stays slash-less throughout — a bare name becomes a
wire path in exactly one place, `MatchingPolicyTranslator.toFieldPath`, applied only when writing
`matchingPolicy.fields[].field` and every `decisionTree...fields[].field`. Idempotent: a name that already
carries a leading slash (a future grouped attribute path, e.g. `Address/City` written with its own leading
slash) is never doubled; an internal slash inside a grouped path is left untouched.

**Fix 3 — a translator self-check.** After building the policy, `MatchingPolicyTranslator` now walks the built
decision tree and asserts every field it references is present in `matchingPolicy.fields`, throwing a clear
`IllegalStateException` naming any gap otherwise — the exact invariant `generate_matching_policy` itself
enforces, checked here first. Given Fix 1's union construction this is currently unreachable through the
public API (a regression would surface as an uncaught exception in an existing pure test, not as tonight's
live `INVALID_PARAMS`) — kept anyway as a standing assertion for a future edit. `ebx.MatchingConfigurator` now
also catches this (a `RuntimeException`, since the translator stays pure/EBX-free) and ends the entity's
`PipelineStep` as `FAILED` rather than letting it escape unrecorded; `PipelineSteps.isDone` only ever matches
`DONE`, so a `FAILED` step never blocks a later re-run of `matching/configure` for the same entity.

**Fix 4 — a second, independent pre-flight guard against the live instance** (§3.1, "Added 2026-09-21,
between row 1 and row 2"): `MatchingConfigurator.checkFieldCapabilities` now also asks
`matching_config_schema(table[, dataModel])` for `fieldCapabilities` and refuses before ever calling
`generate_matching_policy` if a declared field is missing or structurally incapable of pre-clustering.

**Checked for the same two mistakes elsewhere in the configure chain, per the coordinator's own request**:
`generate_merge_policy`'s payload never carries a per-field survivor override yet (`buildMergePolicy`'s
`survivors` array is always empty — no producer of `requirements` populates one), so there was nothing to fix
there; the day one exists its field path needs the same `toFieldPath` treatment (now noted inline in
`buildMergePolicy`'s own comment). `patch_matching_config`'s only operation this codebase ever sends is
`set_merge_policy_link` (a `policyCode`, not a field path). `master.MatchingRunScope`'s `./_loadId`/`./id`
predicates and `ebx.MameMatchingApi`'s inputs (an `AdaptationTable`, an XPath predicate string, a master
record's own primary key) are plain EBX XPath/record-key values, a different namespace entirely from a MAME
field path — nothing to change there.

### 3.4 `autoMerge` is applied at translation time, not as a merge-policy setting

CLAUDE.md §8, quoted in full because it directly shaped this design: *"MATCHED groups are merged
automatically during the run even with merge mode DISABLED (mode only drives auto-creation of a new
golden record) ... If a data steward must confirm every merge, route MATCH outcomes to SUSPECTED in the
tree."* A merge policy's `mode` field does **not** gate auto-merge — only the decision tree's own leaf
name does. So `MatchPlan.autoMerge` (schema default `false`) is applied inside
`MatchingPolicyTranslator.buildMatchingPolicy`: with `autoMerge=false`, **every** tier's outcome — even
one `MatchPlanRules` itself proposed as `MATCH` (an exact identifier tier) — is forced to `SUSPECTED`;
with `autoMerge=true`, an exact tier's own `MATCH` outcome survives translation, but the fuzzy tier's
`SUSPECTED` never changes either way (`MatchPlanRules` never proposes anything else for it — nothing
fuzzy-only ever auto-merges, regardless of the flag). Unit-tested (`MatchingPolicyTranslatorTest`,
`autoMergeFalse_exactTierForcedToSuspected` / `autoMergeTrue_exactTierStaysMatched_fuzzyTierStillSuspected`).

**`useForManualMerge` is always `true` (coordinator follow-up, 2026-09-22)** — measured live the same day that
a policy this factory writes carried `"useForManualMerge":false` on `/root/Company`, which refuses
`MergeOperations.mergeGroup` (the call the Record lineage screen's own "confirm duplicate" action makes,
`docs/RECORD-LINEAGE.md` "Deciding on a suspect") on every instance; `buildMergePolicy` now writes `true`
unconditionally rather than the previous `false` — a fixed default, not a per-project choice, since a policy a
steward cannot use by hand from that screen is useless to this factory's whole model. Tested
(`MatchingPolicyTranslatorTest#mergePolicy_useForManualMergeIsTrue`).

### 3.5 Ownership guard — never overwrite a configuration this generator did not create

Same philosophy as `master.MasterResetEligibility` (`docs/MASTER-ZONE.md`'s own 2026-09-21 incident
writeup). Ownership evidence is simply *"this project's own `MATCHING_CONFIG` `PipelineStep` for this
entity has already completed"* (`PipelineSteps.isDone`, the same resumable-skip convention every other
generator in this codebase already uses): if `get_matching_config` finds a real, existing configuration
and the step has never completed, `MatchingConfigurator` refuses outright, naming the table. This is a
**deliberately narrower** promise than "detect and reuse ours, refuse everyone else's" — nothing about
telling the two apart from a bare `MameConfig` read (no ownership marker exists in the shape itself) was
established this session, so reconfiguring/patching a pre-existing configuration is simply never
attempted by this lot.

### 3.6 The second real failure, 2026-09-22 08:58 — `valid:true` read as invalid, fixed (`fix/validate-response-shape`)

`POST /projects/Companies/matching/configure` got all the way through `generate_matching_policy` and
`generate_merge_policy` (policy `Company`, a 2-tier tree over `/name`/`/city`/`/country`, merge policy
`Company` linked — all verified afterwards with `get_matching_config`), then REFUSED with:

```json
{"data":{"messages":[],"table":"/root/Company","valid":true},"success":true}
```

— a plainly `valid:true` answer read as invalid. `ebx.MatchingConfigurator` read `valid` at the ROOT of the
`validate_matching_config` answer (`validateResult.json.path("valid")`), while this tool — like every
match-merge tool (`get_matching_config`, `get_matching_activation_status`, `activate_matching`, ...) — wraps
its payload under `data`: `{"success":true,"data":{"valid":true,"messages":[],"table":"/root/Company"}}`.
`activate`'s own parsing a few lines below already read `data.state` with a root fallback; the validate
parsing had simply been left inconsistent with it.

**Fix — one pure helper, `master.MameAnswer`, shared by every answer-shape read in `MatchingConfigurator`.**
`MameAnswer.success(json, defaultWhenAbsent)` reads the root `success` flag (a `null` json defaults exactly
like a present-but-absent field); `MameAnswer.code(json)` reads the root `code` of a soft miss;
`MameAnswer.field(json, name)` reads `data.<name>` first, the ROOT `<name>` as fallback (a `MissingNode`,
never a crash, when neither is present) — the exact double-read `activate_matching`'s own `state` check
already did, now shared instead of duplicated. `MatchingConfigurator` now uses it for `get_matching_config`'s
`success`/`code`, `validate_matching_config`'s `valid`/`messages`, and `activate_matching`'s `state`; a
`success:false` soft miss on the validate call itself (e.g. a stale `CONFIG_NOT_FOUND` between the patch and
the validate) is now reported as its own distinct refusal instead of silently reading as "invalid" by the
same accident. A `valid:false` refusal now quotes the `messages` array (code, path, severity, message, hint
per entry) via `describeValidationMessages`, not the raw JSON blob.

**The same fix applied to `matching_config_schema`'s `fieldCapabilities` read** (`master.MatchPlanProfileReader
.readFieldCapabilities`), a related but DIFFERENT bug: both call sites (`MatchingConfigurator
.checkFieldCapabilities`, `MatchPlanLlmSuggester`) already resolved the string-wrapped `data` correctly
before calling it — the defect was inside `readFieldCapabilities` itself, which read a `fieldCapabilities`
key that never exists anywhere in the real shape. The table-scoped `matching_config_schema(table=...)`
answer's resolved `data` document IS the field-capabilities document itself: `{"description":...,
"table":"/root/Company","fields":[{"field":"/name","available":[{"searchStrategy":"@default",
"resolvesTo":"@Name"}],"default":"@default"},...]}` (measured live by the coordinator, night of 2026-09-21 /
morning of 2026-09-22) — the array is at `fields`, never nested under a `fieldCapabilities` key. This made
every `preClusteringCapabilityNotVerified` note fire even when the server genuinely answered capabilities,
symptom quoted verbatim in the live refusal: `"Company: matching_config_schema(table=...) returned no
fieldCapabilities"`. Fixed by reading `MameAnswer.field(pSchemaDocument, "fields")` instead — harmless reuse
of the same data-or-root helper even though this particular document never carries a `data` wrapper of its
own (the fallback lands on the real `fields` key on the first try).

**Idempotence corollary, same review.** The failed attempt above had already run `generate_matching_policy`/
`generate_merge_policy`/`patch_matching_config` to completion before failing at validate — so a plain retry
finds a REAL, already-`success:true` configuration on the table while the project's own `MATCHING_CONFIG`
step for the entity is still `FAILED`, not `DONE`. Before this fix §3.5's ownership guard could not tell that
config apart from a stranger's and refused outright, forever — a genuine deadlock, not just this bug's
runtime symptom, since nothing ever marks the step `DONE` to unblock the next retry. `configureOne` now
checks its OWN most recently recorded step detail for this exact project/entity
(`lastConfigStepDetail`/`priorAttemptCompletedGenerationAndLink`): only when that self-recorded detail shows
`generate_matching_policy`, `generate_merge_policy` AND `patch_matching_config` all answered success does it
resume straight at `validate_matching_config`/`activate_matching`, skipping every write call — never by
re-parsing the live server's own found-config shape, which (unlike `MameDataModelResolution`'s
`AMBIGUOUS_TABLE` candidates) is not established well enough this session to key on safely. A found config
with no matching recorded attempt (a stranger's, or this project's own from before this fix shipped) still
hits the original unconditional refusal — resuming is "trust our own bookkeeping," never "guess from their
answer." **Not exercised live** (write tools are forbidden in the session that wrote this fix) — verified by
unit test against the exact captured answers above, never by a live retry.
