## 4. Where results live, and the scoped run

### 4.1 The metadataset (READ (live), `docs/MASTER-ZONE.md` §1.2, re-confirmed this session on `Companies_Companies_MDS`)

`RecordMetadata` (PK `functionalId`, FK into the business table itself; `goldenId`, FK into the same
table, null unless merged away; `state`, `groupId`, `autoCreated`, `hasSuspects`), `Matched`,
`Suspected`, `MergeValueLineageCompact` — all inside `<masterDataspaceKey>_<masterDatasetName>_MDS`,
following the one live naming convention this codebase has ever observed (`MasterLoader.RecordMetadataMergeCheck`'s
own Javadoc: dataspace and dataset both named `Companies` on the one real example — **still unverified for
a name where dataspace and dataset differ**, and `Companies_Master`/`Master` genuinely is such a case:
`<Companies_Master>_<Master>_MDS`, never observed live since the metadataset does not exist yet, §2.4).

### 4.2 `MatchPlanSuggester` (task 2) — deterministic proposal

`ebx.MatchPlanSuggester.suggest` (route `POST /projects/{code}/matching/suggest`, administrators): reuses
`master.MasterModel.buildFromStaging(...).builtEntities` to get the exact same "promoted" set
`ebx.MasterGenerator` computes (never re-derived), runs `ebx.MemberEntitiesBackfill` first for the same
reason `MasterGenerator`/`MasterLoader` do, then hands each promoted entity's accepted attributes plus
any accepted `CHECK_DIGIT` `QualityRule` evidence (`FactoryPaths.QualityRule.KIND`/`ARGUMENT`) to
`master.MatchPlanRules.propose` (pure, unit-tested). **`Contact` is not proposed by default**: it carries
an accepted `accountIdRef` attribute referencing `Company` (a different entity), which
`MatchPlanRules.childOf` detects as a child relationship — de-duplicating a child independently of its
parent risks a suspect queue that never converges and duplicates a decision the parent's own plan already
drives. A self-reference (e.g. a hypothetical `Account.parentAccountId`) is explicitly NOT treated as a
child (tested).

**Historical record, kept as-is — REVERSED 2026-09-22, see §12.** The paragraph above described the
2026-09-21 decision exactly as it stood at the time; it is left unedited so this file stays a true evidence
trail of what changed and when. As of `feature/child-entities-match-too`, a child entity (`Contact` included)
IS proposed by default, exactly like any other entity with a validated identifier — `MatchPlanRules.childOf`
(renamed `childLink`) is no longer used to skip an entity, only to (a) offer its reference attribute as an
additional clustering candidate and (b) word the rationale. Read §12 before assuming the behaviour described
above still holds.

Never touches a `MatchPlan` already `ACCEPTED`/`REJECTED`/`APPLIED` — only a still-
`PROPOSED` plan (or none) is written/refreshed, the same rule `StagingSuggester`/`QualitySuggester` already
apply to their own tables.

**2026-09-21 rework — the field-role recipe (fuzzy name, `country` blocking, `city` supporting) was
removed, on the product owner's explicit instruction.** It imitated the real `Companies` policy
field-role by field-role (§1.1 of `docs/MASTER-ZONE.md`, quoted again in an earlier revision of this
file), which is company-specific naming knowledge — useless, and actively misleading, on a product,
material or site repository ("no field there is ever going to be called `country`"). The product owner
judged generalizing that heuristic (e.g. "the first STRING field" or some other name-shape guess) to be of
little interest and asked for it to be removed outright, not patched. `master.MatchPlanRules` now proposes
**only** an EXACT, `MATCH`-terminal tier per validated identifier (an attribute carrying an accepted
`CHECK_DIGIT` `QualityRule`, whatever KIND of identifier it validates — the class never branches on the
specific `IBAN`/`LEI`/`GTIN`/… string) — the one field role that is genuinely structural, true of any
domain. An entity with no validated identifier is skipped, naming §4.2.1 below as the next step. See
`master.MatchPlanRules`'s own Javadoc (rewritten the same day) for the full, short list of what stayed and
why (the child-entity skip; the `autoMerge=false`/merge-policy defaults) versus what was removed.

### 4.2.1 `matching/suggest-llm` (new, 2026-09-21; **redesigned same day after coordinator review**) — the
language-model field-role pass

**What it does.** `ebx.MatchPlanLlmSuggester.suggest` (route `POST /projects/{code}/matching/suggest-llm`,
administrators — same guard as `staging/suggest-llm`), backed by the pure `master.MatchPlanLlmPass` (same
shape as `staging.StagingLlmPass`: value objects, a `Session` with local tool handlers, systemPrompt/
userPrompt) plus a second pure class, `master.MatchPlanProfileReader` (JSON parsing of the `match-merge`
MCP responses — split out specifically so it is unit-tested with hand-built fixtures, see below). It
proposes the field ROLES `MatchPlanRules` can no longer infer from a name — a fuzzy anchor, its supporting
fields, and blocking/clustering fields — for every PROMOTED, non-child entity, then writes a `MatchPlan`
row per entity (origin `LLM`, status `PROPOSED`), through the exact same structured `requirements` JSON
shape §3.2 describes (unchanged contract: `master.MatchingPolicyTranslator` needed no change at all — it
already treats `tiers`/`clusteringFields`/`mergePolicy` generically, whoever wrote them).

**Blocking redesign, coordinator review 2026-09-21: this pass no longer profiles data itself, and no
longer invents its own algorithm vocabulary.** The first version scanned the project's STAGING table with
a hand-rolled, capped Java loop and hardcoded its own allowed-algorithm list plus a guessed
algorithm-needs-STRING compatibility table. All three removed:

- **Profiling now goes through the `match-merge` MCP server's own `profile_table_for_matching`**, called
  on the project's **MASTER** table (`Project.masterDataspace`/`masterDataset` — matching runs on master,
  not staging; the route refuses outright if the master zone was never generated/loaded), the same
  `McpServers.client(pFactory, McpServers.MATCH_MERGE)`/`McpClient.callTool` pattern
  `MatchingConfigurator` already uses. The real, live response shape (captured by the coordinator,
  2026-09-21):
  ```json
  {"success":true,"data":{"table":"/root/Company","rowCount":107,"fields":[
   {"field":"/name","fillRate":1,"cardinality":103,
    "mostFrequentValue":"<real value>","mostFrequentValueCount":2,
    "mostFrequentToken":"<real token>","mostFrequentTokenDocFrequency":23,
    "provenance":{"cardinality":"EXACT","fillRate":"EXACT","mostFrequentToken":"EXACT","mostFrequentValue":"EXACT"}},
   {"field":"/vatNo","fillRate":0.439,"cardinality":46,"provenance":{"cardinality":"SAMPLED", ...}}
  ]}}
  ```
  Every statistic carries its OWN `provenance`: `EXACT`, `SAMPLED` (a lower bound over at most 10000
  records/1024 distinct values — **never divided by row count**), `NOT_SUPPORTED` (the accompanying `0`/
  `null` means nothing), `FAILED`. This removes the previous design's worst defect: a hardcoded scan cap
  made a genuinely unique identifier on a large table read as barely distinct, since volume is never
  marginal in this project (`PLAN.md`) — the server's own `SAMPLED` tag now tells the guards exactly when a
  ratio is unsafe to trust, instead of a wrong number being trusted silently.
- **The allowed algorithm/null-handling/merge-function vocabulary now comes from `matching_config_schema`**
  (called per entity, with `table=<its path>` — the same call also returns `fieldCapabilities`, see below).
  `master.MatchPlanLlmPass.AllowedVocabulary` is a run-time parameter of `Session`/the tool schema now, not
  a class constant; the algorithm-needs-`STRING` guard is gone entirely (it was this codebase's own guess,
  never sourced from anything authoritative) — the editor's own `matching_guide` text is fed to the model
  instead (see next bullet), and its first rule is literally *"Pick the algorithm from the field's data
  profile, not from its name."*
- **The editor's own guidance, not a recipe written in this codebase.** `matching_guide` is called once per
  run for all three topics (`algorithm-selection`, `threshold-tuning`, `merge-strategy` —
  `{"success":true,"data":"<markdown>"}` each) and the three texts are prepended to `userPrompt` verbatim.
  `systemPrompt` now only ever states the ROLES, the output contract and the guards — no algorithm-choice
  advice of its own (tested: `MatchPlanLlmPassTest` asserts the system prompt never mentions `jarowinkler`/
  `levenshtein` by name).

**`matching_config_schema`'s real shape, measured live by the coordinator, 2026-09-21 — on a SECOND review,
after this document's first revision guessed flat keys (`algorithms`/`nullHandlings`/…) that turn out not
to exist at all.** Two real, measured facts that shaped the fix:

- **The envelope is `{"success":true,"data":"<STRING>"}`** — unlike `profile_table_for_matching`, whose
  `data` is already an object, THIS tool's `data` is a JSON document serialized as a plain STRING that must
  be parsed a second time. `MatchPlanProfileReader.resolveSchemaData` handles both shapes (an object passes
  straight through, a string is re-parsed, a malformed string degrades to an empty document rather than
  throwing).
- **The parsed document is a JSON Schema of `MameConfig`** (sibling top-level keys: `patchOps`, `errorCodes`,
  `messageCodes`, `businessObjectConfig`, `applyConfig`, `mergeChains`), not a flat object. The enums this
  class needs live at exact, deep, measured paths — `MatchPlanProfileReader.at(node, "a.b.c")` walks them,
  and a missing path fails naming THAT path, never a guessed fallback:
  - algorithm: `properties.matchingPolicies.items.properties.decisionTree.properties.fields.items.properties.algorithm.enum`
    → the 11 `ebx-addon-mame@…` codes (`exact`, `jarowinkler`, `levenshtein`, `beider-morse`, `soundex`,
    `range`, `operator`, `hybridFuzzy`, `fuzzyFullText`, `exactFullText`, `phoneticFullText`).
  - null handling (`bothNullValueHandling`/`oneNullValueHandling`, same enum): `…fields.items.properties.bothNullValueHandling.enum`
    → `DO_NOTHING, NOT_MATCH, MATCH` (a third value, `MATCH`, this codebase had never seen before).
    **Two enums since the add-on build 6.3.0.5-RC3 of 2026-10-10 (§55):** the line above is the DECISION-TREE field
    (`matchingPolicies[].decisionTree.fields[]`) and now reads `MATCH, NOT_MATCH`; the matching-POLICY field
    (`matchingPolicies[].fields[]`, the pre-processing / candidate fields) has its own
    `…matchingPolicies.items.properties.fields.items.properties.{both,one}NullValueHandling.enum` =
    `DO_NOTHING, NOT_MATCH, MATCH`. `MatchPlanProfileReader.readVocabulary` reads them separately
    (`AllowedVocabulary.nullHandlings` = policy field, `treeNullHandlings` = tree field); a schema with only one
    (builds up to 2026-09-27) serves for both.
  - record selection: `properties.mergePolicies.items.properties.recordSelectionFunctionChain.items.properties.function.enum`
    → six RAW i18n keys (`mame.addon.reference.data.recordSelectionPolicy.{firstAcquired,lastUpdate,
    mostCompleted,mostRecentlyAcquired,mostTrustedSource,wasGolden}.label`) — `MatchPlanProfileReader.shortenI18nKey`
    recovers the short middle segment (`mostCompleted`, …) this codebase's `requirements` JSON already uses.
  - required runtime params per algorithm are only in that same node's `description` TEXT, not parsed
    programmatically: `jarowinkler` defaults `jaroWinklerThreshold` to 0.7 (usable with no params); `range`
    defaults `rangeValue`/`rangeUnit` (usable with no params); `hybridFuzzy` (three params) and `operator`
    (one param) are REQUIRED with no default — confirming the refused pair (`ALGORITHMS_REQUIRING_PARAMS`)
    is exactly right, kept as a documented constant citing this source rather than parsed from prose.
  - decision node function (`…decisionTree.properties.function.enum` → `"All fields match","At least N
    fields match","Average","Predicate"`) and terminal leaf names (`…trueNode.properties.name.enum` →
    `MATCHED, SUSPECTED, NOT_MATCHED`) and merge mode (`properties.mergePolicies.items.properties.mode.enum`
    → `DISABLED, DUPLICATES_AND_SINGLETONS, ONLY_DUPLICATES, ANY_DUPLICATES`) and default field merge
    (`…defaultFieldMergeFunctionChain.items.properties.function.enum` → `last update, longest, max, min,
    most frequent, most trusted source`) were also read, but nothing in this lot exposes any of them as a
    model choice (`Session` fixes the decision-tree shape itself, `mode`/`defaultFieldMerge` stay the fixed
    defaults `MatchPlanRules` always used) — recorded here for the next lot, not wired to anything yet.
  - pre-clustering `searchStrategy` is a free string (a template key, e.g. `@default`/`@Levenshtein`), no
    enum to validate against — unrelated to `fieldCapabilities`' own `available` list, which is what the
    clustering guard actually checks.

**`fieldCapabilities` (only returned when `matching_config_schema` is called WITH a `table` argument) could
NOT be captured live** — on the demo master table the call answers `{"success":false,"code":
"TABLE_NOT_FOUND","message":"Table not found: /root/Company","nextStep":"…"}`, with and without the same
`dataModel` argument `MatchingConfigurator.configureOne` passes (`ebx-mdm-factory/src/main/java/com/on/ebx/factory/ebx/MatchingConfigurator.java:152`)
— the table is not registered with the add-on yet. `ebx.MatchPlanLlmSuggester` therefore calls the schema
TWICE: once WITHOUT `table` for the vocabulary (measured to always work — a failure there aborts the whole
route, the guards depend on it), and once PER ENTITY WITH `table`+`dataModel` for `fieldCapabilities` alone
(a soft miss there NEVER aborts the route or skips the entity — the pre-clustering guard is simply not
enforced for it, and the run's own `notes`/`preClusteringCapabilityNotVerified` say so). **Genuinely
unverified**: `fieldCapabilities` itself has never been observed to return real data on this instance.

**Every `match-merge` tool's soft-miss shape, measured live**: `{"success":false,"code":"…","message":"…",
"nextStep":"…"}` — `MatchPlanProfileReader.describeSoftMiss` surfaces the real `message`/`nextStep` the
server gives (replacing an earlier revision's own guessed, code-keyed hint text, which is now gone).

**`ebx.MatchPlanLlmSuggester` cross-checks** the literal `"ebx-addon-mame@exact"` is actually present in
whatever algorithm list came back (the `MATCH`-terminal guard depends on recognising it by name) and refuses
the whole route if not, rather than silently running with that guard disabled; and it intersects the
schema's own six record-selection functions with the three `master.MatchingPolicyTranslator` actually knows
how to translate to a real i18n key. **Translator finding, as asked**: `MatchingPolicyTranslator.buildMergePolicy`
(`ebx-mdm-factory/src/main/java/com/on/ebx/factory/master/MatchingPolicyTranslator.java:222-227`) does NOT
send the short name to the server as is — it looks the short key up in its own `RECORD_SELECTION_FUNCTIONS`
map (lines 68-74, three entries: `mostCompleted`/`lastUpdate`/`mostTrustedSource`) and always sends the
FULL i18n key (defaulting to `mostCompleted`'s full key if the short key is not one of those three) — which
is exactly why the intersection above is necessary: the other three real enum values (`firstAcquired`,
`mostRecentlyAcquired`, `wasGolden`) have no entry in that map and would silently collapse to `mostCompleted`'s
key if ever offered to the model.

**What the model sees — metadata and AGGREGATE numbers only, never a record's actual value unless the
project opted in.** For each eligible entity: its accepted attributes' name/label/dataType/maxLength, the
accepted cleaning steps and quality rules on each (`kind` + `argument`, e.g. `"CHECK_DIGIT (IBAN)"` — never
a value), the foreign keys to other entities, and — from `profile_table_for_matching` on the MASTER table —
row count, fill rate and distinct count/ratio (each tagged with its own provenance), and the most-frequent-
value/token **share as a count** (`mostFrequentValueCount`/`mostFrequentTokenDocFrequency` — "this value
covers N of 107 rows" is exactly the "placeholder dominates the field" signal `matching_guide`'s own
threshold-tuning topic talks about). **`average length` is no longer part of the context at all** — a gap,
not a design choice: `profile_table_for_matching`'s real response (above) has no such statistic, and this
lot does not re-derive it with a custom scan (the whole point of the redesign was to stop doing that). If a
future lot needs it, it has to come from the `match-merge` MCP server too, or be explicitly flagged as a
capability gap to the add-on's own team — never quietly reintroduced as a Java-side scan.

**Value sharing is the PROJECT's own decision, never a caller's** (coordinator review, 2026-09-21, after
`feature/quality-llm` merged into `main` and added `Project.llmValueSharing`): the earlier revision's
`shareValues` query parameter is GONE — a URL must never be able to override a project owner's own
data-sharing choice. `ebx.MatchPlanLlmSuggester.suggest` reads it exactly the way
`ebx.QualityLlmSuggester.suggest` reads the same field for its own quality pass
(`ebx-mdm-factory/src/main/java/com/on/ebx/factory/ebx/MatchPlanLlmSuggester.java:137`):
`"SAMPLE_VALUES".equals(project.getString(FactoryPaths.Project.LLM_VALUE_SHARING))` — null/absent/anything
else (in particular the default, `SHAPES_ONLY`) reads `false`. This gates `mostFrequentValue`/
`mostFrequentToken` specifically: `MatchPlanProfileReader.readFieldStats` (pure JSON parsing) always
extracts them raw — it is explicitly documented as "not a security boundary" — and
`ebx.MatchPlanLlmSuggester.toLlmEntity` is the ONE place they are copied into an `AttributeInfo`
conditionally on that value; the counts are copied unconditionally, since they are numbers. The route's own
JSON response echoes the effective mode as `valueSharing: "SAMPLE_VALUES"|"SHAPES_ONLY"`
(`MatchPlanLlmSuggester.java:342`), the same key `quality/suggest-llm` already echoes. Tested
(`MatchPlanLlmPassTest.shareValuesGatesTheActualValue`): a sentinel value/token is shown when the pure
`ProjectInfo.shareValues` flag is true and hidden — while its count still shows — when false.

**Tools**: `propose_match_plan(entity, tiers[], clusteringFields[], mergeHints, rationale, confidence)` —
producing exactly `MatchPlan.requirements`'s own shape; `skip_entity(entity, reason)`; `note(text)`. No
`autoMerge` property exists on the schema at all — the model has no channel to set it, the same guarantee
`MatchPlanRules` gives structurally by never deciding it either.

**Guards, every one an actionable refusal plus the same 3-strikes circuit breaker `StagingLlmPass.Session`
established (keyed on the entity AND the actual repeated tiers/fields, not the entity alone — three
DIFFERENT correction attempts on one entity is normal, expected model behaviour and must not trip it)**:
every field must be a real accepted attribute of the entity; the algorithm must be one the schema reports
as allowed (never hardcoded any more); `hybridFuzzy`/`operator` are refused outright even if in the allowed
list — they need a runtime parameter this pass does not populate (a fixed technical fact `matching_guide`
states, not a domain guess: a policy generated without it persists clean and fails when the engine starts;
`jarowinkler`, by contrast, defaults its own threshold to 0.7, so it is not refused); a `MATCH`-terminal
tier only ever uses the exact algorithm at `minimumScore 100` on every field, anything fuzzy must terminate
`SUSPECTED`; a clustering field must be reported as CAPABLE of pre-clustering by `fieldCapabilities` (an
empty `available` list there means no) — a structural capability limit, refused outright, never merely
"unmeasurable"; a clustering field must ALSO — but only when its statistic's own provenance is `EXACT` —
have fill rate ≥ 50%, distinct ratio ≤ 90%, at least 2 distinct values (INFERRED thresholds, each one's
Javadoc says exactly what is measured and that it only applies under `EXACT` provenance) — **except** a
field already validated as a near-unique identifier by the `MATCH`-tier guard, exempt from the ceiling:
blocking directly on an exact identifier is cheap (one exact lookup, not a fuzzy scan of a whole bucket)
and precise (it already passed the strictly stronger near-unique guard) — a structural argument, true of
any domain, not "because one demo policy does it"; a `MATCH`-tier field itself needs distinct ratio ≥ 95%
and fill rate ≥ 30%, again only enforced under `EXACT` provenance; a clustering field must already be used
by one of the plan's own tiers; at least one tier is required. **A statistic whose own provenance is not
`EXACT` is NEVER the reason a proposal is refused** — the field is allowed through, added to that call's
"unmeasurable" set, and the whole plan's confidence is capped (`Session.UNMEASURABLE_CONFIDENCE_CAP = 60`,
the same reasoning `StagingLlmPass.Session`'s own single-source cap already established) with a rationale
note naming which fields. Child entities are never shown as eligible at all (same structural reason as
`MatchPlanRules`' own skip) — refused with a message naming the parent if the model tries anyway.

**Historical record, kept as-is — REVERSED 2026-09-22, see §12.** As of `feature/child-entities-match-too`,
a child entity is a normal, eligible entity of this pass too; the sentence above described the 2026-09-21
behaviour only. Its own `REFERENCE`-role attribute (the link to its parent) may now be proposed as a
lower-weight SUPPORTING field of a SUSPECTED/AVERAGE tier — never a MATCH-terminal or EXACT-tier one.

Idempotence: never touches a `MatchPlan` already decided (`ACCEPTED`/`REJECTED`/`APPLIED`) nor a
`USER`-origin one, even while still `PROPOSED` — checked once inside `Session` before a tool call is even
accepted, and again, defensively, at write time.

**A real `PipelineStep` is now recorded for this route** (coordinator review, 2026-09-21, after
`feature/quality-llm` merged into `main` first and added its own `QUALITY_SUGGEST_LLM` enum value the same
way). `MATCHING_SUGGEST_LLM` was added to `PipelineStep.step` in `tools/build_xsd.py`, next to
`MATCHING_CONFIG`/`MATCHING_RUN` — the XSD was regenerated with the tool, never edited by hand; the diff is
exactly the one new `xs:enumeration` block (`git diff` of `MdmFactory.xsd`, +6 lines). `ebx.MatchPlanLlmSuggester.suggest`
is wrapped in `PipelineSteps.begin`/`PipelineSteps.end` exactly the way `ebx.QualityLlmSuggester.suggest`
already does for its own step — empty `""` scope, not `null` (the "empty-scope trap": an EBX `null` would
never match `PipelineSteps.isDone`'s own `scopeEquals` predicate the way a stored empty string does — see
that class' own Javadoc, `CLAUDE.md` §9). Full traceability of the run itself also still exists via
`AgentRun`/`AgentStep` (`AgentRuntime.run`), the same mechanism every other language-model pass in this
codebase already relies on for its own trace.

**Tests**: `master.MatchPlanLlmPassTest` (the pure `Session` guards, including the new provenance-aware
ones, the pre-clustering-capability guard, the value-sharing gate, and a structural reflection proof that
`AttributeInfo` has exactly two `String` fields that can ever carry a value) and
`master.MatchPlanProfileReaderTest` — hand-built MCP response fixtures with placeholder values (never a
real one), now including the REAL measured `matching_config_schema` nesting (string-wrapped `data`, the
full `properties.matchingPolicies…`/`properties.mergePolicies…` paths, the six raw record-selection i18n
keys, all 11 algorithm codes): one profile field with `EXACT` everything, one with `SAMPLED` cardinality
(`vatNo`, mirroring the coordinator's own live example), one whose `mostFrequentToken` is `NOT_SUPPORTED`
(reads back `null`, not a placeholder), a technical field (`/id`) excluded from the business-attribute map,
a `success:false` soft-miss response degrading to zero/empty rather than throwing, `resolveSchemaData`
proven both on a string and on an already-parsed object (`profile_table_for_matching`'s own shape) and on a
malformed string, and `describeSoftMiss` proven to surface the real `message`/`nextStep`.

**What is NOT verified**: never exercised against the live instance this session (no MCP call, no real
language model call, no EBX write) — the test suite covers the pure decision/parsing logic and prompt
content only. `fieldCapabilities`' own shape is the single biggest remaining unverified assumption (see
above: the table-scoped call has only ever been observed to soft-miss on this instance); the clustering/
identifier/confidence-cap thresholds (50%/90%/95%/30%/60) are this lot's own inferred choices, not read
from a product document — a real run against `Companies`' own master data (or a product/site dataset once
one exists on this instance) should confirm they neither refuse a genuinely useful field nor accept a
useless one, and be retuned if not.

### 4.2.2 Attribute ROLES and cross-system usefulness (branch `fix/matching-child-detection`, second
finding from the same real run, 2026-09-21)

**The real run's second defect.** With the child-detection fix from §4.2.1 in place, the FIRST real run of
`matching/suggest-llm` against `Companies`' own master data proposed a useless EXACT tier on `supplierId` (a
per-source record key — unique within its own source by construction, so it can never repeat, whether
against another record of the SAME source or a DIFFERENT one) while never proposing anything on `vatNo` (a
genuine, validated, cross-system identifier, 44% filled but 98% distinct AMONG ITS FILLED VALUES). Root
cause: the identifier guard's near-unique ratio was `cardinality / TOTAL row count` — `supplierId` is
100%-filled and 100%-distinct, so it trivially cleared the 95% threshold either way, while `vatNo`'s 44
filled, 43-distinct values (98% distinct among filled) divided by the table's full row count read as only
~43% distinct, well under the threshold, and was wrongly refused. The total-row ratio was simply the wrong
number for an identifier question.

**Fix 1 — a structural `role` per attribute, enforced everywhere, never inferred by the model.**
`master.MatchPlanLlmPass.AttributeInfo` gained a `role` field (`ROLE_SOURCE_KEY`/`ROLE_REFERENCE`/
`ROLE_BUSINESS` constants) and a new pure static `MatchPlanLlmPass.deriveRole(boolean pHasReferenceEntity,
List<Boolean> pMappingsAreOnSourceKeyColumns)`:
- `REFERENCE` when the attribute carries an accepted `referenceEntity` (a foreign key) — checked first, so a
  reference wins even if its own mappings happen to also read a source-key column.
- `SOURCE_KEY` when the attribute has at least one ACCEPTED-or-APPLIED mapping AND every one of them reads a
  landing column its own landing table's `SourceKeyRule` flagged as (part of) that source's own record key
  (`LandingColumn.sourceKey`). Deliberately ALL, not ANY: a canonical attribute that unifies one source's own
  key with another source's ordinary business column is not a source key overall — at least one source gives
  it real business meaning.
- `BUSINESS` otherwise — including an attribute with NO accepted mapping at all (never defaults to
  `SOURCE_KEY`, since that would claim a fact never established).
`ebx.MatchPlanLlmSuggester.mappingsAreOnSourceKeyColumns` (the only EBX-side caller) reads the booleans:
every ACCEPTED-or-APPLIED `AttributeMapping` of the attribute, its `landingColumn`'s own `sourceKey` flag.
`Session.proposeMatchPlan` refuses a `SOURCE_KEY` field in ANY tier (not only `MATCH` — a per-source key is
never a useful comparison field, fuzzy or exact) and, defensively, a second time in the `clusteringFields`
loop (structurally unreachable in practice, since a `SOURCE_KEY` field can never enter `fieldsUsedInTiers`
in the first place — kept explicit because the coordinator asked for the refusal "in clusteringFields" too).
`TECHNICAL_KEY` (`sourceSystem`/`sourceId`) is not a role of this enum at all — those never reach
`AttributeInfo` to begin with, excluded upstream (`!attribute.primaryKey` in `toLlmEntity`) the same way they
always have been.

**Fix 2 — `distinctAmongFilled`, not `distinctRatio`, for the identifier guard.** `AttributeInfo` gained
`filledCount(rowCount)` (`fillRate × rowCount`, rounded — null unless `fillRateReliable()`),
`distinctAmongFilled(rowCount)` (`distinctCount / filledCount` — null unless both `cardinalityReliable()` and
`fillRateReliable()`), and `neverRepeats(rowCount)` (`distinctCount == filledCount` — a field whose every
filled value is unique, not even a same-system duplicate, so an EXACT match on it can structurally never
find two different records to match; `Boolean`, not `boolean` — "not measured" must never read as "safe").
`Session.MIN_DISTINCT_RATIO_FOR_IDENTIFIER`/`MIN_FILL_RATE_FOR_IDENTIFIER` now compare against
`distinctAmongFilled`; a `Boolean.TRUE` `neverRepeats` refuses the tier outright, with its own message,
distinct from the `SOURCE_KEY` refusal (`vatNo`'s 44%/98%-among-filled shape now correctly passes; a
100%-filled/100%-distinct `BUSINESS` field like a generated document number is refused by `neverRepeats`,
not by the role guard — same practical effect, different reason surfaced to the model). The CLUSTERING guard
deliberately keeps the OLD `distinctRatio` (over total row count) — its own semantics (bucket distribution
over the real population, nulls included) are genuinely different from an identifier question, not the same
number computed twice; `Session.MIN_DISTINCT_RATIO_FOR_IDENTIFIER`'s own Javadoc says so explicitly, to stop
a future edit from "fixing" it back to one shared ratio.

**Fix 3 — cross-system usefulness, measured live by SQL, lazily, with a documented "not measured" fallback
(REWRITTEN after coordinator review, 2026-09-21, BLOCKING before merge).** The first version of this fix
measured `crossSystemSharedCount` for EVERY non-`SOURCE_KEY` candidate attribute, up front, in `toLlmEntity`,
with a self-join statement. The coordinator flagged this as blocking: a self-join is on the order of
rows²/distinct-value-count — harmless on the 107-row demo table, catastrophic on this project's real tables
(hundreds of millions of rows, `CLAUDE.md`: "volume is never marginal in this project") — and a low-cardinality
field (a country code) would have triggered a disproportionately expensive query for a number the guard does
not even need most of the time. The coordinator ran BOTH forms live on the demo master table (read-only SQL
tool, 2026-09-21) and reported both results:
- the self-join (`FROM "Company" a, "Company" b WHERE a.f=b.f AND a."sourceSystem"<>b."sourceSystem"`) IS
  accepted by the EBX SQL engine (answered 0 for `vatNo` and for `supplierId` on that table) — so the earlier
  documented uncertainty ("never verified live") is resolved: it was never a rejected statement, only the
  wrong statement to run at this project's real volume;
- a `GROUP BY ... HAVING` derived table is ALSO accepted and is the linear-in-row-count shape to use:
  `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT c."name" AS v FROM "Company" c WHERE c."name" IS NOT NULL GROUP BY c."name"
  HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT c."sourceSystem") > 1) t` answered `4`.

`ebx.MatchPlanLlmSuggester.crossSystemSharedCount` now runs exactly that shape:
```sql
SELECT COUNT(*) AS SHARED FROM (
  SELECT a."<field>" AS v FROM "<Entity>" a WHERE a."<field>" IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY a."<field>" HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT a."sourceSystem") > 1
) t
```
(Java query API — `Adaptation.createQuery`/`Query<Tuple>`/`QueryResult<Tuple>`, the same shape
`ebx.RelationChecker#runCount` already established; every identifier shape-checked
(`[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`) before being concatenated into SQL text; on ANY failure the method still returns
`null` — "not measured" — never throws, caught with a broad `RuntimeException` since this exact statement,
while verified by the coordinator's own hand-run probe, has never been run live BY THIS CODEBASE.)

**The measurement itself moved from eager (up front, per candidate attribute) to lazy (per accepted
`MATCH`-tier field, at proposal time).** `MatchPlanLlmPass.AttributeInfo.crossSystemSharedCount` — the old
precomputed field — was removed entirely; `master.MatchPlanLlmPass` gained a new public interface,
`CrossSystemUsageLookup` (`sharedCount(entityName, fieldName) -> Integer`), the ONE EBX-touching seam this
otherwise-pure file needs (the same dependency-injection reasoning `AgentRuntime`/local-tool handlers already
use). `Session` takes it as an optional 5th constructor argument (a `NO_OP` default answers null for every
call, so every test that does not care about this behaviour keeps using the old 4-arg constructor
unchanged). `Session.proposeMatchPlan` calls `this.crossSystemUsageLookup.sharedCount(entityName, fieldName)`
lazily, inside the `MATCH`-tier branch, AFTER the near-unique/`neverRepeats` checks already passed — so it is
called ONLY for a field the model actually proposed in an accepted `MATCH` tier, never for every candidate
attribute in the prompt's context, never for a fuzzy `SUSPECTED`-tier field, never for a field refused before
reaching that point. `ebx.MatchPlanLlmSuggester.suggest` builds the one real implementation once per run — an
anonymous `CrossSystemUsageLookup` closing over the caller's `Session` and the already-opened master
`Adaptation`, calling `crossSystemSharedCount(pSession, masterDataset, pEntityName, pFieldName)` — and passes
it into the `MatchPlanLlmPass.Session` constructor. Zero shared values still does NOT refuse a tier (a
same-system duplicate is still a legitimate match); the count (or "not measured") is folded into the accepted
tier's own rationale exactly as before — "the two counts... in the stored rationale/evidence of an accepted
tier" — `"<field>: <distinct-among-filled count> distinct value(s) among filled rows, <N> shared across at
least two source systems"` (or `"cross-system sharing not measured"` when null). Since the number is no
longer available before the model proposes anything, `userPrompt` no longer renders it per attribute — the
model is told, in `systemPrompt`, that this check happens automatically after an EXACT/MATCH proposal and is
recorded as evidence, and is pointed at `role`/distinct-among-filled to judge a candidate identifier instead.

**Requirement 3 checked, no change needed**: `neverRepeats` (`MatchPlanLlmPass.java:354-362`) already refuses
only when `cardinalityReliable()` (`"EXACT".equals(cardinalityProvenance)`) AND `filledCount` is non-null
(which itself requires `fillRateReliable()`, `"EXACT".equals(fillRateProvenance)`) — both provenances must be
`EXACT` before it ever returns `true`/`false` rather than `null` ("not measured" is never read as "safe").

**Prompt changes.** `systemPrompt` now explains the three roles (neutral wording — no company-specific
example), states that a `MATCH`-tier proposal is checked for cross-system sharing automatically AFTER the
call (never shown in advance, never refusing on zero), and points the model at `role`/distinct-among-filled
to judge a candidate identifier up front; `userPrompt` renders `role` and `<N>% distinct AMONG ITS FILLED
VALUES` per attribute (the cross-system count is deliberately NOT rendered there any more — see above);
`candidateHint` (the informational `[near-unique: candidate identifier]`/`[well-distributed: candidate
blocking/clustering field]` tag, unchanged from the prior revision) uses `distinctAmongFilled` for the
identifier hint (suppressed when `neverRepeats` is true) while keeping `distinctRatio` for the clustering
hint, and tags a `SOURCE_KEY` field explicitly rather than computing either hint for it.

**Tests**: `MatchPlanLlmPassTest` now has 10 new pure tests over the prior revision's 8 — `deriveRole` (all
mappings on key columns → `SOURCE_KEY`; one mapping on a non-key column → `BUSINESS`, even with others on key
columns; no mappings at all → `BUSINESS`, never `SOURCE_KEY`; `referenceEntity` wins over source-key columns
→ `REFERENCE`), a `SOURCE_KEY` field refused in a `MATCH` tier, in a fuzzy `SUSPECTED` tier, and (defensively)
as a clustering field, while an ordinary field is unaffected; a 100%-filled/100%-distinct `BUSINESS` field
refused by `neverRepeats` with its own distinct message; the exact `vatNo` shape (44% filled, 98% distinct
among filled) now ACCEPTED where the old total-row ratio would have refused it; the stored rationale carrying
both counts on an accepted tier, proven against a fake `CrossSystemUsageLookup` (including its null-answer
"not measured" path); and — new this revision — a dedicated test proving the lookup is called exactly once,
for the right (entity, field), only for an accepted `MATCH`-tier field, and never for a fuzzy tier or a field
refused before reaching the evidence step. `tools/test_local.sh` green (existing `MatchPlanRulesTest`/
`MatchPlanProfileReaderTest`/rest of the suite unaffected — this fix touches only `master.MatchPlanLlmPass`
and `ebx.MatchPlanLlmSuggester`).

**What is NOT verified**: the exact `GROUP BY ... HAVING` SQL statement has never been run live BY THIS
CODEBASE this session (no MCP call, no live EBX call, no real language model call — the coordinator's brief
for this branch forbids all three) — the coordinator's own hand-run probe (quoted above, read-only SQL tool)
is the only live confirmation this shape works, on `Company.name`, not on `vatNo`/`supplierId` specifically,
and not through this method's own code path (session/table-open plumbing). `mappingsAreOnSourceKeyColumns`'s
own EBX read (walking `AttributeMapping` → `LandingColumn.sourceKey`) is equally unverified live — the pure
`deriveRole` logic it feeds is tested, the EBX-side plumbing around it is not. The role/distinctAmongFilled/
never-repeats thresholds are read from the SAME data the near-unique guard already used (no new statistic
category beyond what §4.2.1 already established as `EXACT`/`SAMPLED`/`NOT_SUPPORTED`/`FAILED`), so no new
provenance-handling risk beyond what that section already documents as unverified.

### 4.2.2a A `DONE` run that recorded nothing at all — the model answered in prose (branch `fix/agent-prose-answer`, 2026-09-21)

A real run over the project's promoted entities ended `DONE`, but wrote no `MatchPlan` row, no `skip_entity`,
no `note`. The `AgentStep` trace showed the model's own final text correctly described what it would propose
for each entity — it simply never called `propose_match_plan`/`skip_entity`, only wrote prose. `AgentLoop` has
no way to distinguish "described a plan in English" from "proposed nothing": both end `stop_reason: end_turn`,
`Status.DONE`.

**Fix: `ebx.ProseAnswerRecovery`, ONE shared helper used by all three LLM passes** (`capability`/`quality`/
`master` — see `docs/QUALITY-LLM.md` §1.4 and `docs/CAPABILITY-SUGGESTIONS.md` for the identical mechanism
applied there; the three passes share this one class rather than three copies of the same logic). When the
run ends `DONE` and `MatchPlanLlmPass.Session` recorded nothing at all —
`createdPlans().isEmpty() && notes().isEmpty()` (`skip_entity` also writes to `notes`, so a deliberate skip is
never mistaken for "nothing" — `MatchPlanLlmPass.Session#skipEntity`) — `ebx.MatchPlanLlmSuggester.suggest`
runs ONE follow-up `AgentRuntime.run` call on the SAME `Session`/tools/system prompt, with a new task quoting
the model's own previous text (bounded) and stating plainly that nothing was recorded, only a tool call is
saved. The `Session` is a plain mutable Java object kept across both calls — whatever it already resolved
(guide texts, allowed vocabulary, prior refusal counters) survives; only the CONVERSATION resets, since
`AgentLoop.run(String, String)` always starts a brand-new one (see `docs/QUALITY-LLM.md` §1.4 for the exact
file:line and why a continued conversation is not an option the shared `on-ebx-agent` library offers). If the
follow-up still records nothing, the route's own top-level `status` becomes `NO_OUTPUT` (never `DONE`), `ok`
is `false`, the `PipelineStep` is not marked done, and `modelText` carries the model's own last words (bounded)
for a person to read. `proseAnswerRecovered` (`true`/`false`) says whether a follow-up was needed and worked;
`agentRun.steps`/token counts become the SUM of the first run and the follow-up, when one happened.

**System prompt**: `MatchPlanLlmPass.systemPrompt()`'s own closing line used to invite exactly this failure
("... answer with a short final summary") — replaced with an explicit "a plain text answer records NOTHING"
sentence, and the run is now told to close with ONE final `note` call instead of a separate prose wrap-up.

**Tests**: the shared mechanism/orchestration is covered once, at the helper level —
`ebx.ProseAnswerRecoveryTest` (fake outcomes/runner, no live EBX) and
`capability.CapabilityLlmPassTest#agentLoopRecoversFromProseOnlyAnswer` (a real `AgentLoop` against a fake HTTP
provider, proving the Session-carries-over/fresh-conversation mechanism itself); `MatchPlanLlmPassTest` only
adds the system-prompt wording assertions, not a second copy of the mechanism test — same division of labor
`docs/QUALITY-LLM.md` §1.4 documents for its own pass. **Not verified**: whether a real deployed model, given
the new system-prompt sentence, ever needs the follow-up again in practice — this fix was built and tested
against the FAKE provider only, per this branch's own constraints (no live EBX, no real LLM call).

### 4.2.3 `CrossSystemFieldGuard` — a plan proposing what it can never actually match (branch
`feature/match-plan-cross-system-guard`, 2026-09-21)

**The real incident this closes.** The same night the fixes of §4.2.2/§4.2.2a landed, two more real
`matching/suggest-llm` runs against `Companies`' own master data (`Company`, 107 rows: 55 `ERP` + 52 `CRM`)
were accepted by every guard that existed at the time, although neither plan could ever bring one `ERP`
record and one `CRM` record together:

- **Plan A** clustered on `legalForm`. `CRM` wrote `Customer`/`Prospect`/`Partner`, `ERP` wrote
  `SA`/`AG`/`PLC`… — **zero value shared between the two systems**, ever; pre-clustering on it partitions
  the two source systems apart instead of bridging them. After a later reload, `CRM.legalForm` became
  entirely null (0 of 52 filled), a second, equally fatal shape of the same underlying problem.
- **Plan B** clustered on `country`/`city`, both compared with `ebx-addon-mame@exact`, while `CRM` wrote
  `Fr`/`France`/`Suisse` + `Paris`/`Zürich` and `ERP` wrote `FR`/`CH` + `PARIS`/`ZURICH` — zero shared value
  again (fixed upstream since, for `country`, by a normalisation step; `city` still differs by case and
  accents).

Every existing guard (fill rate, distinctness, pre-clustering capability, `SOURCE_KEY`/`neverRepeats`) was
satisfied by both plans — none of them ever asked whether a field's values are actually **written the same
way** across the systems being matched, which is the one property that decides whether an exact comparison
or a clustering bucket can ever bridge two systems at all.

**The guard, purely structural (`master.CrossSystemFieldGuard`, `master/CrossSystemFieldGuard.java`) — no
field-name list, no "country-like" detection, per the product owner's standing rule that suggestions come
from the LLM and the Java side only checks structure against measured data.** Given two live-measured
numbers — how many distinct values of a field are shared by at least two source systems (the pre-existing
`crossSystemSharedCount`/`CrossSystemUsageLookup`, §4.2.2) and, new this lot, per source system how many
rows have the field filled at all (`PerSystemFillLookup`, `SELECT "sourceSystem", COUNT("field") ... GROUP
BY "sourceSystem"` — a `GROUP BY` with no `WHERE` returns one row per source system that holds at least one
row in the table at all, whether or not the field itself is filled there, so the returned map's key set
doubles as "which source systems are present") — `CrossSystemFieldGuard.evaluate` decides:

1. **Refuse** a `clusteringFields` entry, or any field compared with the EXACT algorithm in ANY tier (not
   only `MATCH`-terminal), when it has zero values shared across at least two systems, or is entirely null
   for at least one source system present in the table. A **fuzzy** algorithm on the same field is never
   checked — fuzzy is precisely what bridges `Paris`/`PARIS`. **When both conditions hold at once** (Plan A's
   own shape after the reload: `legalForm` is both entirely empty for `CRM` and, trivially, shares zero
   values with it) **the more actionable "entirely empty for source system …" wording always wins** over the
   generic "no value is shared" one — the empty-system check runs first and returns before the zero-shared
   check is even reached (coordinator review, second pass — `CrossSystemFieldGuardTest`'s own Plan A fixture
   now asserts this explicitly, not merely by construction).
2. **Record evidence, never refuse, when a `clusteringFields`/EXACT-algorithm field passes (1) and both
   numbers were actually measured** — **revised, coordinator review, second pass**: the first version of this
   guard only recorded a note when the cross-system share was LOW (below `LOW_SHARE_RATIO_FOR_NOTE = 0.25`,
   INFERRED); the coordinator asked for the measurement to reach the plan's own rationale **whenever the
   guard accepts the field**, not only the sparse case, so a reviewer always sees what was actually checked.
   `CrossSystemFieldGuard.Check#evidence` is now built unconditionally once both numbers are in hand — e.g.
   `"city: 3 value(s) shared across systems out of 47 distinct; ERP 55 filled, CRM 52 filled."` — with a
   trailing `" Low share - review."` emphasis (never a refusal reason) only when the share is actually below
   the threshold.
3. **Never refuse on a measurement failure.** A `null` from either lookup — the query was refused, a
   transport error, anything — is recorded as "not verified" in the plan's own rationale, the same
   discipline `preClusteringCapabilityNotVerified` (§4.2.1) already established; a shared-value count of
   exactly zero **without** the per-system fill measurement having independently confirmed at least two
   systems are present is treated the same way (on a genuinely single-system table, "shared by ≥ 2 systems"
   is trivially and meaninglessly zero, so it is never trusted alone).
4. **Never apply at all on a single-system table** — the per-system fill measurement itself is what proves
   this (fewer than two entries in its own result), not a separate query: matching is a cross-system
   concern, and with nothing to bridge the whole question is moot. Surfaced once per plan as a note, never a
   refusal.

**Wired identically into both proposal paths**, per the coordinator's own instruction ("a rule must not
propose what the guard would refuse"):

- **`MatchPlanLlmPass.Session.proposeMatchPlan`** — checked for every `clusteringFields` entry and every
  EXACT-algorithm field of every tier, MATCH or not (Plan B's own `country` field sat inside a SUSPECTED/
  AVERAGE tier, not a MATCH-terminal one — the earlier §4.2.2 near-unique guard never even looked at it).
  Live lookups are memoized per `(entity, field)` **within one `proposeMatchPlan` call** (two small
  `LinkedHashMap` caches, `sharedCountCache`/`perSystemFillCache`) — a field used both as a tier field and a
  clustering entry triggers each lookup at most once, matching the "measure on demand, only for the fields
  actually used" discipline the pre-existing `CrossSystemUsageLookup` already established (§4.2.2). A field
  already exempted from the clustering ceiling because it is a validated `MATCH`-tier identifier
  (`matchTierFields`) is not re-evaluated in the clustering loop either — it was already checked once, in
  the tier loop.
- **`master.MatchPlanRules.propose`** — the deterministic pass proposes each validated identifier as BOTH an
  exact tier and a clustering field (§4.2's own shape), so it is subject to exactly the same fact. A new
  2-lookup overload, `propose(List, MatchPlanLlmPass.CrossSystemUsageLookup, MatchPlanLlmPass.PerSystemFillLookup)`,
  activates the guard only when a caller actually wires at least one lookup; the pre-existing 1-arg
  `propose(List)` passes both as `null`, which is deliberately read as **"never wired"**, not as "every
  measurement failed" — this class' original, unguarded behaviour is preserved byte-for-byte for every
  existing caller/test. When wired and an identifier fails the guard, it is **excluded from that entity's
  proposal**, not a whole-entity refusal — a different, still-usable identifier on the same entity is still
  proposed; only when every candidate identifier fails is the entity skipped, naming each excluded
  identifier and why (mirrors the pre-existing "no validated identifier" skip).

**Coordinator review, second pass, same day — the route that matters was only half wired.** The first pass
above wired `MatchPlanRules`/`MatchPlanSuggester` (the deterministic route) with a real `PerSystemFillLookup`,
but `ebx.MatchPlanLlmSuggester.suggest` — the route `matching/suggest-llm` actually uses, the one the demo
runs — still built its `MatchPlanLlmPass.Session` with only the pre-existing `CrossSystemUsageLookup`, no
`PerSystemFillLookup` at all, defaulting to the NO-OP one. On that route every guarded field therefore always
read `filledCountBySystem == null`, so the "entirely empty for source system …" refusal (requirement 1's
more specific half) could never actually fire, and every guarded field fell through to "could not be fully
measured" instead. The cause was the coordinator's own concurrency warning from the first pass — touching
`MatchPlanLlmSuggester.java` was believed off-limits because of an unrelated change in flight on that file
the same night; that branch merged the same day and the constraint was lifted. Fixed:

- `ebx.MatchPlanLlmSuggester.suggest` now also builds a real `MatchPlanLlmPass.PerSystemFillLookup` (masking to
  `null` under the exact same `masterDataset == null` condition the existing `crossSystemLookup` already
  used) and passes it into the new 6-arg `MatchPlanLlmPass.Session` constructor, next to `crossSystemLookup` —
  `ebx-mdm-factory/src/main/java/com/on/ebx/factory/ebx/MatchPlanLlmSuggester.java:374-390` (the exact call
  site where both lookups are built and handed to `Session`, immediately before `ToolSet.build`).
- **The SQL itself moved into one shared, package-private helper — `ebx.CrossSystemMeasures`
  (`ebx-mdm-factory/src/main/java/com/on/ebx/factory/ebx/CrossSystemMeasures.java`)** — rather than a THIRD
  private copy: `sharedCount`/`perSystemFilledCounts`/`isQuotable`/`quoteIdentifier` now live there, and both
  `ebx.MatchPlanLlmSuggester` and `ebx.MatchPlanSuggester` call it instead of keeping their own copies. The
  duplicate `MatchPlanSuggester` grew in the first pass (on the belief that touching `MatchPlanLlmSuggester.java`
  was off-limits) is deleted; `MatchPlanLlmSuggester`'s own **original** `crossSystemSharedCount` — the one the
  coordinator verified live — moved into the helper **unchanged, not rewritten**: same derived-table/
  `GROUP BY`/`HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT …) > 1` shape, same `isQuotable`/`quoteIdentifier` pair, byte-for-byte.
  `MatchPlanLlmSuggester.java` itself lost ~90 lines (the method plus its two helpers plus the now-unused
  `Query`/`QueryResult`/`Tuple` imports) and gained the two-lookup call site above.
- **Identifier quoting, confirmed**: `CrossSystemMeasures.isQuotable` — the same check both routes' entity/
  field names go through before either is concatenated into SQL text — accepts only `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`.
  An embedded double quote (which could otherwise close the generated statement's own quoting early and
  inject arbitrary SQL) does not match this pattern at all, so it is **refused outright, never escaped** — the
  measurement degrades to "not measured" rather than building an unsafe or broken statement. This matters
  specifically because `matching/suggest-llm` accepts an entity/field name **the model itself proposes**
  (checked against the entity's real attributes by `Session` before ever reaching a lookup, but that is Java
  string equality, not a SQL-injection guard) — a would-be `Company" a WHERE 1=1 --` field name is refused by
  `isQuotable`, never assumed safe just because an earlier layer looked at it. Proven directly by the new
  `ebx.CrossSystemMeasuresTest` (ordinary names accepted; an embedded double quote, a single quote, a space, a
  semicolon, a dot, a backslash, a leading digit, null, and blank all refused; `quoteIdentifier`'s own
  wrapping checked) — pure string-logic tests, no live EBX needed, the same way the rest of this guard is
  tested.

**Never a real field VALUE anywhere in a refusal/note message** — only the field's own name, the source
systems' names (already structural identifiers the model already reasons about, not confidential data), and
counts. `CrossSystemFieldGuard.evaluate`'s own signature has exactly one `String` parameter beyond the field
name it is never branched on — the field name itself — proven by a reflection test
(`CrossSystemFieldGuardTest#evaluateHasNoValueCarryingParameter`), the same structural-proof convention
`MatchPlanLlmPassTest#noUngatedValueChannelExists` already established for `AttributeInfo`.

**Tests**: `master.CrossSystemFieldGuardTest` (pure — Plan A's own shape refused naming the empty system and
the measured fill counts, and an added assertion, second pass, that the "entirely empty" wording wins over
the generic "no value is shared" one when both conditions hold at once; Plan B's own shape refused on zero
shared values; the brief's own `city` example numbers producing exactly `"city: 3 value(s) shared across
systems out of 47 distinct"` **plus, second pass, the per-system fill breakdown in the same evidence string**
and a "Low share" emphasis; a high-share field, second pass, still producing evidence — just without the
emphasis — since evidence is now unconditional on acceptance; a single-system table never guarded and never
producing evidence at all; both measurements missing / an unconfirmed zero-shared count / only the shared
count missing all reading as "not verified" and never refusing); `ebx.CrossSystemMeasuresTest` (new, second
pass — pure identifier-quoting proof: ordinary names accepted, an embedded double quote/single quote/space/
semicolon/dot/backslash/leading digit/null/blank all refused, `quoteIdentifier`'s own wrapping); `MatchPlanLlmPassTest`
(Plan B's `country` refused inside a non-MATCH tier, the same field with a fuzzy algorithm instead never
checked, Plan A's `legalForm` refused as a clustering field, `city`'s evidence — numbers and fill breakdown —
landing in the stored rationale, a single-system table noted and not refused, a measurement failure noted
"Not verified" and not refused, and a field used both as a tier field and a clustering entry triggering each
live lookup exactly once); `MatchPlanRulesTest` (the 1-arg `propose(List)` overload's own behaviour completely
unaffected, a single failing identifier falling back to "no usable identifier", two identifiers where only one
fails still proposing the other, excluding the failed one from both the tiers and the rationale, **second
pass**: the surviving identifier's own cross-system evidence — numbers and fill breakdown — now also present
in the rationale, item 5's "both routes" requirement). `tools/test_local.sh` green (this repo's full suite,
existing and new).

**What is NOT verified**: never exercised against the live instance this session (no MCP call, no live EBX
call, no real language model call — forbidden this session either way) — the exact `SELECT "sourceSystem",
COUNT("field") ... GROUP BY "sourceSystem"` statement shape was run live by the coordinator against the real
demo master table before this lot started (that is where the "one more measurement" instruction comes from),
but never through `ebx.CrossSystemMeasures#perSystemFilledCounts`'s own code path (session/table-open
plumbing) on either route specifically — `sharedCount`'s own statement was independently verified live by the
coordinator before this lot even started (§4.2.2), and moving it into the shared helper changes nothing about
what is sent to the database, but that fact alone does not make the NEW method's own code path live-verified.
The `LOW_SHARE_RATIO_FOR_NOTE` (0.25) threshold is this lot's own inferred choice, like the identifier/
clustering thresholds §4.2.1 already documents as unverified — a real run against `Companies`' own master
data should confirm it neither over-notes a genuinely fine field nor under-notes a barely-adequate one.
**Merge-ready, never run live.**

#### 4.2.3a The empty-field refusal is judged per PATH, not per field (branch `feat/cross-system-guard-per-path`, 2026-10-12)

**The measured case (Vol100kN, 2026-10-12).** Four source systems: CRM, ERP and LOYALTY fill `birthDate` in
85-95 % of their rows, ECOM never (0 %). A reviewer asked, through "Propose another" with a comment, for a path
`nameMatchKey exact AND birthDate exact -> SUSPECTED` aimed at the 4,700 true pairs that share neither an e-mail
nor an address. The model answered that no `birthDate` path could be added because the validator refuses its exact
algorithm on the 0 % ECOM fill, "it cannot bridge that system". The guard of §4.2.3 (1) did refuse the FIELD, whatever
the rest of the tree looked like - although the plan's other paths (e-mail exact, address keys, phone) already
cover the pairs involving ECOM, and the refused path would only have been silent for those pairs. Recall against
the ground truth stayed at 89 % on the LOYALTY pairs; the refused path would have reached part of the misses.

**The rule now (`master.CrossSystemPathRule`, pure, no field name).** "Entirely empty for source system S" is no
longer a refusal made while the nodes are built (the tree does not exist yet): `CrossSystemFieldGuard.Check`
now says WHICH systems are empty (`emptySystems`, `refusedOnEmptySystem()`), `Session.buildAndAppendNode` keeps the
field aside (`deferredEmptySystemFields`) and the verdict is given on the assembled, validated tree:

- a **positive path** is a path from the root to `MATCH` or `SUSPECTED`; it is **blocked for S** when a node it PASSES
  (leaves through `onTrue`) cannot be passed by a pair that has the fields empty in S null on one side. A node left
  through `onFalse` never blocks (a pair with a null cannot pass it; that is the route it takes).
  `ALL_FIELDS`: blocked when such a field has `oneNull` NOT_MATCH (absent = NOT_MATCH) or when the node compares nothing
  else. `AT_LEAST_N`: blocked when fewer than `minimumMatches` fields can still match (NOT_MATCH cannot, DO_NOTHING counts,
  as the counting function reads it). `AVERAGE`: blocked when the best reachable average - the field scoring 0 under
  NOT_MATCH, or leaving the average under DO_NOTHING ("not required") - is below `minimumScore`, i.e. when its weight is
  needed to reach it. `PREDICATE` or unknown: blocked (cannot be judged, the old refusal stands). Relation fields
  (`via`) are not judged.
- the field is **refused only when, for one of its empty systems, every positive path is blocked** (all the empty
  fields of that system are counted together: two fields empty in ECOM cannot each lean on a path the other blocks), or
  when the tree has no positive path, or more than 512 of them (not analysed: the old refusal stands). The refusal keeps
  its original text and adds: `Path by path: for pairs involving ECOM, every path of the proposed tree to MATCH or
  SUSPECTED needs 'birthDate' (N1 (nameMatchKey + birthDate -> SUSPECTED)), so no such pair could ever be found. A field
  empty in one system is accepted when at least one other path that does not need it still reaches MATCH or SUSPECTED:
  add such a path, or drop this field.`
- otherwise the field is **accepted with the null handling the model gave**, and the answer of `propose_match_plan`
  (the text the model reads), the stored rationale ("Cross-system warning: ...") and the field's evidence row say, per
  empty system: `field 'birthDate' is empty in system ECOM: the path(s) N1 > N2 (nameMatchKey + birthDate -> SUSPECTED)
  will never fire for pairs involving ECOM; the other path(s) N1 (emailKey -> MATCH) still cover them.` (when no path
  needs the field at all: `... no path to MATCH or SUSPECTED needs it, so pairs involving ECOM are not held back by
  it; the path(s) ... cover them.`). The other half of the guard still runs on the systems that DO fill the field:
  `CrossSystemFieldGuard.evaluateFilledSystems` (zero shared values between them: refused as ever; measured evidence
  otherwise).
- the system prompt (`MatchPlanLlmPass.systemPrompt()`, next to the single-source paragraph) says so in two sentences,
  so the model stops giving up such a path on its own.

**Left alone on purpose.** (a) `clusteringFields`: a clustering field entirely empty for a system is still refused outright
- the candidate search is not a path, and a record of that system is not found through that key at all; a field both in
the tree and in `clusteringFields` is therefore still refused through the clustering loop. (b) `MatchPlanRules` (the
deterministic pass proposes each identifier as a one-field tier AND a clustering field: no second path to lean on) keeps
reading `Check.refuse`. (c) The "no value is shared between any two systems" refusal and the single-system/unmeasured
behaviour are unchanged. (d) `bothNull` is not read: it concerns pairs inside S, which a "bridge the systems" guard never
asked about; only `oneNull` decides whether a cross-system pair can pass a node. (e) A field filled in only ONE system
(three empty) is accepted the same way when another path covers the empty ones; with fewer than two filled systems no
shared-value check remains to make, and the warning is the whole story.

Tests: `CrossSystemPathRuleTest` (pure trees: the Vol100kN tree and its exact warning, a single path refused, every
path needing the field, a field only on an `onFalse` edge, `AVERAGE` weight needed / not needed / DO_NOTHING,
`AT_LEAST_N`, two fields empty in the same system, no positive path, a relation field),
`CrossSystemFieldGuardTest` (`emptySystems`, `evaluateFilledSystems`), `MatchPlanLlmPassTest` (the session with four
systems and `birthDate` 0 % in ECOM: accepted with the warning, the single-path case refused, the `AVERAGE` cases, the
clustering field still refused, the prompt). **Not deployed, never run live, no language model called.** Live check: on
Vol100kN, entity Person, re-run "Propose another" with the same comment; the model must now be able to add the
`nameMatchKey + birthDate` path and the answer must carry the warning above.

### 4.3 `MatchingConfigurator.configure` (task 3) — see §3 in full

### 4.4 `MatchingConfigurator.run` — the scoped run, now via the Java API (revised, replaces the REST design)

**The original design (commit `1cdb8bd`) POSTed to `/ebx-addon-mame/rest/v1/matchingProcesses` with the
agent account's HTTP credentials — GONE.** Coordinator review, same day: the add-on's own public Java API
(§2.6) does the same job in-process, with the caller's own session, no HTTP call at all. The REST endpoint
is documented here only as the alternative that was tried first and abandoned, not as something the code
still does:

- **Scope**: `master.MatchingRunScope` (pure, unit-tested) decides the XPath predicate. Default
  (`incremental`): `./_loadId='<max _loadId on the master table>'` — see that class' own Javadoc for why
  there is no dedicated "master load run id" to key on instead (`ebx.MasterLoader` carries `_loadId`
  through unchanged from staging, by its own design — READ `master/MasterTransferPlan.java` via
  `MasterLoader`'s Javadoc, already established before this lot). `?scope=all`: `./id='k1' or ./id='k2' or
  ...` over every non-blank `Xref.masterKey` of this project for the entity (the master PK is always the
  plain auto-increment `id` — `master.MasterModel`'s own design). **Both modes refuse outright, naming why,
  when the computed scope would be empty** — never a fallback to no predicate at all, per §2.1's own
  quoted warning that an unscoped run discards every existing verdict of the whole table, across every
  policy.
- **Launch**: `MameMatchingApi.launchScoped` → `MatchingOperations.matchRecords(masterTable, request,
  entityName)` (`request.setXPathFilter(scope.xpathPredicate)`) — asynchronous, per §2.6. Polled, bounded,
  never blocked on `waitingForBackgroundProcessDone` (§2.6) — `?maxWaitMs=N` on the route, default 30s.
- **`Xref.goldenKey` is refreshed only when the process reports `DONE`** within that window — a
  still-`RUNNING` result is reported as such in the JSON response (`goldenKeyRefreshSkipped`, naming the
  status and recommending a later re-run), never silently skipped without saying so.
- **Runs with the CALLER's own session** (`MatchingOperations`/`ProcessOperations` obtained from the
  `SessionContext`-injected `Session`, same as `StagingLoader`/`MasterLoader`) — no agent-account
  credentials on this path at all, unlike `configure` (which still needs the agent's MCP access).

After a `DONE` process, `ebx.GoldenKeyRefresher.refresh` (the one class that reads `RecordMetadata`, per
the coordinator's brief "the EBX reads isolated in one class") re-reads every relevant `Xref` row and
applies `master.GoldenKeyRefreshDecision.decide` (pure, unit-tested): a record with a `RecordMetadata` row
and a null `goldenId` is currently its own golden (`goldenKey` becomes its own `masterKey` — so a lineage
read never has to special-case "not merged" vs. "merged"); one with a non-null `goldenId` gets that value;
one with no `RecordMetadata` row at all (matching hasn't touched it, or the metadataset doesn't exist) is
left/cleared blank, matching the XSD field's own comment ("Empty until the matching lot fills it").

**What is still unverified about this call, honestly**: the Java API's own exception/return-type contracts
are READ (javap)/READ (on-disk Javadoc) — real, not guessed — but no `matchRecords`/`simulateMatch` call
was ever actually EXECUTED this session (both are write/state-touching from the add-on's own perspective,
forbidden either way). The bounded-poll design (§2.6) is this document's own choice, not something the
Javadoc prescribes — the Javadoc's own sample blocks unboundedly via `waitingForBackgroundProcessDone`,
which this class deliberately does not do, for the reason given there. A first live run should be watched
end to end (does the poll actually see `RUNNING` → `DONE`, does `getDetail()` say anything useful, is
30 seconds enough for the reference demo's own 107/89-row tables).

### 4.4a The first real `matching/run`, 2026-09-22 09:04 — a bare 500 after a genuine success, fixed (`fix/validate-response-shape`)

`POST /projects/Companies/matching/run?scope=all` matched all 107 records to completion — the add-on's own
summary in `ebxLog/ebx-addon-mame.log`: 0 MATCHED, 38 SUSPECTED, 0.9s — and then the route answered a bare
HTTP 500:

```
java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "RunMatchPhase.name()" because the return value of
"MatchingOperationProcess.getCurrentPhase()" is null
	at MatchingOperationProcess.getDetail(MatchingOperationProcess.java:627)
	at ebx.MameMatchingApi.launchScoped(MameMatchingApi.java:144)
	at ebx.MatchingConfigurator.run(MatchingConfigurator.java:442)
```

`javap -p` on the deployed `com.orchestranetworks.addon.mame.common.process.MatchingOperationProcess`
(`ebx-addon-mame/WEB-INF/classes`, the concrete type behind the public `MatchingProcess` interface this
codebase holds) confirms `getDetail()` depends on `getCurrentPhase()`, which can legitimately answer null
once the process has finished — an internal type (`common.process`, not `service.*`), so this could only be
guarded at the CALL, never fixed by touching the add-on's own code. Consequences before the fix: the route
500'd although the run genuinely succeeded, and the factory's own `MATCHING_RUN` `PipelineStep` (id 78)
stayed `RUNNING` forever, because `MatchingConfigurator.run`'s per-entity `try` only caught `OperationException`
— a bare `RuntimeException` propagated straight out with nothing ending the step.

**Fix 1 — none of `getDetail`/`getCompletionRate`/`getDuration` may ever fail the whole call.**
`MameMatchingApi` now reads each of the three independently (`safeDetail`/`safeCompletionRate`/
`safeDurationMs`), catching `RuntimeException` around each one on its own: a failure yields `null`/`-1` for
that field plus a `RunResult.reportNotes` entry naming the method and the exception class/message, never
re-thrown. `getMatchingStatus()` itself is NOT wrapped this way — `RunResult.done()` keys on it alone, and it
answered correctly throughout the run that hit this bug (the poll loop already saw the terminal status before
the NPE ever fired) — wrapping it too would risk hiding a genuine "the process itself cannot be read" failure
behind a fabricated status.

**Fix 2 — `MatchingConfigurator.run`'s per-entity loop now also catches `RuntimeException`**, mirroring the
pattern `configureOne` already applies to its own translator exception (§3.3a, Fix 3): the step is ended
`FAILED` with the exception's class name and message, and the entity is added to `refused` — a `RUNNING` step
must never be left behind by an exception, in `run` any more than in `configure`.

**No public getter exists for the MATCHED/SUSPECTED/isolated/group counts the log line shows.** Same `javap`
pass: `MatchingOperationProcess` keeps `matchedNumber`/`suspectedNumber`/`isolatedRecordNumber`/
`processedGroup` as PRIVATE fields with no accessor (the only public numeric getter besides the
`MatchingProcess` interface's own is `getSelectedRecordNumber()`, unrelated to this breakdown); the
`MatchingProcess` interface itself (the only type this codebase may reference) declares only
`getMatchingStatus`/`getDetail`/`getExecutionDate`/`getCompletionRate`/`getDuration`/`cancel` — none of them
this breakdown either; `ProcessInfo getProcessInfo(Locale)` (also on the concrete, off-limits class) only
carries a UI progress percentage/remaining-time/error string. `RunResult` therefore does NOT carry a
matched/suspected/isolated/group breakdown — there is no supported way to read it from Java at all; a caller
that needs it has only the add-on's own log line, never scraped by this codebase (CLAUDE.md's own "an
internal API found by javap is build-specific" caution applies doubly to a log line, which is not even an
API).

**Verified by unit test** (`MameMatchingApiTest`, a fake `MatchingProcess` whose `getDetail()` throws the
exact live exception class): status stays `DONE`, `done()` stays true, `reportNotes` names `getDetail()` and
the exception, nothing is re-thrown. **Never re-run live from this branch** (write tools are forbidden here
either way) — the live run above is not repeated to confirm the fix; only the guarded-read behaviour itself
is unit-tested.

### 4.5 `MatchingConfigurator.simulate` (new, coordinator review of 1cdb8bd)

`POST /projects/{code}/matching/simulate?entity=..&masterKey=..` — `MameMatchingApi.simulate` →
`MatchingOperations.simulateMatch(Adaptation, policyCodeOrNull)` (§2.6): zero-risk by the add-on's own
contract (nothing persisted), requires only an `APPLIED` `MatchPlan` (the policy must exist and be
activated — `configure` must have succeeded), reports every `MatchingEngineResult` the simulation found:
`{targetRecordPrimaryKey, pivotRecordPrimaryKey, result}` (`result` = `MATCHED`/`SUSPECTED`/`NOT_MATCHED`
or null). A safe, concrete way for the product owner to see the policy actually work on one real record before
trusting `matching/run` — never exercised live this session (the add-on API is entirely off-limits, same
as every other write path), but the read is genuinely read-only by the product's own documented contract,
not merely by this class' own restraint.

## 5. Closing the `osd:addon` gap inside the factory (`ebx.MasterGenerator.ensureMameAddon`)

### 5.1 `list_operations` findings (READ (live), this revision)

`list_operations(category="modelsettings")` lists, among others: `add_addon` — *"Declare an add-on on the
model. INERT until the model is republished."* (behavior `ADDITIVE_RETRYABLE`) — and `list_addons` —
*"List the add-ons declared on the model, and the installable catalogue."* (behavior `READ_ONLY`).
`list_operations(name="add_addon")` quotes the full contract: *"Reference an add-on already installed and
activated at the repository level (DMA \"Configuration → Add-ons\") ... Verify with list_addons;
version/activated are computed, not written. Unknown/inactive name → soft-miss (code ADDON_NOT_AVAILABLE)
carrying availableAddons; throws on blank name or duplicate. Cross-endpoint: a declaration only reaches
the compiled schema at the next publication."* `list_operations(name="list_addons")`: *"Each entry
enumerates id, name, version, activated, label."*

The on-disk admin guide (`ebx-addon-mame/www/common/html/onHelp/simple/admin_guide/updating_data_model.html`,
READ (on-disk Javadoc), titled **"Task 1: Updating the model"**) confirms this is the exact UI equivalent:
*"Before creating a match configuration, you must update and publish the EBX® data model using the Data
Model Assistant (DMA) ... From the main menu bar, select the Data models panel and select the data model
to update. Expand Configuration and select Add-ons. Select '+' to add a new entry and choose Match and
Merge. After saving, publish the data model."* — followed by **"Task 2: Registering tables"**
(`activating_tables.html`, a `TableConfiguration` — `MatchingConfigurator.configureOne`'s own job, §3/§4,
unrelated to this section).

**Confirmed live, this revision**: `get_data_model(data_model_name="Companies_Master", deep=true)` and
`get_publication(publication_name="Companies_Master")` on the real, already-published model both carry NO
add-on information anywhere — the full ~58KB deep-tree response was grepped case-insensitively for
"addon", zero hits. **A regeneration diff built from `get_data_model` alone (`staging.StagingModelDiff`,
what `MasterGenerator.runRegeneration` already uses for table/field changes) can never see this gap** —
`list_addons` is the only way to know, and `ensureMameAddon` calls it explicitly rather than folding it
into that diff.

### 5.1.1 `list_addons`'s real response shape — READ LIVE by coordinator, 2026-09-21

The coordinator ran the actual read-only `execute_query(operation="list_addons")` against `Companies_Master`,
superseding this document's earlier depth-bounded-search guess at the envelope. Verbatim:

```json
{"dataModelName":"Companies_Master","operation":"list_addons","found":true,"addons":[],
 "availableAddons":[{"label":"Digital Asset Manager","name":"ebx-addon-dama"},
                     {"label":"Match and Merge","name":"ebx-addon-mame"}],
 "code":null,"message":null,"nextStep":null}
```

So: **`addons`** = what is DECLARED on this model (empty on `Companies_Master` today — the gap §2.2
found). **`availableAddons`** = what is installed and activated at the REPOSITORY level. The add-on's real
name is confirmed **`ebx-addon-mame`** — not a guess.

### 5.2 `master.MameAddonDecision` (pure, tested against this exact JSON) and `ensureMameAddon`

Every actual decision now lives in `master.MameAddonDecision.decide` (pure, no EBX class, unit-tested with
the verbatim response above plus a declared variant) — `ebx.MasterGenerator.ensureMameAddon` only makes
the two MCP calls and acts on the decision:

1. `execute_query(operation="list_addons")` on the `data-model` MCP server (same call shape
   `ensureEmbedded` already uses for `get_global_properties`).
2. `MameAddonDecision.decide(response)` — an entry of `addons` whose `name` equals `ebx-addon-mame` →
   `ALREADY_DECLARED` (or `NOT_AVAILABLE`, named, if that entry explicitly carries `activated: false` —
   **only when the field is present**: `list_addons`'s own contract says an entry carries "id, name,
   version, activated, label", but the live `availableAddons` entries above carry only `label`/`name`, so
   a missing `activated` field reads as "unknown", not "false"). Not declared, but present in
   `availableAddons` → `DECLARE("ebx-addon-mame")`. Neither → `NOT_AVAILABLE`, naming Administration >
   Add-ons. An unparseable response (`found` missing/false, or no `addons` array at all) → `UNREADABLE`.
3. **`ALREADY_DECLARED` never calls `add_addon`** — its own contract: "throws on blank name or duplicate."
   Only `DECLARE` calls `execute_operation(operation="add_addon", arguments_json={"name":
   "ebx-addon-mame"})`, one shot, no fuzzy retry — the name is confirmed, so nothing to self-correct.
   `NOT_AVAILABLE`/`UNREADABLE` refuse immediately, cleanly, naming what to do.

`add_addon`'s full contract (`list_operations(name="add_addon")`, verbatim): args = `name` (required, "the
add-on name, from list_addons"); behavior `ADDITIVE_RETRYABLE`; *"Declare an add-on on the model. INERT
until the model is republished."*; *"version/activated are computed, not written."*; *"Unknown/inactive
name -> soft-miss (code ADDON_NOT_AVAILABLE) carrying availableAddons; throws on blank name or
duplicate."* — the "INERT until republished" half is exactly why `ensureMameAddon`'s callers must still
publish afterward unconditionally, see §5.3.

**What remains genuinely unverified**: `list_addons`/`add_addon` were called live only by the coordinator's
own separate, supervised probe — not by `ensureMameAddon` itself, which has still never run end to end.
The JSON shape above is real, not guessed, but the full `master/generate` call sequence through
`execute_query`/`execute_operation` (session, error paths, `arguments_json` encoding) remains to be watched
on the first real run — read `MASTER_MODEL`'s own `PipelineStep.detail` (`listAddons`/`addAddon`/
`addonDecision` keys) to see exactly what was sent and what came back.

### 5.3 Regeneration: the real `Companies_Master` case, concretely

`MasterGenerator.runRegeneration`'s own `diff.isUpToDate()` fast path used to mean "the promoted entities
already match the published tables exactly, nothing to change, don't even publish." **That is exactly the
state the real `Companies_Master` is in today** (generated before this fix existed, `Company`/`Contact`
tables already correct) — under the old logic, this project's `master/generate` would forever report
`UP_TO_DATE` and never declare the add-on. Fixed: `ensureMameAddon` is now called unconditionally inside
`runRegeneration`, before the `isUpToDate` check; when it returns `false` (just declared), the mode
becomes `REGENERATE` even with zero table/field operations, `applied[]` gains a line naming it, and
`publish_data_model` is called unconditionally in that branch (previously gated behind
`operations.size() > 0`, which a pure add-on declaration would never satisfy on its own).
