## 13. Review — the simulation panel reworked (review-match-plan-simulation lot, 2026-09-22)

The Matching review line's block 3 ("what the plan would give on your data", §11) is rewritten entirely.
The old version picked up to 10 master keys SHARED by at least two source systems and called
`MatchingConfigurator.simulate` once per pair (§4.5) — the product owner rejected it: every pair shared the
plan's own clustering key by construction, so every verdict was Suspect, and the per-field cells compared
raw text side by side (never a folded value, never a score). The validated mockup is
`docs/mockups/review-match-plan-simulation.html` — read it before touching any of the classes below.

### 13.1 What `javap` found on the add-on's public Java API this session

Beyond `MatchingOperations.simulateMatch`/`MatchingEngineResult` (§2.6, §4.5 — verdict + the two primary
keys, no score, no node), the SAME interface (`ebx-addons.jar`,
`com.orchestranetworks.addon.mame.service.matching.MatchingOperations`) also declares:

```
DecisionTreeExecutionResult executeDecisionTree(Adaptation pivot, Adaptation candidate, String policyCodeOrNull);
EvaluateMatchingResult evaluateMatching(Adaptation pivot, Adaptation candidate, String policyCodeOrNull);
```

`com.orchestranetworks.addon.mame.service.decisiontree.DecisionTreeExecutionResult`:

```
MatchingResultType getMatchingResult();
Iterable<DecisionNode> getDecisionNodes();
Map<Integer, List<ScoreField>> getNodeScores();
```

and its nested `ScoreField`:

```
double getScore();
String getField();
String getFieldType();
Object getPivotRecordRawValue();
Object getSuspectRecordRawValue();
```

`com.orchestranetworks.addon.mame.model.decisiontree.DecisionNode`: `getName()`, `getComparisonFunction()`,
`getComparisonFunctionParameters()`, `getDecisionFields()`, `getMatchingResult()`, `isLastNode()` —
`getName()` is the SAME string `master.MatchingPolicyTranslator#tierLabel` writes when the policy is
generated ("Same X", "Similar X and Y"), so a node here can in principle be matched back to a specific
tier by name (not attempted — this lot correlates by POSITION instead, see below).

This is genuinely new information for this codebase: the earlier per-field-score search (§2.6's own
`MatchingEngineResult`, no score at all) concluded the add-on exposed no field-level detail. It does — just
not through `simulateMatch`. `ebx.MameMatchingApi#evaluatePair` wraps `executeDecisionTree` and returns a
plain (`TreeEvaluation`/`FieldScore`) value object — never leaking an add-on type past that one class, the
same discipline §4.4's own class Javadoc already documents for `launchScoped`/`simulate`.

**Two things read from method signatures only, never confirmed live:**

- `getNodeScores()`'s `Integer` key is ASSUMED to be the zero-based position of the corresponding node in
  `getDecisionNodes()`'s own iteration order — neither `DecisionNode` nor `ScoreField` carries a shared id
  field, so this is the only correlation the two methods could plausibly share, not something `javap` can
  itself confirm.
- `ScoreField.getScore()`'s numeric scale (0-100, matching a tier's own `minimumScore`, or already 0-1) is
  UNKNOWN. `ebx.MameMatchingApi`/`review.MatchSimulationBlock` never convert it by any assumed factor — a
  score is only ever compared against a `minimumScore` in whatever units both happen to share. If the real
  scale turns out to be 0-1, every "borderline" flag in this lot is almost certainly wrong (a margin of 3
  units on a 0-1 score is enormous) — the FIRST live run of this button should log a few raw `getScore()`
  values before trusting the borderline family at all.

### 13.2 What is real vs. what is this class' own derivation

`review.MatchSimulationBlock`'s own class Javadoc is the authoritative, maintained version of this; summary:

- The verdict of every pair, and every raw field value read off the pivot/candidate records
  (`MatchingEngineResult.getPivotRecordAdaptation()`/`getTargetRecordAdaptation()` — plain `Adaptation`s,
  read directly, no second table lookup) — **real**.
- An EXACT-role field's `=`/`≠` cell — a plain comparison of those same real values — **real**.
- A fuzzy/AVERAGE-role field's own similarity score, when present — the add-on's own `ScoreField.getScore()`
  via `evaluatePair` — **real**, never a factory-side estimate; absent (not a fabricated zero) whenever
  that extra call was not attempted (bounded cap) or failed for that specific pair.
- An AVERAGE tier's own COMBINED score (weighted mean of the real per-field scores above, using the plan's
  own declared weights) and everything built on it — the "borderline" flag, an AVERAGE tier's own
  "accepted"/"refused" contribution to the "leaf reached" column — **this lot's own re-derivation**,
  mirroring `MatchingPolicyTranslator`'s "Average" node (weighted mean vs. `minimumScore`) but never
  confirmed against the add-on's own real combination/null-handling arithmetic (§13.1).

### 13.3 Sampling: random pivots, not shared keys

`ebx.MatchPlanSimulationRunner.simulate` now draws up to `MAX_PIVOTS` (20) master rows at random —
`PIVOTS_PER_SYSTEM_QUOTA` (10) per source system present on the table (`CrossSystemMeasures.rowCountsBySystem`,
a plain per-system `COUNT(*)`, built by direct analogy to `perSystemFilledCounts`, §2.5.2 — never run live
this session). With more than two systems the quota is spread evenly so the total still respects the cap —
the task brief's own "10 per system" example only covers exactly two. The draw is Algorithm R reservoir
sampling over each system's own rows, bounded at `MAX_SCAN_PER_SYSTEM` (2000) rows scanned — unbiased over
every row it actually sees, but not a true whole-table uniform sample on a project whose master table
exceeds that bound (CLAUDE.md: "EBX tient le volume" — never assume this demo-scale table is representative
of every deployment). A fresh draw happens on every click (the task brief explicitly allows this).

For each drawn pivot, `MameMatchingApi.simulate` (the SAME call §4.5 already used) returns every candidate
in that pivot's own pre-clustering group and its real verdict — nothing here hand-picks a target any more.
Self-pairs are dropped; a pair seen from both directions (its target was itself separately drawn as a
pivot) is counted once. For up to `MAX_DETAIL_PAIRS` (60) of the unique pairs collected this way,
`MameMatchingApi.evaluatePair` additionally fetches the real per-field scores (§13.1) — every OTHER pair
still contributes its verdict and its exact-field comparison to the summary, just with an empty
`fieldScores` map ("not verified for this pair", never a fabricated score).

### 13.4 The three families, and what was left out

`review.MatchSimulationBlock.analyze` sorts every examined pair deterministically (pivot label, then
target label — the DRAW is random, the DISPLAY never is) and classifies it:

1. **Caught without an exact key** — verdict `SUSPECTED` and the plan's own EXACT-role fields (read from
   the requirements' own `algorithm` — `...@exact`, never re-derived) explicitly disagree.
2. **Same key, but refused** — verdict `NOT_MATCHED` and every EXACT-role field explicitly agrees.
3. **Borderline** — the AVERAGE tier's own re-derived weighted score (§13.2) within `BORDERLINE_MARGIN_UNITS`
   (3, in the tier's own `minimumScore` units — see §13.1's own open question) of that tier's threshold,
   whatever the verdict.

Each family caps its DISPLAYED rows at 3 (`MAX_FAMILY_ROWS`) but counts every matching pair in the numeric
summary card regardless of the cap. An empty family renders an explicit "no pair of this kind in this
sample" line — never a fabricated row.

**Not attempted, task brief's own explicit permission to skip it**: the "never compared" pair (a same-key
pair the add-on's own pre-clustering never even offered as a candidate, because the two records land in
different clustering groups). Identifying one cheaply would need scanning every other row sharing a
pivot's own exact-key value across systems and diffing that set against what `simulateMatch` actually
returned — not attempted this lot. Family 2 therefore only ever contains real "same key, refused" pairs.

### 13.5 What was NOT run live — read this before trusting a number above

No EBX access this session (task constraint), so nothing in §13.1-§13.4 was exercised against a real
instance:

- `executeDecisionTree`/`evaluatePair` itself — the getNodeScores()-index-correlates-with-getDecisionNodes()
  -order assumption and the score's numeric scale (§13.1) are both read from method signatures alone.
- `CrossSystemMeasures.rowCountsBySystem`'s own SQL text — built by direct analogy to `perSystemFilledCounts`
  (verified live, §2.5.2), never itself run.
- The reservoir sampling and the whole draw/classify/render pipeline — proven correct against hand-built
  fixtures only (`MatchSimulationBlockTest`, `MatchPlanViewTest`), never against a real master table or a
  real add-on response.
- Whether an `Adaptation` returned from `MatchingEngineResult.getPivotRecordAdaptation()`/
  `getTargetRecordAdaptation()` stays readable after the enclosing `SimulationResult` is closed
  (`MameMatchingApi.SimulationMatch`'s own Javadoc) — reasoned from `Adaptation` being a plain data-home
  handle, never observed.

### 13.6 Probed pairs — 2026-09-22, `fix/simulation-probed-pairs` — the random draw alone proved empty

the product owner's own live run on the expanded MATCH-1 line, 2026-09-22 ~17:50: "Simulate on 20 pivots" rendered 20
pivots drawn, 14 candidates examined, all 14 SUSPECTED — families 1 ("caught without an exact key"), 2
("same key, but refused") and 3 ("borderline") all empty, all three printing the bare "No pair of this kind
in this sample." His verdict: "Le sample est vide" — an empty panel proves nothing. Root cause, measured:
`MatchingOperations.simulateMatch` (§13.3's own random-pivot draw) only ever returns pairs the engine's own
pre-clustering already retains — on this demo data (ERP/CRM copies differing by case/accents) that is
essentially every candidate it offers, so families 1-3 (which specifically need a pair the engine's own
clustering would NOT retain trivially) had nothing to draw from.

**The fix does not touch the random-pivot draw at all** — it ADDS two bounded, live-SQL probe sets that
select pairs the engine's own clustering would never volunteer, then judges each with `MameMatchingApi
#evaluatePair` (`executeDecisionTree`) instead of `simulateMatch` — the ONLY add-on call able to score a
pair the engine never grouped together (task brief's own insight, confirmed against the add-on's public
API, §13.1):

- **Probe set A — shared key** (`MatchPlanSimulationRunner#probeSharedKeyPairs`): up to 20 pairs of two
  records of DIFFERENT source systems sharing the SAME value of the plan's own identifying key field — a
  `FOLD_KEY`-derived attribute (e.g. `nameKey`) when the entity has one (ACCEPTED-or-APPLIED status only,
  the same guard `MatchPlanLlmSuggester#readDerivedFromByName` already applies), else the plan's own first
  exact-tier field. Feeds family 2. The SQL is a straight restoration of the ORIGINAL "10 shared-key pairs"
  design removed by commit c08a5b1 when the random-pivot rework replaced it (`git log -p` on
  `MatchPlanSimulationRunner.java`) — the exact statement the coordinator verified live, 2026-09-21:
  ```sql
  SELECT a."nameKey" AS V FROM "Company" a WHERE a."nameKey" IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY a."nameKey" HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT a."sourceSystem") > 1
  ```
- **Probe set B — near miss** (`MatchPlanSimulationRunner#probeNearMissPairs`): up to 20 pairs of two
  records of DIFFERENT source systems sharing every one of the plan's own non-fuzzy EXACT-tier fields
  (`country`/`cityKey` on the live plan) while carrying a DIFFERENT value of the identifying key — the
  "only the fuzzy anchor field can decide" pairs. A NEW statement, `nearMissGroupsSql` — same derived-table/
  `GROUP BY`/`HAVING` shape as the one above, extended to every exact field together plus a SECOND
  `HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ...) > 1` clause on the key field (a group needs at least two different keys to
  hold a near-miss pair at all) — never a self-join, same reasoning `CrossSystemMeasures`'s own class
  Javadoc gives (linear in row count; CLAUDE.md: "EBX tient le volume"):
  ```sql
  SELECT a."country" AS G0, a."cityKey" AS G1 FROM "Company" a
  WHERE a."country" IS NOT NULL AND a."cityKey" IS NOT NULL AND a."nameKey" IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY a."country", a."cityKey"
  HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT a."sourceSystem") > 1 AND COUNT(DISTINCT a."nameKey") > 1
  ```

Both statements are pure functions of their arguments (`sharedKeyValuesSql`/`nearMissGroupsSql`,
package-private, unit-tested without EBX in `MatchPlanSimulationRunnerSqlTest` — the same discipline
`CrossSystemMeasuresTest` already applies) — callers check `CrossSystemMeasures.isQuotable` on every
identifier first, degrading to "nothing probed" rather than an unsafe statement. Each candidate group/key
value found is then read back with a small, bounded XPath lookup (`rowsForFieldValue`/`rowsForFieldValues`,
capped at 200 rows scanned) and a qualifying pair (different system, and — for probe B — different key) is
picked from it (`firstDifferentSystem`/`firstNearMissPair`).

**Every probed pair still needs a real verdict, and gets it from `evaluatePair`, never fabricated.** Unlike
an engine candidate (whose real verdict already comes from `simulateMatch`), a probe pair has NO verdict at
all until `evaluatePair`'s own `DecisionTreeExecutionResult.getMatchingResult()` answers one — so probe
pairs are evaluated FIRST, ahead of engine candidates' own (optional) per-field-score enrichment, within the
SAME shared 60-call-per-click cap (`MAX_DETAIL_PAIRS`, unchanged from the pre-probes lot). A probe pair
`evaluatePair` cannot judge (call fails, or answers no verdict) is dropped outright — never shown with an
invented verdict, and never counted anywhere.

**Origin and the real key, threaded through `MatchPlanView.SimulationPair`.** Two fields were added
(additively — the pre-existing 8-arg constructor still works, defaulting to `ORIGIN_ENGINE`/`sameKey=null`,
so every existing test/fixture keeps behaving exactly as before): `origin` (`ORIGIN_ENGINE` /
`ORIGIN_PROBE_SHARED_KEY` / `ORIGIN_PROBE_NEAR_MISS`, rendered as a new "Source" column — task brief: every
row must say where it came from) and `sameKey` (`Boolean`, computed ONCE by the runner from the two real
records' identifying-key field — `review.MatchSimulationBlock` has no EBX access and cannot look that
field's NAME up itself). Families 1 and 2 now key on `sameKey` when the runner supplied it, falling back to
the OLDER `exactFieldsEqual` test (the plan's exact-TIER fields, e.g. country/cityKey — a related but
different question) when it is null: `keyEqual = pair.sameKey != null ? pair.sameKey : exactFieldsEqual(...)`.
Family 1 also now counts a `MATCHED` verdict with a different key, not only `SUSPECTED` (task brief: "verdict
is SUSPECTED/MATCHED").

**Family 0 — "never an empty panel" (task brief).** Up to 3 engine-candidate `SUSPECT` pairs that already
carry at least one real per-field score, shown ONLY when families 1-3 are all empty (hidden otherwise, to
keep the panel short) — exactly the rescue the observed bug needed: the 14 real SUSPECT candidates would
have populated it directly. Every family's own empty line now says why, with real numbers, e.g. "No refusal
among the 0 shared-key pair(s) probed (1 pair(s) examined overall)." or "No pair scored within 3 points of
the threshold, across 1 pair(s) examined." — never the bare pre-lot "No pair of this kind in this sample."
A new summary card, "N pairs probed by the factory" (with its own shared-key/near-miss split), sits next to
"candidates examined"; every other card's sub-count already reads off the enlarged (engine + both probe
sets) pair list, since `MatchSimulationBlock.analyze` always runs over the merged set unconditionally.

**What was NOT run live this session** (no EBX access, same constraint as every other section of this
lot): both probe SQL statements (probe A's text is the ORIGINAL, coordinator-verified-live one; probe B's
is new and unverified); the row-lookup XPath predicates built from a probed key/group value;
`evaluatePair`'s own verdict for a pair the engine never itself compared (reasoned from the add-on's public
API only, §13.1); the ordering/priority of probe-vs-engine `evaluatePair` calls under the shared 60-call cap
at real data volume; and the rendered panel end to end against a real master table. Proven only against
hand-built fixtures (`MatchPlanSimulationRunnerSqlTest`, extended `MatchSimulationBlockTest`/
`MatchPlanViewTest`) — `tools/test_local.sh`: all green.

### 13.7 Self-heal before simulating — the boot-race defect (branch `fix/simulate-self-heal-activation`, 2026-09-22 23:30)

**Measured live twice, both right after a Tomcat restart, both on Proposal review → "Simulate on 20 pivots"
on `Company`: 2026-09-22 15:11 and again 23:26.** `kernel.log`:
`java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: field [Linked_Field_State] not found; input fields are: [id,
sourceSystem, …, ebx-metadata, $docid, …]`, thrown INSIDE the add-on —
`com.orchestranetworks.cce.lucene.clustering.canopy.CnyFilterBuilder.addTableParameters` ←
`CnyCanopyProducer.getSimilar` ← `addon.mame.service.matching.SimilarFinder.getSimilar` ←
`SimulateMatchingService.simulate` ← `MatchingOperationsImpl.simulateMatch` ← this module's own
`ebx.MameMatchingApi.simulate` ← `MatchPlanSimulationRunner.collectEngineCandidates` ←
`ProposalReviewUserService.simulateOne` — and the panel showed EBX's generic "A fatal error occurred"
instead of anything actionable.

**Root cause, per CLAUDE.md §8 ("huge Calcite stack trace at boot")**: on some boots the add-on's own
`MameDataModelModifier` fails with `IllegalStateException: Recursive load of: LogicalProject(...)` and the
`MatchingTableTrigger` is never attached to `/root/Company` — the boot log has no
`"Add MatchingTableTrigger to /root/Company, publication urn:ebx:publication:Companies_Master"` line for
that boot. Without the trigger, the business table's own Lucene index never gains the metadataset-linked
fields (`Linked_Field_State`/`GroupId`/`GoldenId`/…) the canopy filter unconditionally expects.
`get_matching_activation_status(table)` answers exactly this situation with `state: DISABLED`,
`published: true`, `metadatasetExists: true` — a genuinely published, metadataset-backed table whose trigger
the boot simply never attached. `activate_matching(table)` repairs it with no restart (measured live
2026-09-22 12:54, a different lot the same day: it resets the schema, recompiles it on an HTTP thread and
re-attaches the trigger) — this is exactly the one repair `ebx.MatchingActivationGuard` (new file) performs.

**What was built** (`ebx.MatchingActivationGuard`, called from both `MatchPlanSimulationRunner.simulate` —
covers both the preview-policy and the applied-policy branch, since either way it is the SAME underlying
master table — and `MatchingConfigurator.simulate`, the single-record REST route):

1. **Self-heal, once per Simulate click, before the first `simulateMatch`/`executeDecisionTree` call.**
   `get_matching_activation_status(table)` (resolving `AMBIGUOUS_TABLE` the same way every other match-merge
   call in this codebase already does — never the publication name up front, CLAUDE.md §8/§2.2): `ENABLED` →
   proceed; not `ENABLED` but `published && metadatasetExists` (the exact defect above) → one
   `activate_matching(table)` call, then re-decide from ITS OWN answer (never a second status read); still not
   `ENABLED` after that → refuse, naming the state and the remedy (restart). Anything else (not published at
   all, or published with no metadataset — e.g. a preview policy that only ever ran
   `generate_matching_policy`, never `activate_matching`: `ebx.MatchingPreviewPolicy` never calls it) is a
   DIFFERENT situation, not this bug, and refuses outright naming the remedy (configure/activate) rather than
   guessing a repair. A successful repair leaves a note (`"matching trigger was not attached after the last
   boot - re-activated"`) on `MatchPlanView.SimulationResult#activationNote`, shown warn-styled in the panel
   header next to the preview/applied-policy line (`review.match.simulate.activation.reactivated`,
   `.mdmf-hint-warn` — same `--warn` token `.mdmf-chip-warn`/`.mdmf-notice-warn` already use).
2. **Defense in depth inside `ebx.MameMatchingApi.simulate` itself**: an `IllegalArgumentException` whose
   message contains `Linked_Field_`, or any other `RuntimeException` from the add-on's own
   `com.orchestranetworks.cce.*` canopy/Lucene layer (walking the full cause chain), is translated into an
   `OperationException`: *"The add-on's index of &lt;table&gt; has no metadataset-linked fields
   (Linked_Field_State): the matching trigger is not attached — re-activate matching (activate_matching) or
   restart; raw: &lt;message&gt;"* — never reaches the user service raw. Never load-bearing on its own (job 1
   above should catch the real situation first); only for whatever races or slips past it.
3. **A dedicated refusal message in the panel.** `ProposalReviewUserService.simulateOne` tags
   `MatchingActivationGuard`'s own refusals with an internal marker (`MATCHING_NOT_ACTIVATED: `, stripped
   before display) so they render through `review.match.simulate.activation.refused` ("Simulation refused:
   matching could not be activated for this table. {0}") instead of the generic
   `review.match.simulate.failed` every other failure of that method still uses.

**Bundles**: `review.match.simulate.activation.reactivated` (no args — apostrophes left as-is, `MessageFormat`
is skipped for a 0-arg call, same rule as `.policy.applied`) and `review.match.simulate.activation.refused`
(one arg — the French text's apostrophe is doubled, `n''a`, the standard escape the existing
`review.cascade.none` bug already documents) in both `Messages_en.properties`/`Messages_fr.properties`.

**Never exercised live this session** (task constraint: no EBX access) — `MatchingActivationGuard.decide`/
`refusalMessage`/`isAddonIndexFailure`/`translateAddonIndexFailure`/the marker helpers are pure and
unit-tested directly (`MatchingActivationGuardTest`) against the exact shapes quoted above; the MCP
orchestration (`ensureActivatedBeforeSimulate`) reuses the same `get_matching_activation_status`/
`activate_matching` call/answer shapes `ebx.MatchingConfigurator`'s own `activate` step already sends live
(§4, including its `MameAnswer.success(json, false)` discipline for THIS specific tool's answer, deliberately
different from `requireSuccess`'s default-`true` convention for most other write tools) but the
already-published-but-disabled `ActivationStatus` shape itself was never independently confirmed against a
live `activate_matching` answer. `tools/test_local.sh`: all green.

### 13.8 The self-heal's own ORDER and gate were both wrong — second live incident, `Contact`, 2026-09-23 07:45

**Live result on main `a9fe317`** (Proposal review → `Contact`, plan `PROPOSED`, table `/root/Contact` NEVER
configured before): "Simulation refused: matching could not be activated for this table.
`get_matching_activation_status` answered `{"code":"CONFIG_NOT_FOUND","message":"No matching/merge
configuration for table /root/Contact","nextStep":"Generate a matching policy first.","success":false} for
/root/Contact even after resolving dataModel=urn:ebx:publication:Companies_Master`." — the exact wording §13.7's
own self-heal used to build for "found nothing at all", except this time it fired even though
`MatchPlanSimulationRunner.simulate` DOES call `MatchingPreviewPolicy.ensure` (which writes the table's first
configuration via `generate_matching_policy`/`generate_merge_policy`) textually BEFORE the activation check.

**Two real bugs, neither one "wrong order" as such — the coordinator's own diagnosis was the right symptom, the
wrong single cause**:

1. **The self-heal's own gate refused a config that was simply never activated for the first time.**
   `MatchingActivationGuard.decide` used to require `published && metadatasetExists` before even attempting
   `activate_matching` — but a config `ensureFresh` JUST generated (`generate_matching_policy`/
   `generate_merge_policy`, both additive, neither one calls `activate_matching`) is ALWAYS unpublished with no
   metadataset yet, by construction. So the very first time an entity's table is ever activated at all (as
   opposed to RE-activated after a boot race), the old gate refused outright instead of self-healing. Fixed:
   `decide` no longer reads `published`/`metadatasetExists` at all — `state != ENABLED` on a config that WAS
   found gets exactly one repair attempt, unconditionally (`activate_matching`'s own contract only requires a
   configuration to already exist, nothing about it being published yet).
2. **`ensure` and the activation check each independently resolved `AMBIGUOUS_TABLE` from a DIFFERENT tool's own
   candidate list** (`get_matching_config` vs. `get_matching_activation_status`) — nothing guaranteed the two
   resolutions agreed on the same `dataModel` string, so a config `ensure` wrote under one candidate could read
   back `CONFIG_NOT_FOUND` when the guard, moments later, independently resolved a DIFFERENT candidate for the
   same ambiguous table path. This is almost certainly what the live `Contact` run actually hit (a genuine,
   reproducible `CONFIG_NOT_FOUND` right after a successful write, not a timing race). Fixed: `MatchingPreviewPolicy
   .Result` now carries a new field, `dataModel` — the EXACT value `ensure` resolved and used for every
   `generate_matching_policy`/`generate_merge_policy` call it made — and `MatchPlanSimulationRunner.simulate`
   threads that SAME value straight into the new `MatchingActivationGuard.ensureActivatedAfterPreviewEnsure`,
   never re-resolving. The applied-plan path (`ensureActivatedBeforeSimulate`, no `ensure` call at all — used by
   `MatchingConfigurator.simulate` too, §4.5, unaffected by either bug since it never touches a preview) keeps
   self-resolving `AMBIGUOUS_TABLE` exactly as before.

**The call sequence, per the coordinator's own explicit recipe — "re-read", not a reuse of `activate_matching`'s
own answer.** `MatchingActivationGuard`'s retry core (`activateIfNeeded`, now `McpClient`-free — see below) is:
read status once; if already `ENABLED`, done (sequence: `status`). Otherwise: `activate_matching` once, then a
GENUINE SECOND `get_matching_activation_status` read (never trusting `activate_matching`'s own returned status
as final, per the coordinator's own instruction) — `ENABLED` now → done, note recorded (sequence: `status,
activate, status`); still not `ENABLED` → refuse, naming the state and the remedy (check the config, or
restart). A `CONFIG_NOT_FOUND` (or any soft miss) on the FIRST status read is still a hard refusal — worded
differently depending on context: "the preview write may have failed silently" when this run just called
`ensure` (a genuinely alarming situation, since `ensure` is assumed to have succeeded — it throws otherwise),
vs. the ordinary "run matching/configure first" for the applied-plan path (which never calls `ensure` and
genuinely expects the config to pre-exist). A `CONFIG_NOT_FOUND` on the SECOND (re-)read, after
`activate_matching` itself reported success, gets its own distinct, alarming wording too — that combination was
never supposed to be possible and is not a normal "not configured yet" situation.

**Consequence, documented rather than hidden: Simulate on a never-configured table now creates its metadataset.**
Once `activate_matching` is allowed to run the very first time (bug 1's fix), its own fan-out
(`get_matching_activation_status`'s own tool description: "fans out the companion metadataset to every
open-branch dataset using the table's data model") happens as a side effect of clicking "Simulate" on a
`PROPOSED`/`ACCEPTED` plan, not only after `matching/configure` explicitly activates it. This is a one-way but
harmless write — the metadataset is exactly what the table needs to be simulated or matched at all, and leaving
the plan itself unaccepted afterward undoes nothing else.

**Testability seam added: `MatchingActivationGuard.StatusPort`.** `McpClient` is `final` with a package-private
`ToolResult` constructor — this codebase's established rule is to never construct a real one in a test
(`MatchingPreviewPolicyTest`'s own class Javadoc: `ensure`/`remove` are "NOT exercised here (they need a live
add-on)"). `activateIfNeeded` now depends only on a small local interface (`readStatus`/`activate`, both keyed
by an ALREADY-resolved `dataModel`), never on `McpClient` directly — the ONE place that still touches
`McpClient`/`ToolResult` is a private `McpStatusPort` adapter, and `AMBIGUOUS_TABLE` resolution stays entirely
outside the interface's contract (in `resolveDataModel`, used only by the self-resolving, applied-plan entry
point). `MatchingActivationGuardTest` drives `activateIfNeeded` directly against a hand-written fake
`StatusPort` that records the exact call sequence and the `dataModel` passed on every call — genuine behavior
coverage of the retry/re-read core, not a placeholder. **What this seam does NOT reach**: the OUTER order
"`ensure` (preview only) → activation check → `simulateMatch`" inside `MatchPlanSimulationRunner.simulate`
itself is three un-catch-wrapped statements in a row (each one's own thrown `OperationException` skips every
statement after it) — verified by reading that method, not by a fake-client integration test: `ensure` needs a
live `Session`/`Adaptation` (no fake `Adaptation` implementation exists anywhere in this codebase, by
deliberate, stated convention) and `MameMatchingApi.simulate` calls the add-on's Java API directly, no
`McpClient` involved at all, so it could never join the SAME recorded sequence as the two MCP calls even with a
faked transport.

**Never exercised live this session** (task constraint: no EBX access) — same discipline as §13.7:
`MatchingActivationGuardTest` is pure/fake-based; the real `McpStatusPort`/`resolveDataModel` reuse the same
call/answer shapes already sent live elsewhere in this codebase, but the specific "found, not enabled, re-read
after activate" sequence against a genuinely fresh table was never itself run against a live instance this
session — only reasoned from the coordinator's own live report above and the tools' own descriptions.
`tools/test_local.sh`: all green.

## 13. Survivorship and trusted sources (branch `feature/trusted-sources-survivorship`, 2026-09-22)
## 14. Survivorship and trusted sources (branch `feature/trusted-sources-survivorship`, 2026-09-22)

### 14.1 The gap, measured live before this lot

The factory's first real merge (Company 322 "BPCE", ERP 290 + CRM 248) took `sourceSystem` from 290 and
`sourceId`/`supplierId` from 248, `_loadId` from 290 — every field chosen by the merge policy's single
default function, `longest`. Cause, in `MatchingPolicyTranslator.buildMergePolicy`: record selection
`mostCompleted`, `defaultFieldMergeFunctionChain: [longest]`, `survivors: []`, and no trusted sources were
ever pushed to the add-on — although the project wizard already collects a trust rank per source
(`ProjectSource.trustRank`, "lower wins", default 100) whose own UI hint promised it "feeds the
most-trusted-source order of the eventual merge policy" (`Messages_en.properties`,
`wizard.field.trustRank.hint`) — before this lot it only ever fed the Record lineage screen's own lane
ordering (`ebx.RecordLineageReader#readSourceTrustRank`), never `match-merge` itself. This lot makes the hint
true.

### 14.2 What is pushed, and when

`ebx.MatchingConfigurator.configureOne` (the `matching/configure` path, a FRESH table) now calls
`set_trusted_sources` right after the field-capabilities pre-flight check and BEFORE
`generate_matching_policy`/`generate_merge_policy` — the task brief's own contract (never independently
re-verified this session, no EBX access):

```json
{"table": "/root/Company",
 "trustedSources": {"sourceField": "/sourceSystem",
   "tableTrustedSourceList": ["ERP", "CRM"]}}
```

**Hotfix 2026-09-22 17:40 (coordinator, after the first live `get_matching_config` on `/root/Company`):** the
`sources` member is NOT sent any more. It is the instance-wide source catalogue — the live answer listed the
PointOfSale project's `ERP_AMER`, `ERP_APAC`, `ERP_EU`, `GROUP_ERP`, `MDM`, `POS_ENRICH` and the built-in
`Data Steward decision` — and a supplied member replaces the stored one wholesale, so the two-entry list this
lot first emitted would have wiped every other project's sources. `tableTrustedSourceList` alone auto-creates
the codes. Also measured live: the existing `Company` merge policy reads `recordSelectionFunctionChain:
[{constantValue: null, dateFieldPath: null, function: "mame.addon.reference.data.recordSelectionPolicy.mostCompleted.label"}]`,
`defaultFieldMergeFunctionChain: [{…, function: "longest"}]`, `survivors: []`, `relatedTables: [{Contact, MANUAL}]`,
`useForManualMerge: true`, `mode: "ONLY_DUPLICATES"`; `trustedSources.sourceField: null`, `tableTrustedSourceList: []`,
`fieldTrustedSources: []` — the chain-entry shape `MergeConfigPatchPlanner` assumed.

`dataModel` is NEVER passed to this call (stated as an explicit "OMIT" in the task brief, unlike every other
call in `configureOne`, which threads a `MameDataModelResolution` outcome through when one was found —
CLAUDE.md §8's "dataModel is never the publication name" applies here too, but this tool's own contract goes
further and says to leave the argument out altogether). A supplied list REPLACES the table's whole
trusted-source configuration wholesale (never a delta) — `master.TrustedSourceRanking.order` computes the
order from the project's own `ProjectSource` rows, ascending `trustRank` ("lower wins"), ties broken
alphabetically by `code` (a real, otherwise-arbitrary choice, documented in that class' own Javadoc since
nothing else breaks a tie between two equally-trusted sources). `code` is the source's own `sourceSystem` —
see §14.5 for why that, and only that, is the right identifier to use. `description` prefers the linked
catalog source's own label (`ebx.WizardData`'s own lookup, reused) and falls back to the bare `sourceSystem`
code.

### 14.3 The merge policy `MatchingPolicyTranslator.buildMergePolicy` now emits

Signature gained a third parameter, `pSourceKeyFieldNames` (see §14.4). For an entity named `Company` with
one structurally-identified source-key attribute `supplierId` and every hint left at its default:

```json
{
  "code": "Company",
  "mode": "ONLY_DUPLICATES",
  "useForManualMerge": true,
  "applyPermission": false,
  "recordSelectionFunctionChain": [
    {"function": "mame.addon.reference.data.recordSelectionPolicy.mostTrustedSource.label"},
    {"function": "mame.addon.reference.data.recordSelectionPolicy.mostCompleted.label"}
  ],
  "defaultFieldMergeFunctionChain": [
    {"function": "most trusted source"},
    {"function": "longest"}
  ],
  "survivors": [
    {"field": "/sourceSystem", "mergeFunctionChain": [{"function": "constant", "constantValue": "MDM"}]},
    {"field": "/sourceId", "mergeFunctionChain": [{"function": "no merge"}]},
    {"field": "/_loadId", "mergeFunctionChain": [{"function": "no merge"}]},
    {"field": "/_receivedAt", "mergeFunctionChain": [{"function": "max"}]},
    {"field": "/supplierId", "mergeFunctionChain": [{"function": "no merge"}]}
  ]
}
```

Rules, in order:

- `recordSelectionFunctionChain`/`defaultFieldMergeFunctionChain` always try **most trusted source first**,
  then the project's own hint (default `mostCompleted`/`longest`) as the fallback MAME's own chain semantics
  fall through to when the first entry cannot decide (e.g. no trusted-source ranking configured for any
  contributing source of a given group) — never dropped, never replaced. If the hint itself already IS "most
  trusted source" (either short key, for record selection, or the literal string, for default field merge),
  the chain collapses to that ONE entry rather than duplicating it (`recordSelectionFunctionChain` uses the
  RAW I18N KEY the schema documents — `mame.addon.reference.data.recordSelectionPolicy.<key>.label` — exactly
  like the pre-existing `RECORD_SELECTION_FUNCTIONS` map already produced for a single entry;
  `defaultFieldMergeFunctionChain`/survivor chains use LITERAL enum strings, never i18n keys — a genuine,
  measured asymmetry between the two chain families, task brief's own contract).
- `sourceSystem` → `constant "MDM"` **(superseded by lot M1, §56: `no merge` + `autoCreateNewGoldenSource = MDM`; the constant overwrote records that were not merged)** (the fixed value the factory itself writes for a record it creates —
  CLAUDE.md's own convention for such a value); `sourceId`/`_loadId` → `no merge` (a golden record has no
  single source system/load batch of its own, so neither field should ever be silently overwritten by
  whichever contributor happened to sort first); `_receivedAt` → `max` (the freshest contribution wins,
  never the longest string).
- Every SOURCE-KEY business attribute (`StagingAttribute.businessKey = true`, structurally read — never a
  name match, see §14.4) → `no merge`, for the same reason as `sourceId`: a per-source natural key has no
  single "most complete" or "longest" value that means anything once several sources are merged.
- A field path already carrying a survivor rule is never given a second one (`addSurvivor`'s own dedupe,
  defensive — e.g. a source-key attribute that happened to be literally named `sourceId`: the FIRST
  (technical) rule silently wins, the source-key loop is skipped for that path).
- A new self-check, `assertMergePolicyWellFormed` (the merge-policy analogue of `buildMatchingPolicy`'s own
  `assertEveryTreeFieldIsDeclared`), asserts every chain is non-empty, every function non-blank, `constant`/
  `no merge` never appear in `recordSelectionFunctionChain`/`defaultFieldMergeFunctionChain` (only a survivor
  chain may use them, per `matching_config_schema`'s own enum), a `constant` entry is always LAST and always
  carries a non-blank `constantValue`, and no two survivors target the same field — a defect in the building
  logic above is now caught by a unit test, never by a live `generate_merge_policy`/`patch_matching_config`
  refusal.

### 14.4 How the source-key attribute(s) are identified — structurally, never by name

> **2026-09-23 correction (§19.10): this section describes the LEAF-entity rule only.** For a CANONICAL
> entity (`StagingEntity.memberEntities` non-empty, e.g. `Company` unifying `Supplier`/`Account`), the
> `businessKey` flag lives on each MEMBER's own attribute, never on the canonical entity's own attribute of
> the same name (measured live: `Company.supplierId` itself carries `businessKey: false`) - `ebx.
> MatchingConfigurator.readSourceKeyFieldNames` now also follows `memberEntities` and maps each member's own
> source key onto this entity's same-named attribute (`master.SourceKeyResolver`) - see §19.10 for the full
> rule, why same-name matching is the only mapping this schema supports, and the live `Company` result.
> Everything below this note is still accurate for the LEAF half of the rule.

`ebx.MatchingConfigurator.readSourceKeyFieldNames` reads `StagingAttribute` rows of the entity directly (a
read independent of the `StagingModel`/`MasterModel` pipeline, deliberately — see the note below on why) and
keeps a row when ALL of: `businessKey = true` ("the SOURCE's own key", `ReviewLine`/`WizardSnapshot`'s own
field Javadoc — e.g. `supplierId` on `Supplier`, `contactId` on `Contact`), `primaryKey = false` (the
technical row identity — `sourceSystem`/`sourceId` — is already covered by its own fixed rule, §14.3),
`referenceEntity` blank (see below), and an accepted-like status (`TechnicalKeyRule.isAcceptedLike`).

**Deliberately excludes a business-key attribute that is ALSO a foreign key.** On the master table such an
attribute is promoted as a `"<name>Ref"` field (`master.MasterModel.buildTable`, with its own collision
suffix via `unique(...)` when a name clash occurs) — this method has no reliable, independent way to
reproduce that exact generated name without re-running `MasterModel`'s own field-building logic a second
time. Rather than duplicate that logic (or thread a new field through `StagingModel.AttributeInfo`/
`MasterModel.AttributeInfo`, both of which are constructed at dozens of call sites across this codebase — a
blast radius far beyond this lot's scope, and a real risk of touching a file a concurrent branch owns), a
business-key attribute that is also a reference is simply left out of the survivor list. Every source-key
attribute seen so far in this codebase (`docs/MATCHING.md`, `PLAN.md`) is plain source-system data, never a
reference to another entity, so this is a scoping choice, not a known correctness gap — flagged here in case
that assumption ever stops holding for a future project.

`master.MatchingPolicyTranslator` itself never reads `StagingAttribute`/EBX at all (kept pure, same
discipline as the rest of the class) — it only ever receives the already-resolved, bare field-name list.

### 14.5 How source codes are matched between the wizard and `sourceSystem`

The wizard's `ProjectSource.sourceSystem` (typed once, at `matching/wizard` step 2 — `WizardRules.SourceDraft
.sourceSystem`, `ebx.WizardData#addSource`) is written VERBATIM, with no translation step anywhere in
between, into every landing row's `_sourceSystem` field (`ebx.LandingGenerator`/the landing model's own
technical field, `FactoryPaths.Landing.SOURCE_SYSTEM`), which `ebx.StagingLoader`/`ebx.MasterLoader` carry
through unchanged into the staging and master rows' own `sourceSystem` business field
(`master.MasterModel`'s own `SOURCE_SYSTEM` constant, `"sourceSystem"`) and into every `Xref.sourceSystem`
row (`FactoryPaths.Xref.SOURCE_SYSTEM`). So the exact string `ebx.MatchingConfigurator.readTrustedSources`
reads off `ProjectSource.sourceSystem` is, byte for byte, the same string a master record's own
`sourceSystem` field holds — no separate mapping table, no normalization, nothing to keep in sync. This was
read from the existing code (`WizardData`, `MasterModel`, `MasterLoader`), never independently verified live
this session.

### 14.6 Re-applying to an EXISTING configuration — `POST /projects/{code}/matching/survivorship?entity=<name>`

The live `Company` policy `matching/configure` already created must NOT be deleted and regenerated just to
pick up this lot's new rules (deleting the decision tree would also throw away any manual tuning). The new
route:

```
curl -s -u admin -X POST -w '\n' 'http://localhost:8080/ebx-mdm-factory/rest/v1/projects/Companies/matching/survivorship?entity=Company'
```

1. `get_matching_config(table)` — same `MameDataModelResolution` dance as `configureOne` (never the
   publication name as `dataModel` — CLAUDE.md §8), refuses outright if no configuration exists yet
   ("run `matching/configure` first").
2. `set_trusted_sources` — same call as §14.2, no `dataModel` ever.
3. `master.MergeConfigPatchPlanner.plan` computes the MINIMAL, order-safe `patch_matching_config` op list
   between the config just read and `MatchingPolicyTranslator.buildMergePolicy`'s desired shape — see that
   class' own Javadoc for the exact algorithm (overwrite the shared prefix in place with `set_chain_entry`,
   only ever ADD past the current end, only ever REMOVE from the current end backwards) and for why it never
   violates "the last entry of a required chain cannot be removed".
4. `patch_matching_config` is called ONLY if the op list is non-empty (an already-up-to-date policy sends
   nothing — a genuinely idempotent re-apply).

Against the real, live, PRE-this-lot `Companies` shape `docs/MASTER-ZONE.md` §1.1 recorded
(`recordSelectionFunctionChain: [mostCompleted]`, `defaultFieldMergeFunctionChain: [longest]`,
`survivors: []`) and the desired shape in §14.3, the planner used to emit exactly 9 ops with 0-based
`position` and an `add_survivor_field` value of `{"mergeFunctionChain":[...]}` — see the "measured live"
note right below for why that list was wrong, and the corrected 10-op list that replaces it.

**Measured live, 2026-09-22 23:40 — this exact 9-op list was refused.** `POST
/projects/Companies/matching/survivorship?entity=Company` ran for real: `set_trusted_sources` succeeded
(`{"table":"/root/Company","trustedSources":{"sourceField":"/sourceSystem","tableTrustedSourceList":
["CRM","ERP"]}}`), then `patch_matching_config` answered

```json
{"code":"INVALID_PARAMS","message":"Invalid operations payload.",
 "nextStep":"Pass a non-empty JSON array of {op, target, value}; see the tool description."}
```

recorded verbatim on the failed PipelineStep 107. Re-reading the tool's own live description and
`matching_config_schema.patchOps` the same night (23:45) surfaced two structural mistakes in the list above,
neither of which `validate_matching_config` or any compile-time check had a chance to catch (same "no
line/column, re-verify against the actual instance" discipline as CLAUDE.md §13):

- **`position` is 1-based** ("position addresses one of its entries, 1-based"; "position 1 is the first
  entry") — the list above sent `position: 0` for the first entry of every chain.
- **`add_chain_entry` appends when `target.position` is omitted** — the list above sent a stale post-append
  index (`position: 1`) instead of leaving it out.
- **`add_survivor_field`'s `value` is a bare merge-FUNCTION-NAME STRING**, never the `{"mergeFunctionChain":
  [...]}` envelope the list above sent for every one of its five entries. It only ever creates a single,
  parameter-less entry — a first entry needing `constantValue`/`dateFieldPath` (here, `/sourceSystem`'s
  `constant("MDM")`) has to be completed right after with a `survivor_field` chain op: a `set_chain_entry` at
  position 1 to attach the parameter, since the created slot never carries one.
- **Several chain ops in one call apply in array order against ONE running chain; a removal renumbers later
  positions** — not exercised by this particular list (nothing needed removing here), but load-bearing for
  `master.MergeConfigPatchPlanner.planChain`'s own "remove from the current end backwards" discipline (class
  Javadoc) once a chain shrinks.

Fixed 2026-09-22 23:45, branch `fix/patch-ops-contract` (`master.MergeConfigPatchPlanner`; every case pinned
by `MergeConfigPatchPlannerTest`, including this exact Company fixture). Against the SAME pre-lot `Companies`
shape and the SAME desired shape in §14.3, that FIRST fix produced a 10-op list (one more than the original
9 — the `/sourceSystem` `constant("MDM")` follow-up `set_chain_entry` the bare-string `add_survivor_field`
can no longer smuggle in) whose chain-entry `value`s were still raw JSON OBJECTS
(`{"function":"...mostTrustedSource.label"}` etc.) — see the SECOND "measured live" note right below for why
that was also wrong, and the actually-corrected op list that replaces it.

**Measured live, 2026-09-23 01:03/01:10 — the 23:45 fix above was deployed (117e193) and run for real, then
probed directly three more times.** `set_trusted_sources` succeeded; `patch_matching_config` on the chain ops
did not. Four findings:

1. The one remaining op from that run, `{"op":"set_chain_entry","target":{"policyCode":"Company",
   "chain":"record_selection","position":2},"value":{"function":"...lastUpdate.label"}}` — a RAW JSON OBJECT
   `value`, exactly what the 23:45 fix still sent for a parameter-less entry — was refused, the same generic
   `"Invalid operations payload."`
2. The SAME op with `"value":"most trusted source"` (a plain STRING) on `default_field_merge` position 1 was
   **ACCEPTED**.
3. `"value":"{\"function\":\"mame.addon.reference.data.recordSelectionPolicy.lastUpdate.label\",
   \"dateFieldPath\":\"System date\"}"` — the entry object JSON-ENCODED AS A STRING — was **ACCEPTED**.
4. A raw JSON object as `value` is what triggers the refusal, full stop. **So the rule for every op:
   `value` is a JSON STRING — either the bare function name, or the entry object serialized to a JSON string
   (`{function, constantValue?, dateFieldPath?}`) — never a JSON object.** This applies uniformly to
   `set_chain_entry`/`add_chain_entry` on every chain this class writes to (`record_selection`,
   `default_field_merge`, `survivor_field`) — the 23:45 fix had gotten `position`/append-shape right but never
   applied this rule anywhere, so every chain-entry op it emitted was still shaped wrong.

A fifth, unrelated finding from the same round: the add-on itself **stores `dateFieldPath: "System date"` on
a date-aware entry it created without one** — a fresh `get_matching_config` read-back of the `lastUpdate`
entry this class wrote with no `dateFieldPath` at all comes back carrying `"System date"`, which the planner
must treat as EQUAL to "no `dateFieldPath`" (never emit `"System date"` itself) or it spuriously rewrites an
already-correct entry on every subsequent re-apply. A sixth, also caught this round: the planner compared
`constantValue`/`dateFieldPath` **explicit JSON `null` vs. absent as DIFFERENT** — the live shape §14.2
already recorded (`constantValue: null, dateFieldPath: null`) is a real answer shape, and Jackson's
`NullNode#asText()` returns the four-character string `"null"`, not empty, so a stored explicit null used to
compare unequal to a desired entry that never set the field at all.

Fixed 2026-09-23 01:10, same branch `fix/patch-ops-contract`, on top of the 23:45 commit
(`master.MergeConfigPatchPlanner`; every op site now goes through one `entryValueString` helper: a bare
function-name string when the entry has no `constantValue`/`dateFieldPath`, the entry serialized to a JSON
string otherwise; `dateFieldPath: "System date"` and explicit JSON `null` both normalize the same as "unset"
before any comparison). Against the SAME pre-lot `Companies` shape and the SAME desired shape in §14.3, the
ACTUALLY-corrected planner emits the same 10 ops as before, but with every `value` now a JSON STRING:

```json
[
  {"op":"set_chain_entry","target":{"policyCode":"Company","chain":"record_selection","position":1},
   "value":"mame.addon.reference.data.recordSelectionPolicy.mostTrustedSource.label"},
  {"op":"add_chain_entry","target":{"policyCode":"Company","chain":"record_selection"},
   "value":"mame.addon.reference.data.recordSelectionPolicy.mostCompleted.label"},
```

## 15. LLM-proposed survivorship rules (branch `feature/survivorship-llm-review`, 2026-09-22)

`## 14. Survivorship and trusted sources` above closed the gap for the four fixed TECHNICAL fields and the
trusted-source ORDER — it never let anything propose a rule for a BUSINESS field (`vatNo` picks the more
complete value from whichever source happens to sort first, `city` the same, `name` the same). This lot lets
the SAME language-model pass that proposes an entity's matching tiers (`master.MatchPlanLlmPass`) propose,
alongside them, per-field survivorship rules for its BUSINESS fields — the validated mockup is
`docs/mockups/review-match-plan-survivorship.html`, section "4 · Survivance" of the expanded Matching review
line. **Nothing in this lot was run against a live instance or a real LLM — no EBX access, no MCP access this
session.** Every claim below is either read from source or proven by `tools/test_local.sh` (`all green`,
new/changed tests: `MatchPlanSurvivorshipTest`, `MatchingPolicyTranslatorTest`, `MergeConfigPatchPlannerTest`,
`TrustedSourceRankingTest`, `MatchSurvivorshipBlockTest`).

### 15.1 What the LLM sees, in addition to the existing matching-tier prompt

`master.MatchPlanLlmPass.userPrompt` (the SAME prompt that lists tiers/clustering candidates) gained two
additions, both fed through the SAME `ProjectInfo`/`EntityInfo`/`AttributeInfo` value objects the tier-proposal
side already used — no second prompt, no second tool call, one `propose_match_plan` call now covers both a
plan's matching AND its survivorship:

- **The project's trusted-source ranking**, once, before the entity list — `master.MatchPlanLlmPass.
  TrustedSourceInfo{code, rank, description}`, `rank` 1-based, most trusted first. `ebx.MatchPlanLlmSuggester`
  builds it from `MatchingConfigurator.readTrustedSources` (now package-visible, not `private`, precisely so
  this class can reuse it) ordered by `TrustedSourceRanking.order` — the exact same read `matching/configure`
  itself uses to build the real `set_trusted_sources` call, never a second query with its own chance to drift.
- **Per business/reference attribute, of a multi-source entity**: a per-system FILL RATE
  (`AttributeInfo#fillCountBySystem`, rendered against `EntityInfo#rowCountBySystem` — both new fields, `ebx.
  CrossSystemMeasures.perSystemFilledCounts`/`rowCountsBySystem`, both already existed for other callers) and,
  for a field that HAS its own derived matching key (the 2026-09-22 `FOLD_KEY` contract, `AttributeInfo#matchKey`),
  TWO clearly distinguished divergence numbers — see the coordinator fix in §15.9 below for the live measurement
  that made this a two-number question, not one:
  - **Cosmetic spelling variants** (`AttributeInfo#cosmeticVariantGroupsCount`, denominator
    `AttributeInfo#sharedFoldGroupCount`): among the groups that already share THIS attribute's own folded key
    across systems, how many still show more than one distinct RAW spelling (accents/case/spacing) - `"Paris"` vs
    `"PARIS"`. Never itself evidence of a real disagreement - folding is exactly what makes this noise disappear.
  - **Genuine divergence after folding** (`AttributeInfo#divergingGroupsCount`, denominator `EntityInfo
    #sharedIdentityGroupCount`): among the groups that share the ENTITY's OWN identity key across systems (e.g.
    `nameKey` - "these two records are confidently the same company"), how many still disagree on THIS
    attribute's folded value. THIS is the number that means two sources really disagree - never computed at all
    when the entity has no identity key yet (`EntityInfo#identityKeyField` null); the prompt then says so in
    words rather than showing a fabricated zero.

  Example prompt line (`city`, matching key `cityKey`, entity identity key `nameKey`) - the LIVE numbers measured
  on `Companies_Master/Master/"Company"` (§15.9):

  ```
  - city (type STRING, maxLength 80), role BUSINESS, fill rate 98.0% [EXACT], distinct 30 (30.0% of all rows) [EXACT],
    matching key: cityKey, per-system fill: ERP 98.0% (54), CRM 100.0% (52), cosmetic spelling variants (same
    folded value, different raw spelling) among values sharing its own matching key across systems: 32 of 33
    shared group(s), genuine divergence after folding (grouped by this entity's own identity key 'nameKey'): 0
    of 33 shared identity group(s)
  ```

  **Capped, not exhaustive** (`ebx.MatchPlanLlmSuggester.MAX_SURVIVORSHIP_MEASURED_ATTRIBUTES = 30`, INFERRED):
  the per-system fill call is only made for the first 30 BUSINESS/REFERENCE attributes of an entity that has
  two or more source systems present at all (`EntityInfo#rowCountBySystem.size() >= 2`) — a single-source entity
  gets none of this (no survivorship question to ask), and an attribute past the cap is still listed in the
  prompt, just without the per-system line. Both divergence numbers are only ever computed for an attribute that
  already has a `matchKey` — never for a plain field, and never up front for every candidate the way the original
  cross-system-sharing count was rejected for doing (§14.1's own "coordinator review, 2026-09-21" precedent).

`master.MatchPlanLlmPass.systemPrompt` gained one new paragraph ("SURVIVORSHIP (optional, per entity, ...)")
right after the matching-key paragraph, spelling out: never a rule for a technical/`SOURCE_KEY` field (the
factory always sets those), the six allowed functions and what each means, the `trustedSourceList` override,
"ground every rule in the evidence given ... skip it when a field is already near-identical", and the
high/medium/low confidence contract ("a rule you are unsure of should still be proposed at low confidence
rather than omitted"). The closing instruction line was extended from "Propose a matching plan per entity ..."
to also say "... including — where the evidence supports it — the optional survivorship rules".

### 15.2 The schema the LLM answers — `propose_match_plan`'s new `survivorship` argument

Additive to the existing `tiers`/`clusteringFields`/`mergeHints` object — nothing about the mandatory tier
contract changed. Optional at the top level; when absent, `requirements` carries no `survivorship` key at all
("a field with no rule = policy default", task brief's own words — proven by
`MatchPlanSurvivorshipTest#noSurvivorshipArgument_noKeyInRequirements`):

```json
{
  "entity": "Company",
  "tiers": [ ... ],
  "clusteringFields": [ ... ],
  "survivorship": {
    "fields": [
      {
        "field": "vatNo",
        "chain": [ { "function": "most trusted source" } ],
        "rationale": "ERP is the legal registry of record and is 96% filled vs. 4% on CRM.",
        "confidence": "high"
      },
      {
        "field": "city",
        "chain": [ { "function": "last update", "dateFieldPath": "/_receivedAt" } ],
        "rationale": "CRM is kept current by sales reps; 4 of 33 shared groups disagree, all more recent on CRM.",
        "confidence": "low"
      }
    ]
  },
  "rationale": "...",
  "confidence": 85
}
```

`chain[].function` is one of exactly six literal strings (`master.MatchPlanLlmPass.BUSINESS_SURVIVOR_FUNCTIONS`,
the SAME literal-string family `matching_config_schema`'s own `defaultFieldMergeFunctionChain` enum documents,
minus the two TECHNICAL-only entries `constant`/`no merge`): `"last update"`, `"longest"`, `"max"`, `"min"`,
`"most frequent"`, `"most trusted source"`. `dateFieldPath` is only meaningful with `"last update"`/`"max"`.
`trustedSourceList` (an array of source codes, most trusted first) is only meaningful with `"most trusted
source"` — a per-field override of the table's own trusted-source order, for a field one specific source
genuinely maintains better than its overall ranking. `confidence` is one of `"high"`/`"medium"`/`"low"`
(`master.MatchPlanLlmPass.SURVIVORSHIP_CONFIDENCES`) — distinct from the plan-wide 0-100 `confidence`.

### 15.3 Validation — dropped with a named reason, never a refusal of the whole call

Unlike a bad tier/clustering entry (which makes `propose_match_plan` answer an error and counts toward the
repeated-refusal circuit breaker), a bad survivorship RULE is simply dropped, with a one-line reason folded
into the accepted plan's own `rationale` ("Survivorship notes: ...") — survivorship is optional guidance on
top of the mandatory tiers/clustering contract, never a reason to make the model retry the whole entity.
Implemented in `master.MatchPlanLlmPass.Session#buildSurvivorship`, proven by `MatchPlanSurvivorshipTest`:

- **Unknown field** (not an accepted attribute of the entity) → dropped ("not an accepted attribute of...").
- **A `SOURCE_KEY`-role field** (e.g. `supplierId`) → dropped ("it is a per-source record key - the factory
  always sets it to 'no merge' itself"). A technical field (`sourceSystem`/`sourceId`/`_loadId`/`_receivedAt`)
  is never even a candidate — it is not in the entity's own attribute list to begin with, so it is refused the
  same way as any other unknown field, one level up.
- **Empty chain**, or a chain entry whose `function` is not one of the six allowed strings (this is also how a
  sneaked-in `"constant"`/`"no merge"` is refused — the enum simply excludes them) → the WHOLE rule dropped.
- **Blank rationale** → dropped ("empty rationale").
- **Missing/unrecognised `confidence`** → NEVER dropped for this alone — defaults to `"medium"`
  (`SURVIVORSHIP_DEFAULT_CONFIDENCE`). Only an unknown field or function drops a rule; confidence is never
  that strict a gate.
- **`"low"` confidence** → kept, not dropped — this is the one case the task brief calls out by name ("keep
  but flag"): the rule reaches `requirements.survivorship.fields[]` and `MatchPlan.evidence` exactly like a
  `"high"`/`"medium"` one, and `review.MatchSurvivorshipBlock` renders a "to verify" chip next to it.

A dropped rule never prevents the OTHER rules of the same call from being kept, and never prevents the plan's
own tiers from being accepted — only that one field-level rule is missing from the stored `requirements`.

### 15.4 Evidence — `MatchPlanEvidence.Field` gained a `confidence`, and a `SURVIVORSHIP` role

`master.MatchPlanEvidence.Field`/`review.MatchPlanFieldEvidence` both gained an additive `confidence` member
(nullable String, new constructor overload, old ones default it to null — every existing caller/JSON document
keeps reading exactly as before) and a new role constant, `ROLE_SURVIVORSHIP`, combinable with any of the
existing matching-side roles (`ANCHOR_FUZZY`/`SUPPORTING_EXACT`/`CLUSTERING`) — a field used as both a fuzzy
anchor AND given a survivorship rule (e.g. `city`) ends up as ONE evidence entry with a combined role
(`master.MatchPlanLlmPass#mergeSurvivorshipEvidence`, proven by
`MatchPlanSurvivorshipTest#evidenceMergesWithAnExistingMatchingRole`), never two entries for the same field.

**A survivorship rule's own numbers (`AttributeInfo#fillCountBySystem`) fill a gap the matching guard leaves
empty**: `CrossSystemFieldGuard` only ever measures a field compared with the EXACT algorithm (a `MATCH`-tier
identifier, or a clustering field) — a plain fuzzy anchor like `city`/`name` gets no evidence at all from the
matching side (role `ANCHOR_FUZZY`, verdict `NOT_MEASURED`, no `filledBySystem`). `mergeSurvivorshipEvidence`
fills `filledBySystem` from `AttributeInfo#fillCountBySystem` ONLY when there is no existing measurement to
overwrite — an existing one (from the matching guard) always wins, since it was measured for a stronger reason
(an actual comparison the engine will run), but the survivorship number is exactly what the review screen's own
per-system fill bars (§15.5) need for a field the matching side never had a reason to measure.

### 15.5 The translator merge — `MatchingPolicyTranslator.buildMergePolicy` unchanged signature, new behaviour

**No public signature changed.** `buildMergePolicy(pMergePolicyCode, pRequirements, pSourceKeyFieldNames)` reads
`pRequirements.path("survivorship").path("fields")` itself, internally, the same way it already reads
`pRequirements.path("mergePolicy")` for the record-selection/default-field-merge hints — every existing call
site (`ebx.MatchingConfigurator#configureOne`/`#applySurvivorship`) needed NO change to pick this up.

- **Technical always wins.** The four fixed technical survivors and the per-entity source-key survivor(s) are
  added to the `survivors[]` array FIRST, exactly as before this lot; a business rule from `survivorship.fields[]`
  targeting a field path already claimed is silently skipped (`addSurvivor`'s own pre-existing dedupe — no new
  code needed for this either). `MatchingPolicyTranslator.technicalSurvivorFieldNames()` (new, public) exposes
  the four literal names for a caller/test that wants to name the collision explicitly, without duplicating the
  list. Proven: `MatchingPolicyTranslatorTest#mergePolicy_businessSurvivorRuleDroppedWhenCollidesWithTechnical`
  (a rule on `sourceSystem` never displaces the factory's own `constant "MDM"`).
- **A business rule becomes a plain `survivors[]` entry**, `{field: "/<name>", mergeFunctionChain: [...]}` —
  `trustedSourceList` is stripped from every chain entry before it reaches this array (it has no place in
  `matching_config_schema`'s own `mergeFunctionChain` entry shape; it belongs in the trusted-sources payload
  instead, see below) and `rationale`/`confidence` never reach the wire payload either (they stay in
  `MatchPlan.requirements`/`evidence`, read back by the review screen, never sent to the add-on).
- **`extractFieldTrustedSourceOverrides(pRequirements)`** (new, public, pure) walks the same
  `survivorship.fields[]` and returns `[{field, trustedSourceList}, ...]` for every field whose chain has a
  `"most trusted source"` entry WITH a non-empty override — `TrustedSourceRanking.buildTrustedSourcesPayload`
  gained a third, optional `ArrayNode` argument (`fieldTrustedSources`, the 2-arg overload delegates with
  `null`, unchanged behaviour) that adds this array to `trustedSources.fieldTrustedSources` verbatim, per the
  live hotfix's own rule (§14.2): "a supplied fieldTrustedSources list deletes any override not present", so
  `ebx.MatchingConfigurator#configureOne`/`#applySurvivorship` always sends the FULL current list (this method
  itself is pure/stateless — it re-derives the whole list from `requirements` fresh every call, so there is
  nothing to accidentally send a delta from).

### 15.6 The patch planner — needed NO code change

`master.MergeConfigPatchPlanner.plan`'s own `planSurvivors` was already a GENERIC field-by-field diff of a
merge policy's `survivors[]` array (§14 lot) — it has no idea a survivor entry came from a technical rule, a
source-key rule, or now an LLM-proposed business rule, and does not need to. A business rule that is new
(current config has none for that field) emits exactly one `add_survivor_field` op; a business rule that
changes an already-patched field's chain goes through the existing `survivor_field` chain ops. Proven by
`MergeConfigPatchPlannerTest#businessSurvivorRule_addedAsASingleSurvivorFieldOp` (fed the translator's own real
output on both sides — a `city` `"most frequent"` rule added to an otherwise-identical policy → exactly one op).
