### 15.9 Coordinator follow-up, 2026-09-22 18:20 — two fixes before merge

**Fix 1 — `divergingAfterFoldCount` measured the wrong thing.** Ran live on `Companies_Master/Master/"Company"`:
as this lot's own `MatchPlanLlmSuggester` called it for `city` (grouping key = `city`'s OWN fold key `cityKey`,
counted field = raw `city`), the statement answered **32 of 33** — read by the prompt/evidence as "city diverges
in 32 of 33 shared groups". That is circular: grouping by a folded key and then counting how often the RAW text
still differs measures spelling noise (`"Paris"` vs `"PARIS"`), not disagreement — folding is exactly what makes
that noise irrelevant. The real question groups by the ENTITY's OWN identity key instead (`nameKey`, the field
`Company`'s own matching plan actually blocks/anchors on) and counts distinct FOLDED values of `city` (`cityKey`)
inside each shared group: on the same data, that answers **0 of 33** — every pair the entity already treats as
confidently the same company also agrees on the folded city.

Split into two honestly-named, separately-computed statistics:

- `CrossSystemMeasures.cosmeticVariantGroupsCount` (was `divergingAfterFoldCount`, same SQL shape, renamed) -
  groups by the ATTRIBUTE's own folded key, counts distinct RAW values. Denominator: `sharedCount` on that same
  key (`AttributeInfo#sharedFoldGroupCount`).
- `CrossSystemMeasures.divergingGroupsCount` (new) - groups by the ENTITY's own identity key
  (`EntityInfo#identityKeyField`), counts distinct FOLDED values of the attribute under test. Denominator:
  `sharedCount` on the identity key (`EntityInfo#sharedIdentityGroupCount`). Never computed at all when the
  entity has no identity key yet (see below) - the prompt then states "not measured - no identity key yet"
  rather than a fabricated or degenerate number.

`EntityInfo#identityKeyField` (new) is read by `ebx.MatchPlanLlmSuggester#entityIdentityKeyField`: the entity's
OWN prior `MatchPlan.requirements.clusteringFields[0]` (the primary blocking field a plan already declares -
typically a derived key like `nameKey`), or null for a brand-new entity with no prior plan, or one whose plan
proposed no clustering field at all. **Deliberately no fallback to the attribute's own key when the entity has
none** - grouping and counting the SAME column is tautologically always 0, which is worse than an honest "not
measured": a reviewer or the model could read a guaranteed-zero as "checked, found nothing", when nothing was
actually checked. `master.MatchPlanLlmPass.userPrompt`/`systemPrompt` were both rewritten to explain the
distinction (never call cosmetic variation "divergence") and to say so explicitly when genuine divergence could
not be measured. The exact SQL text of both statements is unit-tested in `CrossSystemMeasuresTest`
(`cosmeticVariantGroupsSql`/`divergingGroupsSql`, split out purely as testable string builders) - the live
32/33 vs. 0/33 NUMBERS themselves were the coordinator's own measurement, not reproduced by a test here.

**Fix 2 — section 4 now reads a REAL `MatchSurvivorshipBlock.Input`.** `ebx.ProposalReviews
.attachSurvivorshipInputs(Adaptation, Session, projectId, lines)` (new, called from `ebx.ui
.ProposalReviewUserService.write` - the one call site among several `ProposalReviews.lines(...)` callers that
actually renders the page and therefore the only one with a live `Session` to spend on it) builds, per `MATCH`
line:

- **Source cards** - `TrustedSourceRanking.order(MatchingConfigurator.readTrustedSources(...))` (the SAME read
  `matching/configure` itself uses) for rank/code/description, plus `CrossSystemMeasures.rowCountsBySystem` for
  each source's record count - ONE query per DISTINCT entity (cached by entity name across every line of that
  entity), not per line, and skipped entirely (record counts stay null, cards still render) when the project has
  no `MASTER_DATASPACE`/`MASTER_DATASET` set yet or the master dataset cannot be opened.
- **Source-key field names** - `MatchingConfigurator.readSourceKeyFieldNames` (made package-visible, not
  `private`, for exactly this reuse - never a second copy of the structural detection the trusted-sources lot
  already built).
- **Derived matching-key fields** - `MatchPlanLlmSuggester.readDerivedFromByName` (same reuse rule, same
  package-visibility change).
- **Per-attribute per-system fill rates** - deliberately NOT recomputed here. `review.MatchSurvivorshipBlock`
  already reads them back from each line's own `MatchPlan.evidence` (`MatchPlanFieldEvidence#filledBySystem`,
  persisted at PROPOSAL time by `master.MatchPlanLlmPass#mergeSurvivorshipEvidence` - see §15.4) - exactly the
  "persist once, read back at render time, never a SQL call per page view" split the task brief asked for.

`ReviewLine` gained an additive `survivorshipInput` field (`MatchSurvivorshipBlock.Input`, null until attached)
and a `withSurvivorshipInput` wither, the SAME "attach after the fact, from a separate live read" convention
`withMatchExtras` (reviewComment/message) already established - chosen specifically so this fix touches neither
`ProposalReviews.lines`'s own long-standing `readMatchPlans` reader nor its equally long `ReviewLine` constructor
call. `review.ReviewPage.renderMatchExpandedRow` now passes `pLine.survivorshipInput` instead of always
defaulting through `MatchPlanView.Input`'s own null-degrades-to-`emptyInput()` constructor path - a line the new
attach step has not reached (or could not resolve an entity for) still degrades exactly the same way as before
this fix, never a crash.

`MatchSurvivorshipBlock`/its three value classes (`Input`, `SourceCard`, `DerivedKeyField`) had to become
`public` (were package-private) so `ebx.ProposalReviews`, outside the `review` package, can construct them -
`render`/`emptyInput` themselves stay package-private, only `review.MatchPlanView` (same package) ever calls
those.

**What section 4 renders now, exactly:**

- **A plan WITH survivorship evidence** (the LLM pass proposed at least one field-specific rule, or considered
  the entity and left evidence behind either way): source cards with real rank/code/description/record count,
  the two fixed sentences, one row per proposed business rule with real per-system fill bars (from evidence) and
  the rationale/confidence, the four technical rows (now naming the entity's REAL source-key field(s) in the
  combined row, e.g. `sourceId · supplierId · _loadId`), and one row per REAL derived-key field (e.g. `cityKey`
  "follows city").
- **A plan with SOME evidence but no field-specific rule proposed** (the model considered survivorship and chose
  not to propose anything - or a plan from between the review-match-plan and survivorship lots, which has
  matching-side evidence but nothing survivorship-specific): same source cards/sentences/technical rows, plus
  "No field-specific survivorship rule proposed for this plan." under the table.
- **A plan with NO evidence at all** (predates even the review-match-plan lot, `MatchPlan.evidence` never
  written): same source cards/sentences/technical rows (these are read from live EBX state and the entity's own
  requirements, not from evidence, so they still show up), plus "Measures not available for this plan - it
  predates survivorship proposals; re-propose it to get them." instead of the generic empty-state line -
  `review.MatchSurvivorshipBlock` distinguishes the two cases by whether the parsed evidence list is empty.
  **Not a perfect signal** (see the block's own inline comment): a plan run between the two lots also reads as
  "considered" here even though survivorship itself never ran for it - the only signal actually available
  without a schema change.

**What is still unverified after this follow-up** (in addition to everything already listed in §15.8):

- Neither fix was run against a live instance THIS session - the coordinator's own 18:20 measurement (32/33,
  0/33) is quoted from their report, not reproduced by a live call in this worktree; `attachSurvivorshipInputs`'
  own live reads (`rowCountsBySystem`, `readSourceKeyFieldNames`, `readDerivedFromByName` against a real
  project) were never exercised either - only unit-tested with hand-built fixtures.
- `entityIdentityKeyField`'s own read (`MatchPlan.requirements.clusteringFields[0]` of the entity's PRIOR plan)
  assumes the first clustering field is always the entity's real identity signal - true for every plan this
  codebase's own translator builds (`clusteringFields` is ordered with the primary blocking field first, `docs/
  MATCHING.md` §3's own field-order union), but never independently confirmed against a plan a person hand-edited
  to list clustering fields in some other order.
- `tools/test_local.sh` is green (`CrossSystemMeasuresTest` extended for the two new SQL builders; `EntityInfo
  .identityKeyField` added to `MatchPlanLlmPassTest`'s reflection allow-list; `MatchSurvivorshipBlockTest`
  extended for the two empty-state messages) - no new EBX-bound test exists for `attachSurvivorshipInputs` itself
  (it has no pure logic to unit-test in isolation; a full exercise needs a live project).

### 15.10 Coordinator fix, 2026-09-22 21:36 (agent run 29, project Companies) - the 18:20 fix above read the WRONG field

**The 18:20 fix's own "unverified" bullet just above was the actual bug.** `entityIdentityKeyField` read
`MatchPlan.requirements.clusteringFields[0]` on the theory that the first clustering field is always the
entity's real identity signal. On `Company` that field is `country` - a BLOCKING/clustering field (candidate
pairs are only compared when they share a bucket on it), never an identity signal. Measured live on run 29:
`CrossSystemMeasures.divergingGroupsCount`, grouped by `country`, answered a HUGE number for `name` (many
different `nameKey` values naturally share one country - that is not remotely "divergence") and exactly **0**
for `country` itself (a field can never disagree with its own grouping key - that is tautological, not a
finding). The LLM pass then wrote, verbatim, into its own survivorship rationale: `name` needed a "most
frequent" rule "due to the high genuine divergence after folding", and `country` needed a "most trusted source"
rule because it showed "no divergence" - both sentences are artefacts of grouping by the wrong field, not real
measurements, and both would have been shipped into a real merge policy if not caught.

**The fix:** `ebx.MatchPlanLlmSuggester#entityIdentityKeyField` no longer reads `clusteringFields` at all. The
entity's identity key is now its own MATCHING key, chosen in this order, never falling back to a clustering
field at any step:

1. the derived key (`<attr>Key`, `StagingAttribute.derivation = FOLD_KEY`) of the field the prior plan's
   decision tree compares with a non-exact (fuzzy) algorithm - the plan's fuzzy ANCHOR (`name` -> `nameKey` for
   `Company`) - skipping a candidate that is itself a derived key (`MatchPlanLlmPass.deriveRole`'s
   `ROLE_MATCH_KEY`) or a `REFERENCE` attribute (a foreign key is never this entity's own identity);
2. else the first of the entity's own accepted attributes (staging order) that has a derived key at all, whether
   or not the prior plan even proposes a fuzzy tier for it;
3. else, if the prior plan's `root` node is a single-field `ALL_FIELDS` node using the exact algorithm (a real,
   validated single-field identifier, e.g. a registration number), that field itself;
4. else `null` - "this entity has no identity key yet" (the branch that already existed; unchanged). An entity
   with a raw, un-folded identity and a single source - `Contact`'s `firstName`/`lastName` in this project - is
   the ordinary case this covers: it is never even reached in practice (single-source entities skip the
   identity-key computation entirely, `multiSource` gate in `toLlmEntity`), but the pure rule itself also
   answers `null` for it directly (no plan, no derived key, no exact identifier).

Split into a thin EBX-reading wrapper (`entityIdentityKeyField`) and a pure decision
(`MatchPlanLlmSuggester.chooseIdentityKeyField`, package-private, unit-tested without an `Adaptation`) - the same
split `filterToEntity` already established for the `?entity=` filter (§4.2.1).

**Re-measured the same day, live SQL, with the corrected key** (`nameKey`, 33 groups shared across ERP/CRM):
`cityKey` diverges in 0 of them (genuinely no disagreement, once folded); the raw `city` spelling differs in 32
of 33 (cosmetic only, `cosmeticVariantGroupsCount`). These are the SAME numbers the 18:20 fix already reported -
they were only ever right because `nameKey` happened to also be `clusteringFields[0]` on that one plan; the
fix makes them right by construction rather than by that coincidence. `CrossSystemMeasures.divergingGroupsCount`
and `cosmeticVariantGroupsCount` themselves are UNCHANGED (they group by whatever key they are given) - only
what the caller passes as the grouping key changed.

**The prompt sentence was also rewritten to be unambiguous about what was grouped**, so the model cannot read a
blocking-key artefact as divergence again even if a future bug reintroduces a wrong key: instead of "genuine
divergence after folding (grouped by this entity's own identity key 'nameKey'): 0 of 33 shared identity
group(s)", `MatchPlanLlmPass.userPrompt` now says "among the 33 group(s) of records sharing the same 'nameKey'
across systems, the folded 'city' value differs in 0 of them" - naming the grouping key, the population it
produced, and the attribute actually being compared, in that order, in one sentence. The "not measured" branch
also dropped its now-inaccurate "no prior clustering field" reason in favour of naming the three real
preconditions (no fuzzy matching key, no attribute with a derived key, no prior exact single-field identifier).

**Tests** (`MatchPlanLlmSuggesterIdentityKeyTest`, new, package `ebx`): the four-step precedence in isolation
(anchor's derived key wins; never falls back to a clustering field even when one is present and would otherwise
look plausible; falls back to the first attribute with a derived key when there is no fuzzy anchor; falls back
to a prior exact single-field identifier when there is no derived key anywhere; the exact-identifier fallback
refuses a multi-field root; the anchor search skips a `REFERENCE` field and a field that is itself a derived
key; a `Contact`-shaped entity with no prior plan and no derived key answers `null`; blank/unparsable
requirements degrade to `null`, never throw), a regression fixture reproducing run 29's own Company plan
(`clusteringFields: ["country"]`, fuzzy anchor `name` with derived `nameKey`) asserting the resolved key is
`nameKey`, and the two prompt-sentence shapes (identity key present; identity key absent). `tools/test_local.sh`
is green. **Not run against a live instance this session** - the run-29 numbers/rationale are quoted from the
task brief, not reproduced by a live call in this worktree; the live SQL re-measurement (`nameKey`, 0/33
diverging, 32/33 cosmetic) is likewise quoted, not reproduced here.

### 15.11 Coordinator fix, 2026-09-22 22:50 (branch `fix/survivorship-source-codes-and-clustering-keys`, agent run 30, project Companies) - a trusted-source override carried a LABEL, not a code

**Measured live, `matching/suggest-llm`, agent run 30, 22:43.** The LLM answered, for `legalForm` and `vatNo`:
`{"function":"most trusted source","trustedSourceList":["ERP - Snowflake - analytics (demo)"]}` - that string is
the wizard's own source DESCRIPTION, while the code the master rows actually carry in `sourceSystem` (and that
`set_trusted_sources` expects in `trustedSourceList`) is `ERP`. `MatchPlanLlmPass.Session#buildSurvivorship`
copied it into `MatchPlan.requirements.survivorship` unvalidated (confirmed in the stored plan). Had this reached
acceptance, `MatchingPolicyTranslator` would have pushed it as `trustedSources.fieldTrustedSources[{field:
"/legalForm", trustedSourceList:["ERP - Snowflake - analytics (demo)"]}]`, and `set_trusted_sources`' own
contract ("any referenced code is auto-created if it doesn't exist") would have created a PHANTOM trusted source
in the instance-wide catalogue.

**Root cause: the prompt could not be told apart.** §15.1's own listing (`MatchPlanLlmPass.userPrompt`) rendered
each source as `"1. ERP - ERP - Snowflake - analytics (demo)"` (`rank. code - description`) - two hyphen-joined
segments with nothing marking which one is the code the model must echo back.

**Three independent fixes, none of them alone sufficient on its own:**

1. **The prompt** (`MatchPlanLlmPass.userPrompt`) now renders `"1. code \"ERP\" (label: ERP - Snowflake -
   analytics (demo))"` and adds one sentence: "A per-field trustedSourceList entry below MUST be one of these
   CODES, exactly as written between quotes above - never the label shown in parentheses." The SURVIVORSHIP
   guidance paragraph (`systemPrompt`) gained the matching cross-reference at the point it first mentions
   `trustedSourceList`. This is the FIRST line of defence - stopping the mistake at the source is cheaper than
   catching it downstream, and is the only one of the three that helps a plan the model has not proposed yet.
2. **Proposal-time validation** (`MatchPlanLlmPass.Session#buildSurvivorship`/`#resolveTrustedSourceCode`, new).
   `Session` gained an 8th constructor argument, `List<TrustedSourceInfo> pTrustedSources` (the SAME list
   `ebx.MatchPlanLlmSuggester` already builds for `ProjectInfo#trustedSources` - one read, two uses, wired
   through the existing 7-arg constructor with a `null` default = empty list, so every other caller/test keeps
   compiling unchanged). A `trustedSourceList` entry is now resolved against it: an entry equal to a source's
   `code` is kept as-is; one equal to a source's `description` (case-insensitive, trimmed) is mapped to the code,
   with a note ("... is a source's LABEL, not its code - mapped to '...'.") folded into the plan's own
   `Survivorship notes:` rationale (same channel as every other survivorship drop, §15.3); anything else is
   dropped, named (`UNKNOWN_SOURCE_CODE`). If a field's WHOLE override list resolves to nothing, the override is
   dropped entirely (not an empty `trustedSourceList`) and the plain `'most trusted source'` function survives -
   it then falls back to the table's own `tableTrustedSourceList` (§14.3's own contract), never a phantom.
3. **Acceptance-time self-check** (`MatchingPolicyTranslator.extractFieldTrustedSourceOverrides`, signature
   changed: takes the project's ordered `List<TrustedSourceRanking.Source>` and an optional `pDroppedNotes`
   output list). This is the LAST call before `set_trusted_sources` and the genuine backstop for a plan stored
   BEFORE this lot existed (exactly the run-30 case: the live plan already has the bad label on disk) - it
   repeats the identical code-or-description resolution independently (never trusts that `buildSurvivorship`
   already ran), then asserts its own output only ever names a known code
   (`assertEveryFieldTrustedSourceIsKnown`, `IllegalStateException` if not - defensive, should never fire given
   the filtering just above, same "guard a future edit" pattern as `assertMergePolicyWellFormed`).
   `ebx.MatchingConfigurator#configureOne`/`#applySurvivorship` both now collect the translator's drop notes into
   a new `detail.trustedSourceOverrideNotes` array (only when non-empty) - a legacy plan's silent correction is
   now visible in the recorded step detail, not just in a freshly-proposed plan's rationale.

**Also (small, prompt-only):** the SURVIVORSHIP guidance now says a field with zero genuine divergence after
folding gains nothing from `'most frequent'` on a two-record group (a tie of one against one decides nothing) -
prefer `'most trusted source'` or no rule at all. Run 30 proposed `name -> most frequent` with the rationale
"Zero genuine divergence after folding", which is exactly the case this sentence now steers away from. No new
validation - guidance only, the model remains free to propose it.

**Tests** (`MatchingPolicyTranslatorTest`: `extractFieldTrustedSourceOverrides_run30Case_labelMappedToCode`,
`_unknownEntryDropped_knownEntryKept`, `_everyEntryUnknown_overrideDroppedEntirely`, plus the three pre-existing
`extractFieldTrustedSourceOverrides_*` tests updated to the new signature; `MatchPlanSurvivorshipTest`:
`trustedSourceListLabelMappedToCode_run30Case` (the exact run-30 string), `trustedSourceListUnknownEntryDropped`,
`trustedSourceListNoConfiguredSources_allDropped`, plus `trustedSourceListOverridePreserved` updated to declare
real `ERP`/`CRM` sources rather than relying on an unvalidated pass-through). `tools/test_local.sh` is green.
**Not run against a live instance this session** - the run-30 answer is quoted from the task brief's own measured
transcript, not reproduced by a live LLM call in this worktree.

## 16. The decision tree as a binary tree (branch `feature/binary-decision-tree-model`, 2026-09-22)

the product owner, reviewing `docs/mockups/review-match-plan-binary-tree.html`: "C'est parfait." The mockup fixes the
model this section documents - read it first, it is the authoritative source for the shape, the wording, and
the validation rules; this section is the implementation record.

### 16.1 The decision (what changed, and why)

Every matching plan this codebase produced before today represented its decision tree as `requirements.tiers`
- an ORDERED, LINEAR cascade: tier 1's "true" branch is always a terminal leaf (`MATCH`/`SUSPECTED`), its
"false" branch always falls through to tier 2, and so on, the last tier's "false" branch always the final
`NOT_MATCHED`. This is not what the `match-merge` add-on's own `decisionTree` actually is - CLAUDE.md §8/§1's
own note, and `matching_config_schema` itself (measured 2026-09-21/22): a BINARY tree of unbounded depth,
where a node's `trueNode` can itself be another comparison node, not only a leaf. A cascade is simply the
special case where every `trueNode` already is a leaf - real add-on configurations are not always shaped that
way (the mockup's own six-node Company example branches on `onFalse` at N1 into an entirely different subtree,
something `tiers[]` cannot express at all).

This lot replaces the internal/stored representation with `DecisionTreePlan` (`master/DecisionTreePlan.java`)
- a flat `{root, nodes[]}` list mirroring the add-on's own tree exactly, every node naming its own
`onTrue`/`onFalse` branch (another node's `id`, or one of `MATCH`/`SUSPECTED`/`NOT_MATCHED` directly) - and
propagates it through every producer (`MatchPlanRules`, `MatchPlanLlmPass`) and consumer
(`MatchingPolicyTranslator`) of a plan's `requirements`. **Nothing needs to be re-entered**: `DecisionTreePlan
.readFrom` reads either the new `requirements.decisionTree` or a pre-lot `requirements.tiers` transparently
(`fromTiers` converts a cascade into the equivalent flat model), so every existing `MatchPlan` row keeps
working exactly as it always has.

### 16.2 The model (`master/DecisionTreePlan.java`)

- **`Plan`** = `{root, nodes: List<Node>}`. **`Node`** = `{id, function, label?, minimumScore?, minimumMatches?,
  fields: List<FieldRef>, onTrue, onFalse, rationale?}`. **`FieldRef`** = `{field, algorithm, weight?,
  minimumScore?, predicate?, bothNull?, oneNull?, extraParams}` - the stored JSON uses the SHORT names
  `bothNull`/`oneNull` (never the nested add-on shape's `bothNullValueHandling`/`oneNullValueHandling` - that
  renaming happens only at the `toNested`/`fromNested` boundary, exactly the same "internal representation
  stays slash-less/short, the wire boundary renames" discipline `MatchingPolicyTranslator.toFieldPath` already
  established for field paths, §3).
- **Four functions**: `ALL_FIELDS` (every field its own `minimumScore`, default 100), `AT_LEAST_N` (node
  `minimumMatches`, required, ≤ field count), `AVERAGE` (node `minimumScore`, required), `PREDICATE` (every
  field needs its own `predicate` string) - the add-on's own four (`matching_config_schema`'s
  `decisionTree...function.enum`, `CLAUDE.md` §"the add-on's tree shape").
- **Three leaves**: `MATCH`, `SUSPECTED`, `NOT_MATCHED` - a node id may never collide with one of these
  (`validate` reports `NODE_ID_RESERVED` if it does).
- **`validate(Plan[, allowedFunctions, allowedAlgorithms])`** - pure, never throws, always returns EVERY named
  reason it found (never stops at the first): `NO_ROOT`, `NO_NODES`, `TOO_MANY_NODES` (cap `MAX_NODES = 64`,
  INFERRED - a tree beyond this stops being reviewable by a person on one screen), `NODE_MISSING_ID`,
  `NODE_ID_RESERVED`, `DUPLICATE_NODE_ID`, `ROOT_NOT_FOUND`, `UNKNOWN_FUNCTION`, `NODE_HAS_NO_FIELDS`,
  `AVERAGE_MISSING_MINIMUM_SCORE`, `AT_LEAST_N_INVALID_MINIMUM_MATCHES`, `PREDICATE_FIELD_MISSING_PREDICATE`,
  `DISALLOWED_ALGORITHM` (only when `allowedAlgorithms` is non-null), `MISSING_BRANCH`,
  `UNKNOWN_BRANCH_TARGET`, `CYCLE_DETECTED`, `UNREACHABLE_NODE`, `TOO_DEEP` (cap `MAX_DEPTH = 32`).
- **`toNested(Plan)`** builds the add-on's own nested `{name, function, params, fields, trueNode, falseNode}`
  shape recursively - a node's `name` is `label` when given, else auto-generated with the SAME convention the
  pre-lot `MatchingPolicyTranslator.tierLabel` used ("Same X [and Y]" for `ALL_FIELDS`, "Similar X [and Y]" for
  `AVERAGE`, extended here for `AT_LEAST_N`/`PREDICATE`), so a plain cascade's nested output is byte-for-byte
  identical to what the pre-lot code built (regression-pinned, `DecisionTreePlanTest
  #toNested_matchesTheLegacyLabelAndShapeForACascade`). **Deliberately never applies the `autoMerge` forcing**
  (a `MATCH`-terminal leaf is always written `MATCHED`) - that policy decision stays in `MatchingPolicyTranslator`
  (§16.3), which this class stays neutral about on purpose.
- **`fromNested(JsonNode)`** reads ANY add-on tree back - ids `N1..Nn` assigned in PRE-ORDER (root first), a
  leaf's outcome read TOLERANTLY by substring (`"Suspect"`/`"Not Match"`/`"Match"`, the LIVE Companies
  configuration's own display strings, never assumed to be the schema's documented `SUSPECTED`/`NOT_MATCHED`/
  `MATCHED` tokens - checked in the order SUSPECT, then NOT, then MATCH, so "Not Match" is never mistaken for a
  match), an unrecognised `function` string kept as a `PREDICATE` passthrough with a named warning - **never a
  lost node**. Returns `FromNestedResult{plan, warnings}`.
- **`fromTiers`/`toTiersView`** - the backward-compatibility pair (§16.1). `toTiersView` is best-effort: `null`
  (never a lossy guess) for anything that is not, in fact, a plain cascade (a real branch, `AT_LEAST_N`/
  `PREDICATE`, a cycle, an orphan node).
- **`sameStructure(Plan, Plan)`** - ids and node ORDER both ignored: compares the RECURSIVE `toNested`
  rendering of each plan (which carries no ids at all), so a re-proposal that only renumbers/reorders nodes is
  not a real change, while a changed branch/function/field/threshold anywhere is.
- **`compatibilityTiersView(requirements)`** - the one entry point `ebx.MatchPlanSimulationRunner`/
  `ebx.RecordLineageReader` use: the stored `tiers` verbatim when present, else `toTiersView` of
  `decisionTree` when it happens to be a cascade, else an empty array.

### 16.3 The translator (`master/MatchingPolicyTranslator.java`)

`buildMatchingPolicy` now reads `pRequirements` via `DecisionTreePlan.readFrom` (transparently handling either
shape), builds the `matchingPolicy.fields` union by walking `plan.nodes` instead of a `tiers` array, and calls
`DecisionTreePlan.toNested(plan)` for the tree itself - the ONE thing this class still does on top of that
neutral rendering is `forceMatchedLeavesToSuspected`, a small recursive walk that replaces every `MATCHED` leaf
with `SUSPECTED` when `MatchPlan.autoMerge` is false (the exact behaviour `buildNode`'s own `pAutoMerge`
parameter had before this lot - CLAUDE.md §8's "route MATCH outcomes to SUSPECTED"). **A plan that is a plain
cascade emits the identical nested JSON as before this lot** (regression-tested against
`MatchingPolicyTranslatorTest`'s own existing fixtures, all of which build `requirements` with `tiers` directly
and pass unchanged through `DecisionTreePlan.fromTiers`'s fallback). `buildMergePolicy`/survivorship/trusted-
sources are untouched - they never read the decision tree at all.

### 16.4 The LLM pass (`master/MatchPlanLlmPass.java`)

`propose_match_plan`'s tool schema now advertises the FLAT `{root, nodes[]}` shape directly (`buildProposeSchema`):
`function` enum is `ALL_FIELDS`/`AT_LEAST_N`/`AVERAGE` only - **`PREDICATE` is never offered**, and the system
prompt says so explicitly ("Never propose a PREDICATE node... leave that for a person to author by hand"): a
predicate is free-form logic no metadata/profiling number can validate. The prompt explains the binary-tree
model in the mockup's own words (nodes compare fields with a function, two branches `onTrue`/`onFalse` -
"passes"/"does not pass" - each naming another node or one of `MATCH`/`SUSPECTED`/`NOT_MATCHED` directly; a
simple plan is one node whose both branches are leaves; the `MAX_NODES`/`MAX_DEPTH` caps).

**Validation is shape-agnostic by construction**: the per-field guard body (SOURCE_KEY refusal, REFERENCE-role
rules, algorithm allow-list, matching-key substitution, the MATCH-terminal identifier guard,
`CrossSystemFieldGuard`) was extracted into `Session#buildAndAppendNode`, called once per node/tier regardless
of which wire shape produced it - `matchTerminal` (the old "outcome==MATCH" test) is now "either branch of this
node is the `MATCH` leaf", the REFERENCE/AVERAGE-only rule reads `!average || matchTerminal` in place of the old
`!average || outcome==MATCH`. After every node is built, `DecisionTreePlan.validate(plan)` catches anything the
per-field loop cannot (an unknown `onTrue`/`onFalse` target, a cycle, an unreachable node) - refused with every
named reason it found, never a bare "invalid tree".

**`Session#proposeMatchPlan` still ACCEPTS the legacy `tiers[]` wire shape too** (`legacyTiersShape =
!pArguments.has("nodes") && pArguments.has("tiers")`) - a deliberate, documented compatibility floor, not a
second contract: the tool schema never advertises it, no real model is ever expected to send it, and it exists
purely so the several hundred existing `tiers[]`-shaped test fixtures in `MatchPlanLlmPassTest` keep exercising
every guard unchanged (re-deriving them into the new shape would have tested the same guard logic a second
time, at a large diff cost, for no behavioural gain - a judgement call made explicitly under this lot's time
budget, flagged here rather than silently). Every NEWLY created plan, from either wire shape, is stored as
`requirements.decisionTree` - `requirements.tiers` is never written by this pass again.

`sameStructure` now calls `DecisionTreePlan.readFrom`/`sameStructure` for the tree comparison (ids/order
ignored, see §16.2), `clusteringFields`/`survivorship` still compared as plain, order-sensitive JSON equality
exactly as before.

### 16.8 Coordinator follow-up, same day (before merge) — a plan is a TREE, not a DAG

The mockup was first misread as allowing one node to be reached from two different parents (N5 from both N3's
false branch and N4's true branch in the six-node Company example). Re-reading the SVG paths shows the mockup
is in fact a STRICT tree: N3's false branch is its own `NOT_MATCHED` leaf; only N4's true branch reaches N5.
The coordinator settled the underlying design question either way, independently of the misreading: **a node
has exactly one parent, like the add-on's own nested `trueNode`/`falseNode` shape** (which has no way to
reference a node twice at all).

- `DecisionTreePlan.validate` gained a new reason, checked in addition to everything §16.2 already lists:
  **`NODE_SHARED`** — a node id named by more than one `onTrue`/`onFalse` anywhere in the plan, e.g.
  `NODE_SHARED: 'N5' is referenced by N3.onFalse and N4.onTrue - each node must have exactly one parent, like
  the add-on's own nested tree.` Every referencing branch is named, not just the first. A leaf being referenced
  by many nodes is of course still fine (that is the whole point of a leaf) — only a real node id counts.
- `DecisionTreePlan.toNested`'s own recursion-guard (a genuine cycle-prevention stack, not a "visited-once"
  set) is now DEAD CODE for any plan that passed `validate()` — documented as such in its own Javadoc, kept
  only as a defensive backstop for a plan built by hand and never validated. It never "unrolls" a legitimate
  shared subtree into two copies any more, because `NODE_SHARED` makes that input impossible for any plan this
  codebase's own callers can produce.
- `MatchingPolicyTranslator.buildMatchingPolicy` now calls `DecisionTreePlan.validate` itself, right after
  `readFrom`, and throws `IllegalStateException` naming every reason if the plan is not structurally valid —
  the same self-check discipline as its own `assertEveryTreeFieldIsDeclared`/`assertMergePolicyWellFormed`,
  so `toNested` is never reached with an invalid plan from this entry point either (belt and braces alongside
  `MatchPlanLlmPass.Session`'s own `validate()` call before a plan is ever stored).
- `MatchPlanRules.fromTiers` and `DecisionTreePlan.fromNested` both produce a single-parent model BY
  CONSTRUCTION (a cascade's `onFalse` chain never repeats a node; a nested tree has no syntax to name a node
  twice in the first place) — pinned by two new tests, `fromTiers_alwaysProducesASingleParentModel`/
  `fromNested_alwaysProducesASingleParentModel`, each asserting `validate()` reports `ok` on their own output.
- The LLM system prompt and the `propose_match_plan` tool schema's own `nodes` description both now say
  explicitly: "each node id is used as a branch target exactly once... never point two different branches at
  the same node id."
- `DecisionTreePlanTest`'s own six-node mockup fixture is corrected to match the real (strict-tree) mockup
  shape, and a new `validate_nodeShared` test builds a genuinely shared node (two nodes both branching into a
  third) and checks it is refused, naming both referencing branches.

`tools/test_local.sh`: still all green after this follow-up.

### 16.9 Lot 2, 2026-09-22 (`feature/binary-decision-tree-screen`, separate worktree) — the review screens draw the real tree

Lot 1 (above) built the model and left `review/*` on the pre-lot cascade-only compatibility view
(`review.DecisionTreeCompat`) - "reviewer screens not yet rewritten for a general tree". This lot rewrites the
three of them (the diagram, the evidence panel, the simulation panel's path naming) against
`docs/mockups/review-match-plan-binary-tree.html` (the product owner: "C'est parfait" - the same mockup lot 1 already
cites as authoritative for the shape/wording/validation rules; this subsection is lot 2's own implementation
record). No running EBX, no live `match-merge` call, no real language model this session either - proved by
`tools/test_local.sh` (unit tests only, all listed below) and by reading; see 16.9.6 for what that leaves open.

#### 16.9.1 The layout (`review/MatchPlanTreeLayout.java`)

Pure geometry, no SVG/HTML: given a `ReviewDecisionTree.Plan` (16.9.2), a pre-order walk (TRUE branch before
FALSE, matching the mockup's "left = passes" convention) assigns every LEAF OCCURRENCE the next column index
- the same outcome (e.g. `SUSPECTED`) reached from two different parents gets two distinct columns, since each
is its own box in the drawing. A node's own column range is the `[min, max]` of its descendant leaves' columns
(computed bottom-up); its `x` is the MIDPOINT of that range - **never the average of its two children's own
`x`**, which is a materially different number as soon as the two subtrees don't have equal leaf-widths (measured
against the mockup's own `N1`: its two children span 3 and 4 leaf-columns respectively; averaging their centres
would land `x` at 455, not the mockup's own 490). `y` is `depth * ROW_SPACING` for both nodes and leaves alike -
a leaf sits at its parent's depth plus one, so two leaves reached at different depths are drawn on different
rows, exactly like the mockup's own picture (its `N2`-true leaf and its `N4`-false leaf are both drawn one row
below the root even though they come from different branches, while leaves further down the `N4` side sit two
and three rows lower).

**Every one of these numbers is pinned against the mockup's own SVG**, node by node
(`MatchPlanTreeLayoutTest#sixNodeMockup_matchesTheValidatedDrawingExactly`, coordinates read directly off the
mockup file's own `<rect>` elements, offset by the row-0-at-depth-0 convention this class uses - the diagram
adds the clustering-band offset back at render time): `N1` (490, 0), `N2` (210, 110), `N4` (700, 110), `N3`
(280, 220), `N5` (630, 220), `N6` (700, 330), and all seven leaf occurrences (columns 70/210/350/490/630/770/910,
depths 2/3/3/3/4/4/2 in the mockup's own drawing order). A one-node cascade (both branches leaves) collapses to
the pre-lot single-tier picture (`MatchPlanTreeLayoutTest#oneNodeCascade_rendersLikeASingleTier`).

**Folding** (task brief: "beyond 12 leaves, subtrees below depth 2 fold"): when total leaf occurrences exceed
`FOLD_LEAF_THRESHOLD` (12), every INTERNAL node at depth exactly 2 becomes a `foldRoot`; every box in its
subtree (itself included) carries `hiddenGroupId` set to that node's id. Depth 2 alone is enough to catch every
deeper node too, because depth increases by exactly one per edge - any node at depth &ge; 2 has exactly one
ancestor at depth 2 (or IS that ancestor), so there is never more than one fold boundary on any root-to-leaf
path, and a fold never nests inside another fold. **Known, documented simplification**: folding hides CONTENT,
never RESERVED WIDTH - a folded subtree's leaves still occupy their normal columns, so the canvas is sized for
the FULL unfolded tree even while parts of it are collapsed (a one-pass layout that never needs to re-run when a
fold is expanded, at the cost of sometimes leaving blank horizontal space next to a collapsed placeholder - a
fully compacting alternative, a local re-centred layout per collapsed subtree, was out of this lot's budget).
Pinned by two more tests: exactly 12 leaves never folds (`FOLD_LEAF_THRESHOLD` is a strict `>`), 13 leaves folds
the one depth-2 node and hides everything under it, `MatchPlanTreeLayout.subtreeSize` counting exactly what is
hidden.

#### 16.9.2 The shared tree model (`review/ReviewDecisionTree.java`) and diagram (`review/MatchPlanTreeDiagram.java`)

`review/DecisionTreeCompat` (lot 1, cascade-only, `null`/empty for any real branch) is DELETED - grep after this
lot found nothing left depending on it. Its replacement, `ReviewDecisionTree`, reads the SAME flat
`{root, nodes[]}` JSON `master.DecisionTreePlan` writes (`decisionTree`, or a pre-lot `tiers[]` cascade via its
own `fromTiers`) as a REAL tree - `Plan`/`Node`/`Field`, no validation (that stays `master`'s job, already run
before a plan is ever stored), no `toNested`/`fromNested` (this class never talks to the add-on). Deliberately
independent of `master.DecisionTreePlan` - same "review never imports ebx/master, and vice versa is avoided
too" convention `MatchPlanFieldEvidence`'s own Javadoc already documents; `master/DecisionTreePlan.toTiersView`/
`compatibilityTiersView` are removed IN TURN (16.9.5) once nothing calls them either.

`ReviewDecisionTree.engineName(Node)` replicates `DecisionTreePlan.autoLabel`/`toNestedTarget`'s exact English
label algorithm (`label` when set, else `"Same X [and Y]"`/`"Similar X"`/`"At least N of X"`/`"Predicate on X"`)
- this is the ONE piece of add-on-facing behaviour this class deliberately duplicates, because it must produce
the literal string the add-on stores as a `DecisionNode`'s own name, needed to match a real execution path back
to a node (16.9.4).

`MatchPlanTreeDiagram.build` renders: a clustering band (unchanged from the pre-lot diagram) above the tree;
node cards (`{id} - {FUNCTION WORDS}` header, e.g. `N1 - ALL FIELDS MATCH` / `N4 - WEIGHTED AVERAGE >= 80` /
`N6 - AT LEAST 2 OF 3`, a compact one-line field summary, and the node's own `rationale` truncated as a third
line when present - the full per-field detail lives in the DETAIL PANEL, not the compact card); elbow
connectors (`M anchorX,fromY L anchorX,midY L childCx,midY L childCx,toY`, true-branch anchor 50 units left of
the parent's centre, false-branch 50 right - a constant offset that matches the mockup exactly regardless of
node width) labelled `passes`/`does not pass` (or `>= {threshold}`/`< {threshold}` for an `AVERAGE` node); leaf
boxes (green MATCH/amber SUSPECTED/grey NOT_MATCHED, same wording as the pre-lot cascade diagram); and, for
each node, a pre-rendered (mostly hidden) detail panel: a fields table (algorithm, weight/minimum, null
handling), the rationale, and "reached by: {parentId} {branchWord}" (the single immediate parent edge, not the
full path - that is section 3's job, 16.9.4). The root's own card starts selected, its detail panel starts
visible; every other detail panel starts `display:none`.

**`autoMerge` and the `MATCH` leaf, generalized**: a leaf occurrence whose outcome is `MATCH` renders as the
real green box only when `autoMerge` is true; otherwise it renders exactly like `SUSPECTED` (mirrors
`MatchingPolicyTranslator.forceMatchedLeavesToSuspected`, now per LEAF OCCURRENCE rather than per plan, since a
general tree can reach `MATCH` more than once). A single STANDING note ("AUTOMATIC MERGE - disabled for this
plan", the pre-lot annotation's own exact wording) is shown once, above the diagram, whenever `autoMerge` is
false and the plan is not empty - regardless of whether the plan has a `MATCH`-terminal leaf at all, exactly the
pre-lot per-plan (not per-tier) annotation's own behaviour, pinned by both an `autoMerge` true and false test
against the mockup's own six-node tree.

**Selection and folding are pure client-side script** (`MatchPlanTreeDiagram.SCRIPT`, exposed to `ebx.ui` via
`MatchPlanView.treeScript()` since the diagram class itself is package-private): every node card carries
`class="mdmf-tree-node" data-tree-node="<id>"`; clicking one hides every `.mdmf-tree-detail` inside the closest
`.mdmf-tree-diagram` container, shows the one whose `data-tree-detail` matches, and toggles a
`mdmf-tree-node-selected` CSS class for the highlight - scoped per diagram container so several expanded MATCH
lines on one page keep independent selections. A fold placeholder carries `data-tree-fold="<id>"`; its own real
content is pre-rendered inside `<g class="mdmf-tree-real" data-tree-real="<id>" style="display:none">`; clicking
the placeholder reveals that group and hides itself - one-way, no re-collapse (matches the task brief's own "open
on click", nothing asked for a collapse-again). Appended by `ebx.ui.ProposalReviewUserService.pageJs` into the
page's single `addJS_cr` script - CLAUDE.md &sect;9's own rule, never a hand-written `<script>` tag.
`MatchPlanTreeDiagramTest` covers: every node selectable with a pre-rendered detail panel, the root selected by
default, the `autoMerge` true/false leaf/standing-note behaviour, folding on a synthetic 13-leaf cascade (the
one depth-2 node folds, `T1`/`T2` never do), the empty-plan message, and field-name XSS escaping.

#### 16.9.3 The evidence panel (`review/MatchPlanView.java`) - fields from ALL nodes, role wording per node

`comparedFieldNames`/`MatchSimulationBlock.exactFieldNames`/`firstAverageTier` (used by the simulation table's
own columns and family classification) now walk `ReviewDecisionTree.readFrom(...).nodes` in full (union,
pre-order) instead of a cascade-only view - identical output for a plain cascade (which this method already
scanned end to end before this lot), complete for a genuinely branching tree instead of an empty one.

The evidence table's Role column (task brief item 2: "the fields come from ALL nodes (union), with the role
wording per node... a field used in several nodes lists them all") now shows, for every field, one mention per
NODE that actually compares it - `"N1 all fields match"`, `"N4 average, weight 10"`, `"N6 at least 2 of 3"`,
`"N7 predicate"` - joined with `·` when a field is used by more than one node (`MatchPlanView.nodeRoleWords`/
`nodeMentionWords`). A field no node of THIS tree mentions at all (a genuinely `REJECTED` field, or a plan whose
evidence predates node-level tracking) falls back to the pre-lot coarser `ANCHOR_FUZZY`/`SUPPORTING_EXACT`/
`CLUSTERING`/`REJECTED` wording - never blank. `MatchPlanView.unionWithNodeFields` additionally adds one
`NOT_MEASURED` stub row for any field a node compares but the stored `evidence` document never recorded -
applied only when `evidence` is non-empty (a plan with GENUINELY no evidence at all still shows the honest "not
recorded" message, never a table of bare stubs). Pinned by `MatchPlanViewTest#evidence_nodeMentionWordsAndUnionOfMissingFields`
(a two-node tree where `country` is used by both nodes and `name` is missing from the stored evidence entirely).

#### 16.9.4 Simulation path naming (`review/MatchSimulationBlock.java`, `ebx/MatchPlanSimulationRunner.java`)

`SimulationPair` gains `enginePath` (`List<String>`, never null) - `TreeEvaluation.nodeNames` for that specific
pair, wired through by `MatchPlanSimulationRunner` for both probe pairs (available synchronously at
construction) and engine candidates (the SAME shared-mutable-list trick `fieldScores` already used - the pair is
built before `evaluatePair` ever runs, so its `enginePath` field can only be filled by mutating that same list
object afterwards). Every pre-lot call site keeps the 8/10-arg constructors unchanged (`enginePath` defaults to
empty), so every existing fixture in `MatchSimulationBlockTest`/`MatchPlanViewTest` keeps behaving exactly as
before.

`leafWords` tries two sources, in order:

1. **A real `enginePath`** - `MatchSimulationBlock.matchEnginePath` walks it against the plan, matching each
   name to a node's own `ReviewDecisionTree.engineName` (falling back to whichever branch target is itself a
   node, not a leaf, when a name matches neither/both branches unambiguously - a relabelled node, or two
   siblings whose auto-labels happen to collide - and marking the WHOLE path `approximate` when this happens
   even once: "fall back to the node order when labels are ambiguous and say so", task brief item 3). The final
   step's own branch is decided by matching the last visited node's `onTrue`/`onFalse` leaf against the pair's
   REAL verdict category (never guessed). An `AVERAGE` node's own step names its real computed weighted score
   (`"N4 score 93"`), not a generic pass/fail word - matching the mockup's own "chemins" table, which shows the
   pair's actual score at an `AVERAGE` node, not the node's static threshold (that static `>= 80`/`< 80` wording
   stays in the DIAGRAM's own branch labels, section 1, a different, non-per-pair question).
2. **The pre-lot field/score heuristic, generalized from "check every tier independently" into a real WALK of
   the tree** (`MatchSimulationBlock.heuristicWalk`) - at each node, decide the branch the same way the pre-lot
   code decided a tier's own accept/refuse (`ALL_FIELDS`/`AT_LEAST_N` by raw value equality, exactly the pre-lot
   `exactTierAccepted`'s own tolerance for an incomparable field; `AVERAGE` by `weightedAverageScore` against the
   node's own threshold; `PREDICATE` never - free-form logic no comparison can reproduce), then continue into
   whichever node or leaf that branch names. Reproduces the pre-lot cascade behaviour exactly (a single
   accept/refuse decision on a cascade's one tier immediately reaches a leaf). Returns nothing - never a
   misleading "clean" path - the moment either a node's acceptance genuinely cannot be told, or the walk DOES
   reach a leaf that disagrees with the pair's own real verdict (the heuristic guessed a branch the real engine
   did not take).

Neither source produces a path: the honest `review.match.simulate.leaf.unknown` fallback, same as the pre-lot
code's own "nothing to report" case. The four mockup "chemins" examples are all pinned
(`MatchSimulationBlockTest`): example 1 (`BPCE - FR <-> BPCE - FR`, `N1 passes -> N2 passes -> Match`) and
example 2 (`Exemplar Industries FR <-> BE`, `N1 passes -> N2 does not pass -> N3 passes -> Suspect`) via the heuristic
walk (no real `enginePath` needed - both routes never touch `N4`'s null handling, which the heuristic cannot
model); examples 3 (`HSBC Bank <-> HSBC BANK`, VAT empty, `N1 does not pass -> N4 score ... -> N5 passes ->
Suspect`) and 4 (`Bankinter <-> Bankia`, `N1 does not pass -> N4 score ... -> Not a duplicate`, stopping at `N4`,
never reaching `N5`) via a hand-built `enginePath` (the real thing a live `evaluatePair` would have returned) -
examples 3/4 both route through `N1`'s own "empty on one side" null-handling rule, which the field/score
heuristic has no model of at all (it only compares raw values; it does not know a field's `bothNull`/`oneNull`
configuration), so they are deliberately NOT exercised via the heuristic path. A fifth test builds a relabelled
node the engine path cannot match by name and confirms the positional fallback finds the right node anyway and
marks the result `approximate`.

**Borderline detection uses the AVERAGE node actually reached, not always the plan's first one**
(`MatchSimulationBlock.resolveAverageTierForPair`): when a pair carries a real `enginePath`, the AVERAGE node
found while matching it is used for `isBorderline`/the field-cell threshold display; otherwise (no real path -
every pre-lot fixture) falls back to `firstAverageTier` unchanged, so every existing test keeps its old
behaviour. `firstAverageTier`/`exactFieldNames` themselves now walk `ReviewDecisionTree` (pre-order over every
node) instead of the retired `DecisionTreeCompat` cascade view - a plan with two `AVERAGE` nodes at different
points in the tree is now handled correctly for whichever node a specific pair actually reached, something the
pre-lot single-cascade-tier assumption could not represent at all.

`ebx.MatchPlanSimulationRunner.firstExactTierField` (the plan's own identifying-key field, used for
`sameKey`/probe set A) is scoped to the ROOT node's own fields alone - unchanged meaning from "the plan's first
tier" (a cascade's tier 1 IS its root); `comparedFieldNames`/`exactFieldNames` in the same file walk ALL nodes
(union), matching `review.MatchPlanView`/`MatchSimulationBlock`'s own equivalent methods field for field (both
sides re-parse the same JSON independently, same convention as before this lot).

### 16.10 Tree diagram rendering fix (`fix/tree-diagram-labels`, separate worktree, 2026-09-22)

the product owner saw the lot 2 diagram live (Proposal review, expanded MATCH-1, one AVERAGE node) and flagged two
rendering defects visible in his screenshot; this small fix lot addresses both, worktree-isolated from `main`,
proved the same way as lot 2 - no running EBX, `tools/test_local.sh` and reading only.

1. **Branch labels collided with their own connector.** `MatchPlanTreeDiagram.renderConnector`'s label used
   to sit CENTRED on the elbow connector's horizontal run (`labelX = (anchorX + childCx) / 2`) - fine when the
   two ends of that run are far apart, but the AVERAGE node's own `>= 80`/`< 80` labels in the product owner's
   screenshot sit close together, so the centred label landed right on top of a vertical segment. Fixed by
   placing the label BESIDE the connector's own FIRST vertical segment instead: `labelX = anchorX + 8`,
   `labelY` vertically centred on that segment's own span - a position that depends only on the ONE connector
   being drawn, never on how far away its sibling connector's own vertical segment happens to be. A white halo
   (`style="paint-order:stroke;stroke:#fff;stroke-width:4px;stroke-linejoin:round"` on the `<text>` itself, no
   separate `<rect>`) keeps the label legible on the rare case it still crosses a line. `paint-order` is an SVG
   presentation property with broad support (Chromium, Firefox, Safari) but was never verified in an actual
   browser this session (no browser tool used, task constraint) - see the "not verified" list below.
2. **A leaf box was a fixed 120px regardless of its own text.** The SUSPECT leaf's pre-lot English wording,

### 16.11 Coordinator fix, 2026-09-22 22:50 (branch `fix/survivorship-source-codes-and-clustering-keys`, agent run 30, project Companies) - the clustering guard refused a derived key of a tree field

**Measured live, `matching/suggest-llm`, agent run 30, first attempt for `Company`.** The tree compared `name`
fuzzily; the model proposed `clusteringFields: ["city","country","nameKey"]` and was refused: "clustering field
'nameKey' must already be used by one of this plan's own tiers above" (`MatchPlanLlmPass.Session#proposeMatchPlan`,
the clustering loop). The model then DROPPED `nameKey`, losing the best blocking key available (33 shared values
across ERP/CRM, per §15.10's own re-measurement) - a real regression in plan quality, not a false refusal of
something genuinely wrong.

**Why the guard was wrong.** `nameKey` is `name`'s own derived `FOLD_KEY` (`AttributeInfo#derivedFrom` on the
key, `#matchKey` on the source - §9.2). Comparing `name` fuzzily in the tree while BLOCKING on `nameKey` is
exactly the intended pattern - the SAME loop already substitutes the other direction automatically (propose
`city` as a clustering field when the tree names its key `cityKey`, or vice versa when the tree names `city` and
`cityKey` is proposed for blocking - `matchKeySubstitutions`, §9.3). What the guard missed is the specific shape
run 30 hit: the clustering field names the DERIVED KEY DIRECTLY, while the tree instead compares the KEY'S OWN
SOURCE fuzzily - the membership check only ever looked at `fieldsUsedInTiers.contains(fieldName)` (after
substitution) or `.contains(rawFieldName)` (before it), neither of which is `nameKey` when the tree only ever
names `name`.

**The fix** (`MatchPlanLlmPass.Session#proposeMatchPlan`, the clustering loop): a clustering field is now accepted
in any of three forms - (1) itself already compared by the tree (unchanged), (2) the tree's own derived key (the
pre-existing substitution, unchanged), or (3) **new** - the derived key OF a field the tree already compares
(`attribute.derivedFrom != null && fieldsUsedInTiers.contains(attribute.derivedFrom)`, checked against both the
plain tier-field set and the MATCH-tier identifier set `matchTierFields`). A field with NO relation to the tree
at all - not compared, not a derived key of a compared field, not the source of a compared key - is still
refused; the widening only recognises the same matching-key relation the substitution logic already encodes the
other way round, never an arbitrary field. The refusal wording was rewritten to name all three accepted forms
("... must be a field this plan's decision tree already compares, that field's own derived matching key, or the
source field of a matching key the tree compares ... - it names none of these"), replacing the old, now-inaccurate
"must already be used by one of this plan's own tiers above" (a "tiers" reference stale since the binary-tree
lot, §16.1, anyway).

**Tests** (`MatchPlanLlmPassTest`, new): `clusteringFieldNamesTreeFieldOwnDerivedKeyDirectly_accepted_run30Case`
(the exact run-30 shape: tree compares `city` fuzzily, `clusteringFields:["cityKey"]` - accepted, `cityKey`
carried verbatim, `city` in the tree untouched) and `clusteringFieldUnrelatedToTree_stillRefused` (a plain
`region` attribute with no matching-key relation to anything the tree compares - still refused, new wording
checked). The pre-existing `decisionLogicScriptedSequence`'s own "clustering field absent from every tier"
assertion (`country`, genuinely unrelated) was updated to the new wording rather than the old one.
`tools/test_local.sh` is green.

**Not run against a live instance this session** - the run-30 refusal/tool-call transcript is quoted from the
task brief, not reproduced by a live LLM call in this worktree.

## 17. Simulating a proposal: the preview policy (branch `feature/simulation-preview-policy`, 2026-09-22)

**The defect (the product owner, 2026-09-22 19:45) and the decision ("Oui, c'est bien").** On the Proposal review,
"Simulate on 20 pivots" on a PROPOSED (not yet accepted) matching plan used to answer a flat refusal —
`review.match.simulate.notApplied`, "Simulate needs the plan configured on the add-on - accept it first, then
Simulate." — because `MatchingOperations.simulateMatch`/`executeDecisionTree` (§4.4, wrapped in
`ebx.MameMatchingApi`) only ever evaluate a `processCode` the add-on already knows about, and nothing writes
one until `matching/configure` runs on an ACCEPTED plan. Decision: at each Simulate click on a plan that is not
yet APPLIED, the factory writes the PROPOSAL into the add-on as a dedicated **preview policy** — code
`<Entity>__preview` — runs the simulation on it, and leaves it there, inactive; it is rewritten at every click
and removed once the entity is actually accepted.

### 17.1 What is written, and when — `ebx.MatchingPreviewPolicy`

`MatchingPreviewPolicy.ensure(session, factory, projectCode, entityName, plan)` is called from
`ebx.MatchPlanSimulationRunner#simulate` whenever the `MatchPlan` row (looked up fresh by its own row id, never
trusted from a possibly-stale `ReviewLine.status`) is not `APPLIED`. It reads `get_matching_config(table)`
first (with the SAME `dataModel` resolution discipline as `MatchingConfigurator.configureOne` — §2.2, never the
publication name itself) and branches on what it finds. **A table declared under more than one data model
(`Contact`, in this instance's own FastTrack module) genuinely needs this resolution to work** — see §2.2.2/
§2.2.3 for the two real `AMBIGUOUS_TABLE` bugs this exact path exposed live, 2026-09-23 (one right after the
other, on the same deployment), and their fixes (in `master.MameDataModelResolution`, shared by every caller of
it — not specific to this class).

- **Table has NO configuration at all yet** (`CONFIG_NOT_FOUND`) — the only tools that can write anything here
  are the additive `generate_matching_policy`/`generate_merge_policy` (§8: `apply_matching_config` is a
  wholesale REPLACE of an EXISTING list, not a way to create the table's first one). Both are called with the
  preview code (`processCode`/`code` = `<Entity>__preview`, `active: true` — see §17.1.1, this was `active:
  false` before a live refusal corrected it — execution modes forced to MANUAL instead), building the policy
  from the plan's CURRENT `requirements` via `MatchingPolicyTranslator.buildMatchingPolicy`/`buildMergePolicy`
  exactly as `matching/configure` itself would, minus the real code.
- **Table already carries SOME configuration** (a real `<Entity>` policy from a prior accept, a leftover preview
  from an earlier Simulate click, or both) — `apply_matching_config` rewrites `matchingPolicies`/`mergePolicies`
  WHOLESALE: the current lists are read, any existing `<Entity>__preview` entry is dropped from each, the
  freshly-built preview entry is appended, and the WHOLE lists are resent. The real `<Entity>` policy, if one
  exists, is copied over byte-for-byte unchanged — this is the one invariant the task brief calls out
  explicitly ("never touch the real policy's merge link").

Either way the preview matching policy links to the table's EXISTING real merge policy when one exists (the
first `mergePolicies[]` entry whose `code` is not itself a preview code — never assumed to be named after the
entity, though every merge policy `MatchingConfigurator`/`MatchingPolicyTranslator` itself ever writes IS);
only when the table carries no real merge policy at all does `ensure` also generate a second, equally-preview,
merge policy under the SAME `<Entity>__preview` code, purely so the preview matching policy has something to
link to. `tableSettings.defaultMatchingPolicy` is never touched, `trustedSources` is never sent (omitted
sections of `apply_matching_config` are left unchanged per §8's own contract).

Every call is recorded as a `PipelineStep` of the new kind `MATCHING_SIMULATE_PREVIEW` (`tools/build_xsd.py`,
`PipelineStep.step` enum — a static enumeration, §"General debugging heuristics" of `CLAUDE.md`: adding a value
means regenerating the XSD, not hand-editing it), scope = the entity name, same resumable/per-entity bookkeeping
convention every other generator in this module already follows.

**`apply_matching_config`'s exact argument shape — corrected by the coordinator, 2026-09-22 22:10, from the
LIVE tool signature, not guessed.** An earlier revision of this section (and of `ebx.MatchingPreviewPolicy`
itself) assumed a flat `{table, matchingPolicies:[...], mergePolicies:[...]}` argument, by analogy with
`generate_matching_policy`'s own bare `matchingPolicy` argument — wrong. The tool's real parameters, read live:
`table` (required), `config` (required — "The full MameConfig to apply, same shape `get_matching_config`
returns … Nested JSON object or a JSON string encoding it"), an optional `dataModel`, and `businessObject`
(must be omitted — a non-blank value is rejected with `INVALID_PARAMS`). So every call this class makes sends
`{table, config: {matchingPolicies:[...], mergePolicies:[...]}}` — `config` NESTED, `dataModel` (when present,
via the same `MameDataModelResolution` decision as every other call in this class) a SIBLING of `config`, never
inside it. Also per that same live description: `matchingPolicies`/`mergePolicies` must be supplied TOGETHER or
both omitted (this class always supplies both); a `null` for either is `INVALID_PARAMS` — send `[]` to clear
(this class never sends `null`, and never needs to clear both to empty); `tableSettings` is a PARTIAL update and
`trustedSources` members REPLACE when supplied (this class omits both — unaffected); several members
(`useRelationships`, `location`, `workflowOnCreate`/`Update`, `pkFieldMergeFunction`, `builtIn`, and also
`executePurge`/`showMatchType`) are read-only and ignored on input, so copying an existing real policy verbatim
(§17.1's own "copied over byte-for-byte unchanged") is safe even though it carries those fields; "any key the
model does not declare is reported back on the successful result rather than dropped in silence" — logged into
the caller's own `PipelineStep` detail (or the `remove` route's own JSON result) by
`MatchingPreviewPolicy.logIgnoredKeysIfAny`, whose exact candidate field name is itself a guess (never quoted to
this session — see that method's own Javadoc); and applying `apply_matching_config` on an ALREADY-ACTIVATED
table is explicitly allowed. `MatchingPreviewPolicyTest#buildApplyConfigArgs_nestsUnderConfig_noDataModel`/
`_dataModelStaysTopLevel_outsideConfig` pin this exact shape (a pure, EBX-free argument builder,
`MatchingPreviewPolicy.buildApplyConfigArgs`, extracted for that reason).

### 17.1.1 The `active: false` refusal — measured live, 2026-09-22 22:45, and the execution-mode fix

the product owner's first real "Simulate on 20 pivots" against the preview policy this lot originally shipped
(`Company__preview`, `active: false`) answered:

```
Simulation failed: simulateMatch refused (invalid state - matching paused or policy inactive): The Run match
service cannot be executed. Please check the Matching policy configuration.
```

— the exact risk this document's own §17.6 had flagged as unconfirmed. An INACTIVE policy cannot be simulated
at all; `active` must be `true` for `MatchingOperations.simulateMatch`/`executeDecisionTree` to accept it. The
preview is kept harmless the other way instead — through its EXECUTION MODES, `javap` on the add-on's
`com.orchestranetworks.addon.mame.model.config.MatchingPolicy$ExecutionMode` (war `WEB-INF/classes`, static
initializer):

| Constant | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `MANUAL` | 0 |
| `AFTER_SUBMISSION` | 1 |
| `BEFORE_CREATION` | 2 |
| `INLINE_MATCHING` | 3 |

The config XSD field is `matchingExecOnCreation`/`matchingExecOnUpdate` (MCP names `matchingOnCreation`/
`matchingOnUpdate`), `xs:int`, default `0`, enumeration class `ExecuteMatchingOnCreationEnumeration`. The LIVE
real `Company` policy uses `1` (AFTER_SUBMISSION) — and so does `MatchingPolicyTranslator.buildMatchingPolicy`'s
own default, unchanged for the REAL `matching/configure` path. `ebx.MatchingPreviewPolicy.applyPreviewSafetyOverrides`
now writes the preview with `active: true`, `matchingOnCreation: 0`, `matchingOnUpdate: 0` (MANUAL): only an
EXPLICIT run could ever use a MANUAL-mode policy, and `MatchingConfigurator.run` already refuses outright to
launch a real run against anything whose code looks like a preview (`MatchingPreviewPolicy.isPreviewCode`, §17.4)
— so nothing on the table (a save, an update) ever triggers matching against the preview on its own, and no
code path in this factory ever runs one deliberately either. `tableSettings.defaultMatchingPolicy` is still
never touched. Pinned by `MatchingPreviewPolicyTest#applyPreviewSafetyOverrides_activeTrueManualExecutionModes`/
`_overridesAnExistingNonManualValue` (the second fixture starts from `buildMatchingPolicy`'s own real
AFTER_SUBMISSION default, confirming the override actually changes something rather than matching it by luck).

If `simulateMatch`/`executeDecisionTree` ever refuse a preview run again for some OTHER "invalid state" reason,
`ebx.MatchPlanSimulationRunner` now appends the preview's own known-good shape to the add-on's own refusal text
— `"... - preview policy <Entity>__preview: active=true, matchingOnCreation=0 (MANUAL), matchingOnUpdate=0
(MANUAL)"` — so the next diagnosis does not have to re-derive what was actually written.

### 17.2 Removal — `MatchingPreviewPolicy.remove`

Drops `<Entity>__preview` from whichever of `matchingPolicies`/`mergePolicies` actually carries it, again via
`apply_matching_config` (a fresh-table preview leaves BOTH sides under the preview code; a rewritten one may
leave only the matching side if a real merge policy was linked instead). Idempotent: nothing to remove (table
not found, no configuration, or no entry actually named `<Entity>__preview`) is a no-op, never an error.

Two callers: `MatchingConfigurator.configureOne` calls it automatically, best-effort, right after a successful
`markApplied` (a removal failure is recorded in that step's own `detail` and otherwise ignored — it must never
undo an otherwise-successful `configure`, the same "a report-only follow-up never fails the call that matters"
discipline `ebx.MameMatchingApi`'s own `safeDetail`/`safeCompletionRate`/`safeDurationMs` already apply); and
the stand-alone cleanup route `POST /projects/{code}/matching/simulate-preview/remove?entity=<name>`, for the
cases that leaves uncovered (a plan that was simulated and then explicitly rejected instead of accepted, or an
abandoned draft).

### 17.3 The interaction with `matching/configure`'s own ownership check — `isPreviewOnly`

`MatchingConfigurator.configureOne` refuses to overwrite a matching configuration it did not create (§ "Refuses
to overwrite a configuration it did not create") whenever `get_matching_config` finds something and this
project's own `MATCHING_CONFIG` step for the entity has never completed. Before this lot, the very first real
accept of an entity that had ever been simulated pre-acceptance would hit that refusal FOREVER — a leftover
preview policy is "something found", and nothing about writing a preview ever marks the project's own
`MATCHING_CONFIG` step `DONE`. Fixed with `MatchingPreviewPolicy.isPreviewOnly(answer, entityName)`: `true` when
every `matchingPolicies[]`/`mergePolicies[]` entry the answer carries is this entity's own preview code (or the
lists are empty) — a preview-only config is then treated exactly like `CONFIG_NOT_FOUND`, proceeding straight to
generating the REAL policy, never like a stranger's configuration. Unit-tested (`MatchingPreviewPolicyTest`)
against hand-built fixtures: a real policy alongside a preview is correctly NOT preview-only; a preview policy
for a DIFFERENT entity sharing the table is correctly not mistaken for this entity's own.

### 17.4 Readers filtered — grep of every `matchingPolicies[]`/`mergePolicies[]` consumer in this module

- `ebx.MatchingConfigurator.configureOne`'s found/ownership check — filtered via `isPreviewOnly` (§17.3).
- `ebx.MatchingConfigurator.run` — refuses outright (defense in depth, never expected to trigger: `entityName`
  here is always a real `StagingEntity.name` `MasterModel` built, never carrying the `__preview` suffix) if the
  entity name it is about to launch a real matching run against looks like a preview code
  (`MatchingPreviewPolicy.isPreviewCode`).
- `master.MergeConfigPatchPlanner.findMergePolicy` — reviewed, needs NO code change: it matches by EXACT `code`
  equality against the real entity name, and a preview entry's code (`<Entity>__preview`) never equals it by
  construction. Locked down with a regression test (`MergeConfigPatchPlannerTest
  #findMergePolicy_neverMatchesAPreviewEntry`) carrying both a real and a preview entry in the same fixture.
- `master.MatchPlanProfileReader` — reviewed, needs NO code change: it only ever reads `matching_config_schema`'s
  JSON-SCHEMA document (enum vocabularies at fixed dotted paths — algorithms, null-handling, record-selection
  functions), never a stored `matchingPolicies`/`mergePolicies` INSTANCE list keyed by `processCode`/`code`. There
  is nothing for a preview policy to contaminate here.
- `ebx.MatchPlanLlmSuggester`'s own `get_matching_config` probe (line ~349) — reviewed, needs NO code change: it
  only reads the answer to resolve a `dataModel` (via `MameDataModelResolution`), never the policy lists
  themselves. (This file is owned by a concurrent lot, `fix/diverging-identity-key` — not touched here either
  way.)

### 17.5 What the simulation panel now says

`ebx.MatchPlanSimulationRunner#simulate` threads the resolved `processCode` (the real one when `APPLIED`, the
freshly-`ensure`d preview one otherwise) into every `MameMatchingApi.simulate`/`evaluatePair` call it makes —
before this lot every one of those calls passed the bare entity name, silently assuming it was already a
configured policy. `review.MatchPlanView.SimulationResult` now also carries `onPreviewPolicy`/`policyCode`, and
`renderSimulationBlock` prints a one-line header before the numbers: "Simulated on the preview policy
`<Entity>__preview` (proposal, not yet accepted) - written just for this click, never used for a real matching
run." vs. "Simulated on the applied policy - the one actually configured and activated on the add-on." — so a
reviewer never mistakes a preview run for the plan already being live.

The button's own enabled state (`review.match.simulate.disabled.reason`) no longer requires `APPLIED` —
`PROPOSED`/`ACCEPTED`/`APPLIED` all simulate now; only `REJECTED` (or no plan proposed yet) still disables it,
with a reworded default reason ("No matching plan to simulate for this entity - it was explicitly ruled out").
The "add-on not registered on the master model at all" failure class (`TABLE_NOT_FOUND` from `ensure`'s own
`get_matching_config` read) is NOT modelled as a static disabled-button state — detecting it ahead of a click
would need a live call at render time, which this lot deliberately does not add — it surfaces instead as a
click-time failure (`review.match.simulate.failed`, which already carries the descriptive exception message).

## 18. Launching a matching run from EBX Workflow (`MatchingRunTaskBean`, branch `feature/matching-workflow-bean`, 2026-09-22)

Today `matching/run` (§4, `MatchingConfigurator.run`) is only reachable by hand, over REST
(`POST /ebx-mdm-factory/rest/v1/projects/{code}/matching/run?scope=...`, `FactoryResource.runMatching`,
administrators only). This lot adds a **workflow task bean**,
`com.on.ebx.factory.workflow.MatchingRunTaskBean` (`extends com.orchestranetworks.workflow.ScriptTaskBean`),
so the SAME run can also be launched through EBX's own Workflow engine — which unlocks the Workflow REST
API (`POST /ebx-dataservices/rest/workflow/v1/publications/{name}/workflows`, even for a one-step
workflow), the Task Scheduler's built-in `SchedulerWorkflowLaunchTask` (`workflowLauncherName` parameter),
or an EBX Script trigger that launches a workflow publication running this bean as its one step. No new
Java API surface was invented for this: the bean's `executeScript` reproduces `FactoryResource.runMatching`'s
own body exactly, using `ScriptTaskBeanContext.getRepository()`/`getSession()` in place of the REST
resource's session context — no HTTP call, no agent-account credentials, same discipline
`ebx.MameMatchingApi`'s own class Javadoc already states for this module ("Replaces the earlier
REST-loopback design entirely"). `ScriptTaskBean`/`ScriptTaskBeanContext`'s exact method signatures were
re-confirmed live this lot by `javap -p` on `ebx-lib.jar` (matches the task brief's own quote exactly, no
drift). No live EBX access this session (task constraint) — nothing below was exercised against a running
instance or a real workflow model; everything is proved only by `tools/test_local.sh` (the two pure
helpers below) and by the class compiling against the real `ebx-lib.jar` signatures.

### 18.1 Bean properties

Plain private fields with public getter/setter pairs, so a workflow model's `beanParams` can bind them
(§7's own "plain bean property = workflow input/output parameter" convention, `ScriptTaskUpdateRecordStringValue`):

- **`projectCode`** (String, input, required) — the MDM Factory project code. `executeScript` throws an
  `OperationException` naming the missing property if it is `null`/blank, before touching the repository.
- **`scope`** (String, input) — `"all"` (case-insensitive, trimmed) for a full re-match, anything else
  (including `null`/blank) for incremental — mirrors `FactoryResource.runMatching`'s own
  `"all".equalsIgnoreCase(pScope)` exactly. Extracted into a pure static helper, `isScopeAll(String)`,
  unit-tested (`MatchingRunTaskBeanTest`) without any EBX dependency.
- **`maxWaitMs`** (String, input) — parsed to a `long`; `null`, blank, or unparsable all fall back to
  `MatchingConfigurator.DEFAULT_MAX_WAIT_MS` (30000), matching the REST route's own
  `pMaxWaitMs == null ? DEFAULT_MAX_WAIT_MS : pMaxWaitMs.longValue()` fallback, extended to cover a blank/
  garbage string (a `beanParams` value is always a string, never a nullable boxed `Long` the way a REST
  query parameter is). Extracted into a pure static helper, `parseMaxWaitMs(String)`, also unit-tested. No
  range validation, same as the REST route: a negative value is parsed and passed through as-is.
- **`resultJson`** (String, output) — set from `executeScript` to `MatchingConfigurator.run(...).toString()`
  (the same Jackson `ObjectNode` the REST route returns, serialized). Exposed only through a getter,
  following the `ScriptTaskGetRecordValue.value` getter+setter convention (§7) for whoever wires the
  workflow model's output mapping later.

`executeScript` never wraps or swallows `MatchingConfigurator.run`'s own `OperationException` — it
propagates as-is, same as `FactoryResource.runMatching` lets it reach its own `catch` clause unchanged.

### 18.2 No permission check inside the bean, on purpose

Unlike the REST route (`ADMINISTRATOR`-only), the bean itself does not check who is running it — see the
class' own Javadoc. A workflow step's effective caller identity is governed by EBX's own workflow
permissions (who can launch or be allocated the publication this bean is wired into), not by a check
duplicated in Java. Restricting who can launch that publication is the responsibility of whoever builds
the workflow model around this bean.

### 18.3 `module.xml` wiring

`ebx-mdm-factory/src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/ebx/module.xml` gained a top-level `<beans>` element (new to this
module), sibling to `<services>`, in the order `services` → `beans` → `ajaxComponents` per
`module_2.4.xsd`'s own declared sequence (re-checked this lot):

```xml
<beans>
    <bean className="com.on.ebx.factory.workflow.MatchingRunTaskBean" />
</beans>
```
