## 19. `configure` on an existing policy: compare, then rewrite in place (2026-09-22 23:50)

### 19.1 The gap, read in `ebx.MatchingConfigurator.configureOne` after a live sequence, 2026-09-22 23:39

Before this lot, `configure`'s outer loop skipped an entity ENTIRELY the moment its own `MATCHING_CONFIG`
step was already `DONE` (`skippedAlreadyDone`) — `configureOne` was never even called again for it. And
inside `configureOne` itself, whenever `get_matching_config(table)` found a REAL (not preview-only)
configuration, the method treated the call as a pure RESUME: it checked whether THIS project's own last
recorded attempt had already run `generate_matching_policy`/`generate_merge_policy`/`patch_matching_config`
to completion (`priorAttemptCompletedGenerationAndLink`, the 2026-09-22 08:58 fix, §"Idempotence corollary"
in this class' own Javadoc) and, if so, skipped straight to `validate_matching_config`/`activate_matching` —
**never comparing the stored policy against the plan actually being applied.**

Live consequence, 2026-09-22: this morning's plan (a genuine, already-`DONE` `MATCHING_CONFIG` step) had
generated and activated `Company` as AVERAGE ≥80 on `name` (fuzzyFullText, weight 10), `country` (exact,
weight 5), `cityKey` (exact, weight 5), clustering on `country`. the product owner then reviewed the entity again and
accepted a NEW plan — run 31: one AVERAGE ≥80 node on `name` (fuzzyFullText, weight 3) ONLY, `clusteringFields:
["nameKey"]`, survivorship `name` → most trusted source, record selection `lastUpdate`, default field merge
`longest`. Calling `matching/configure` again for `Company` would have hit the outer `skippedAlreadyDone`
short-circuit and never even reached `configureOne` — the add-on would have kept serving the MORNING's policy
forever while run 31 sat marked `APPLIED` by nothing at all. A narrower version of the same bug would have hit
even if the outer skip were removed: `configureOne`'s old RESUME branch would have found `Company` "already
configured" and jumped straight to validate/activate, again never noticing the accepted plan had changed.

### 19.2 What changed — two levels

1. **`configure`'s outer loop no longer skips an entity because its `MATCHING_CONFIG` step is `DONE`.** It
   always calls `configureOne`, which now returns a `MatchingConfigurator.ConfigureDecision` the loop buckets
   into the response: `GENERATE_FRESH`/`REWRITE` → `configured` (the rewritten case annotated "(policy
   rewritten in place - the accepted plan changed since the last successful configure)"), `RESUME_SAME` →
   `skippedAlreadyDone` (annotated "stored policy already matches the accepted plan"). `REFUSE` never reaches
   the loop as a decision — it is thrown as an `OperationException` exactly as before, landing in `refused`.
2. **`configureOne` itself now COMPARES before resuming.** Whenever `get_matching_config` finds a real,
   OWNED configuration (see §19.3 for what "owned" now means), it always builds the CURRENT accepted plan's
   translation (`MatchingPolicyTranslator.buildMatchingPolicy`/`buildMergePolicy` — exactly the fresh path's
   own calls, now made unconditionally) and structurally compares it against the live stored entry with the
   new `master.MatchingPolicyComparator.compare(...)`. `Diff.same()` → `RESUME_SAME` (validate/activate only,
   no write at all). Otherwise → `REWRITE`: `master.MatchingConfigRewriteBuilder.build(...)` builds the FULL
   desired `matchingPolicies[]`/`mergePolicies[]` arrays and a single `apply_matching_config` call rewrites the
   entity's own two entries in place — never a second `generate_matching_policy`/`generate_merge_policy` call
   for a `processCode` that already has a real, live configuration (never measured what a duplicate `processCode`
   answers there, and there is no need to find out: `apply_matching_config` is exactly the tool built for a
   desired-state rewrite, CLAUDE.md §8).

The decision itself is a small, pure, independently-tested function, `MatchingConfigurator.decideConfigureAction
(found, previewOnly, ownsExistingConfig, storedMatchesDesired)`:

```
!found || previewOnly              -> GENERATE_FRESH
found && !previewOnly && !owns     -> REFUSE
found && !previewOnly && owns:
    storedMatchesDesired == true   -> RESUME_SAME
    storedMatchesDesired == false  -> REWRITE
```

### 19.3 Ownership — unchanged in spirit, widened in practice

The refusal itself ("refusing to overwrite a configuration this generator did not create") is UNCHANGED in
philosophy from `master.MasterResetEligibility`'s own rule: a real, non-preview configuration this project
never finished configuring — **ever, not just on the most recent attempt** — is still someone else's, and
`configureOne` still refuses outright rather than guess. What changed is that ownership is now established
by EITHER of two signals, `owns = isDoneStep || priorAttemptOwnership`:

- `isDoneStep` — `PipelineSteps.isDone(project, MATCHING_CONFIG, entity)` finds ANY past `DONE` row, not only
  the immediately-preceding attempt. This is the NEW signal this lot adds — it is what lets a plan accepted
  AFTER a genuinely successful prior configure still be recognised as "ours to rewrite."
- `priorAttemptOwnership` — the pre-existing `priorAttemptCompletedGenerationAndLink` check on the most
  recently recorded step detail (a `FAILED` attempt that had already run generate+generate+patch to
  completion before failing later, e.g. at the old validate-shape bug, §"Idempotence corollary"). Kept
  unchanged, still useful on its own for an entity whose FIRST-ever attempt failed partway through.

A preview-only config (§17.3, `MatchingPreviewPolicy.isPreviewOnly`) is still treated exactly like
`CONFIG_NOT_FOUND` regardless of ownership — `decideConfigureAction`'s first branch checks `previewOnly`
before `owns` is ever consulted.

### 19.4 What is compared, and what is deliberately left alone — `master.MatchingPolicyComparator`

Pure Jackson, no EBX class, no MCP call — takes the stored `matchingPolicies[]`/`mergePolicies[]` entries
(read from the SAME `get_matching_config` answer `configureOne` already fetched — no second read) and the
freshly-translated desired objects, and reports a `Diff` with five independent booleans:

- **`decisionTreeChanged`** — the nested `decisionTree` shape, compared STRUCTURALLY via a generic `normalize`
  that (a) drops any `null`-valued key so a `null` and an ABSENT key never register as a difference, and (b)
  drops an INTERNAL decision node's own `name` (a cosmetic display label — `DecisionTreePlan.Node#label`/
  `#autoLabel`, never read by the matching engine) while KEEPING a LEAF's `name` (the real outcome, `MATCHED`/
  `SUSPECTED`/`NOT_MATCHED` — a leaf is told apart from an internal node the same way `DecisionTreePlan`
  itself does: its own `function` is always explicit `null`).
- **`candidateFieldsChanged`** — `matchingPolicies[].fields[]`, compared as a SET keyed by `field` path (order
  never matters here), each entry canonicalised to `{weight, searchStrategy, bothNullValueHandling,
  oneNullValueHandling}` with `MatchingPolicyTranslator`'s own defaults backfilled.
- **`mergePolicyCodeChanged`** — the matching policy's own `mergePolicyCode` link, read against the CALLER-
  supplied desired code (by convention the entity name itself — never read off the translator's own matching-
  policy object, which does not carry that key at all; only `patch_matching_config`'s `set_merge_policy_link`
  op sets it, on the fresh path).
- **`mergeChainsChanged`** — `recordSelectionFunctionChain`/`defaultFieldMergeFunctionChain`, ORDER-SENSITIVE
  (a chain's own fallback semantics assign priority to position).
- **`survivorsChanged`** — `survivors[]`, compared as a SET keyed by `field` path (order across fields does
  not matter — a stored answer may list them differently than the translator builds them in) but
  order-SENSITIVE within one field's own `mergeFunctionChain`.

Deliberately NOT compared, per the task brief's own scope: `active`, `matchingOnCreation`/
`matchingOnUpdate`, `executePurge`, `showMatchType`, `matchAgainstMergedRecords`, any `workflowOn*` key, and
on the merge policy `mode`/`useForManualMerge`/`applyPermission`/`relatedTables` — operational/admin settings
a data steward may have tuned live, never something a plan translation should silently clobber — plus the
whole `trustedSources`/`tableSettings` surface, the survivorship route's own exclusive concern (§14.6).

**Measured against the exact live pair above** (`MatchingPolicyComparatorTest#compare_liveRun31Pair_...`,
both sides built through the REAL `MatchingPolicyTranslator`, never hand-typed JSON pretending to be its
output): `decisionTreeChanged`, `candidateFieldsChanged`, `mergeChainsChanged` (record selection `mostCompleted`
→ `lastUpdate`, both behind `mostTrustedSource`) and `survivorsChanged` (run 31 adds a `name` survivor rule the
morning's policy never had) all report `true`; `mergePolicyCodeChanged` reports `false` (both link to `Company`
either way) — `Diff.same()` is `false`, exactly the REWRITE case. A second test re-translates the SAME
requirements twice and confirms `Diff.same()` is `true`.

**Best-effort, like every other "shape read from a live answer" class in this module**: the fixture above was
never captured from a real `get_matching_config` call this session (write tools forbidden either way) — a live
answer could in principle echo additional keys `normalize` would then treat as significant, reading as
"differs" even when nothing meaningful changed. Whoever first runs this against a real instance should verify
a genuinely unmodified round trip (re-`configure` a plan with no changes) reports `RESUME_SAME` before trusting
a `REWRITE` decision against a live table.

### 19.5 The rewrite itself — `master.MatchingConfigRewriteBuilder`

Mirrors `ebx.MatchingPreviewPolicy#ensureRewrite`'s own pattern exactly (CLAUDE.md §8: `apply_matching_config`
is a wholesale REPLACE of `matchingPolicies`/`mergePolicies`, never a partial patch): read the current lists,
drop the entity's own STALE entry and any leftover `<Entity>__preview` entry from EACH list, add the freshly
-rewritten entries back, resend the WHOLE lists — every OTHER entry on the table (a different entity, a stray
policy) is copied over VERBATIM.

The rewritten matching-policy entry is built by **deep-copying the STORED entry, then overwriting only
`decisionTree`, `fields`, `mergePolicyCode`** — every other key the stored entry carries (`processCode`,
`active`, `matchingOnCreation`/`matchingOnUpdate`, `executePurge`, `showMatchType`,
`matchAgainstMergedRecords`, any `workflowOn*` key, and anything else present) survives BY CONSTRUCTION, never
by re-asserting a literal "fields to keep" list that could drift from a future schema addition. Same discipline
for the merge policy: deep-copy the stored entry, overwrite only `recordSelectionFunctionChain`,
`defaultFieldMergeFunctionChain`, `survivors` — `code`, `mode`, `useForManualMerge`, `applyPermission`,
`relatedTables` (and anything else) survive untouched. `trustedSources`/`tableSettings` are never part of this
payload at all — the survivorship route (`set_trusted_sources` + `master.MergeConfigPatchPlanner`'s own op
list) stays the only writer of the table-level trusted-source ranking, unchanged by a plan rewrite.

**The exact `apply_matching_config` payload the live Company case above would send** (schematically — see
`MatchingConfigRewriteBuilderTest` for the fixture-level proof of the keep/replace split):

```json
{
  "table": "/root/Company",
  "config": {
    "matchingPolicies": [
      { "...every other entity's entry, untouched...": "..." },
      {
        "processCode": "Company",
        "active": true, "matchingOnCreation": 1, "matchingOnUpdate": 1,
        "executePurge": "MANUAL", "showMatchType": false, "matchAgainstMergedRecords": false,
        "mergePolicyCode": "Company",
        "decisionTree": { "...run 31's one-node AVERAGE tree over /name only...": "..." },
        "fields": [ { "field": "/nameKey", "weight": 1, "...": "..." }, { "field": "/name", "weight": 3, "...": "..." } ]
      }
    ],
    "mergePolicies": [
      { "...every other entity's entry, untouched...": "..." },
      {
        "code": "Company", "mode": "ONLY_DUPLICATES", "useForManualMerge": true, "applyPermission": false,
        "relatedTables": [ "...kept exactly as stored, e.g. CrossRefCompanies/Roles/...": "..." ],
        "recordSelectionFunctionChain": [ { "function": "mame.addon.reference.data.recordSelectionPolicy.mostTrustedSource.label" }, { "function": "mame.addon.reference.data.recordSelectionPolicy.lastUpdate.label" } ],
        "defaultFieldMergeFunctionChain": [ { "function": "most trusted source" }, { "function": "longest" } ],
        "survivors": [
          { "field": "/sourceSystem", "mergeFunctionChain": [ { "function": "constant", "constantValue": "MDM" } ] },
          { "field": "/sourceId", "mergeFunctionChain": [ { "function": "no merge" } ] },
          { "field": "/_loadId", "mergeFunctionChain": [ { "function": "no merge" } ] },
          { "field": "/_receivedAt", "mergeFunctionChain": [ { "function": "max" } ] },
          { "field": "/name", "mergeFunctionChain": [ { "function": "most trusted source" } ] }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

(The `Company__preview` entry, if one existed from an earlier Simulate click on this same entity, is dropped
from both lists in the same write — so the fresh path's own `MatchingPreviewPolicy.remove` call afterwards
becomes a documented no-op, never an error, exactly as it already was for the pre-existing RESUME path.)

### 19.6 Activation is gated on a REWRITE, unchanged on every other path

A REWRITE calls `get_matching_activation_status(table)` first and skips `activate_matching` entirely when it
already reports `ENABLED` — re-activating an already-running configuration is a heavier operation than a plain
policy edit (CLAUDE.md §8's own "Calcite" trigger-reattach note: `activate_matching` resets the schema and
reattaches the matching trigger) and the task brief is explicit about the gate. An unreadable status (transport
failure, soft miss) is treated the same as "not `ENABLED`" and falls back to the pre-2026-09-22 unconditional
`activate_matching` call — the same "never let a report-only check fail the call that matters" discipline
`MameMatchingApi`'s own `safeDetail`/`safeCompletionRate` already apply. `GENERATE_FRESH` and `RESUME_SAME`
both keep the pre-existing unconditional `activate_matching` call — this lot only narrows the ALREADY-heavier
REWRITE path, nothing else.

### 19.7 Never re-runs matching, never touches the metadataset

Rewriting the stored policy/merge chains changes what the NEXT matching run will compute — it does not, by
itself, re-run matching or touch a single existing `RecordMetadata`/`Matched`/`Suspected` row of the table's
own MAME metadataset (§8's own metadataset section). A rewritten `Company` keeps serving its OLD match/suspect
verdicts, computed under the OLD policy, until the product owner explicitly launches `POST /projects/<code>/matching/run`
again. This is deliberate, not an oversight: nothing in this task brief asks for an automatic re-run, and doing
one silently would discard existing suspect/match state the moment ANY plan edit landed, which is exactly the
kind of unscoped side effect §2's own `matching_guide` warning (CLAUDE.md §8) cautions against.

### 19.8 What was NOT run live — read this before trusting any of the above against a real project

No running EBX instance, no live `match-merge` MCP call, this session either (task constraint: work only in
the isolated worktree, prove by unit test and reading, same discipline as every other lot in this document).
Everything above is proved by `tools/test_local.sh` (green, `MatchingPolicyComparatorTest`/
`MatchingConfigRewriteBuilderTest`/`MatchingConfiguratorTest`'s new cases) and by reading the existing,
already-measured shapes this lot reuses (`MatchingPreviewPolicy`'s own `apply_matching_config` argument shape,
§17.1; `get_matching_activation_status`'s own live-measured answer, `docs/MASTER-ZONE.md` §1.1). Specifically
UNVERIFIED: whether a real `get_matching_config` answer's `matchingPolicies[]`/`mergePolicies[]` entries carry
any extra echoed key `MatchingPolicyComparator.normalize` would treat as significant (§19.4's own caveat); and
the whole REWRITE path end to end against a live add-on (the `apply_matching_config` call itself, `validate_
matching_config` on the rewritten shape, and the `get_matching_activation_status`/`activate_matching` gate).
## 19. Simulation per-field scores: making the failure visible (branch `fix/simulation-scores-and-near-miss`, 2026-09-22 23:55)

### 19.1 What was measured live, 2026-09-22 23:38

Proposal review → "Simulate on 20 pivots", `Company`, on the preview policy `Company__preview` (plan run 31
— ONE `AVERAGE ≥ 80` node on `name`, `fuzzyFullText` only, `clusteringFields: ["nameKey"]`): 20 pivots, 32
candidates (12 engine + 20 shared-key probes), 32 Suspect, "2 caught by the fuzzy field(s) alone". **Every
row's NAME cell said "score not exposed by the engine"**, and the leaf-reached column said "N1 score ? →
Suspect (approximate match)" for every row. `kernel.log` had **no line about it at all**: `ebx.MameMatchingApi
.evaluatePair` caught every `RuntimeException` and degraded to `TreeEvaluation.UNAVAILABLE` in total silence,
so there was no way to tell — from the panel or from any log — whether `executeDecisionTree` had thrown, had
answered no `getNodeScores()` entry for the one AVERAGE node, or had answered one under a key this codebase's
own index-based lookup did not consult. The verdicts of all 20 probed pairs DID come back (they were counted),
so `executeDecisionTree` itself answered `getMatchingResult()` correctly — only the per-field score was
missing.

### 19.2 What changed

**`ebx.MameMatchingApi`** (`evaluatePair`/`TreeEvaluation`):

- `TreeEvaluation` gained two fields: `diagnostic` (a `String`, non-null whenever this evaluation has
  something worth reporting) and `failed` (`true` only when the add-on call itself threw). `UNAVAILABLE`
  (never attempted at all — the `MAX_DETAIL_PAIRS` cap, or a probe pair `evaluatePair` was never called for)
  keeps `diagnostic == null`/`failed == false`, now genuinely distinct from an ATTEMPTED call that failed.
- On an exception, the diagnostic is `"<exception class name>: <message> at <up to 5 stack frames>"` — built
  by the new `exceptionDiagnostic`/`topFrames` helpers. `evaluatePair` itself never logs (it runs up to
  `MatchPlanSimulationRunner#MAX_DETAIL_PAIRS` — 60 — times per click; logging per call would spam
  `kernel.log`) — see §19.2 below for where the ONE-per-click log line actually happens.
- On a SUCCESSFUL call, the diagnostic is always populated too — `"getNodeScores() answered N node(s), field
  names: […]; nodeNames: […]"` — whether `fieldScores` ended up empty or not. This is informational, not
  necessarily a problem; `ebx.MatchPlanSimulationRunner` decides whether it is worth surfacing (§19.2 below).
- The success-path body was split out of `evaluatePair` into a new package-private, directly-testable method,
  `buildTreeEvaluation(DecisionTreeExecutionResult)` — the SAME testability split the class already applies to
  `launchScoped`/`buildResult` (class Javadoc): `OperationsFactory.getMatchingOperations(Session)` only
  initializes against a live server, so `evaluatePair`'s own try block can never be exercised end to end
  outside one, but `buildTreeEvaluation` can, against a hand-built fake `DecisionTreeExecutionResult`
  (an interface, confirmed by `javap` on `ebx-addons.jar`, so no mocking library needed — `MameMatchingApiTest`
  now has `FakeExecution`/`FakeDecisionNode`/`FakeScoreField`, the same discipline as the existing
  `FakeProcess`).
- **One-node-tree defensive read** (the live incident's own shape): `buildTreeEvaluation` now special-cases a
  tree with exactly ONE decision node whose `getNodeScores()` answers exactly ONE map entry — that entry is
  used regardless of what its own `Integer` key actually is. With only one node and one entry there is exactly
  one thing the entry could mean, so the pre-lot "key equals node index" assumption (REASONED, NEVER OBSERVED
  LIVE — see the class' own Javadoc) is never even consulted for this common single-AVERAGE-node preview-policy
  shape. For two or more nodes, the index-based lookup is unchanged.

**`ebx.MatchPlanSimulationRunner`** (`simulate`, new helpers):

- `mergeFieldScores` replaces the pre-lot exact-string-match copy of `evaluation.fieldScores` into the pair's
  `scores` map. It matches a raw `FieldScore#field` name to one of the plan's own `comparedFields` by
  NORMALISING both sides first (`matchScoreFieldToPlanField`/`normalizeFieldPath`/`lastPathStep` — strip a
  leading `./` or `/`, then compare the last path step too, case-insensitively) — the pre-lot exact match
  silently dropped a score whenever the add-on's own raw spelling did not happen to equal the plan's.
- The same method decides whether `evaluation.diagnostic` is worth adding to a click-wide aggregation list:
  ALWAYS when the call itself `failed`; otherwise only when at least one of the plan's compared fields is
  neither an exact field nor a FULL-TEXT field (`fullTextFieldNames`/`isFullTextAlgorithm`, the same
  `fuzzyFullText`/`phoneticFullText`/`exactFullText` suffix check `review.MatchSimulationBlock` independently
  computes) and NONE of those fields ended up with a matched score. **A full-text-only plan — the exact live
  incident — never adds a diagnostic this way**: the add-on not exposing a per-field `ScoreField` for a
  full-text algorithm is treated as an expected characteristic (a HYPOTHESIS, never measured live), not a bug.
- At the end of `simulate`, every collected diagnostic is aggregated into ONE `MatchPlanView.ScoreDiagnostics`
  (count of every occurrence + up to 3 distinct messages, first-seen order) and logged to `kernel.log` **exactly
  once per click** — `LoggingCategory.getKernel().warn(...)`, the same category every other class of this
  module uses (CLAUDE.md §9: the module's own category writes nowhere on this instance) — never once per pair.
- `SimulationResult` also now carries `nearMissApplicable` (`false` only when the near-miss probe could not
  even be BUILT — no exact, non-full-text field besides the plan's own identifying key) and `keyFieldName`
  (the resolved identifying key, e.g. `nameKey`), both computed once in `simulate` and threaded through to the
  panel.

**`review.MatchSimulationBlock`/`MatchPlanView`** (rendering):

- A field cell with no score no longer shows the bare "score not exposed by the engine" on every row. It now
  shows a short "n/a", with the REASON in the cell's own `title` attribute: the full-text HYPOTHESIS wording
  (`review.match.simulate.scoreFullText`) when the field is named in `fullTextFieldNames`, the older generic
  "not exposed" wording (`review.match.simulate.scoreNotExposed.reason`) otherwise.
- `MatchPlanView#renderSimulationBlock` shows a new muted line under the panel header,
  `review.match.simulate.scoreDiagnostics`, whenever `SimulationResult#scoreDiagnostics` is non-null — "Per-field
  scores unavailable for N pair(s): message1 | message2 | message3" — the ONE place the actual failure detail
  (an exception, or a field the engine could have scored but didn't) is shown; it is never repeated per row.
- Family 1's empty line now distinguishes "not applicable" (`review.match.simulate.family1.notApplicable` —
  the near-miss probe could not be built at all) from the pre-existing "probed N, found none" wording — a
  plan with no exact supporting field besides the key must never claim a probe ran and found nothing when no
  probe ran at all. The "pairs probed by the factory" card mirrors this
  (`review.match.simulate.card.probed.detail.nearMissNotApplicable`).
- The "not a duplicate" card's detail line names the identifying key explicitly ("N with the same nameKey",
  `review.match.simulate.card.notMatch.detail.namedKey`) when the plan's ONLY exact notion is the derived key
  itself (no other exact-tier field configured) — the pre-lot generic "N with the same exact key" wording is
  kept for a plan that DOES have a separate exact tier.

### 19.3 The three report scenarios, exact diagnostic text

- **(a) An exception** (e.g. the canopy/Lucene `IllegalArgumentException` §7/§8 already documents elsewhere):
  `"java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: field [Linked_Field_State] not found at com.orchestranetworks.addon.mame....SomeClass.someMethod(SomeClass.java:123); ..."`
  (up to 5 frames) — always aggregated into the panel's muted line and `kernel.log`, regardless of the plan's
  own fields.
- **(b) An empty score map** on an otherwise-successful call: `"getNodeScores() answered 0 node(s), field
  names: []; nodeNames: [N1]"` — aggregated ONLY when at least one of the plan's compared fields is neither
  exact nor full-text (i.e. the engine really was expected to score something here).
- **(c) A full-text-only plan** (the live incident's own shape — one AVERAGE node on a `fuzzyFullText` field):
  the SAME empty-score-map diagnostic as (b) is produced by `MameMatchingApi`, but `mergeFieldScores` never
  adds it to the aggregation, because the one field that needed a score (`name`) is full-text. The per-cell
  reason for that field is instead the dedicated `review.match.simulate.scoreFullText` wording — "full-text
  algorithm: no per-field score exposed (hypothesis, never measured live)" — never the generic "not exposed"
  text, and never surfaced in the muted summary line at all.

### 19.4 What is still unverified

- **The `getNodeScores()` `Integer` key semantics remain unmeasured against a live add-on** — the one-node
  special case (§19.2) sidesteps the question for a single-node tree entirely, but a genuinely branching tree
  with two or more AVERAGE nodes still relies on the pre-lot "key equals node position" assumption, reasoned
  from the add-on's own method signatures only (`javap`), never observed. The next live "Simulate" click on a
  plan with two or more scored nodes should be checked against `kernel.log`'s new diagnostic line to confirm
  or refute it.
- **Whether `fuzzyFullText`/`phoneticFullText`/`exactFullText` genuinely never carry a `ScoreField` is a
  HYPOTHESIS, not a measurement** — it is consistent with the one live incident seen so far (a full-text-only
  plan producing an empty `getNodeScores()`), but no plan mixing a full-text field with a real exact/average
  field alongside it in the SAME node was available to confirm the full-text field specifically (as opposed to
  the whole node) is what the add-on skips.
- **None of this lot's code paths were run against a live server this session** (task constraint: no EBX
  access) — proved only by the unit tests in `MameMatchingApiTest`/`MatchPlanSimulationRunnerScoreMatchTest`/
  `MatchSimulationBlockTest`/`MatchPlanViewTest` (`tools/test_local.sh`, all green) and by reading the add-on's
  own interfaces with `javap`. The next live "Simulate" click on `Company__preview` (or any full-text-only
  plan) is the real test of §19.1's fix.

## 20. Keeping Xref.goldenKey fresh (2026-09-23)

`Xref.goldenKey` ("Current golden record") is a CACHED copy of the add-on's `RecordMetadata.goldenId`
(resolved to the golden's own formatted primary key) — §4.4 above already established that `matching/run`
refreshes it via `ebx.GoldenKeyRefresher`/`master.GoldenKeyRefreshDecision` once a scoped matching process
reports `DONE`, and `ebx.MasterReset` blanks it on reset. Until this lot, nothing else ever touched it: a
steward accepting/rejecting a suspect on the Record lineage screen, or performing an Unmerge/Change-state
through the add-on's OWN standard table-Actions services, left every affected `Xref` row silently stale —
`docs/RECORD-LINEAGE.md`'s own "Suspects and groups"/"Deciding on a suspect" sections already establish that
`acceptSuspectsAndMergeGroups` can merge on the spot, and CLAUDE.md §9 confirms there is no listener/callback
type anywhere in the add-on's public API to react to a table-Actions merge/unmerge. **Branch
`feature/golden-key-freshness`, worktree `ebx-mdm-factory-golden-key`. No EBX instance was reachable that
session (task constraint) — every claim below was proved only by `tools/test_local.sh` (all green) and by
reading the add-on's/EBX's own APIs, nothing run live. Mechanism 2 (self-heal on read) WAS since run live by
the coordinator, 2026-09-23 ~01:00 — it found a real gap, since fixed on branch
`fix/self-heal-isolated-and-xref-columns`; see §20.4.**

### 20.1 Three complementary mechanisms, not one

1. **Scoped refresh right after a suspect decision** (`ebx.RecordLineageReader#decideSuspect`) — after a
   SUCCESSFUL `MameSuspectDecision#accept`/`#reject` (a reject is included too: the add-on's own group
   bookkeeping can change state on either side of a pairwise false-positive decision, so this is never
   gated on `pAccept`), the scope is built by `#suspectDecisionRefreshScope`: the suspect's own key, the
   anchor's own key, and — via the NOW-EXTRACTED `#reverseGoldenIdScan` (the exact `./goldenId=...` reverse
   lookup `#computeMerge` already used inline for a plain lineage read, factored out so both call sites share
   one query) — every other record whose `RecordMetadata.goldenId` now equals EITHER record's own current
   effective golden (`#effectiveGoldenKey`, re-read fresh from `MameRecordState` right after the decision,
   since either side may have just become `MERGED`). `ebx.GoldenKeyRefresher` gained a second entry point,
   `refreshScoped(..., Set<String> masterKeys)`, sharing every read/decide/write line with the original
   `refresh` — only the query's scope differs, via `master.GoldenKeyRefreshScope#xpathPredicate` (pure,
   unit-tested, same `MatchingRunScope#all`-style `(./masterKey='k1' or ./masterKey='k2' or ...)` predicate
   over `Xref.masterKey`, never falling back to an unscoped read when the scope is empty). The outcome is
   reported on `RecordLineageReader.DecisionResult` (new fields `goldenKeyRefreshSet`/`Cleared`/`Unchanged`/
   `Error`, additive — every existing reader of `.success`/`.outcome`/`.detail` is unaffected) — a refresh
   failure is caught, reported on `goldenKeyRefreshError`, and NEVER turns a successful decision into a
   reported failure (same discipline §4.4a already applies to `run`'s own per-entity loop).
2. **Self-heal on every lineage read** (`ebx.RecordLineageReader#read`, right after `#computeMerge`) — `#read`
   already resolves the real truth (`goldenAnchorKey` + `contributingKeys`) for its own field-by-field/journey
   rendering; `#selfHealGoldenKeys` reuses that SAME truth (no second `RecordMetadata` read) to compare every
   contributing key's current `Xref.goldenKey` against it and correct whatever differs, in one `Procedure` —
   pure "which rows differ" decision in `master.GoldenKeySelfHeal#rowsToWrite` (unit-tested: "given a truth and
   a map of current values, which master keys need writing, and to what"). Gated on
   `RecordLineageReader#canReadWrite(pSession, pFactory)` — write access to the FACTORY dataset itself (the
   dataset the `Xref` rows live in), not the master record being examined (that permission already gates
   `merge.group.actions.canAcceptSuspects` elsewhere) — a read-only caller triggers no write attempt at all,
   silently, never a note in the response. Every EBX call in `#selfHealGoldenKeys` is wrapped; a failure is
   logged (`com.orchestranetworks.service.LoggingCategory.getKernel().error(...)`, the same "log, never throw"
   convention `ebx.CapabilityApplier`'s own `LoggingCategoryHolder` already uses) and swallowed — **a read must
   never fail because the heal failed**, and `#read`'s own return value carries no trace of whether a heal ran.
3. **Whole-project refresh, on demand or on schedule, no matching run involved**
   (`ebx.MatchingConfigurator#refreshGoldenKeys(Session, Adaptation, projectCode, entityNameOrBlank)`) —
   loops the promoted entities of the project (or just one, if named) calling the ORIGINAL, unscoped
   `GoldenKeyRefresher#refresh` per entity (never `refreshScoped`: every promoted record of the entity is
   already the intended target, so "scoped" would mean nothing here), with a `PipelineStep`
   (`GOLDEN_KEY_REFRESH`) per entity, same failure discipline as `#run`'s own per-entity loop (an
   `OperationException`/`RuntimeException` ends the step `FAILED` and adds the entity to `refused`, never
   leaves a step `RUNNING`). Exposed two ways, both calling this SAME method so they always agree:
   - `POST /projects/{code}/matching/refresh-golden-keys[?entity=<name>]` (`FactoryResource`, administrators
     only, same shape as every other write route in this module).
   - `com.on.ebx.factory.scheduler.GoldenKeyRefreshScheduledTask` (new package `scheduler`, `extends
     com.orchestranetworks.scheduler.ScheduledTask`) — bean properties `projectCode` (required) and `entity`
     (optional, blank means every promoted entity), a one-line `addExecutionInformation` summary built by the
     pure, unit-tested `#summary` helper from the result's own `refreshed`/`refused` array sizes (never the
     full per-entity JSON — a scheduler execution log is not the place for that).

### 20.2 Registering the scheduled task — no `module.xml` change, unlike the workflow bean

§18 above documents that `MatchingRunTaskBean` (a workflow `scriptTask` bean) genuinely needs a `<beans>`
block in `module.xml`, confirmed live. **A Task Scheduler task is a different registration mechanism
entirely, and needs none of that** (CLAUDE.md §2, "taskScheduler" bullet, and §6's "Registering a schedule"
sub-point): the *task* (the Java class) is registered at RUNTIME as a plain row on
`POST /ebx-dataservices/rest/scheduler/v1/tasks`, body a BARE JSON ARRAY (not the Data Services
`{"rows":[...]}` envelope, and not a single bare object either — confirmed by the coordinator's own live
measurement on a different task registration, 2026-09-21, quoted in CLAUDE.md):

```json
[{
  "key": "GoldenKeyRefresh",
  "classToInstantiate": "com.on.ebx.factory.scheduler.GoldenKeyRefreshScheduledTask",
  "module": "<this module's module.xml name>",
  "recover": false
}]
```

**Never set `userReference` on that row** — the CLAUDE.md-documented trap: the row is stored exactly like a
UI-created one, but every execution then dies inside EBX before `execute` is ever called, with
`ClassCastException: String cannot be cast to UserReference` (`ExecutableTask.createSession`); a `PUT` of the
task without the field is the fix, and the task still gets a real session (it can launch procedures and read
tables, exactly what `#refreshGoldenKeys` needs). The *schedule* (cron `expression`, `taskKey` = the `key`
above, and a `parameters` map whose keys are this class' own bean-property names — `projectCode`, `entity`)
is a separate `POST .../schedules` call, same bare-array body shape. There is no "run now": to test after
registering, `PUT` the schedule with a one-minute cron, then read
`GET /ebx-dataservices/rest/scheduler/v1/executions?taskFilter=<module>|GoldenKeyRefresh` (`report[].
information` carries the `addExecutionInformation` summary text, `#summary` above), then put the real cron
back. None of this was exercised this session (task constraint) — the exact request/response shapes above are
carried over from CLAUDE.md's own prior live measurement of a *different* scheduled task, not re-verified for
this one.

### 20.3 What the product owner must check on BPCE once the instance is back

The 2026-09-22 measurement already on record (`PLAN.md`, "Suspects et groupes" / "décider d'un suspect"
entries): `Companies_Master`/`Master`/`/root/Company`, suspect 248 confirmed into 290's group, golden 322
auto-created, 290/248 both `MERGED` with `goldenId "322"`. None of this lot's three mechanisms were exercised
against that data. Once the instance is back:

1. **Scoped refresh after a decision** — pick a NEW, not-yet-decided suspect pair on a different record, open
   its Record lineage, confirm or reject it, and check the JSON `decideSuspect` produces (or the screen's own
   notice, once the other agent's UI change reads these new fields) carries a non-null
   `goldenKeyRefreshSet`/`Cleared`/`Unchanged` rather than `goldenKeyRefreshError`.
2. **Self-heal on read — the concrete BPCE check the task brief asked for. DONE, 2026-09-23 ~01:00, and it
   found a real defect — see §20.4 for the full account and the fix.** Summary: Unmerge on golden 322 (290/248
   `MERGED` into it) left 290 and 248 `PENDING_APPROVAL` with `goldenId` null. A lineage read of 290 correctly
   computed `goldenKey = "290"` for the SCREEN, but did NOT correct `Xref.goldenKey` (stayed `322`) — because
   `selfHealGoldenKeys` returned early whenever `contributingKeys.size() <= 1`, on the wrong assumption that a
   record isolated NOW can never disagree with its own CACHED value. 322 itself (the DELETED auto-created
   golden) has no `Xref` row of its own, so it was never expected to self-heal anything — confirmed. The
   whole-project route (mechanism 3, item 3 below) did correct all three rows, which is how the gap in
   mechanism 2 was isolated. Fixed on `fix/self-heal-isolated-and-xref-columns` (§20.4); re-run this exact
   check once that branch is deployed to confirm the fix live.
3. **Whole-project refresh route** — `POST /ebx-mdm-factory/rest/v1/projects/Companies/matching/refresh-golden-keys`
   as an administrator; confirm the JSON's `refreshed`/`results.Company.{set,cleared,unchanged}` shape matches
   §20.1 above, and that it requires no matching process to be running or even configured (a project with
   matching activated but no plan `APPLIED` should still refresh cleanly — every row degrades to "no metadata"
   per `GoldenKeyRefreshDecision`'s own existing rule, never an error).
4. **The scheduled task, end to end** — register the task and a one-minute schedule per §20.2, confirm
   `execute` actually runs (an execution row appears, `addExecutionInformation` carries the expected one-line
   summary), and only then decide on a real production cron.

### 19.9 Live run, 2026-09-23 00:25 (PipelineStep 108, main `117e193`) — the path works end to end; one defect fixed

The REWRITE path was exercised live for the first time, on the real `Company` table: `configure` answered
`comparisonResult: "differs: decisionTree, fields (candidate gate), merge policy chains, merge policy
survivors"`, applied the rewrite, `validate_matching_config` passed (two warnings about `/nameKey` being a
candidate-gate field the tree itself never compares — expected, harmless: run 31's own `clusteringFields`
names the blocking key, not a tree field), and `activate_matching` was correctly skipped (`get_matching_
activation_status` already reported `ENABLED`) — confirming §19.6's gate fires as designed. The leftover
preview policy was already gone.

**One defect found**: the survivors actually SENT by the rewrite (`[/sourceSystem constant, /sourceId no
merge, /_loadId no merge, /_receivedAt max, /name most trusted source]`) were missing a `/supplierId` "no
merge" rule — `Company`'s own structurally-detected source-key attribute (`ebx.MatchingConfigurator
#readSourceKeyFieldNames`), which the fresh-configure path and the survivorship route both pass to `Matching
PolicyTranslator#buildMergePolicy`. Traced in `configureOne`: the desired merge policy IS built with `source
KeyFieldNames` (the single, shared call at the top of the method every branch reads from — §19.2), so the
plumbing itself was already correct by inspection; the live gap was not reproduced by re-reading the source.
Fixed defensively rather than left unexplained: `detail.sourceKeyFieldNames` now records the resolved list on
every `configureOne` run, so a future occurrence is diagnosable straight from the `PipelineStep`'s own detail
(an empty list for an entity known to carry a business-key attribute points at `readSourceKeyFieldNames`/
`MatchPlan.entity`, never at the comparator or the rewrite builder). A new end-to-end regression test,
`MatchingConfigRewriteBuilderTest#build_liveCompanyCase_sourceKeySurvivorSurvivesTheRewrite`, builds the
desired merge policy through the REAL translator with `sourceKeyFieldNames = ["supplierId"]` against a stored
fixture whose own survivors never had it (the pre-lot shape) and asserts the rewritten survivors carry a
`/supplierId` "no merge" rule — locking in the exact pipeline this defect report is about. Whether the live
gap's true root cause was a stale deployed build or a genuine runtime condition this session could not
reproduce remains open — the next live `matching/configure` re-run on `Company` should be checked against
`detail.sourceKeyFieldNames` directly.

### 20.4 Self-heal missed an isolated record — measured live 2026-09-23 ~01:00, fixed on `fix/self-heal-isolated-and-xref-columns`

**Facts, measured live by the coordinator** on `Companies`/`Company`, `Companies_Master`/`Master`,
`/root/Company`: golden 322 (auto-created) had merged 290 (ERP) and 248 (CRM). A lineage read of 322 correctly
self-healed both 290's and 248's `Xref.goldenKey` from their stale own keys to `322` (mechanism 2 working as
designed for a multi-key group). the product owner then ran the add-on's own **Unmerge** (Manage group → Actions →
Unmerge on 322). The metadataset afterwards: 290 and 248 `state` `PENDING_APPROVAL` with `goldenId` null
(same `groupId` kept, `isolated: false`), 322 `state` `DELETED` (its business row still exists). A lineage
read of **290** then answered `merge.state = PENDING_APPROVAL`, `goldenKey = "290"`, `sources = ["290"]` for
the SCREEN — but `Xref.goldenKey` of 290 stayed `322`: `#computeMerge` had resolved `contributingKeys =
{"290"}` (a single key — 290 is its own golden again post-unmerge, and nothing else's `RecordMetadata.goldenId`
equals `"290"` yet), and `#selfHealGoldenKeys` returned early on `pContributingKeys.size() <= 1`, on the
Javadoc's own (wrong) reasoning: "an isolated record can never disagree with itself". That reasoning conflated
two different things — `contributingKeys` is the CURRENT truth, freshly resolved from `RecordMetadata` on
every read; `Xref.goldenKey` is a CACHE that does not move on its own when the truth changes on a path with no
hook (CLAUDE.md §9: the add-on's public API has no listener/callback type). An Unmerge is exactly such a path:
it changes `RecordMetadata.goldenId` (hence `contributingKeys`) without touching `Xref` at all, and it can
easily leave a record newly isolated (`contributingKeys` collapsing to size 1) while its `Xref` row still
points at the golden it just left. The whole-project route
(`POST .../matching/refresh-golden-keys?entity=Company`, mechanism 3) fixed it in the same measurement session
(set 4, cleared 0, unchanged 103) — confirming the bug was specific to mechanism 2's shortcut, not to the
underlying decision logic (`master.GoldenKeySelfHeal#rowsToWrite`, unchanged and already correct for a
single-entry map, see the new `singleKeyStaleValue_oneRowWritten` test).

**Fix** (`ebx.RecordLineageReader#selfHealGoldenKeys`): the early return no longer looks at
`contributingKeys.size()` at all — only at whether `pGoldenKey` is blank or `pContributingKeys` is null/empty
(nothing to correct TOWARDS, or nothing resolved to check against). The read-only-session guard
(`canReadWrite`) and the "never fails the read" wrapping are unchanged. The method now always issues the
scoped `Xref` read for every contributing key, single or not — one extra query per lineage read in the
already-common case where a record has never been merged with anything, which is the accepted cost noted in
the task brief.

**The DELETED auto-created golden case, checked explicitly**: looked up directly, an auto-created golden
whose group has since been fully unmerged resolves `contributingKeys = {itself}` too (nothing else's
`goldenId` points at it any more) — but an auto-created golden was never assigned an `Xref` row of its own (it
is not a source record from any load), so the scoped `Xref` read in `#selfHealGoldenKeys` finds nothing for
that key, `currentByMasterKey` arrives at `GoldenKeySelfHeal#rowsToWrite` empty, and the map returned is empty
— nothing is written. Documented and asserted in the pure test rather than measured live directly (a `DELETED`
golden's own lineage read was not separately re-checked after the fix): `GoldenKeySelfHealTest
#singleKeyNoXrefRow_nothingWritten`.

**Tests**: `GoldenKeySelfHealTest` gained `singleKeyStaleValue_oneRowWritten` (a single contributing key whose
cached value disagrees with the truth is still corrected — the exact 290-after-Unmerge shape) and
`singleKeyNoXrefRow_nothingWritten` (a single contributing key with no matching entry in the current-value map
— the DELETED-golden shape — writes nothing). `master.GoldenKeySelfHeal#rowsToWrite`'s own contract did not
change; no existing test needed updating. `tools/test_local.sh` is green.

**What remains unverified**: the fix itself was not re-run against the live instance (the coordinator runs
live checks, not this worktree) — the next Unmerge-then-open-290's-lineage check per §20.3 item 2 should now
find `Xref.goldenKey` corrected to `"290"` immediately, with no whole-project refresh needed.

## 21. Cross-references table breaks at narrow pane width — fixed colgroup removed (2026-09-23)

**Facts, screenshot evidence from the product owner**: at a 757px wide pane, `RecordLineagePage
#renderCrossReferencesPanel`'s table (`.mdmf-xref-table`, `docs/RECORD-LINEAGE.md` "Cross-references
(2026-09-23)") broke down — the "SOURCE SYSTEM" and "SOURCE ID" headers overlapped each other, a source id
wrapped one character per line (`001ZAh` / `RgSiG1j` / `5LYkQ`, read letter by letter down the column), and
the load id wrapped across three lines. Cause: the table was given a hard-coded `<colgroup>` (percentages
11/11/16/18/18/12/14) plus `.mdmf-xref-table{table-layout:fixed}` in `www/common/stylesheets/factory/lineage.
css` — a discipline borrowed from `.mdmf-compare-table`, but for the wrong reason: the compare table needs a
fixed layout because it is actually TWO separate `<table>`s (the main comparison rows and the "Other fields"
rows) that must size identically to stay visually aligned (§ "Fix, 2026-09-22" in `lineage.css`'s own
comment) — the cross-references table has no such sibling, so the fixed percentages were only ever a guess,
and a wrong one under ~800px: the base `.mdmf-table th` rule (`factory.css`) is `white-space:nowrap`, so a
header that did not fit its fixed-width column spilled into the next one instead of wrapping, and
`overflow-wrap:break-word` on a column narrower than one token had no choice but to break inside it,
character by character.

**Fix**: `RecordLineagePage#renderCrossReferencesPanel` no longer emits a `<colgroup>` for this table, and
`.mdmf-xref-table{table-layout:fixed}` was replaced with rules that let the browser size each column from its
own header/content: `.mdmf-xref-table th{white-space:normal}` (headers can wrap onto a second line instead of
overlapping their neighbour), `.mdmf-xref-table td{overflow-wrap:break-word;word-break:break-word}` (a long id
can still wrap when a narrow pane genuinely has no room, but never before that — auto layout gives every
column its natural width first), and `.mdmf-xref-table td:nth-child(2),td:nth-child(3){white-space:nowrap}`
(source id and master record — the two columns that carry an actual key — stay on one line above ~600px,
protected by a `@media (max-width:600px)` rule that lifts the `nowrap` back off on a genuinely narrow/phone
pane rather than forcing the table wider than the viewport). `.mdmf-compare-table`'s own colgroup/fixed-layout
rules are untouched — this fix is scoped to `.mdmf-xref-table` only.

**Tests**: `RecordLineagePageTest` has no assertion on `.mdmf-xref-table`'s `<colgroup>` (only
`.mdmf-compare-table`'s is asserted byte-for-byte, unrelated) and its one `mdmf-xref-table` check (the table is
absent when there are no cross-references) is unaffected. `tools/test_local.sh` is green.

**What remains unverified**: no live/browser check was possible from this worktree (task constraint — the
coordinator does live checks); the 757px overlap/letter-wrap screenshot has not been re-captured against the
fixed CSS.
### 19.10 Root cause found, 2026-09-23 01:20 — a CANONICAL entity's source key lives on its MEMBERS

Read live in `MdmFactory`/`StagingAttribute` (coordinator, 2026-09-23 01:20): `Company` is a CANONICAL entity
(`StagingEntity` id 4, `memberEntities` = [1 `Supplier`, 2 `Account`]); its own attribute `supplierId` (id 58)
carries `businessKey: false`, `primaryKey: null` — the business-key FLAG lives on the MEMBER entities' own
attributes (`Supplier.supplierId`, `Account.accountId`), and `Company.sourceId` (id 71) is the technical key
(`primaryKey: true`). So `ebx.MatchingConfigurator.readSourceKeyFieldNames(pFactory, entityId=4)` — reading
`StagingAttribute` rows of entity 4 ONLY, exactly what §14.4 documents and what §19.9 traced as "already
correct by inspection" — LEGITIMATELY answered `[]`: there never was a divergence between the fresh path and
the rewrite path (§19.9's own trace was right about that), the shared function itself was simply asking the
WRONG entity's attributes for a canonical one. §14.4 needs amending: it describes the LEAF-entity rule only,
which is still correct for a leaf entity, but was never the whole story for a canonical one.

**The shared resolver — `master.SourceKeyResolver`, new this lot.** Pure, no EBX class (same convention as
`MatchingPolicyComparator`/`MatchingConfigRewriteBuilder`): given the entity's own `StagingAttribute` rows
and, for a canonical entity, each member's own `StagingAttribute` rows (keyed by member name, read by `ebx.
MatchingConfigurator.readSourceKeyFieldNames` before calling this class), it resolves the UNION of:

1. the entity's OWN attributes directly flagged `businessKey = true` (the pre-existing leaf rule, §14.4,
   unchanged - still the whole answer for a leaf entity, and defensive here too in case a canonical entity
   ever carries a directly-flagged business key of its own).
2. for each MEMBER, that member's own eligible business-key attribute(s) (resolved the identical leaf way,
   recursively), mapped onto the CANONICAL entity's attribute of the SAME NAME - provided that canonical
   attribute is itself structurally safe to declare a survivor rule on (not the technical primary key, not a
   foreign key, accepted-like; its OWN `businessKey` flag is deliberately NOT required here, since the whole
   point of this mapping is that flag is absent/false on the canonical side).

**Same-name matching is not a fallback of last resort - it is the ONLY mapping this schema supports today.**
Searched before implementing (task brief's own suggestions): `StagingAttribute.fromRelation`/`targetPath`
record how a REFERENCE attribute was deduced from a `LandingRelation` - a different, SAME-entity-only concept,
never a cross-entity unification pointer; `StagingEntity.rationale` carries the LLM's prose ("Unifies Supplier,
Account: ...", `MembershipConsistencyCheck`'s own class Javadoc) at the ENTITY level, never per-attribute; no
other field records which canonical attribute a member's attribute was unified into. A member's business-key
attribute with NO same-named, eligible counterpart on the canonical entity is silently DROPPED from the
result - never guessed at a different name - and every resolution (or drop) is recorded in a human-readable
note (`Result.notes`), which `ebx.MatchingConfigurator`/`ebx.MatchingPreviewPolicy` now surface in their own
`detail.sourceKeyFieldNamesNotes` for exactly this reason: same-name matching is an assumption, not a certainty,
and a future reader of a `PipelineStep`'s detail should see that it was used, not just its result.

**Wired into all three consumers the task brief named, plus one it didn't (fixed as a byproduct - a fourth
call site broke compilation otherwise):**

- `ebx.MatchingConfigurator.configureOne` (the compare-then-rewrite path, §19) and `#applySurvivorship` (the
  survivorship route, §14.6) both now call `readSourceKeyFieldNames(pFactory, entityId, notesOut)` - the SAME
  method, extended in place (own-attribute reading factored into a new private `readSourceKeyAttributeInfo`
  helper, called once for the entity and once per member, then handed to `SourceKeyResolver.resolve`).
- `ebx.MatchingPreviewPolicy#ensureFresh`/`#ensureRewrite` used to hardcode an EMPTY source-key list for the
  preview's own merge policy (`new ArrayList<String>()`, unconditionally) - now call the same shared method
  (the entity id threaded down from `MatchPlan.entity`, exactly how `configureOne` already reads it), so a
  Simulate-click preview never omits a survivor rule the REAL policy would carry once accepted.
- `ebx.ProposalReviews#buildSurvivorshipInput` (the review line's own "Survivance" section 4 display, §15.7) -
  not named in the task brief, but calls the SAME 2-arg method and would not compile against the new 3-arg
  signature; fixed identically (notes discarded here - a read-only display list, never a recorded step).

**The live `Company` result this resolver now gives** (Supplier's own `supplierId`, Account's own `accountId`,
both structurally eligible; `Company` itself carries eligible attributes of the same two names, per the
coordinator's own live read): `readSourceKeyFieldNames` answers `["supplierId", "accountId"]` (own-attribute
scan first, empty; then members in `memberEntities` order, `Supplier` before `Account`), with two notes:
`"'supplierId' resolved as a source key from member entity 'Supplier' (its own business-key attribute of the
same name) - matched by NAME, the only mapping this schema records (no per-attribute unification field
exists)."` and the same for `'accountId'`/`'Account'`. `MatchingPolicyTranslator.buildMergePolicy` then adds
BOTH as `"no merge"` survivors - the rewrite `configure` performs on `Company` next should carry `/supplierId`
AND `/accountId`, not just the one the task brief's own live defect flagged.

**Unit-tested** (`SourceKeyResolverTest`, pure, no EBX class): a leaf entity with an eligible own attribute; a
leaf entity with nothing eligible; the exact live `Company` shape (two members, both keys resolved by name,
two notes both naming the mechanism); a member key with no same-named canonical attribute at all (dropped,
noted); a same-named canonical attribute that is itself ineligible - a foreign key here (dropped, noted); a
canonical entity that ALSO carries its own directly-flagged business key alongside a member-resolved one
(union, no duplicate); and the degenerate case where the own rule and the member mapping agree on the same
name (never double-counted, no redundant note). `MatchingConfigRewriteBuilderTest`'s own live-case test
(§19.9) is unchanged and still passes - it exercises the TRANSLATOR+BUILDER pipeline given an already-resolved
`sourceKeyFieldNames` list, independent of how that list gets resolved.

**What was NOT run live**: same discipline as every other lot in this document (§19.8) - no EBX access this
session, `master.SourceKeyResolver` is proved by `tools/test_local.sh` alone. The live `Company`/`Supplier`/
`Account` shape above is read verbatim from the coordinator's own live report, never independently re-queried
this session.

### 19.11 `MatchingPolicyComparator` had read-back normalisation gaps — found live, 2026-09-23 ~09:30 (PipelineStep 128)

**The false positive.** Another session's `matching/configure` re-ran on the SAME `Company` policy this lot's
00:25 rewrite (§19.9) had already written from the SAME accepted plan — a genuine "nothing changed" case,
where `get_matching_config` should read back BYTE-FOR-BYTE what the translator had emitted. Instead
`comparisonResult` answered `"differs: decisionTree, merge policy chains (recordSelection/defaultFieldMerge),
merge policy related tables"`. The `relatedTables` part was real (the cascade lot, §22, changed how that field
compares in a way this exact table was affected by) — but `decisionTree` and the merge chains should have
compared EQUAL, and did not, because `MatchingPolicyComparator`'s OLD comparison (`sameNormalized` - a plain
recursive null-drop then `JsonNode#equals`) could not tell a genuine plan change from an add-on read-back
artifact. Four gaps, all measured live by the coordinator:

1. **Leaf outcomes come back as DISPLAY strings, never the documented enum tokens.** A live read-back leaf is
   `{"name": "Suspect"/"Not Match"/"Match", "function": null, "fields": [], "params": [], "trueNode": null,
   "falseNode": null}` — this class emits `SUSPECTED`/`NOT_MATCHED`/`MATCHED` (`MatchingPolicyTranslator`'s own
   class Javadoc "a genuine, unresolved discrepancy" had already flagged this asymmetry existed; it had simply
   never been wired into the comparator).
2. **A date-aware chain entry (e.g. the `lastUpdate` record-selection entry) comes back carrying
   `dateFieldPath: "System date"` when this class emitted none at all**, and EVERY OTHER chain entry comes back
   carrying `constantValue: null, dateFieldPath: null` explicitly — independently confirmed the same day by
   `master.MergeConfigPatchPlanner`'s own `normalizedDateFieldPath`/`text` helpers (§14.6, "a fifth, unrelated
   finding" / "a sixth, also caught this round") — the exact same add-on behaviour, found twice, by two
   different lots, the same day.
3. **A node's own `params[]` values come back as JSON NUMBERS** (`80`, `3`) where `DecisionTreePlan#addParam`
   always emits STRINGS (`"80"`, `"3"`) — a plain `JsonNode#equals` sees a `TextNode`/`IntNode` pair as
   different even though they mean the identical threshold.
4. **A node's own `fields[]` (the fields THAT node compares) may come back in a different order**, and a
   `bothNullValueHandling`/`oneNullValueHandling` key equal to its own default (`NOT_MATCH` — `DecisionTreePlan
   #nestedField`'s own fallback, NOT the candidate-gate field's `DO_NOTHING` default) may be OMITTED entirely
   by the read-back rather than echoed explicitly.

**Fix: two new structural comparators replace the generic `normalize`-then-deep-equals for exactly the two
places it was insufficient**, both unit-tested directly:

- `sameDecisionTree` walks the stored/desired trees IN PARALLEL (never independently normalizes then diffs) -
  leaf outcomes through `canonicalLeafOutcome` (tolerant of both forms, item 1 above); a node's own `params[]`
  through `sameParams` (a SET keyed by name, values compared NUMERICALLY when both sides parse as one, item
  3); a node's own `fields[]` through `sameTreeFieldSet` (a SET keyed by field path, order-insensitive, each
  entry's null-handling defaulted to `NOT_MATCH` when absent, item 4). An internal node's own display `name`
  is still dropped entirely (unchanged from before this fix).
- `sameChain` replaces `sameNormalized` for BOTH `recordSelectionFunctionChain`/`defaultFieldMergeFunctionChain`
  and each survivor's own `mergeFunctionChain` (order-SENSITIVE, unchanged - a chain's own fallback semantics
  assign priority to position): each entry is canonicalised by `normalizeChainEntry` first, which backfills
  `dateFieldPath` to `"System date"` whenever it is absent, blank, OR explicitly `null` on EITHER side (item 2)
  and drops `constantValue` the same null-vs-absent way `normalize` already did generically.

`sameNormalized`/`normalize` themselves are UNCHANGED and still used nowhere else needs them removed - kept as
a still-tested, still-useful general-purpose utility (see that method's own updated Javadoc for exactly why it
is no longer sufficient for these two specific comparisons). `sameCandidateFields`/`sameRelatedTables` were NOT
touched — the live gap never implicated them, and they already carry their own default-backfill/order
-insensitivity logic from the original compare-then-rewrite lot (§19.4).

**Regression test built from the exact live shape**: `MatchingPolicyComparatorTest#compare_liveStoredPolicyReadBack_matchesRun31Plan_same`
builds the DESIRED side through the real `MatchingPolicyTranslator` for run 31's own plan (§19.1), then applies
to a deep copy EXACTLY the four read-back mutations above — nothing else — and asserts `Diff.same()` is `true`
(decisionTree, chains, survivors, fields, mergePolicyCode, relatedTables all unchanged). Six more focused tests
cover each tolerance individually (`sameDecisionTree_toleratesDisplayLeafNames`, `..._toleratesNumericParamValues`,
`..._fieldsOrderInsensitive_andNullHandlingDefaultsToNotMatch`, `..._aRealDifferenceIsStillCaught` — proving the
tolerance is narrow, not blanket — and the two `sameChain_*` equivalents).

**What was NOT run live**: this fix itself was never applied against a real instance this session (no EBX
access, same discipline as every other lot) — it is built entirely from the coordinator's own live report and
the independently-confirmed `MergeConfigPatchPlanner` findings (§14.6), reproduced as a hand-built fixture, not
captured whole from one single raw `get_matching_config` answer. The candidate-gate field comparison and the
`relatedTables` alignment (§22) were not implicated by this specific live gap and were left untouched — a
future read-back artifact in either would show the identical symptom (a spurious `differs`) until found the
same way.

## 22. Cascade: related tables aligned automatically (lot 2, 2026-09-23)

Numbered 22, not 21, because a `## 21` section ("Cross-references table breaks at narrow pane width") already
exists at this branch's base commit - this file already carries duplicate `## 13`/`## 14`/`## 19` headings from
concurrent lots landing independently; nothing here is renumbered to "fix" that, per this document's own
established convention. The full design lives in §12.4 above, updated in place for this lot (replacing its
2026-09-22 "leave MANUAL, deferred" note) - this section is the short pointer a reader scanning the table of
contents for "what did lot 2 actually do" should land on first.

**One paragraph**: a merge must cascade - `alignForeignKeys` is set to `AUTOMATIC` on a merge policy's
`relatedTables[]` entry whenever that entry's `path` is a table this project itself promoted as a CHILD entity
of the entity being merged (holds a foreign key to it - `Contact` for `Company`, via the redirected
`accountIdRef`; `MasterModel.Result#childTablePaths`). Every other entry - a table belonging to another
model/project, or a promoted entity that is not THIS entity's own child - is left exactly as stored. Nothing
is ever added to or removed from `relatedTables[]`: the add-on owns that list (`generate_merge_policy` is the
only tool that adds an entry, and no `patch_matching_config` op targets the list at all, confirmed live
2026-09-23 against the real `patchOps` catalogue) - this generator only ever realigns an entry already
present. New pure class `master.RelatedTableAlignment`; wired into `master.MatchingPolicyComparator.compare`
(a new `relatedTablesChanged` `Diff` field, matched by `path`, an entry on only one side never counted as a
difference) and `master.MatchingConfigRewriteBuilder.build` (a new `Set<String> pChildTablePaths` parameter);
`ebx.MatchingConfigurator.configureOne` threads the child paths through both the pre-existing REWRITE branch
and a new follow-up step after `GENERATE_FRESH` (re-read `get_matching_config`, since `generate_merge_policy`'s
own answer does not echo what it just wrote, then one more `apply_matching_config` call only if something
would actually change) - so a first-time configuration cascades exactly like a later re-sync would.

**UNVERIFIED, read before trusting this against a real project** (§12.4 carries the same list, verbatim):
(a) whether the add-on genuinely re-points `Contact.accountIdRef` at merge time once `AUTOMATIC` is set - only
confirmable by merging two real suspect records live and checking the child rows afterwards; (b) whether
`apply_matching_config` accepts a `relatedTables` array with every `name`/`path` unchanged and only the enum
different - expected yes (desired-state contract, CLAUDE.md §8) but never exercised against the real tool for
this specific field; (c) what `NONE` actually does at merge time - undocumented in what this session could
read; never written by this generator either way, so a read-only unknown, not a write-path risk.

Tests: `RelatedTableAlignmentTest` (new, exhaustive - child→AUTOMATIC, foreign table stays MANUAL, `NONE`
stays `NONE` when not a child, empty/null-safe, blank-path-safe, never adds/removes an entry, order and extra
keys preserved), `MatchingPolicyComparatorTest`'s new `sameRelatedTables_*`/
`compare_relatedTablesAlignmentSurfacesAsDiff` cases (including the coordinator-requested "an entry present on
only one side is never a diff, in both directions"), `MatchingConfigRewriteBuilderTest`'s new
`build_cascade_childTableSetToAutomatic_nonChildKeptManual`/`build_cascade_namesAndPathsKeptVerbatim` cases
(the second pinning "every entry's own name/path survive verbatim, only the enum changes"), and
`MasterModelTest`'s new `childTablePaths` coverage (child entity, no children, never-promoted entity, and a
dedicated self-reference-excluded/multiple-edges-from-the-same-child-deduped case built on the existing
Order/Customer/Party fixture). `tools/test_local.sh` green with all of the above.
