## 23. Quality-informed survivorship (lot 1, 2026-09-23)

The gap this lot closes: §14/§15 already let a merge policy prefer a SOURCE for a whole field, and the
2026-09-22 lots gave the LLM per-system FILL rates and fold-key divergence to ground that choice - but nothing
ever told the model, or the merge policy itself, whether a source's OWN values are actually *valid* (pass the
field's own check-digit/reference/pattern rule). A field can be 100% filled and still mostly garbage on one
source. This lot adds that missing dimension end to end: a measure (task A), fed to the LLM (task B), folded
into evidence and the review screen (task C), a new derived-field mechanism that lets the merge policy prefer a
clean value with nothing more than `longest` (task D), and the translator wiring that makes it non-overridable
(task E). No EBX/live MCP access this session - everything below is either read from source, proven by
`tools/test_local.sh` (`all green`; new test classes: `ValidityAggregatorTest`, `ValidValueDerivationTest`,
plus extensions to `DerivedFieldRuleTest`, `CrossSystemMeasuresTest`, `MatchPlanEvidenceTest`,
`MatchPlanLlmPassTest`, `MatchPlanSurvivorshipTest`, `MatchingPolicyTranslatorTest`, `MatchPlanViewTest`,
`MatchSurvivorshipBlockTest`), or explicitly flagged UNVERIFIED below.

### 23.1 Task A - the measure: `quality.ValidityAggregator` + `ebx.CrossSystemMeasures#perSystemValidityCounts`

Split exactly the way the task brief asked: SQL/reads in `CrossSystemMeasures` (EBX-bound), the actual scoring
in a small pure class reusable from two different callers.

- **`quality.ValidityAggregator.aggregate(List<DistinctValue>, List<QualityRuleCheck.Rule>, CleaningSteps.Lookups)`**
  - pure, no EBX class - takes one entry per DISTINCT `(sourceSystem, value)` pair with its own occurrence
  count, runs `QualityRuleCheck.passes` on each value ONCE (never once per row) and weighs the verdict by
  count. A value passes only when it passes EVERY rule given (a field can carry more than one validity rule).
  Returns one `SystemValidity{checked, valid}` per system that contributed at least one non-blank value -
  absent, never zero, for a system that contributed nothing (never a fabricated 0/0).
  - **This is the one method BOTH live callers share**: `CrossSystemMeasures#perSystemValidityCounts` (SQL
  rows off the live MASTER table, feeding the LLM prompt, task B) and `quality.ValidValueDerivation` (sampled
  landing-data rows off the STAGING side, feeding the `*Valid` derived-field proposal, task D) reduce to the
  exact same `DistinctValue{sourceSystem, value, count}` shape before calling it - one scoring rule, two very
  different data sources.
- **`ebx.CrossSystemMeasures#perSystemValidityCounts(pSession, pMasterDataset, pEntityName, pFieldName, pRules, pLookups)`**
  - SQL shape (never a self-join, linear in row count - same discipline `sharedCount`'s own Javadoc
  establishes for this whole class):
    ```sql
    SELECT a."sourceSystem" AS SYS, a."<field>" AS V, COUNT(*) AS N
      FROM "<Entity>" a WHERE a."<field>" IS NOT NULL GROUP BY a."sourceSystem", a."<field>"
    ```
    One row per DISTINCT `(system, value)` pair - fed straight to `ValidityAggregator.aggregate`.
  - **Cap**: `MAX_VALIDITY_DISTINCT_VALUES = 5000` (INFERRED, task brief's own "~5000") - more than that many
    distinct `(system, value)` pairs and the method returns `null` ("not reliable") rather than score a
    partial read, the same "never divide a partial count" discipline `MatchPlanLlmPass`'s own
    `fillRateReliable()`/`EXACT`-provenance convention applies one layer up. **Design decision**: unlike the
    `profile_table_for_matching`-sourced statistics, this class has no `EXACT`/`SAMPLED` provenance tag of its
    own - every method in it already returns `null` on ANY failure (a refused statement, a transport error),
    so "the cap was exceeded" is simply one more reason to return `null`, not a new signal shape. A caller
    that wants to distinguish "not measured" from "measured, cap exceeded" cannot, by design - neither can it
    for any other failure this class already collapses to `null`.
  - Returns `null` when `pRules` is empty/null (nothing to score), either identifier fails `isQuotable`, or
    the query/cap fails - same discipline as every sibling method.
  - `REFERENCE`-kind rules resolve through the SAME `CleaningSteps.Lookups` `ebx.StagingLoader`/
    `ebx.QualitySuggester` already build once per run (`QualitySuggester.buildLookups`) - never a second,
    differently-built lookup table.

### 23.2 Task B - feeding the LLM

`master.MatchPlanLlmPass.AttributeInfo` gained `validCountBySystem`/`checkedCountBySystem` (parallel maps,
the `SystemValidity` split into two - mirrors the existing `fillCountBySystem` shape exactly), a new 25-arg
full-form constructor (every existing caller keeps compiling through the pre-existing convenience overloads).
`ebx.MatchPlanLlmSuggester#toLlmEntity` populates them under the EXACT SAME gate as the pre-existing per-system
fill measurement (`fillCountBySystem != null` - i.e. this attribute was already within
`MAX_SURVIVORSHIP_MEASURED_ATTRIBUTES` and multi-source), AND ONLY when the attribute carries at least one
accepted validity rule (`ebx.StagingLoader#readQualityRules`, made package-visible for this reuse - the SAME
reader `StagingLoader.planRow` itself uses at transfer time, so "carries a validity rule" always means exactly
what actually runs on load). `MatchPlanLlmSuggester#suggest` builds one `CleaningSteps.Lookups` for the whole
run (`QualitySuggester.buildLookups`, notes discarded - this route already surfaces several other note lists,
and a reference-table warning here is no more actionable than the numbers it feeds) and threads it through
`toLlmEntity` as a new parameter.

`master.MatchPlanLlmPass.appendPerSystemValidity` (new, mirrors `appendPerSystemFill` exactly) renders, right
after the per-system fill line:

```
- vatNo (type STRING, maxLength 34), role BUSINESS, fill rate 96.0% [EXACT], ..., per-system fill: ERP 96.0%
  (52), CRM 100.0% (50), per-system validity: ERP 92.3% (48/52), CRM 20.0% (10/50)
```

`systemPrompt()` gained a new paragraph, "QUALITY-INFORMED SURVIVORSHIP", right after the pre-existing
SURVIVORSHIP one: prefer `most trusted source` with a PER-ATTRIBUTE `trustedSourceList` ordered by measured
validity (never the project's overall trust order) when two systems' validity rates differ by at least 10
points with a reasonably-checked count on both; prefer `last update` with `dateFieldPath` naming a real
per-system DATE/TIMESTAMP attribute when one is filled and current; reserve `most frequent` for three or more
systems; cite the actual numbers relied on in the rationale. The 10-point threshold and "reasonably-checked"
wording are prompt GUIDANCE only - never enforced structurally (the model decides the trusted-source order
itself from the raw numbers it is given; `buildSurvivorship`'s own validation, below, never re-derives or
checks that ordering).

### 23.3 `dateFieldPath` validation - closing a gap `docs/MATCHING.md` §15 left open

`MatchPlanLlmPass.Session#buildSurvivorship` never validated a proposed `dateFieldPath` against anything - any
string the model sent reached the wire chain verbatim. Per §14.6 finding 5, the add-on stores the literal
`"System date"` on a date-aware entry created with none; an entry created with a MADE-UP `dateFieldPath` is a
worse outcome than that fallback if the model genuinely meant a real per-system date field. New helper
`Session.isValidDateFieldPath(pDateFieldPath, pEntity)`: accepts the fixed technical field (`/_receivedAt` or
`_receivedAt`, always a real timestamp) or a name resolving to an accepted attribute of the entity whose own
`dataType` is `DATE` or `TIMESTAMP` (this schema has no separate `DATETIME` - `staging.StagingLlmPass
.DATA_TYPES`'s own vocabulary). **Design decision**: an invalid `dateFieldPath` drops only the OVERRIDE
(the chain entry keeps its function, with no `dateFieldPath` at all, falling back to whatever the add-on
itself defaults to), never the whole rule - the same softer posture `buildSurvivorship` already applies to an
invalid `trustedSourceList` entry, rather than the harsher "drop the whole rule" treatment reserved for an
unknown field/function. The drop is named in the plan's own rationale ("Survivorship notes: ..."), never
silent.

### 23.4 Task C - evidence and the review screen

`master.MatchPlanEvidence.Field` gained `validBySystem` (`Map<String, Validity>`, new nested `Validity
{checked, valid}` class, a new 9-arg constructor - every existing caller keeps compiling through the
pre-existing 7-/8-arg overloads) and `toJson` OMITS the key entirely when null (never `{}`) - the same
discipline `filledBySystem` uses the opposite way (always an object, even empty) because `filledBySystem` is
"measured or not for every field with matching evidence" while `validBySystem` is genuinely optional (most
fields carry no validity rule at all). `review.MatchPlanFieldEvidence` mirrors the shape exactly (the review
package's own independent JSON reader, `MatchPlanView.parseEvidence` extended to parse the new key) - same
"JSON is the contract, not a shared Java type" discipline as every other field of this class.

`master.MatchPlanLlmPass.Session#buildSurvivorship` builds a `Map<String, MatchPlanEvidence.Validity>` from
the attribute's own `validCountBySystem`/`checkedCountBySystem` (`toValidityMap`, new) and passes it into
`mergeSurvivorshipEvidence` (extended with a new parameter) - same precedence rule as the pre-existing
`filledBySystem` fold: an EXISTING measurement always wins over a freshly-supplied one (in practice always the
survivorship rule's own, since the matching-side guard never measures validity), kept for consistency.

`review.MatchSurvivorshipBlock#renderWhy` renders a second mini-bar right next to the pre-existing fill one,
"ERP 48/52" style, reusing the `.mdmf-mini-bar` visual with a new `.valid` wrapper class
(`review.css`, amber fill `#dc6803` vs. the default teal, so the two are told apart at a glance) - only when
the field's own evidence carries `validBySystem`. No new message-bundle keys needed (the bar's own text is
system code + raw numbers, exactly like the pre-existing fill bar, which likewise needs none).

### 23.5 Task D - the `*Valid` derived field

Reuses the `FOLD_KEY` derived-attribute mechanism from §9 end to end, never a parallel one:

- **`quality.ValidValueDerivation`** (new, sibling of `CrossSystemFold`): `DERIVATION_VALID_VALUE = "VALID_VALUE"`.
  `propose(List<CrossSystemFold.SystemValues>, List<QualityRuleCheck.Rule>, CleaningSteps.Lookups,
  Detectors.ColumnContext)` - takes `CrossSystemFold.SystemValues` VERBATIM as input (never a second,
  differently-shaped sample type), reduces it to `ValidityAggregator.DistinctValue`s and calls the SAME
  `aggregate` method §23.1 describes. Proposes ONE `"<name>Valid"` attribute when at least one measured system
  has `valid < checked` (validity below 100%) - text-like columns only, same gate every detector in this
  package applies.
  - **Deliberately NOT gated on `attributeMappings.size() >= 2`**, unlike `CrossSystemFold` - a SINGLE-source
    attribute whose one contributing system is only partially valid still benefits from a `*Valid` field (the
    golden record then shows the clean value, or an honest empty, instead of silently keeping an invalid one).
    Design decision, not proven at real project scale.
- **`ebx.QualitySuggester`**: `groupMappingsByAttribute` extracted (was inline in `proposeCrossSystemFolds`) so
  BOTH `proposeCrossSystemFolds` and the new `proposeValidValueDerivations` share one grouping pass over the
  run's accepted mappings, never two. `proposeValidValueDerivations` mirrors `proposeCrossSystemFolds`
  structurally (same accepted-pipeline replay, same SCOPED-`TRANSCODE_REFERENCE` skip with a named
  not-measured note) but reads the attribute's own validity rules FIRST (`StagingLoader.readQualityRules`,
  made package-visible for this reuse too) and skips entirely - never even reading the accepted pipeline -
  when there are none (the overwhelming majority of attributes). `writeDerivedValidValueAttribute` mirrors
  `writeDerivedFoldKeyAttribute` field-for-field (`derivedFrom`, `derivation VALID_VALUE`, `origin RULE`,
  `status PROPOSED`, same idempotence via `validValueAttributeExists` and the SAME `attributeNameExists`
  collision guard - reused verbatim, not duplicated, since a name collision is the same question whatever the
  colliding derivation). `withdrawStaleValidValueAttributes` mirrors `withdrawStaleFoldKeyAttributes`
  identically (measured-this-run gate, WITHDRAW only a still-PROPOSED RULE-origin row, WARN/flag an
  ACCEPTED/APPLIED one, never touch REJECTED or a USER/LLM-origin row). New counters
  (`validValueAttributesProposed/LeftAlone/NameCollision/Withdrawn/FlaggedStale`) and a `validValueNotMeasured`
  note array mirror the `foldKeyAttributes*`/`crossSystemFoldNotMeasured` ones in the `suggest()` response.
- **`staging.DerivedFieldRule`**: `Field` gained `derivation` (defaults to `FOLD_KEY` via the pre-existing
  2-arg constructor, every caller built before this lot keeps compiling) and `validityRules` (empty unless
  `VALID_VALUE`). `apply` gained a `CleaningSteps.Lookups` parameter (needed only by a `REFERENCE`-kind
  validity rule) and now branches per-field on `derivation`: `FOLD_KEY` computes exactly as before
  (`CleaningSteps.foldKey`); `VALID_VALUE` keeps the source value UNCHANGED when it passes every one of
  `validityRules`, or writes `null` otherwise (an empty rule list - defensive, the proposer never creates one
  this way - also yields `null`, never a guessed "valid"). The ONE call site
  (`ebx.StagingLoader.planRow`/`loadFeed`) already had `pLookups` in scope - threaded through with no new
  plumbing. `ebx.StagingLoader#readDerivedFields` reads each derived row's own `derivation` value and, only
  for `VALID_VALUE`, calls `readQualityRules` on the SOURCE attribute id to attach its rules.
- **No `StagingModel`/`StagingModelDiff` change was needed** - a `VALID_VALUE` derived attribute is a plain
  optional `StagingAttribute` row exactly like a `FOLD_KEY` one; both promote to the master table the same
  way, proven by the pre-existing `StagingModelTest`/`StagingModelDiffTest` staying green with no changes to
  either.
- **The proposal goes through the normal review** (`PROPOSED` → a person accepts it in the staging review, or
  `staging/suggest` leaves it be) - exactly like a `FOLD_KEY` proposal, never auto-applied.

### 23.6 Task E - the translator: an explicit, non-overridable survivor

`master.MatchingPolicyTranslator.buildMergePolicy` gained a FOURTH parameter, `pValidValueFieldNames` (a bare
list of `"<name>Valid"` master field names) - threaded the SAME way `pSourceKeyFieldNames` itself was added
(that parameter's own Javadoc precedent), never a second read of `pRequirements`: the caller resolves the list
structurally and hands it in, exactly like the source-key list. New `ebx.MatchingConfigurator
.readValidValueFieldNames(pFactory, pEntityId)` - a single, direct query of THIS entity's own
`StagingAttribute` rows (`derivation = VALID_VALUE`, accepted-like), unlike `readSourceKeyFieldNames`/`master
.SourceKeyResolver` (§19.10) which also follows `memberEntities` for a canonical entity - a `VALID_VALUE`
field's `derivedFrom` is always a foreign key WITHIN the same entity (`staging.DerivedFieldRule`'s own
Javadoc), so there is no canonical/member split to resolve here. Wired into all FOUR existing call sites of
`buildMergePolicy` (`ebx.MatchingConfigurator#configureOne`/`#applySurvivorship`, `ebx.MatchingPreviewPolicy`
twice) - a coordinator note mid-lot flagged that `buildMergePolicy` already reads
`requirements.survivorship.fields[]` itself (§15.5) and that `master.SourceKeyResolver` (§19.10) already
supplies the "no merge" source-key survivors, so this task hooks into that SAME existing read path rather than
adding a second one.

New private `addValidValueSurvivors(pSurvivors, pSeenFieldPaths, pFieldNames)`: one `{field: "/<name>",
mergeFunctionChain: [{function: "longest"}]}` survivor per name, called in `buildMergePolicy` right AFTER the
technical/source-key survivor block and right BEFORE `addBusinessSurvivors` - `addSurvivor`'s own pre-existing
dedupe (`pSeenFieldPaths`) then makes the full precedence automatic: **technical/source-key (always wins) >
`*Valid` field (fixed `longest`, never overridable) > LLM business rule (only ever reaches a field none of the
above already claimed)**. Never a trusted-source step on a `*Valid` field's own chain, and never a second read
of `pRequirements` for this - matches the task brief's own instruction. `:447-448` (the `relatedTables`
comment, owned by another concurrent branch per the task brief) was left untouched; the new call sits well
below it, between the source-key loop and the business-survivor call.

**UNVERIFIED (say so explicitly, per the task brief) - the add-on's own runtime behaviour of `longest` when
every contributing record's value is `null`/empty was never measured live this lot** (no EBX access this
session): reasoned only, from the function's own name and its documented "the least abbreviated value" framing
- an empty string has length zero, so it should never beat a non-empty one, and when EVERY contributing value
is empty the golden record presumably stays empty. Never confirmed against a live `generate_merge_policy`/
real merge run. Equally unverified: whether the add-on's `most trusted source` function, applied to a field
whose most-trusted contributor happens to be empty on THIS group, falls through to a later chain entry the way
`longest` is assumed to behave, or takes the empty value anyway - not tested here because a `*Valid` field's
own survivor chain never uses `most trusted source` in the first place (deliberately - see §23.5), but the
general question is worth flagging for whoever next tunes a chain that DOES mix the two.

### 23.7 Design decisions made without a live instance to check against - a summary

- **The validity measure's cap (5000 distinct `(system, value)` pairs) degrades to `null`, with no
  provenance tag distinguishing "cap exceeded" from any other failure** - a deliberate simplification, since
  every other method of `CrossSystemMeasures` already collapses every failure mode to the same "not measured"
  signal (§23.1).
- **`*Valid` derivation is never gated on multi-source**, unlike `FOLD_KEY` - a single-source attribute with a
  measured validity gap still gets a proposal (§23.5). Reasoned from the field's own purpose (a cleaner golden
  value, not a cross-system reconciliation), never measured against a real single-source project.
- **An invalid `dateFieldPath` drops only the override, keeping the function** (§23.3) - the softer of the two
  precedents this codebase already has (compare the harsher "drop the whole rule" for an unknown field/
  function), chosen because omitting `dateFieldPath` is a graceful, already-handled degradation (the add-on's
  own `"System date"` fallback, §14.6), not a broken rule.
- **`toValidityMap`'s "existing measurement wins" precedence in `mergeSurvivorshipEvidence` is untested by any
  real conflict** (§23.4) - kept only for structural consistency with the pre-existing `filledBySystem` fold;
  in practice a survivorship rule is always the field's first and only source of `validBySystem`, since the
  matching-side guard never measures it.
- **The 10-validity-point / "reasonably-checked" thresholds in the new system-prompt paragraph are prose
  guidance, never structurally enforced** (§23.2) - the model orders `trustedSourceList` itself from the raw
  numbers; `buildSurvivorship` validates the LIST's entries against the project's known sources (pre-existing
  check, unchanged) but never re-derives or checks the ordering against the measured validity numbers.

## 24. The wizard's Matching step shows the decision tree (branch `feature/wizard-match-tree`, 2026-09-23)

Product report, the product owner, on step 6 of the project wizard (screenshot of Contact / Company on
`Companies_Master`): "Cet partie n'a pas été refaite ? Il faut afficher l'arbre ici pour pouvoir prendre une
décision". The card printed `MatchPlan.requirements` verbatim - the LLM's JSON (`{"decisionTree":{"root":"N1",
…`) - under the entity name, while the Proposal review screen had been rendering the same plan as a real
tree, with evidence, simulation and survivorship, since §11/§16. The wizard's inline-reviews lot
(2026-09-23) had ported the three decisions in place but not the body the decision is taken on.

**What changed - one rendering, reused, never a second tree:**

- `review.MatchPlanView` gained `renderTree(Input)` (block 1 alone: the tree diagram with its node-detail
  panel, in its own `mdmf-match-body` grid) and `renderDetails(Input)` (blocks 2 to 4: evidence, simulation,
  survivorship). `render(Input)` is unchanged and equals both. Same markup, same `treeScript()`.
- `wizard.WizardPage.Model` carries, keyed by `MatchPlan` row id, the same `ReviewLine#MATCH` lines the
  review screen builds (`matchLines`), plus `matchCanSimulate`, `matchSimulationResults`,
  `matchMaxSimulationPairs` and `expandedMatchRowIds` - the exact fields `ReviewPage.Input` has.
  `ProjectWizardUserService.model()` fills them exactly as `ProposalReviewUserService.write` does
  (`ProposalReviews.lines` → `attachMatchExtras` → `attachSurvivorshipInputs`), only when the snapshot has
  plans, so the other steps pay nothing; `attachMatchExtras`/`canSimulateMatchPlan` became package-private
  for that.
- `WizardPage.renderMatchPlanBody`: the card shows the one-line summary (`ReviewLine.proposition`, "N tier(s)
  - suspect only"), then - for a plan still awaiting a decision (`PROPOSED`/`SUPERSEDED`) - the tree ALWAYS
  visible, and a native `<details>` fold ("Show details - evidence · simulation · survivorship",
  `wizard.step6.plan.details`) closed by default. A decided plan (`ACCEPTED`/`APPLIED`/`REJECTED`) folds
  everything, tree included (`wizard.step6.plan.detailsWithTree`). The fold of the plan the postback just
  acted on (a decision, Propose another, Simulate) reopens - `lastActedMatchRowId`, the review screen's item C
  rule (§16.10), so several entities stay readable on one page. A plan whose line could not be built (or a
  test fixture) keeps the pre-lot plain text rather than a blank card.
- `SIMULATE` is now a wizard action too (`simulateMatch`, same gate and same
  `MatchPlanSimulationRunner.simulate` call as `ProposalReviewUserService.simulateOne`, same activation-refusal
  wording); its result stays on the service instance. `wizard.js` shows the progress toast for it
  (`wizard.progress.simulate`). The tree's own node-selection/fold script is appended to the wizard script in
  its own closure (`root` = `.mdmf-wizard`), since `wizard.js`'s `root` is private to that file.
- `wizard.css`: the `<details>` reuses `.mdmf-match-expanded-row`'s summary look on a `div` (review.css is
  already linked by the wizard); the summary line is bold ink, the tree block loses its inner padding.

**Proven by** `WizardPageTest.matchPlanCardShowsTheDecisionTreeNotRawJson` (no raw JSON, one tree per plan,
only the PROPOSED plan's tree outside the fold, Simulate per plan with its row id, exactly the acted-on plan
open, Accept still offered, plain-text fallback without a line); `tools/test_local.sh` all green.
**Not deployed, not seen live** (Tomcat was running when the lot was built; `tools/install.sh` refuses then).

## 25. Preview policy on a never-configured table: LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND — measured live 2026-09-23 12:38, PipelineStep 159

`ebx.MatchingPreviewPolicy.ensureFresh` is the branch `ensure` enters when `get_matching_config` answers
`CONFIG_NOT_FOUND` for a table (e.g. "Simulate on N pivots" clicked on a `MatchPlan` before its entity was ever
accepted once — no matching/merge configuration exists on the table at all). Measured live, PipelineStep 159,
table `/root/Contact`, `dataModel urn:ebx:publication:Companies_Master`:

1. `generate_matching_policy` was called with a matching policy object carrying `"mergePolicyCode":
   "Contact__preview"` (set by `applyPreviewSafetyOverrides`, which links the preview matching policy to a
   merge policy code up front). The add-on answered a soft miss:
   ```json
   {"code":"LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND","message":"No merge policy found for locator: Contact__preview",
    "nextStep":"This table has no configuration yet, so no merge policy can exist on it. Omit mergePolicyCode,
    then create Contact__preview with generate_merge_policy and wire the link with the set_merge_policy_link
    operation of patch_matching_config.","success":false}
   ```
2. `generate_merge_policy` was then called (unconditionally, regardless of step 1's outcome) and answered its
   own soft miss:
   ```json
   {"code":"CONFIG_NOT_FOUND","message":"No matching/merge configuration for table /root/Contact",
    "nextStep":"Create the matching configuration first (generate the matching policy), then add the merge
    policy.","success":false}
   ```
   — a direct consequence of step 1 having failed: with no matching policy ever created, there was still no
   configuration at all for `generate_merge_policy` to attach to.
3. The old `tolerateAlreadyExists` helper treated BOTH soft misses as "the preview policy already exists" —
   its documented premise (CLAUDE.md §8: what a duplicate `processCode` answers was never measured) never
   actually applied here, since `ensureFresh` is only ever entered right after `get_matching_config` itself
   answered `CONFIG_NOT_FOUND` — "already exists" cannot legitimately happen on this branch at all. The
   `MATCHING_SIMULATE_PREVIEW` PipelineStep was ended `DONE` with the message "Preview matching policy
   Contact__preview generated for /root/Contact — created via generate_matching_policy/generate_merge_policy
   (the table had no configuration at all yet)" while **nothing had actually been written**.
4. The caller, `MatchingActivationGuard.ensureActivatedAfterPreviewEnsure`, then re-read
   `get_matching_activation_status`, still saw `CONFIG_NOT_FOUND`, and refused the simulation with: "a preview
   matching policy was just written for /root/Contact but get_matching_activation_status still answers
   CONFIG_NOT_FOUND right after - the preview write may have failed silently" — a symptom pointing at the
   right table but the wrong mechanism (it was never a silent/racy write; the write itself had failed and been
   swallowed).

### 24.1 The fix — follow the add-on's own `nextStep` to the letter

The add-on's `nextStep` in step 1 above describes exactly the sequence `ebx.MatchingConfigurator.configureOne`'s
own `GENERATE_FRESH` case already uses successfully for the real (non-preview) policy: omit `mergePolicyCode`
from the first `generate_matching_policy` call, call `generate_merge_policy`, then link the two with
`patch_matching_config`'s `set_merge_policy_link` op. `ensureFresh` now mirrors that sequence exactly:

1. `generate_matching_policy` with `matchingPolicy` = `MatchingPreviewPolicy.forFreshGenerate(previewMatchingPolicy)`
   — a deep copy of the safety-overridden preview policy with `mergePolicyCode` stripped. `applyPreviewSafetyOverrides`
   itself is left unchanged (it still stamps `mergePolicyCode`) so `ensureRewrite` — which sends the whole desired
   config to `apply_matching_config` in one shot and can therefore set the link inline, no separate `generate_*`
   calls involved — keeps working exactly as before.
2. `generate_merge_policy` with `mergePolicy` = the preview merge policy under the same `<Entity>__preview` code.
3. `patch_matching_config` with one op: `{"op":"set_merge_policy_link","target":{"policyCode":"<Entity>__preview"},
   "value":"<Entity>__preview"}` — the identical shape `MatchingConfigurator.configureOne`'s `GENERATE_FRESH` case
   sends for the real policy.
4. Each of the three calls is now required to succeed via `MatchingConfigurator.requireSuccess` (made
   package-visible for this reuse) instead of the removed `tolerateAlreadyExists`: a transport error OR any
   soft-miss `success:false` fails the `MATCHING_SIMULATE_PREVIEW` step outright, naming the tool and carrying
   the add-on's own `code`/`message`/`nextStep` in the thrown `OperationException` (via `shortText` of the raw
   result text, same as every other `requireSuccess` caller).
5. After the three calls succeed, a fourth `get_matching_config` read-back is run and checked with the new
   `MatchingPreviewPolicy.previewPolicyPresent(json, previewCode)` — true only when `matchingPolicies[]` carries
   an entry with `processCode == previewCode` AND `mergePolicies[]` carries an entry with `code == previewCode`.
   If either is missing, the step fails with a message stating plainly that the three calls answered success but
   the read-back does not show the preview policy — the exact "successful-looking calls that wrote nothing" shape
   measured above should never again be reported as `DONE`.

`tolerateAlreadyExists` is deleted entirely: its premise (a soft miss on this branch means "already exists") was
never true for `ensureFresh`, which is only reachable right after `CONFIG_NOT_FOUND`.

### 24.2 What was NOT changed

- `ensureRewrite` (the table already carries some configuration) is untouched — it uses `apply_matching_config`
  with the FULL desired `matchingPolicies`/`mergePolicies` lists in one call, which already carries the link
  inline via `mergePolicyCode` on the matching-policy object; there is no separate `generate_*` call on that
  path for `mergePolicyCode` to be refused on. Its own tests (`buildApplyConfigArgs_*`,
  `applyPreviewSafetyOverrides_*`) still hold unchanged.
- `applyPreviewSafetyOverrides` itself is unchanged (still stamps `mergePolicyCode`) — only `ensureFresh`'s
  first `generate_matching_policy` call now sends a stripped copy of its output, via the new
  `forFreshGenerate` helper.
- Not run against a live add-on this session (task constraint: no EBX access, write tools forbidden) — this

## 25. The tree in plain words, with room to read (branch `feature/tree-plain-words`, 2026-09-23)

Product report, the product owner, on the wizard's Matching step right after §24 went live (screenshot of the Contact
tree): "Qu'est-ce que signifie PRE-CLUSTERING / Compared only if same firstName, lastName - not measured ?",
"l'affichage est rogné, il faut utiliser plus de place", "les messages affichés sont aussi trop techniques".
Three defects, one lot, shared by the review screen and the wizard (both render `review.MatchPlanTreeDiagram`).

**What the band meant.** The add-on never compares every pair: it first groups records by identical
clustering fields (here `firstName` + `lastName`) and runs the tree inside a group only. "Not measured" was
the evidence's own verdict on the first clustering field (`NOT_MEASURED`: a fuzzy anchor is not profiled for
cross-system sharing), printed where a business reader expected a count.

**What changed:**

- **Words, not identifiers** - `review.FieldWords.humanize` turns `firstName` / `VATNumber` / `vat_no` into
  "First name" / "VAT number" / "Vat no" everywhere the tree names a field (band, node body, detail table -
  the raw name stays as the cell's tooltip). No business label exists for a master field at this point; the
  identifier's own word boundaries are the best available signal.
- **Band**: "STEP 1 · WHO GETS COMPARED / Only records with the same First name and Last name are compared
  with each other." plus, only when the evidence measured it, a second line "About N groups (D distinct
  values, S of them found in more than one system)". An unmeasured count is simply not shown here.
- **Node card**: "N1 · OVERALL SIMILARITY OF AT LEAST 85 %" / "N1 · ALL THESE FIELDS IDENTICAL" / "N1 · AT
  LEAST 2 OF THESE 4 FIELDS IDENTICAL" / "N1 · CUSTOM RULE"; body "First name (weight 2), Last name (weight 3),
  Email, Account id" (a weight of 1 is not spelled out), "Same VAT number, Country", "Among: …".
- **Branches**: "similar enough / too different" (average), "all identical / one differs" (all fields),
  "enough / not enough" (at least N); "passes / does not pass" stays for a predicate and for the simulation
  block's own path wording (`review.match.tree.branch.true/false`, unchanged keys).
- **Leaves**: "POSSIBLE DUPLICATE / A data steward decides", "SAME RECORD / Merged automatically",
  "DIFFERENT RECORDS / Both are kept"; standing note "AUTOMATIC MERGE IS OFF - for this plan, every pair found
  identical still goes to a data steward". Title "How two records are compared", lead rewritten.
- **Detail table**: columns "Field / Compared how / Weight or Min. score / If empty"; the algorithm cell shows
  `ProposalWording.matchAlgorithmShortWords` ("close spelling", "resembles"), the precise words
  ("close spelling (Jaro-Winkler)") as its tooltip; "Reached after N1: similar enough" / "First question asked".
- **Room**: node cards are 300px wide (`MatchPlanTreeLayout.WIDE_NODE_WIDTH`) and their field list WRAPS over
  up to three `<tspan>` lines of ~44 characters (`MatchPlanTreeDiagram.wrap`); a plan's cards all take the height
  of its longest list (`MatchPlanTreeLayout.Geometry.forBodyLines`, row pitch keeps the 50px gap) so rows stay
  aligned; the column pitch grows to half a card (+10) so a wide card never overlaps a neighbour subtree. Only a
  list longer than three full lines is still cut (tooltip keeps the rest). The SVG is widened to the band's own
  sentence when the tree is narrower than it. The two-argument `MatchPlanTreeLayout.layout` keeps the pre-lot
  geometry, so `MatchPlanTreeLayoutTest`'s pinned coordinates are untouched.
- **Detail column**: sized by the block's own width (CSS container query on `.mdmf-match-block-full`), 320px
  beside the tree above 860px of block width, under it below - inside the wizard the block is narrower than
  on the review page and the 300px column broke "Weight"/"Null" mid-word.

Both bundles (en/fr) carry the new wording; `ProposalWording.matchAlgorithmWords` itself stays English-only
(pre-existing). **Proven by** `FieldWordsTest`, `MatchPlanTreeDiagramTest` (wrap, ellipsis only past three
lines, plain branch words, short algorithm words), `MatchPlanViewTest`/`WizardPageTest` updated to the new
leaf wording; `tools/test_local.sh` all green. **Seen rendered** from a static page built with the real Contact
and Company plans (en and fr), not yet on the server.

## 26. The band says how candidates are found; the trust rank is editable per source (branch `feature/trust-rank-edit-and-band`, 2026-09-23)

**Band.** the product owner, on §25's new sentence "Only records with the same First name and Last name are compared
with each other": "Cette phrase est ambiguë. Est-ce qu'ils doivent vraiment avoir les mêmes noms et prénoms ?"
No: the add-on's pre-clustering is a CANDIDATE SEARCH on every field the policy declares -
`MatchingPolicyTranslator` declares the plan's `clusteringFields` first, then every other field the tree
compares, all with the `@default` search strategy (for a name, the add-on's own `@Name` template - an
approximate search, §3.3a) - so the sentence claimed an exact identity the engine never enforces (and the
pre-§25 "Compared only if same firstName, lastName" carried the same error). The band now reads, from the
declared fields in their declared order: "STEP 1 · HOW CANDIDATES ARE FOUND / Candidates are first searched
on First name and Last name, then Email, Account id (approximate search). / Only the pairs found this way go
through the questions below." (+ the rough group count when measured). **Measured live, 2026-09-23 14:35** (the product owner: "levons le doute") with the wizard's own Simulate on Company
(APPLIED policy, 13 pivots, 28 candidates): the ENGINE itself (`Source: Engine candidate`, i.e. the add-on's
`simulateMatch`, not a factory probe) returned for pivot "BNP Paribas Arbitrage" (CRM 236) the candidates
"BNP PARIBAS" (ERP 271) and "BNP Paribas" (CRM 227), both listed under "Caught without an exact key" - their
`nameKey` differs from the pivot's. So the pre-clustering search on `@default`/`@Name` is approximate: it does
NOT require identical clustering values. "Approximate search" in the band is correct. Not repeated on Contact
(its plan is PROPOSED: a Simulate would create the `Contact__preview` policy and the Contact metadataset while
another session was reworking that plan - it now carries two tiers at 80 %).

**Trust rank.** The survivorship block says "Order changeable in the wizard (Sources -> Trust rank), not
here", but the Sources step only showed "Trust rank: N" as text - editable in the add form alone (the product owner:
"dans la partie Sources, je ne vois pas comment le faire"). Each source card now carries a number input and a
Save button (`SOURCE_SET_TRUST` → `WizardData.setSourceTrustRank`, allowed at any status: the rank only feeds
the merge policy's most-trusted-source order, re-read by the matching step's next Configure - the notice says
so). Lower wins, as before. `WizardPageTest` updated; `tools/test_local.sh` all green; band seen on the static
render (en/fr), the editor not seen live.

## 27. Simulate on Contact, second live pass 2026-09-23 13:30 — three measurements (branch `fix/preview-live-measurements`)

Task numbered this section 26, following a briefing written before `feature/trust-rank-edit-and-band` (§26
above) merged into `main` — renumbered 27 here rather than overwrite an existing section; `main` itself was
found at `a8a0e1c` this session, not the `2979054` the briefing named (both are surprises worth recording, not
something worth re-deriving each time: check `git log -1 --format=%H main` before trusting a briefing's own
commit reference).

A "Simulate" click on the PROPOSED Contact plan (table `/root/Contact`, `dataModel
urn:ebx:publication:Companies_Master`) on build 2979054 — the third measurement of this table after §17/§25 —
surfaced three more gaps, all in the same call chain. No EBX access this session (write tools forbidden by the
task, same constraint as most of this file); every fix below is verified by unit test against the exact
captured answers, never replayed live.

### 27.1 Measurement 1 — a survivor field not yet on the master table

After the §25 fix, `generate_matching_policy` (without `mergePolicyCode`) succeeded, then `generate_merge_policy`
answered:

```json
{"code":"INVALID_PARAMS","message":"Survivor field '/emailValid' does not resolve to a field of table /root/Contact","nextStep":"Call profile_table_for_matching for this table's field paths; it takes 'table' plus the 'dataset' holding it, and lists single-valued terminal fields only. A path that leaves the table's own subtree (for example via a '..' segment) is rejected even when it names a real field of another table.","success":false}
```

Cause: `emailValid` was accepted as a staging attribute (`StagingAttribute` 179, derivation `VALID_VALUE`) and
`staging/generate` + `staging/load` ran, but `master/generate` did NOT run since — `MatchingConfigurator
.readValidValueFieldNames` reads the `StagingAttribute` table only, never the master table's own schema, so it
had no way to know the field never actually reached master. The same can happen for any survivor field
(LLM-proposed business fields from `requirements.survivorship.fields[]`, structurally-identified source keys,
*Valid derived fields) that is accepted in staging but not (yet) promoted to master.

**Fix:** `master.MasterFieldFilter.dropSurvivorsNotOnMaster(mergePolicy, tablePath, Predicate<String>)` — a pure
class (no EBX import at all, the schema lookup is a `Predicate<String>` seam) that removes every survivor whose
field is not a node of the master table's record, returning one human note per field dropped ("distinguish a
*Valid field" done by a cheap `endsWith("Valid")` check, wording only). Called right after `MatchingPolicyTranslator
.buildMergePolicy` at EVERY call site that builds one: `ebx.MatchingConfigurator#configureOne` (both the
`GENERATE_FRESH` and `REWRITE` decisions use the SAME filtered `desiredMergePolicy`), `#applySurvivorship`, and
`ebx.MatchingPreviewPolicy#ensureFresh`/`#ensureRewrite` (their own preview merge policy, built the same way).
The master `AdaptationTable` itself is reached through a new shared helper, `ebx.MatchingConfigurator
.findMasterTable(pFactory, pProjectCode, pEntityName)` (package-visible, factored out of `#run`/`#simulate`'s own
inline project → `masterDataspaceKey`/`masterDatasetName` → `AdaptationHome` → `AdaptationTable` lookup so it is
not derived a fourth time) — it throws a clear `OperationException` when the project has no master zone at all
(a merge policy cannot be checked against a table that does not exist). Notes land in the step's own recorded
detail under `survivorsDroppedNotOnMaster`.

**Review screen too.** `review.MatchSurvivorshipBlock.Input` gained a fifth, optional field, `Set<String>
fieldsNotOnMaster` (a new 5-argument constructor overload; the old 4-argument one still exists, defaulting to
"nothing flagged" — no existing caller/test needed to change). `ebx.ProposalReviews#buildSurvivorshipInput`
computes it (same schema check, inlined rather than reusing `MasterFieldFilter` itself — that class stays
EBX-free by design) and a business row whose field is flagged gets a `mdmf-chip-warn` "not on the master table
yet" chip, so a data steward sees the gap before Accept, not only after a failed `matching/configure`. This
was judged cheap enough to do (the master table was already open at that exact call site for the row-count
read) rather than skipped.

### 27.2 Measurement 2 — the add-on makes the FIRST policy on a table its default

The same `get_matching_config` read-back right after the Simulate pass showed the state the add-on itself left:
one matching policy `Contact__preview` (active, modes 0/0, `mergePolicyCode: null`), `mergePolicies: []`, AND
`tableSettings.defaultMatchingPolicy: "Contact__preview"` — the add-on makes the FIRST policy ever generated on
a table its default, whatever that policy's own code, preview policies included.
`ebx.MatchingPreviewPolicy.applyPreviewSafetyOverrides`'s own PRIOR Javadoc claimed "the preview is still never
the table's `tableSettings.defaultMatchingPolicy` (nothing in this class ever touches that field)" — true as to
touching (that method itself never writes it), false as to the outcome (the add-on writes it anyway, as a side
effect of `ensureFresh`'s own first `generate_matching_policy` call). Corrected in place, quoting this exact
measurement.

The live `set_table_settings` tool signature (read the same session): args `table` (required), `settings`
(required, a partial `MameConfig.tableSettings` object: `defaultMatchingPolicy`, `pauseMatching`,
`modifyMergedRecords`, `afterModifyMergedRecords`, `viewMode`, `hideMergedRecords`; only present fields change),
optional `dataModel`. "A blank `defaultMatchingPolicy` ("") clears the default; a non-blank value must be an
existing matching-policy `processCode` on this table." Returns the full re-read `MameConfig` on success. Soft
-miss codes: `ACCESS_DENIED`, `TABLE_NOT_FOUND`, `AMBIGUOUS_TABLE`, `MODEL_NOT_REGISTERED`, `CONFIG_NOT_FOUND`,
`INVALID_PARAMS`.

**Fix:** `master.DefaultMatchingPolicyGate.decide(currentDefault, previewCode, realCodeOrNull)` — a pure,
three-way rule (`CLEAR` / `SET_REAL` / `NONE`): a default naming the preview or blank, with a known real code,
is `SET_REAL`; the same with no real code known is `CLEAR`; a default already naming the real code, or naming
something this fix has no evidence about, is `NONE`. `ebx.MatchingConfigurator.ensureDefaultMatchingPolicy`
(package-visible, shared like `requireSuccess`) applies the decision: calls `set_table_settings` when not
`NONE`, requires success (never best-effort — a wrong default silently mis-points every future manual "Run
match"), and VERIFIES the write actually stuck (reads `tableSettings.defaultMatchingPolicy` off
`set_table_settings`'s own re-read `MameConfig` first, falling back to one more `get_matching_config` only when
that node is missing).

Three call sites, per the coordinator's own precision (the live table this fix was found against was ALREADY
in the state "preview only, `defaultMatchingPolicy = Contact__preview`" — so the very NEXT Simulate click takes
`ensureRewrite`, not `ensureFresh`, and needed the identical correction):

- `ebx.MatchingPreviewPolicy#ensureFresh` — `realCodeOrNull = null` (no real policy exists yet by construction):
  always `CLEAR` when the default names the preview, using the read-back already fetched for
  `previewPolicyPresent`.
- `ebx.MatchingPreviewPolicy#ensureRewrite` — after `apply_matching_config` succeeds, `realCodeOrNull =
  realMergeCode` (the table's remaining real merge-policy code, `firstNonPreviewCode`, or `null`).
- `ebx.MatchingConfigurator#configureOne`, after BOTH `GENERATE_FRESH` (reusing the read-back already fetched for
  the related-table cascade) and `REWRITE` (a fresh `get_matching_config`, since that branch's own
  `apply_matching_config` answer is never assumed to carry `tableSettings`) — `realCodeOrNull = pEntityName`.
- `ebx.MatchingPreviewPolicy#remove` — BEFORE the removal's own `apply_matching_config` (the safe order:
  `set_table_settings` refuses a non-existent code, and it is not known whether removing a policy that is the
  table's own default would itself be refused), `realCodeOrNull` = the remaining real code among the
  post-removal merge policies, or `null`.

### 27.3 Measurement 3 — an add-on-filled algorithm default read as a spurious difference

The same re-read config showed the add-on ADDS `{"name":"jaroWinklerThreshold","value":"0.7"}` to each
jarowinkler field's own `params[]`, even though the desired policy only ever sent `weight`. `master
.MatchingPolicyComparator.sameParams` (line ~458) used to require the STORED and DESIRED sides to carry the
exact same set of param names — which meant a jarowinkler field could never compare as unchanged, forever,
regardless of whether the plan itself had actually changed (the same class of bug §19.11 already fixed for
`dateFieldPath`/leaf names/param VALUE types, one param KEY set too far).

**Fix:** `sameParams` is now asymmetric: a param present in STORED but absent in DESIRED is an add-on-filled
default and ignored; a param present in DESIRED but absent in STORED, or present on both sides with a
different value (numeric-tolerant, unchanged), is still a real difference. Applies to both node-level and
field-level params (both already went through this one shared method). Not specific to
`jaroWinklerThreshold`/jarowinkler — other algorithms likely have their own undocumented defaults the same way;
this rule change covers all of them without needing to enumerate which.

### Tests

`MasterFieldFilterTest` (Fix A, hand-built merge-policy JSON + a fake `Predicate<String>`, no `Adaptation`
anywhere), `DefaultMatchingPolicyGateTest` (Fix B, the pure `decide` rule against all three call sites' own
scenarios, plus `currentDefault`'s `data`/root read), three new cases in `MatchingPolicyComparatorTest` (Fix C:
a stored-only `jaroWinklerThreshold` is same, a desired-only param differs, a shared param with a different
value still differs), two new cases in `MatchSurvivorshipBlockTest` (the review-screen chip, shown/not shown).
`tools/test_local.sh`: all green. None of it replayed live this session (no EBX access, same constraint as the
rest of this file) — fixed strictly from the add-on's own measured answers quoted above.

## 28. AMBIGUOUS_TABLE is per tool, not per table — measured live 2026-09-23 14:20 (branch `fix/mame-always-datamodel`)

A "Simulate" click on the PROPOSED `Contact` plan (table `/root/Contact`, dataModel
`urn:ebx:publication:Companies_Master`) failed:

```
apply_matching_config failed while (re)writing the preview policy Contact__preview for /root/Contact: {"code":
"AMBIGUOUS_TABLE","message":"Table /root/Contact is declared by more than one data model: urn:ebx:module:EBX
FastTrack - TIBCO EBX Presales environment:/WEB-INF/ebx/schemas/Companies.xsd, urn:ebx:publication:
Companies_Master","nextStep":"Pass the optional 'dataModel' to disambiguate; candidates: …","success":false}
```

Two read-only calls right after pinned down why, and why every prior fix in §2.2/§2.2.1/§2.2.2/§2.2.3/§13.8/§25
had not been enough:

- `get_matching_config(table="/root/Contact")` **without** `dataModel` answered `success:true` with the table's
  real, existing configuration (the one under `urn:ebx:publication:Companies_Master`, holding the preview
  policy) — **no** `AMBIGUOUS_TABLE`. Earlier the same day, when no configuration existed yet, the identical
  unscoped call HAD answered `AMBIGUOUS_TABLE` (§2.2.2). Conclusion: once at least one of the candidate data
  models actually carries data for the table, a plain READ stops treating it as ambiguous — it just serves the
  answer from whichever one has something to say. A **write** call (`apply_matching_config`, and presumably
  every other write tool) on the exact same table, same instant, still answered `AMBIGUOUS_TABLE` with both
  candidates.
- `get_matching_activation_status(table="/root/Company", dataModel="urn:ebx:publication:Companies_Master")` —
  `Company`, a table that was **never** ambiguous at all — answered its ordinary `ENABLED`. Passing the real
  publication URN is always accepted, whether the table is ambiguous or not.

**The discipline every match-merge caller in this codebase had independently built between 2026-09-21 and
2026-09-23** — "the first call of a pass omits `dataModel`; resolve it once from that read's own `AMBIGUOUS_TABLE`
answer (or leave it `null`/omitted otherwise); thread that SAME value, possibly `null`, through every later call
of the pass" (`master.MameDataModelResolution`'s own §2.2/§2.2.1 rationale, `ebx.MatchingConfigurator
.configureOne`, `ebx.MatchingPreviewPolicy.ensure`, `ebx.MatchingActivationGuard`'s own probe-based
`resolveDataModel`, `ebx.ProjectDeleter`, `ebx.MatchPlanLlmSuggester`) — is exactly what breaks on this shape: it
assumes the FIRST call's own ambiguity outcome is representative of every later call in the same pass, which is
false the moment a READ and a WRITE disagree on whether the table even looks ambiguous.

### The fix — two layers, both needed

1. **Always pass `dataModel`.** Every match-merge call this module makes for a project's master table now sends
   `dataModel = "urn:ebx:publication:" + master.MasterNames.modelName(projectCode)` from the very first call of
   a pass — never omitted, never "resolved once and reused". New pure helper: `master.MameDataModelResolution
   .publicationUrn(String)` (the existing `PUBLICATION_URN_PREFIX` constant, extracted for reuse — the URN
   -parsing regex/candidate logic in that class is otherwise UNCHANGED). Since the real URN is always accepted
   even on a non-ambiguous table (the `Company` measurement above), this costs nothing on the common case and
   fixes the ambiguous one.
2. **Retry once on a genuine `AMBIGUOUS_TABLE`**, as a safety net for the (now much narrower) case where the
   guessed URN itself still comes back ambiguous — most likely a wrong project/table pairing. New class,
   `ebx.MameCalls` (package `ebx`, alongside every caller): `MameCalls.call(McpClient, String tool, ObjectNode
   args, String publicationName)` sets `args.dataModel` unconditionally (layer 1), calls the tool, and on a
   genuine `AMBIGUOUS_TABLE` answer retries ONCE with `master.MameDataModelResolution.resolve`'s own resolved
   candidate (layer 2, delegating to that class' existing, UNCHANGED candidate-parsing) — refusing outright
   (`OperationException`, named after the tool and the table) if resolution still cannot settle on exactly one
   candidate. The pure decision (`MameCalls.decide(JsonNode, String) -> Decision{AS_IS, RETRY, REFUSE}`) takes
   only the raw answer, never a `McpClient.ToolResult` (whose constructor is package-private in a different jar,
   `com.on.ebx.agent` — this codebase's established rule, `MatchingPreviewPolicyTest`'s own class Javadoc, is to
   never construct a real one in a test) — `MameCallsTest` drives it directly against hand-built fixtures,
   including the exact live `AMBIGUOUS_TABLE` payload quoted above; `MameCalls.call` itself (the transport part)
   is untested, like every other real `McpClient.callTool` caller in this package.

### Call sites changed

Every `callTool(` toward the `match-merge` server (`McpServers.MATCH_MERGE`) across the five files that use it
now goes through `MameCalls.call`, **except** the two the live tool contracts genuinely exclude:
`profile_table_for_matching` (scoped by `dataspace`+`dataset`, not `dataModel` — the task's own stated
exception, `ebx.MatchPlanLlmSuggester`'s profiling call) and any call with no `table`/`businessObject` argument
at all, where `dataModel` would have nothing to disambiguate (`matching_config_schema`'s global-vocabulary call
and `matching_guide`, both in `ebx.MatchPlanLlmSuggester`).

- **`ebx.MatchingConfigurator`** (18 call sites after merging two "resolve-then-rescope" pairs into one call
  each — `configureOne`'s and `applySurvivorship`'s own opening `get_matching_config`, no longer needing a
  second, rescoped call now that the first one already carries the right `dataModel`): `get_matching_config`
  (×4: `configureOne`'s opening read, the post-generate re-read, `ensureDefaultMatchingPolicy`'s own two reads),
  `set_trusted_sources` (×2 — see below), `generate_matching_policy`, `generate_merge_policy`,
  `patch_matching_config` (×2), `apply_matching_config` (×2), `validate_matching_config`, `activate_matching`,
  `set_table_settings`, `get_matching_activation_status`, `matching_config_schema` (`checkFieldCapabilities`).
  `ensureDefaultMatchingPolicy`/`readActivationState`/`checkFieldCapabilities` all had their `pDataModel`
  parameter renamed to `pPublicationName` (bare project master model name, never an already-resolved `dataModel`
  string any more) and now route their own calls through `MameCalls.call`.
- **`ebx.MatchingPreviewPolicy`** (8 call sites, same merge as above in `ensure`): `get_matching_config` (×3:
  `ensure`'s opening read, `ensureFresh`'s post-generate re-read, `remove`'s opening read),
  `generate_matching_policy`, `generate_merge_policy`, `patch_matching_config`, `apply_matching_config` (×2:
  `ensureRewrite`, `remove`). **`remove` used to send `dataModel=null` on every call, unconditionally — a real
  gap (it never even attempted resolution), not a deliberate omission** — now closed the same way as every other
  method in this class.
- **`ebx.MatchingActivationGuard`**: the probe-based `resolveDataModel`/`ResolvedDataModel` (the ONE place this
  class used to do its own independent `AMBIGUOUS_TABLE` resolution, via an unscoped `get_matching_activation_status`
  call purely to decide whether `dataModel` was needed at all) are DELETED — `ensureActivatedBeforeSimulate` now
  computes `dataModel` directly from `pProjectCode`, no probe call. `ensureActivatedAfterPreviewEnsure` gained a
  `pProjectCode` parameter (threaded from its one caller, `ebx.MatchPlanSimulationRunner.simulate`) purely so its
  own `McpStatusPort` can retry on `AMBIGUOUS_TABLE` the same way. `McpStatusPort` (the one class in the file that
  touches `McpClient` — `get_matching_activation_status`, `activate_matching`) now holds the project's bare
  publication name and routes both calls through `MameCalls.call`; `activateIfNeeded`'s own signature and its
  direct unit tests (`MatchingActivationGuardTest`) are UNCHANGED — that method never touched `McpClient` in the
  first place (`StatusPort` seam, class Javadoc).
- **`ebx.ProjectDeleter`**: `delete_matching_config` (`deleteMatchingConfig`) and `get_matching_config`
  (`isConfigured`, the planning-only probe) — the file's other four `callTool` sites target the `ebx-connectors`
  (`connectors_mapping_delete`) and `data-model` (`execute_operation`) servers, untouched.
- **`ebx.MatchPlanLlmSuggester`**: `matching_config_schema`'s per-entity, table-scoped `fieldCapabilities` call
  (`readFieldCapabilities`'s own inline block) — its own preliminary, advisory-only `get_matching_config` probe
  (the exact "resolve once from a read" shape this whole fix retires) is DELETED entirely; `dataModel` is now
  sent unconditionally from the start. The file's other two `table`-less calls (`matching_config_schema`'s global
  vocabulary read, `matching_guide`) and its one `profile_table_for_matching` call are untouched, per the
  exceptions above.

### What was NOT changed

- `master.MameDataModelResolution.resolve`'s own candidate-extraction logic (URN-span parsing, whole-token
  matching, the `message`/`nextStep`-kept-separate fix of §2.2.3) — reused verbatim by `MameCalls.decide`, never
  duplicated.
- `set_trusted_sources` now DOES receive `dataModel` (in both `ebx.MatchingConfigurator.configureOne`'s
  `GENERATE_FRESH` case and `applySurvivorship`) — an earlier task brief had it OMIT `dataModel`
  unconditionally, quoted as "the task brief's own contract, verbatim 'OMIT'". Re-checked against the
  `match-merge` server's own tool-inventory description (`dataModel` is listed as a "Common param" across the
  whole server, with `profile_table_for_matching` the ONE stated exception) — `set_trusted_sources` is not that
  exception, so it now goes through `MameCalls.call` like every other write tool in this module. Never measured
  live either way (no EBX access this session).
- Not replayed live this session (task constraint: no EBX access, write tools forbidden) — the two-layer fix is
  reasoned entirely from the two read-only measurements quoted above and `master.MameDataModelResolution`'s own

## 29. ENABLED without a metadataset — measured live 2026-09-23 15:50 (Test, build e3ac9a1), Simulate on the PROPOSED Contact plan

**The exact live answer.** With §27/§28's own fixes already in — the preview policy written correctly this time
(matching policy and merge policy both linked, the add-on's spurious default already cleared) —
`ebx.MatchingActivationGuard.ensureActivatedAfterPreviewEnsure` read `get_matching_activation_status(table=
/root/Contact, dataModel=urn:ebx:publication:Companies_Master)`:

```json
{"metadatasetExists":false,"paused":false,"published":true,"state":"ENABLED"}
```

`MatchingActivationGuard.decide(status)` — as it stood right after the 2026-09-23 07:45 fix (§13.8) — was
`status.enabled() ? PROCEED : ACTIVATE_THEN_RECHECK`, i.e. it read `state` alone. `state == "ENABLED"` →
`PROCEED`, so the guard never called `activate_matching` at all. `simulateMatch` then failed exactly the way
§13.7's own boot-race defect does:

```
The add-on's index of /root/Contact has no metadataset-linked fields (Linked_Field_State): the matching trigger
is not attached - re-activate matching (activate_matching) or restart; raw: field [Linked_Field_State] not
found; input fields are: [id, sourceSystem, sourceId, contactId, accountId, accountIdRef, firstName, lastName,
title, contactRole, email, phone, preferredLanguage, hasOptedOutOfEmail, lastModifiedDate, _loadId,
_receivedAt, ebx-metadata, $docid, $score, $pk, $adaptation, $highlights]
```

**So `state: ENABLED` means "the matching trigger is attached", not "ready to simulate".** The two are usually
set together (the boot-race defect at §13.7 leaves BOTH unset at once, which is why `decide`'s original,
`state`-only check happened to work for that incident), but this measurement proves they are not always the
same fact: a table can report `state: ENABLED` while `metadatasetExists: false`, and every matching/merge call
that touches the add-on's Lucene index fails on it regardless of `state`. `activate_matching`'s own tool
description says it "prepares the metadataset" AND enables — this table's `state` was flipped to `ENABLED`
(most likely by the same `configureOne` activation step, §4, on an earlier attempt) without the metadataset
side of that contract actually completing.

### The fix

1. `MatchingActivationGuard`: new package-private `isReady(StatusSnapshot)` — `state == ENABLED AND
   metadatasetExists` — is now the ONE place both fields are read together. `decide` and the post-`activate_matching`
   recheck inside `activateIfNeeded` both call it instead of `StatusSnapshot.enabled()` directly, so `PROCEED`
   (skip the repair) and "the repair worked" are both now gated on the SAME, stricter test. Nothing about the
   unconditional-repair-attempt discipline from §13.8 changed — a not-ready table still gets exactly one
   `activate_matching` attempt, then a genuine re-read (never trusting `activate_matching`'s own returned status,
   unchanged).
2. `refusalMessage` now branches: `state == ENABLED but metadatasetExists == false` after the repair attempt gets
   its own wording ("reports state=ENABLED ... but metadatasetExists=false ... this is a different failure than
   'not enabled' - try activate_matching again from the MAME administration screen, or restart") instead of being
   folded into the generic "is still not activated" text, which read as if the trigger itself were the problem.
3. The constant `REACTIVATED_NOTE` (a single fixed phrase, "matching trigger was not attached after the last
   boot - re-activated") is gone — it was already misleading for exactly this incident, since the trigger was
   never the problem here. Replaced by `reactivatedNote(StatusSnapshot pBefore)`, which reads the PRE-activation
   snapshot and says which half was actually missing: trigger only, metadataset only (this incident's case:
   "the matching trigger was attached (state=ENABLED) but its metadataset did not exist yet after the last boot
   - re-activated"), or both (the §13.8/§13.7 boot-race shape).
4. `MatchingConfigurator.configureOne`'s OWN activation gate had the identical narrower check in two places,
   fixed with the same `isReady` test rather than a second, independent copy of the rule:
   - The `REWRITE` branch's `readActivationState` (renamed `readActivationStatus`) used to return only the bare
     `state` string, and `skipActivateBecauseAlreadyEnabled` trusted `"ENABLED".equals(state)` alone to skip a
     re-activation. It now returns the full `MatchingActivationGuard.StatusSnapshot` and gates on
     `MatchingActivationGuard.isReady(status)` instead — a rewrite onto a table that reports `ENABLED` with no
     metadataset now correctly still runs `activate_matching`, rather than skipping it and leaving the table
     just as unready as before the rewrite.
   - The activation step itself (shared by `GENERATE_FRESH` and `REWRITE`) used to accept
     `activate_matching`'s own answer as successful whenever ITS `state` field read `"ENABLED"`
     (`"ENABLED".equals(MameAnswer.field(activateResult.json, "state").asText(null))`) — the same
     trust-the-tool's-own-answer pattern §13.8 already replaced with a genuine re-read on the `MatchingActivationGuard`
     side, just never carried over here. Minimal fix applied: parse `activateResult.json` with
     `MatchingActivationGuard.parseStatus` and require `isReady`, not a full extra re-read call (this call site
     has never itself been observed to hit the ENABLED-but-no-metadataset shape live — the fix closes the same
     class of gap on the assumption `activate_matching`'s own answer shares the `get_matching_activation_status`
     `ActivationStatus` shape, per §13.7's own note that the two tools answer the same fields).
5. `ensureActivatedBeforeSimulate`'s own class Javadoc (in `MatchingConfigurator.simulate`) updated: it used to
   say `decide`'s gate was "no longer keyed on published/metadatasetExists" (true right after §13.8, no longer
   true after this fix) — corrected to describe both the §13.8 change (stopped refusing outright before
   attempting a repair) and this one (added `metadatasetExists` back in, but only as part of what counts as
   READY, never as an upfront refusal).

### Tests

`MatchingActivationGuardTest`: `decide_enabledButNoMetadataset_activateThenRecheck` (state ENABLED,
metadatasetExists false → `ACTIVATE_THEN_RECHECK`, confirmed against `isReady` directly too);
`activateIfNeeded_enabledButMetadatasetMissing_selfHeals_noteNamesMetadatasetNotTrigger` (status ENABLED/false →
activate → recheck ENABLED/true → the returned note names the metadataset and does NOT say "trigger was not
attached", since the trigger never was); `activateIfNeeded_enabledButMetadatasetStillMissingAfterActivate_refusesNamingMetadataset`
(recheck still ENABLED/false → refusal mentions `metadatasetExists=false` and `state=ENABLED` together, plus
`activate_matching` as the already-tried remedy). The pre-existing
`activateIfNeeded_freshlyGeneratedConfig_neverPublishedNorMetadataset_selfHealsAnyway` (both trigger and
metadataset missing) updated to check the note names BOTH `trigger` and `metadataset`, since it can no longer
assert equality against the now-removed `REACTIVATED_NOTE` constant. `tools/test_local.sh`: all green
(`MatchingActivationGuardTest`, `MatchingConfiguratorTest` included).

### What was NOT changed

- The unconditional-single-repair-attempt discipline itself (§13.8) — a not-ready table (by either half of
  `isReady`) still gets exactly one `activate_matching` attempt before refusing, never a loop or a second retry.
- `MatchingConfigurator.configureOne`'s activation step was given the minimal `isReady` fix on
  `activate_matching`'s OWN answer, not the full status/activate/re-read cycle `MatchingActivationGuard` runs for
  the simulate path — a second, independent `get_matching_activation_status` re-read after `activate_matching`
  was judged out of scope for this fix (this call site has never itself been seen to hit the incident's exact
  shape live; the existing `readActivationStatus` check right before the rewrite branch already provides one
  fresh read per `configureOne` call).
- Not replayed live this session (task constraint: no EBX access, write tools forbidden) — reasoned entirely
  from the exact JSON and error text measured live and quoted above. `tools/test_local.sh`: all green.

## 30. Mandatory parent confirmation node + shape-divergence guard (branch `fix/matching-plan-child-and-identity`, 2026-09-25)

**No EBX/LLM access this session - every claim below is code-level and unit-tested only (`tools/test_local.sh`),
never observed running against a live instance or a real language model.** Fixes two real defects PersVol3
(2026-09-25, entities Personne/Adresse, Adresse a CHILD of Personne via its REFERENCE attribute `personne`, 2 996
persons from 3 sources = 1 594 real people, 4 667 addresses, agent run 96) measured live: persons recall 75%/precision
100% (task 2's target), addresses 56,510 suspect pairs at 5% precision - unusable, because the Adresse plan
(`N1 AVERAGE 85 [fullAddress fuzzyFullText w3, postalCode exact w2, city exact w2, country exact w1]`) never named
`personne` anywhere, so it compared addresses of DIFFERENT persons. §12.7's `checkParentConfirmationNodeShape` only
validates the SHAPE of a confirmation node the model chose to build - it is silent on a field the model never wrote at
all, exactly this case.

### 30.1 Task 1 - the parent confirmation node is now MANDATORY for a child entity

New method `master.MatchPlanLlmPass.Session#requireParentConfirmationNodeForChild`, called from `proposeMatchPlan`
right after `checkParentConfirmationNodeShape` (so a confirmation node found here has already passed that shape
check). Runs only when the entity is a child (`EntityInfo#childOfParent != null` - the same structural detection
`§12`'s prompt annotation already uses, reused, never re-derived) and:

1. **Refuses when no node in the plan is a single-field `ALL_FIELDS` node on `EntityInfo#childOfAttribute` with role
   `REFERENCE`** - i.e. the reference field is never used at all. The refusal names the field and spells out the
   exact two-level shape to build.
2. **Refuses when ANY path from the plan's `root` can reach `MATCH` or `SUSPECTED` without crossing that node** - a
   new depth-first walk, `Session#findOutcomePathBypassingNode` (id-visited set, stops the instant it reaches the
   confirmation node - safe because that node's own `onTrue`/`onFalse` are already shape-checked to be exactly
   `MATCH`/`SUSPECTED` by `checkParentConfirmationNodeShape`, so nothing past it needs walking). This catches a
   second, subtler failure mode never exercised before: a confirmation node can be built and be perfectly
   well-shaped, while a DIFFERENT node's own `onFalse` (or a second, parallel identity node) leaks straight to
   `SUSPECTED`/`MATCH` around it.

The `userPrompt`'s COMBINED IDENTITY paragraph is unchanged for this task (the child-entity contract paragraph
already existed, §12.7); only the enforcement changed, from "correctly shaped if present" to "present and every path
crosses it".

Tests (`MatchPlanLlmPassTest`, fixture `sessionWithContact()`/`contact()`, unchanged): `childEntity_refusedWhenPlanNeverUsesTheReferenceField`
(the exact PersVol3 Adresse shape, reproduced structurally with Contact/Company field names - a single fuzzy node,
`companyId` never named), `childEntity_refusedWhenAnIdentityNodeBypassesTheConfirmationNode` (a correctly-shaped N2
confirmation node exists, but N1's own `onFalse` goes straight to `SUSPECTED` instead of `NOT_MATCHED`),
`childEntity_acceptedCanonicalShapeStillPasses` (the pre-existing canonical accepted shape from §12.7 is not
newly refused), `nonChildEntity_neverRequiresAConfirmationNode` (Company, no `childOfParent`: an ordinary
single-node plan needs nothing extra).

### 30.2 Task 2 - a text field's dominant value SHAPE must agree across source systems before an EXACT comparison

PersVol3's Personne plan also compared `phone` with the exact algorithm although the three sources write it
`+33612345678` / `0033612345678` / `0612345678` - structurally incapable of ever matching across systems, and
`birthDate` (filled on 2 of 3 sources) was never used at all.

**Shapes were not available to this pass before this lot** (checked, per the task brief: `MatchPlanLlmSuggester`
sent fill rate/cardinality/most-frequent-value/token, never a shape) - added end to end, reusing
`ebx.StagingLlmSuggester#fillShapes`/`#topShapes`'s own approach (`quality.Shapes#of`, top-3 shapes with their share)
rather than reinventing it:

- `ebx.CrossSystemMeasures#perSystemValueShapes` (new): per source system present on the entity's master table, the
  top-3 value shapes of a field, reusing the exact SQL `perSystemValidityCounts` already sends (`GROUP BY
  sourceSystem, field`, same `MAX_VALIDITY_DISTINCT_VALUES` cap, same "null on any failure/cap-exceeded" discipline)
  - only what happens to each row differs (shape aggregation here, quality-rule scoring there). `#topShapesBySystem`
    is the sort/format helper, package-private, the same rendering `StagingLlmSuggester#topShapes` established.
- `master.MatchPlanLlmPass.AttributeInfo#shapesBySystem` (new field, full-form constructor gains one trailing
  parameter - every prior constructor kept as a convenience overload passing `null`, so no existing caller/test
  needed to change signature). Rendered in `userPrompt` by the new `MatchPlanLlmPass#appendShapesBySystem`
  (`", value shapes: ERP 9(8) (100%); CRM AAAA Aaaa (87%), Aaaa AAAA (13%)"`).
- `ebx.MatchPlanLlmSuggester#toLlmEntity` (new `pShareShapes` parameter, gated at `LlmDataPolicy.Level != NONE` -
  the same `SHAPES_ONLY` threshold `StagingLlmSuggester`'s own `shareShapes` uses, never `SAMPLE_VALUES`): computes
  `shapesBySystem` for a `STRING`-typed, non-`SOURCE_KEY` attribute already within the existing survivorship
  measurement budget (`fillCountBySystem != null` - never a second, independent query budget), never sensitive
  (`LlmDataPolicy#isSensitive` on the master field/attribute name/label, the same three checks `shareThis` already
  applies for `mostFrequentValue`).
- `AttributeInfo#dominantShapeConflict()` (new): compares each system's own FIRST (most frequent) shape string; null
  when fewer than two systems have one, or they all agree; otherwise a short "system: shape" list.
- The guard itself, in `Session#buildAndAppendNode`, at the top of the pre-existing `if
  (MatchPlanLlmPass.EXACT_ALGORITHM.equals(algorithm))` block (before `CrossSystemFieldGuard`'s own live queries -
  cheaper, and complementary: this catches a FORMAT conflict the shared-value count alone would just read as "zero
  shared", with no hint why): refused when `dominantShapeConflict()` is non-null, naming the field, the disagreeing
  systems, and pointing at the field's own `matchKey` (if any) or a fuzzy algorithm instead. **Never fires on a
  REFERENCE field** (`isReference` already forces EXACT on it for an unrelated, dedicated reason - a foreign key's
  own id format is not this guard's concern) **or on a field already substituted with its own derived `matchKey`**
  (a `FOLD_KEY`'s shapes are normalised by construction, so the substituted attribute's own `shapesBySystem`, if
  ever populated, is expected to already agree - never independently verified this session).

The COMBINED IDENTITY paragraph (`systemPrompt`, §14 above) gained one new sentence: before proposing the exact
algorithm on any TEXT field, read its per-system value shapes when given, and derive a matching key (preferred, for
a field with real structure like a phone) or switch to a fuzzy algorithm when they disagree - the guard above then
enforces it rather than merely suggesting it.

Tests: `dominantShapeConflict_refusesExactComparison` (three systems, three different phone shapes - the exact
PersVol3 numbers reproduced structurally), `dominantShapeConflict_sameShapeAcrossSystemsAccepted` (every system
agrees on `9(8)`, one system additionally shows a minor `9(6)` variant at low share - still no conflict, since only
the DOMINANT shape per system is compared), `dominantShapeConflict_neverCheckedOnAReferenceField` (the canonical
child-entity shape, `companyId` as the sole field of its own confirmation node, still passes with the new guard
active).

### 30.3 What was verified vs. not

**Verified** (`tools/test_local.sh`, all green - see the commit for the exact run): every guard's pure decision
logic, against hand-built fixtures reproducing PersVol3's own numbers/shapes structurally (never the real field
names `personne`/`fullAddress`/`phone`/`birthDate` - this file's own Contact/Company/Person fixture convention, per
§12's "never domain/field-name-specific knowledge in code" discipline).

**NOT verified** (no EBX/LLM access this session, same discipline every prior lot in this file states): neither

PersVol3 re-run - whether a real model, faced with the new refusal texts, actually converges on the canonical
