## 31. A cross-system key derivation is not left out of the one-click accept by the model's own number (branch `fix/match-key-confidence`, 2026-09-26)

**Finding (volume test PersVol4, 2026-09-26).** The capability pass proposed `phoneE164` on `Personne`
(`StagingAttribute` 768, derivation `SCRIPT`, `CapabilitySuggestion` 36, `Fasttrack.lib.phone.toE164`) at
50%. The Mapping matrix's "Accept the N unflagged proposals >= 60%" left out exactly those two rows ("2 left
out below the threshold (lowest confidence 50%)"), while the rule-proposed fold keys `firstNameKey`/
`lastNameKey`/`emailKey` (85%) went through. Without the key the matching plan used neither phone nor birth
date, and person recall fell from 75% to 71%.

**Root cause of the 50%.** Not the model's judgement of the key: the stored binding was
`{"value":"phoneNumber","country":{"toBeProvided":"Country code or value not present ..."}}`, and
`CapabilityLlmPass.TO_BE_PROVIDED_CONFIDENCE_CAP` (50) caps every suggestion with a `toBeProvided` input. Worse,
such a derivation could never have been applied even if accepted by hand: `DerivationApplier` (and
`DerivationBodyBuilder.buildCreateTriggerBody`, `buildTemplateBody` before lot T1) refuse a `toBeProvided` parameter outright. Yet `toE164(value,
country)` documents that a null or blank country reads the country off an international value - a blank
literal was the right binding.

**Fix, two parts, both domain-free.**

1. `CapabilityLlmPass.Session#suggestScriptDerivation` refuses a `toBeProvided` entry while the model can
   still settle it (attribute, or literal - `{"literal":""}` when the function documents a null/blank
   parameter); the schema and the system prompt say so. A stored derivation is therefore always appliable,
   and the 50% cap no longer applies to derivations (it still applies to constraints and services, where a
   person can supply the input later).
2. The derivation schema gains `crossSystemKey` (boolean): the model states the attribute exists to compare
   the same real value across systems. For such a derivation `ebx.CapabilityLlmSuggester` measures the EXACT
   fill (`QualitySuggester.exactAggregates`, counts only) of every attribute the binding reads on every
   system feeding the entity, and the pure `capability.DerivationEvidence#decide` stores
   `max(model, 85)` - the level of the rule-proposed fold keys (`quality.CrossSystemFold`) - when every
   source has at least one value on every system (two systems or more), otherwise the model's number.
   The reason is appended to the rationale of both rows. The matrix safety net is unchanged: a flagged
   attribute or cell stays excluded whatever its confidence.

**What happens once accepted (read in the code, not run).** Accepting in the matrix sets both rows to
`ACCEPTED`; the derivation itself is declared and authored by `DerivationApplier` (lot T1, 2026-10-04: two table triggers feeding a stored field; at the time of this note a `functionField`) (Proposal review, Apply
on the ACCEPTED line, after `staging/generate`), with a body calling `Fasttrack.lib.phone.toE164(_ebx.record.
phoneNumber, '')`. EBX computes it; `StagingLoader` never writes it. On PersVol4's staging data that blank
country yields a value for the international forms (CRM `+...` 1054 rows, ERP `+...`/`00...` 1003 rows,
ECOM `+...` 200 rows) and null for ECOM's 313 national-form numbers (`05...`, `01...`) - a national number
has no country without one. The matching passes see `phoneE164` as an ordinary promoted attribute (role
`BUSINESS`): `readDerivedFromByName`/`readMatchKeyByName` only link `FOLD_KEY` rows to their source, so the
guards never redirect `phoneNumber` to `phoneE164` and it does not get the MATCH_KEY role (exact-only,
never an identifier). PersVol4's existing rows keep their 50% until the capability pass is re-run.

**Tests.** `DerivationEvidenceTest` (the decision: raise, never lower, gap on one system, unmeasured system,
single-system entity, every bound attribute, summed mappings); `CapabilityLlmPassTest`
(`derivationToBeProvidedParameterIsRefused`, `derivationBlankLiteralAcceptedAndCrossSystemKeyRecorded`).

## 32. A child's parent reference is its link field (branch `fix/child-link-single-reference`, 2026-09-26)

PersVol4: the matching pass wrote "skipped the entity Adresse ... because the personne reference field is unfilled in
key systems" - no address plan at all. Cause: `MatchPlanLlmSuggester.childLink` picks the attribute carrying
`referenceEntity` (`personne`), and the model was offered that master column - a plain STRING filled only by the
key-linked ERP root feed (master: ERP 2217, CRM 0, ECOM 0). The master foreign key `personneRef` (the staging
`parentLinkField` lowered by `MasterModel`, filled for every feed and followed to the surviving golden by
`MasterLoader.ParentKeys`) was filled on all 4 210 rows and never shown. `TARGET-MAPPING.md` sec 14 has how each
column is filled.

- `ChildLink` now carries `linkField` (the `MasterModel.ForeignKeyInfo.fieldName` of the link attribute).
  `toLlmEntity` offers it as the parent reference (role REFERENCE, profile of that column, per-system fill always
  measured on it - `COUNT("personneRef")` in EBX SQL works on a foreign key, checked live), drops the plain link

  `EntityInfo.childOfAttribute` is the link field. The mandatory parent confirmation node (sec 30) therefore sits on
  `personneRef`.
- `skip_entity` on a child whose reason talks about the reference/parent/link/fill while the link field is measured

  and the two-level shape to build; a second skip is recorded as given. A real gap is never argued away.

## 33. Child evidence in the parent's matching plan (lot R2, 2026-09-26)

> **2026-10-12 (lot W13): the placeholder/relink workaround described in §33.1-§33.9 and in §36-§38 is GONE.** The `mcpgap` package, the REST route
> `matching/relation-fields/relink` and `docs/RELATION_FIELDS_WORKAROUND.md` were deleted; relation fields are written natively through a business
> object (add-on 6.3.0.5-RC3). Read §33.12 first; the sections below are kept as the history of why the workaround existed.


Business need (the product owner, 2026-09-24): a person's addresses live in a child table (`Adresse.personne -> Personne`,
several rows per person); the parent's decision tree must use them as evidence ("same name at different addresses
must not match"), GRADED - exact address agreement strengthens a match, coarse agreement (city/country) alone needs
an independent identifier of the parent too, no agreement at all must not end in MATCH, missing evidence withholds
confirmation but never disqualifies. Same pattern for other domains (companies/sites, products/packaging variants).

### 33.1 What Match and Merge itself does (§8's own javap note, unchanged here)

A decision-tree field can be a RELATIONSHIP field ("Use relationships = By foreign key", `MatchingField.useAssociation
= 1`): its values are read through the child's own FK, and two parents' child-row lists are compared by BEST PAIR.
The `match-merge` MCP server can neither write nor reference such a field (`useRelationships` is read-only in
`matching_config_schema`; `MamePatchApplier.firstMatchingField` only resolves `useAssociation = NO` fields - javap on
6.3.0.4-RC2, 2026-09-26, unchanged from the earlier finding). This lot's whole placeholder/relink workaround exists
solely because of this gap - see `mcpgap.RelationFieldSpec`/`RelationFieldRelinker`'s own Javadoc (the contract
another agent implements in parallel; `RelationFieldRelinker.relink` still throws `UnsupportedOperationException` at
the time this lot was written and this lot's own code never calls it in a test).

### 33.2 Permanent code (plan, storage, review, guards) vs. temporary (placeholder/relink)

Per the coordinator's own scoping: everything about the PLAN model, the LLM prompt/tool schema, the stored
`MatchPlan.requirements` shape, review rendering and the structural guards is PERMANENT - it stays even after the
vendor fixes the MCP gap and the translator starts sending relation fields natively. Everything about the
placeholder substitution and the relink call is TEMPORARY and confined to exactly two places, both marked with the
comment `// MCPGAP relation-fields`:

- `master.MatchingPolicyTranslator.buildMatchingPolicyWithRelationFields` (the one method that knows about
  `mcpgap.RelationFieldSpec` in the `master` package).
- `ebx.MatchingConfigurator.relinkRelationFields` (the one call site of `mcpgap.RelationFieldRelinker.relink`),
  called right after both matching-policy write paths that can carry a relation field: the GENERATE_FRESH path
  (`generate_matching_policy`) and the REWRITE path (`apply_matching_config`). `ebx.MatchingPreviewPolicy` (the
  Simulate-click preview writer) was DELIBERATELY NOT extended in this lot - see §33.6 "Not done".

Nothing else in `master`/`review` imports `mcpgap` - grep confirms it.

### 33.3 Plan model (`master.DecisionTreePlan`)

`FieldRef` gained two optional properties, round-tripped through `toJson`/`fromJson` (`readFrom` unaffected - it
already delegates): `via` (the child entity name a field is read through - non-null means "this is a relation
field", `FieldRef#isRelation()`) and `dataType` (the field's own declared type, used only by the translator's
placeholder-matching, harmless metadata otherwise). `toNested`'s own `autoLabel` now renders a relation field as
`Child.field` in a generated node label (cosmetic only - never read by the matching engine).

`validate` gained a SECOND overload, `validate(Plan, allowedFunctions, allowedAlgorithms, RelationCatalog,
clusteringFieldNames)`, additive on top of the existing structural checks:

- `RELATION_FIELD_UNKNOWN_CHILD`/`RELATION_FIELD_UNKNOWN_ATTRIBUTE` - a relation field's `via` must name a real
  child (per the caller-supplied `RelationCatalog`) and `field` one of that child's accepted attributes.
- `RELATION_FIELD_ALONE_AT_ROOT` - the root node must compare at least one of the entity's OWN fields too
  (pre-clustering search always runs on the entity's own attributes, CLAUDE.md §8).
- `RELATION_FIELD_IS_CLUSTERING_FIELD` - a relation field's own `field` name may never appear in `clusteringFields`
  (a relationship field is never the add-on's own pre-clustering key).

`relationFromNestedField` (new) - **an ASSUMPTION, not measured live** (this session had no write access to
`match-merge`, so a relinked field's real read-back shape has never been observed): a relinked field is assumed to
carry a non-blank/true `useRelationships` marker and a `location` object naming `table` (`/root/<Child>`, the exact
convention `MasterModel#tablePath` always uses) and, optionally, `foreignKey`. Isolated in this one method precisely
so correcting it later (once measured) touches nothing else; unit-tested against this assumed shape only
(`DecisionTreePlanTest#relationFromNestedField_recognisesAssumedShape`).

### 33.4 Translator (`master.MatchingPolicyTranslator`)

`buildMatchingPolicy` was refactored (no behaviour change) into a thin wrapper over a new private
`buildMatchingPolicyFromPlan(processCode, Plan, requirementsForClustering, autoMerge)`, so the relation-aware path
can run the identical translation logic over an in-memory `Plan` it has already substituted, without a second copy
of the field-order-union/tree-building code.

`buildMatchingPolicyWithRelationFields` (the one MCPGAP-marked method): for every relation field in the tree, picks
a PLACEHOLDER - a parent field already declared on the policy for another reason (a `clusteringFields` entry or
another, non-relation, tree field), of the SAME declared data type, not already used in that SAME node - mutates the
in-memory field to that placeholder, and records a `mcpgap.RelationFieldSpec` (node name via `DecisionTreePlan#labelFor`
- exposed for exactly this purpose - placeholder, child table path, child FK path, child field path). No eligible
placeholder at all: the whole translation is refused with an `IllegalStateException` naming the node and field -
never a wrong/duplicate field silently sent to the add-on. Returns `{matchingPolicy, relationFieldSpecs}`.

### 33.5 Configurator (`ebx.MatchingConfigurator`) and comparator (`master.MatchingPolicyComparator`)

`configureOne` now always calls `buildMatchingPolicyWithRelationFields` (parent field types and child FK info both
read straight off `MasterModel.Result` - `fields`/`foreignKeys`, already computed for every configure call, no new
plumbing) instead of the plain `buildMatchingPolicy`; the returned specs are empty for an ordinary entity with no
relation field, so this is a no-op change for every project that does not use them. `relinkRelationFields` (MCPGAP
marked) calls `RelationFieldRelinker.relink` right after each successful write and turns `ok:false` into a thrown
`OperationException` - a relink failure fails the whole configure step, never silently leaves a placeholder field
standing in for real evidence.

The comparator gained a relation-tolerant overload, `compare(..., List<RelationFieldMapping>)` (a small,
`mcpgap`-independent local class the configurator builds from its own `RelationFieldSpec` list): before the existing
comparison runs, any LIVE field `DecisionTreePlan#relationFromNestedField` recognises as matching one of the
mappings is canonicalised back to the desired placeholder path. A field the relinker has not reached yet (still
literally the placeholder) already compares equal with no canonicalisation needed - both states converge on the
same comparison, so a plan that has not changed never shows up as "decisionTree differs" merely because the add-on
has since relinked the field (`MatchingPolicyComparatorTest#compare_relationField_*`, three cases: unrelinked,
relinked with the mapping supplied, relinked WITHOUT the mapping - genuinely looks different, proving the tolerance
is doing real work rather than always trivially passing).

### 33.6 LLM pass (`master.MatchPlanLlmPass`) and suggester (`ebx.MatchPlanLlmSuggester`)

`EntityInfo` gained `relationChildren: List<RelationChildInfo>` (child entity name, its own measured `AttributeInfo`
list - the SAME class/measurement discipline as the parent's own attributes, never a parallel type - plus per-parent
row-count stats: min/max/avg/share-with-none, null together when not measured). The tool schema's field object
gained an optional `via` property; `userPrompt` renders a "Relation evidence" section per entity with a
DOMAIN-NEUTRAL principle paragraph (persons/addresses AND companies/sites-or-products/packaging, per the LLM-first
rule - no column name, no business word baked into Java) covering: graded confirmation (precise evidence can
confirm, coarse evidence alone needs an independent identifier too, no agreement must not end in MATCH without
strong independent identifiers), missing-evidence-withholds-never-disqualifies (DO_NOTHING), and "say so in your
rationale" when no useful precise key exists on the child (this lot never builds derived keys for a child).

Per-field parsing (`Session#buildAndAppendNode`) routes any field carrying `via` to a NEW, deliberately SEPARATE and
much smaller guard path, `appendRelationField` - most of the ordinary per-field pipeline (`CrossSystemFieldGuard`'s
live SQL against the PARENT table, matching-key substitution against the PARENT's own attributes, near-unique/
never-repeats checks against the PARENT's own row count) is meaningless or outright wrong for a CHILD attribute, so
it is never reused for a relation field. What IS reused: the algorithm must be allowed and not require an
unpopulated runtime parameter. New guards specific to relation fields: refused outright inside a MATCH-terminal node
(an exact identity confirmation must rest on the entity's own fields), refused on a `SOURCE_KEY`/`REFERENCE`-role
child attribute, refused when `via`/`field` do not resolve against `EntityInfo#relationChildren`. The "never alone
at the root" and "never a clustering field" guards are enforced once, structurally, by the new
`DecisionTreePlan.validate` overload (§33.3), called from `proposeMatchPlan` in place of the old, relation-unaware
call - so they can never drift from the pure model's own definition of the rule.

`ebx.MatchPlanLlmSuggester.buildRelationChildren` (new): for a parent entity, finds every promoted child (a
`MasterModel.Result.foreignKeys` entry targeting it), profiles the child's own master table via
`profile_table_for_matching` (same MCP call, same `shareValues`/sensitive-field discipline as the parent's own
attributes), builds a reduced `AttributeInfo` list (accepted, non-technical, non-reference child attributes only -
survivorship/shape/cleaning-step richness is NOT computed for a child attribute in this lot, defaulted null/empty:
out of scope, the relation-evidence prompt does not need it), and measures per-parent row-count stats via the new
`ebx.RelationRowCountMeasures` (package-private, same discipline as `CrossSystemMeasures`: `GROUP BY` the child's own
FK field, "not measured" on any failure - including, if it ever turns out the FK column needs its target key dotted
on rather than compared as a bare scalar in a `GROUP BY`, CLAUDE.md §2's own "a foreign key is a record" warning;
only the two SQL strings in that one class would need to change). Best-effort throughout - a child whose own
profiling call fails is simply skipped, never fails the whole matching-plan-suggestion route.

### 33.7 Review rendering (`review`)

`ReviewDecisionTree.Field` gained the same `via` property (independently parsed from JSON, per that package's own
"never imports `master`" convention) and a `displayName()`/`isRelation()` pair; `review.FieldWords` gained
`humanize(field, via)` rendering `"Adresse › City"` for a relation field. Wired into
`review.MatchPlanTreeDiagram`'s three field-name-rendering call sites (the node body text, the join-helper, and the
per-node detail table) - the tree diagram is the one screen a reviewer actually reads a decision tree's own fields
from. `review.MatchPlanView`'s separate per-field EVIDENCE table (`MatchPlanFieldEvidence`, a pre-existing,
unrelated measurement of the parent's own attributes) was left untouched - it has no notion of a child attribute in
this lot, and folding relation evidence into it was out of scope.

### 33.8 Trigger modes and timing (item 6 - reported 2026-09-26, execution mode fixed the same day, see §33.10)

`MatchingPolicyTranslator.buildMatchingPolicy` used to hardcode `matchingOnCreation = 1` and `matchingOnUpdate = 1` -
`ExecuteMatchingOnCreationEnumeration`'s own `1 = AFTER_SUBMISSION` (CLAUDE.md §8's own javap-derived enum: `0 =
MANUAL`, `1 = AFTER_SUBMISSION`, `2 = BEFORE_CREATION`, `3 = INLINE_MATCHING`) - confirmed by re-reading this file's
own §26/28 (`docs/MATCHING.md` lines ~4359-4374): only the throwaway preview policy is ever written MANUAL
(`0`/`0`); every REAL policy this factory generates runs AFTER_SUBMISSION on both creation and update, of the
ENTITY'S OWN ROW.

**Grepped the whole codebase for anything that would make a CHILD row's own creation/update re-trigger its PARENT's
matching: nothing found.** `matchingOnCreation`/`matchingOnUpdate` are per-table settings on the entity's OWN
matching policy; nothing in `ebx.MatchingConfigurator`, `MasterLoader`, or the workflow pipeline (`docs/MATCHING.md`
§22's transfer workflow) declares a trigger, EBX Script `osd:trigger`, or any other mechanism that re-saves or
re-matches a parent row because one of its children changed. Concretely, for the three modes this file's own
`mdm-factory-matching-trigger-modes` decision covers:

- **AFTER_SUBMISSION (the one the Factory always writes)**: matching for a parent runs the moment THAT PARENT ROW is
  saved. If the load pipeline inserts every parent row before any child row exists (the live, measured shape of
  "flat source -> parent + child" via Connectors, `connectors-flat-source-to-parent-child.md`: a PARENT mapping
  creates the parent by its own source key, a SEPARATE CHILD mapping then creates child rows pointing back at it -
  two distinct `connectors_sync` runs, not one write per source row), every parent's creation-time match runs
  against ZERO child rows, structurally - the relation field's `DO_NOTHING` null-handling then withholds any
  evidence-based confirmation for that run by design (never a wrong confirmation), but it also means the RUN NEVER
  HAPPENS AGAIN once the children do load, unless the parent row is saved a second time for some unrelated reason
  (an update). A parent whose only ever save was its creation-time insert keeps whatever match/suspect verdict it
  got with no child evidence at all, indefinitely, even after its addresses are loaded.
- **BEFORE_CREATION**: not used by this factory's own generated policies; not investigated further here.
- **INLINE_MATCHING**: not used by this factory's own generated policies; not investigated further here.

**So: yes, a parent's matching can (and, for the Factory's own load order, structurally WILL) run before its
children are loaded, in the mode the Factory actually uses; no, a change on a child row does not re-trigger the
parent's matching, in any mode.** This was a real functional gap for the relation-fields feature specifically (its
whole point is comparing child evidence, which may simply not exist yet at the one moment matching runs) - originally
just REPORTED (the task brief's own item 6 only asked for that), then FIXED the same day, on coordinator review: see
§33.10 for the execution-mode change (`matchingOnCreation`/`matchingOnUpdate` = MANUAL for a relation-field policy)
and what is STILL not fixed by it (the automatic-intake gap below).

**Still open even after §33.10's fix**: MANUAL only stops the WRONG-TIME automatic run - it does not, by itself,
guarantee the RIGHT-TIME one happens. The explicit `MATCHING_RUN` step (`ebx.MatchingConfigurator#run`, scoped by
`master.MatchingRunScope`) is a step of the pipeline this factory's own workflow/API callers already trigger once a
load is considered complete (`docs/MATCHING.md` §22's transfer workflow, or a direct `POST .../matching/run`) - for
a relation-field entity, that step must run AFTER both the parent's own load AND every one of its children's loads
have completed, not merely after the parent's. Nothing today enforces that ordering automatically: whoever launches
`MATCHING_RUN` (the pipeline/workflow, or a person) must know to wait for the children too. This becomes acute for
the planned **automatic intake** lot (`mdm-factory-automatic-intake.md`, landing-to-master with no REST call, "calm
+ wake by trigger"): that lot's own design MUST run matching only after a parent's children have themselves reached
master, not merely after the parent row itself has - otherwise MANUAL mode (§33.10) simply moves the same race from
"never re-runs automatically" to "the one explicit run also sees zero child rows, and, being MANUAL, never gets a
second chance either." This is flagged here for whoever designs that lot; not addressed by this lot.

`tools/test_local.sh` green (compiles and every JUnit-free test class passes) after this lot, and again after the
§33.10/§33.11 coordinator-review changes. New/changed tests as of the ORIGINAL lot: `DecisionTreePlanTest`
(via/dataType round-trip, `labelFor`, four `validate(..., RelationCatalog, ...)` cases, `relationFromNestedField`'s
assumed shape and its negative case), `MatchingPolicyTranslatorTest` (placeholder picked + spec built,
no-eligible-placeholder refusal, an ordinary plan with no relation field is unaffected), `MatchingPolicyComparatorTest`
(unrelinked placeholder, relinked with mapping, relinked without mapping), `MatchPlanLlmPassTest` (a relation field
accepted in a SUSPECTED node and written with `via`/`dataType`; refused on an unknown child, on an unknown child
attribute, and alone at the root). §33.10/§33.11 REPLACED/ADDED the MATCH-terminal-specific cases and the execution-
mode cases - see those sections' own test lists.

**Never run live** (no `match-merge` write access, no EBX instance touched this session, per the task's own rules):
`mcpgap.RelationFieldRelinker.relink` itself (still throws `UnsupportedOperationException` - implemented by another
agent in parallel, not called by any test here), the real read-back shape of a relinked relationship field
(`relationFromNestedField`'s own documented assumption), `ebx.RelationRowCountMeasures`'s SQL statement (built by

executed against a real table), and the whole prompt/guard chain against a real language model (whether a model

### 33.10 Coordinator review of ef72fc9 (same day) - MATCH-terminal relation fields, shape-guarded not banned

The original lot refused a relation field outright inside any MATCH-terminal node - **wrong**, per the product owner's own
first business case: "parent identity similar AND an exact, precise child key in common -&gt; MATCH" is exactly the
"agreement on PRECISE child evidence can by itself help CONFIRM a match" half of `userPrompt`'s own graded principle
(§33.6), which the outright ban directly contradicted. Replaced with a shape rule in the same spirit as
`Session#checkParentConfirmationNodeShape` (§7's own parent-confirmation-node discipline), split across a per-field
half (checked at construction time, in `appendRelationField`) and a structural half (checked once per plan, in a new
post-loop method, `Session#checkRelationMatchNodeShape`, called from `proposeMatchPlan` right next to
`checkParentConfirmationNodeShape`):

- **Per-field** (`appendRelationField`): a node whose `onFalse` is `MATCH` may never contain a relation field at
  all, whatever the algorithm - a condition FAILING must never itself confirm a match. A node whose `onTrue` is
  `MATCH` may only contain a relation field compared with the exact algorithm at `minimumScore` 100 (a PRECISE key)
  - a fuzzy algorithm or a coarse threshold can only ever route to `SUSPECTED` or another node.
- **Structural** (`checkRelationMatchNodeShape`): a node comparing a relation field and routing `onTrue` to `MATCH`
  can never be the plan's `root`; it must be reached ONLY via another node's `onTrue` (never `onFalse` - a precise
  child key must never rescue a pair the entity's own fields already found dissimilar); and that reaching node must
  itself compare at least one of the entity's own NON-REFERENCE, NON-RELATION identity fields (never another
  relation-only or REFERENCE-only check) - the exact same three-part discipline `checkParentConfirmationNodeShape`
  already established for a REFERENCE field's own confirmation node, applied here to a relation-evidence MATCH node
  instead.

Both the tool schema's `via` property description and the `userPrompt`'s "Relation evidence" principle paragraph
were reworded to state this same rule (never "never usable in a MATCH-terminal node" - all three texts now agree:
schema, prompt, and the guard code itself).

**Tests replaced/added** in `MatchPlanLlmPassTest` (the old, single `relationField_refusedInMatchTerminalNode` case
removed, since the rule it tested no longer holds): `relationMatchNode_acceptedInCanonicalShape` (the canonical
two-level shape: an AVERAGE identity node on the entity's own `lastName`, onTrue leading to an ALL_FIELDS node on
`cityKey` via `Adresse` at exact/100, onTrue MATCH onFalse SUSPECTED - accepted, and the written JSON checked field
by field), `relationMatchNode_refusedAsRoot` (the relation-evidence MATCH node IS the root - refused), 
`relationMatchNode_refusedWhenReachedThroughOnFalse` (reached via the identity node's `onFalse`, not `onTrue` -
refused), `relationMatchNode_refusedWhenNodeAboveHasNoOwnIdentityField` (a three-node chain where the node
immediately above the MATCH node itself compares only ANOTHER relation field, never a real identity field of the
entity - refused, naming that middle node), `relationMatchNode_refusedWhenRelationFieldIsFuzzy` (the identity node is
correctly shaped, but the relation field itself uses a fuzzy algorithm on the MATCH branch - refused, naming "PRECISE
key"), `relationMatchNode_refusedWhenOnFalseIsMatch` (a relation-bearing node whose own `onFalse` is `MATCH` -
refused, regardless of algorithm). `tools/test_local.sh`: all green.

**Not run live** - same discipline as the rest of this lot: whether a real language model, given the reworded
prompt/schema, actually proposes the two-level canonical shape for a precise-key confirmation (rather than the
simpler, now-forbidden single-node MATCH-terminal shape it might still try) is unknown.

### 33.11 Coordinator review of ef72fc9 (same day) - execution mode: MANUAL for a relation-field policy

§33.8's own finding (a parent is created, and under AFTER_SUBMISSION matched, before its children; a child change
never re-triggers the parent) is now ACTED ON, not merely reported: `MatchingPolicyTranslator.buildMatchingPolicyFromPlan`
writes `matchingOnCreation`/`matchingOnUpdate` as **0/0 (MANUAL)**, instead of the previously-hardcoded 1/1
(AFTER_SUBMISSION), whenever the tree being translated contains at least one relation field anywhere (`hasAnyRelationField`,
a plain scan of every node's fields for `FieldRef#isRelation()` - works identically whether the plan handed to it is
the ORIGINAL, un-substituted one or the one `buildMatchingPolicyWithRelationFields` has already placeholder-substituted,
since that substitution only ever rewrites a relation field's own `field` name, never clears its `via`). **This is
PERMANENT code** - unlike the placeholder/relink workaround (§33.2), it has nothing to do with the MCP write gap and
stays exactly as-is once the vendor fixes it: the reason for MANUAL is entirely about WHEN matching should run
relative to the load, never about how the field is written to the add-on. With MANUAL, the explicit `MATCHING_RUN`
step (`ebx.MatchingConfigurator#run`, scoped by `master.MatchingRunScope`) becomes the ONLY mechanism that applies
matching for such an entity - see §33.8's own updated "still open" paragraph for what this does and does not
guarantee on its own (it stops the wrong-time automatic run; it does not by itself guarantee a right-time explicit
one for the automatic-intake lot still to come).

**Comparator**: already safe by construction, not something this change needed to add - `MatchingPolicyComparator`'s
own Javadoc has always listed `matchingOnCreation`/`matchingOnUpdate` among the fields "Deliberately NOT compared",
and grepping the class confirms neither name is read anywhere in it. A policy that flips from 1/1 to 0/0 (an entity
whose plan gains its first relation field) or the other way round therefore never shows up as `decisionTreeChanged`
or any other `Diff` flag - confirmed by a new test, `compare_matchingOnCreationUpdateDifference_neverCountedAsDrift`
(builds the SAME policy twice, differing only in `matchingOnCreation`/`matchingOnUpdate`, asserts `diff.same()`).

**Tests**: `MatchingPolicyTranslatorTest#relationFields_writtenManual_matchingOnCreationAndUpdateAreZero` (a
relation-field plan translated through `buildMatchingPolicyWithRelationFields` gets 0/0),
`#ordinaryPlan_matchingOnCreationAndUpdateAreOne` (an ordinary plan through plain `buildMatchingPolicy` keeps 1/1,
unchanged behaviour), `MatchingPolicyComparatorTest#compare_matchingOnCreationUpdateDifference_neverCountedAsDrift`
(above). `tools/test_local.sh`: all green.

### 33.12 Native since 6.3.0.5-RC3 (lot W13, 2026-10-12)

Measured live on EBX 6.3.0-rc3 + Match and Merge 6.3.0.5-RC3, scratch model `W13BO` (dataspace and dataset of the same name), 4 persons and their addresses:

1. **The `match-merge` server handles relation fields through a BUSINESS OBJECT.** A matching-policy field carries `businessObjectField`, the ABSOLUTE path of
   the member table's field (`/root/Adresse/city`), instead of `field`; the server sets `useRelationships = BY_FOREIGN_KEY` and `location {associationTable:
   /root/Adresse/personneRef, mode: SAME_DATASET}` from the business object relationship (they are not sent: sent to `generate_matching_policy` with
   `businessObject` they must name the relationship the server derives). In the decision tree the field is `field = /root/Adresse/city` (and `businessObjectField`
   with the same value; `field` alone is what the validator requires) and reads back with `field` only. `generate_matching_policy(table=/root/Personne,
   businessObject=/root/Personne, dataModel=urn:ebx:publication:<pub>, matchingPolicy={...})` accepts it; `patch_matching_config` ops take
   `target.businessObjectField` instead of `target.field` for such a field. `validate_matching_config` takes exactly one of `table` / `businessObject`;
   `apply_matching_config` REJECTS `businessObject` by contract.
2. **Activation.** `activate_matching` on a member table is refused ("part of a business object; use activate_business_object_matching");
   `activate_business_object_matching(businessObject, dataModel)` activates every member (main table AND child: a metadataset for both);
   `get_business_object_activation_status` reads `overallState` and `members[]{table, state, published, paused, metadatasetExists}` (a member with no
   configuration is omitted). `get_business_object_config` answers `BUSINESS_OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` for a table that is not a main table. Like the table tools,
   the business-object tools need `dataModel` (`MameCalls.call` sends it).
3. **The business object is declared on the master DMA model** with the `data-model` server: `execute_operation(enable_extension, {"extension":"businessObjects"})`,
   `create_business_object {name, main_table}`, `add_business_object_relationship {business_object_name, relationship_path}`, then `publish_data_model`. The
   relationship MUST be carried by the MAIN table: an inverse association (`create_field /root/Personne/adresses` string as the host field, then `set_association
   {field_path=/root/Personne/adresses, mode=tableRefInverse, fk_field_path=/root/Adresse/personneRef}`). Passing the child's foreign key as the relationship is
   refused at publication ("recursive business object models are not supported").
4. **End to end:** the run (`POST /ebx-addon-mame/rest/v1/matchingProcesses`) over the 4 persons (3 homonyms, 2 at the same city through `Adresse`) produced
   exactly the pair P1-P2 in `Suspected`; P3 (same name, other city) was excluded.

What the Factory does with it:

- **Master generation** (`ebx.MasterBusinessObjects`, pure decisions in `master.BusinessObjectPlan`; called by `MasterGenerator` before every publish, the
  UP_TO_DATE branch included): for every promoted parent table with promoted child tables, one inverse association per child on the PARENT (host field named
  after the child, `Adresse` -> `adresses`, `_assoc` suffix when taken), the `businessObjects` extension, ONE business object `<Parent>BO`, one relationship per
  child. Idempotent (`BusinessObjectPlan.reconcile`): a second generation writes nothing, an interrupted one resumes at the missing write; an association over the
  same foreign key is reused whatever its name. A refused write ends THAT declaration (a half-declared object would fail the publication) and is a note in the step;
  a self-reference is never a child; a child with two foreign keys to the same parent gets one relationship (the other is listed in `skippedForeignKeys`). A master
  with no child entity declares nothing.
- **Translation** (`MatchingPolicyTranslator.translate`, the ONE path): a relation field (`via`) becomes a policy field `businessObjectField = /root/<ChildTable>/<field>`
  (no `field`) and a tree field `field` + `businessObjectField` of the same path. The pre-clustering weight rule is unchanged (§48: `relationClusteringWeights`, default 0,
  the field is compared in the tree but out of the candidate search); a relation field is counted once, through that weight, in the dominance sum. Node names stay
  the plan's labels (frozen before the rewrite).
- **Configuration** (`MatchingConfigurator.configureOne`, `MameBusinessObjects`): `get_business_object_config(businessObject=<candidate>)` for each candidate main
  table of the entity (its own table when it has children, then each parent's) tells which are declared. `BusinessObjectPlan.route`: a declared object -> the
  business-object tools (`businessObject` on `generate_matching_policy`, `generate_merge_policy`, `patch_matching_config`; `validate_matching_config` with
  `businessObject` instead of `table`; `activate_business_object_matching` + `get_business_object_activation_status`, the table must read ready); no object and a plan
  with relation fields -> the coded refusal `missing.businessObject` (no silent fallback); no object and no relation field -> the table tools, as before.
  `set_trusted_sources`, `set_table_settings`, `get_matching_config` stay table-level; `apply_matching_config` stays for a table that is in no business object only. The simulation preview uses the same scope and, when
  the table has no object, simulates the plan WITHOUT its relation tiers and says so (`RelationTierStripper`, unchanged); the activation guard repairs a member through
  `activate_business_object_matching`.
- **Three more facts, measured on W13BO the same day (after the lot was written), which changed it:**
  1. `apply_matching_config(table=/root/Personne, config={matchingPolicies:[<BO policy>], mergePolicies:[]})` is REFUSED on a business-object member, with or without
     `businessObject`: `INVALID_PARAMS "Table /root/Personne is part of a business object; use the business-object tools instead"`. On such a table it is never used: the REWRITE
     branch goes through `generate_matching_policy` + `generate_merge_policy` with `businessObject` and the `set_merge_policy_link` patch (`BusinessObjectPlan.writeMode` /
     `mayUseApplyMatchingConfig`, `MatchingConfigurator.writePoliciesThroughGenerate`) for a policy that does not exist yet. **The same-`processCode` replacement this item first
     recorded was an assumption, refuted the same night on Vol1mR: see §33.13.** A Simulate preview rewrite uses the same tools (only the preview's own `processCode` is
     replaced, the real policies are not touched); the removal of a leftover preview is skipped there (no tool deletes one policy), and a REWRITE no longer drops it either.
  2. `generate_merge_policy(table, businessObject, mergePolicy={... relatedTables:[{path:/root/Adresse, name, alignForeignKeys:"NONE"}]})` is REFUSED (`INVALID_PARAMS "Related table path '/root/Adresse' is
     not a related table of this table: this table has no related table"`); without `relatedTables` it succeeds and reads back `relatedTables: []`. On a business-object table the child
     relationship replaces the related-table alignment (the add-on cascades through the object), so `alignRelatedTables` is SKIPPED there (`BusinessObjectPlan.alignsRelatedTables`), in the
     fresh branch, in the convergence step and in the final check; the step detail says `alignRelatedTables: {skipped: "business object"}`.
  3. `patch_matching_config(table, businessObject, dataModel, operations=[{op:set_merge_policy_link,...},{op:set_field_weight,target:{policyCode, businessObjectField:"/root/Adresse/city"},value:"0"}])`
     works and reads back (weight 0 on the relation field, link set): `target.businessObjectField` is the key for a relation field in a patch.
- **A fourth fact, measured the same day:** `delete_matching_config` on a business-object member is REFUSED ("Table /root/Personne is part of a business object; use the business-object
  tools instead"), also after `delete_business_object` + `publish_data_model` (the add-on keeps its own business-object record and the `TableConfiguration` rows of the model); the
  match-merge server has no business-object delete tool. The project deletion and the step cleanup therefore report such a configuration as `KEPT_BUSINESS_OBJECT`
  (`engine.external.matchingConfigKeptBusinessObject`), never as a failure, and say when the model or dataspace deletion leaves the rows orphaned (`docs/PROJECT-DELETION.md`).
- **Still not verified live:** the activation of a business object whose child has no configuration yet (the child entity is
  configured after its parent). The first configure of a relation-field plan checks it: the step detail keeps every call (`activateBusinessObjects`).
- A caution that stays (seen on 6.3.0-rc2): a business object whose member table has no matching configuration broke every after-submission matching of its main
  table. Relation-field policies are written MANUAL (0/0), and the child entity gets its own policy; configure the child before running matching.

### 33.13 A business-object table is rewritten in place, and a member takes no execution mode (lot W13b, 2026-10-12)

Two findings from Vol1mR (EBX 6.3.0-rc3 + Match and Merge 6.3.0.5-RC3, Factory 97a2b68a, native business-object route; `PipelineStep` 1433-1436):

1. **A MEMBER table refuses the execution-mode fields.** `generate_matching_policy(table=/root/Adresse, businessObject=/root/Personne, matchingPolicy={..., matchingOnCreation: 1,
   matchingOnUpdate: 1})` answered `INVALID_PARAMS "Could not persist matching policy: An element may not be updated (no write permission on the following element:
   \"/executeMatching/matchingExecOnUpdate\")"`. The SAME policy without the two fields was accepted (read back with both at 0); the main table (Personne) accepts them. The
   object drives the matching of its members. Rule (`BusinessObjectPlan.isMember` = a business-object table that is not the object's main table): a member's policy is sent and
   compared without `matchingOnCreation` / `matchingOnUpdate` (`dropExecutionModesOfMember`, step detail `executionModesOmitted`), `ensureExecutionMode` and its
   `set_execution_mode` patch are not run (`executionMode: {skipped: "business object member"}`), and the step message says "the matching of this table follows its business object
   <main>" instead of an execution mode (`triggerModeSentence`). The Simulate preview policy (`MatchingPreviewPolicy`, 0/0) still sends the fields: **not fixed here, probably refused
   the same way on a member** (to measure).
2. **`generate_matching_policy` does not replace a policy.** A second `configure` (steps 1435 Personne, 1436 Adresse; `failedPhase "writing the matching/merge policy via MCP
   (REWRITE)"`) answered `INVALID_PARAMS "A matching policy with processCode 'Personne' already exists on this table. ... Use patch_matching_config to change it, or choose another
   processCode."` (§33.12 item 1 assumed replacement). On a business-object table a rewrite can therefore go neither through `apply_matching_config` nor through the generate tools,
   and the two steps showed two different causes:
   - Personne: the comparison said `differs: merge policy related tables (alignForeignKeys)` and nothing else. A business-object table does not align related tables (§33.12 item 2;
     the add-on reads `MANUAL` back), so the comparison no longer looks at them there (`BusinessObjectPlan.comparisonChildTablePaths`): that configure resumes (`RESUME_SAME`).
   - Adresse: the matching policy was stored and identical, `mergePolicies` was `[]` and the policy linked to no merge policy (the first attempt, step 1433, had died after the
     matching policy). A merge policy that does not exist is created with `generate_merge_policy`, which is additive.

   **The rewrite** (`MatchingConfigurator.rewriteBusinessObjectPolicies`, decided by the pure `master.BusinessObjectRewritePlan`): the matching policy is `GENERATE` when none of that
   `processCode` is stored, else `PATCH` (the operations of `master.MatchingPolicyPatchPlanner`) or `NONE`; the merge policy is `GENERATE` when none of that `code` is stored, else
   `PATCH` (`MergeConfigPatchPlanner`: record selection / default / survivor chains) or `NONE`; the link `set_merge_policy_link` is added when anything was generated or the stored policy links
   to another merge policy. The generations run first, then ONE `patch_matching_config` call (matching ops, merge ops, link). Everything identical after the add-on's known read-back differences
   (`jaroWinklerThreshold` 0.7 added, leaf names `Match`/`Suspect`/`Not Match`, `DO_NOTHING` on a tree field read as `NOT_MATCH`, null `dateFieldPath`, execution modes 0 on a member) writes nothing:
   `rewrite: {skipped: "identical"}` in the step detail, and the entity is reported in `skippedAlreadyDone`. A **structural** difference of the decision tree writes nothing and ends in the coded
   refusal `conflict.policyRewriteNeedsManualChange` naming the table, the policy and what differs: delete the policy in the Match and Merge administration screen and configure again.

   The operation for each kind of difference (values are JSON strings; `policyCode` = the entity name; the tree is addressed by the stored node `name`, unique in a tree):

   | Difference | Operation |
   |---|---|
   | policy field only stored / only wanted | `remove_matching_field` / `add_matching_field`, `target {policyCode, field}` (`businessObjectField` for a relation field) |
   | field weight / search strategy | `set_field_weight` (value = integer) / `set_field_preclustering` (value = template key), same target |
   | field null handling (policy fields) | `set_field_null_handling`, `target {policyCode, field, paramName: bothNullValueHandling \| oneNullValueHandling}`, value `DO_NOTHING\|NOT_MATCH\|MATCH` |
   | tree field algorithm | `set_algorithm`, `target {policyCode, decisionTreeNode, field}`, value = algorithm code (before the parameters of the new algorithm) |
   | tree field parameter (`minimumScore`, `weight`, `jaroWinklerThreshold`, ...) or null handling | `set_field_param`, `target {policyCode, decisionTreeNode, field, paramName}`, value (null handling: `MATCH\|NOT_MATCH`) |
   | node `minimumScore` alone | `set_threshold`, `target {policyCode, decisionTreeNode}`, value |
   | node function, or another node-level parameter | `set_decision_node_function`, `target {policyCode, decisionTreeNode}`, value = function, `node: {params: [desired node params]}` (after the node's field ops) |
   | node on one side only, leaf versus comparison, leaf outcome, other set of compared fields | no in-place operation: refusal `conflict.policyRewriteNeedsManualChange` |

   **Not measured live** (no write to the instance in this lot): that `decisionTreeNode` is the node `name` (node names are unique, the add-on rejects a duplicate, and the tree already
   carries the names the Factory wrote), the accepted shape of `node` on `set_decision_node_function`, that `set_threshold` without `field` addresses the node-level `minimumScore`, and one
   `patch_matching_config` call carrying policy-field ops and tree ops together. The first rewrite on a real business-object table checks them (`rewrite.patchMatchingConfig` keeps the call).
   Tests: `BusinessObjectRewritePlanTest` (the Vol1mR Adresse / Personne shapes), `EngineMessageCatalogTest`.

## 34. Relation evidence made required, and observable (lot R3, branch `fix/relation-evidence-required`, 2026-09-26)

Follow-up to §33 (lot R2): a real live run exposed two gaps in the same "child evidence in the parent's matching
plan" feature - reported directly by the product owner from a run on project Personnes (agent run 112, gpt-4o, PipelineStep
439, 2026-09-26 21:42). Master `Personnes_Master/Master`: `Personne` 345 rows, child `Adresse` 345 rows all linked
by FK `personneRef`, `mailingCity`/`mailingPostalCode`/`mailingCountry` filled and cross-system comparable. The
model wrote a full plan for `Personne` (AT_LEAST_N email+phone -> SUSPECTED, else AVERAGE first/last name+birthDate
-> SUSPECTED) using NO relation field at all, and never proposed anything for `Adresse`. Nothing in the run's own
`detail` JSON said whether the evidence had even been offered - `ebx.MatchPlanLlmSuggester.buildRelationChildren`
had five silent `continue` statements (no staging entity, no FK field, the profile call failing two different
ways, no usable child attribute), so "the model ignored it" and "the child was never offered in the first place"
were indistinguishable from the outside.

### 34.1 Observability (`ebx.MatchPlanLlmSuggester`)

`buildRelationChildren` now returns a `RelationChildrenResult` (the same `children` list as before, PLUS a
`RelationEvidenceReport`) instead of a bare list - every one of the five points that used to `continue` silently
now appends a `RelationEvidenceReport.Skipped(childEntity, reason)` first (`"no staging entity found for this
child"`, `"no foreign key field on the child's own master table targets this parent"`, the profiling call's own
error/soft-miss/exception text, `"no usable (accepted, non-technical, non-reference) attribute on the child"`), and
a successfully offered child appends a `RelationEvidenceReport.Offered(childEntity, fkField, attributeCount,
rowStatsMeasured)`. `suggest()` collects one report per entity that had at least one candidate child (both lists
empty otherwise - never stored or logged, there is nothing to say), folds them into the step's own `detail` JSON
under `relationEvidence` (keyed by parent entity name, via the new pure `writeRelationEvidence(ObjectNode,
List<RelationEvidenceReport>)` - omitted entirely when there is nothing to report, same "never an empty key"
discipline as `putStrings`), and logs one `[mdm-factory]`-prefixed INFO line per such parent via the new pure
`relationEvidenceLogLine(RelationEvidenceReport)` (e.g. `"relation evidence for 'Personne': offered Adresse
(fkField=personneRef, attributes=4, rowStats=measured)"`, or `"... no child offered; skipped Contrat (no staging
entity found for this child)"`). Both new methods are pure JSON/string assembly with no EBX/MCP access, unit-tested
directly (`MatchPlanLlmSuggesterRelationEvidenceTest`) - the live MCP-calling half of `buildRelationChildren` itself
still needs a real server and is not exercised by a test, same split `MatchPlanLlmSuggesterIdentityKeyTest` already
established for `chooseIdentityKeyField`.

### 34.2 Required consideration (`master.MatchPlanLlmPass`)

An entity with relation evidence (`EntityInfo.relationChildren` non-empty) whose `propose_match_plan` call uses NO
relation field anywhere in the tree is now refused ONCE, naming the child(ren) and their attributes - the exact
same one-shot "challenge, then accept the resubmission regardless" mechanism `Session#challengedSkips`/{@code
parentLinkSkipChallenge} already established for a child's skipped parent reference (§32), reused rather than
duplicated: a new pure decision, `MatchPlanLlmPass.relationEvidenceRequiredChallenge(EntityInfo, DecisionTreePlan.Plan)`
(null when the entity has no relation evidence, or when the plan already carries at least one field with a
non-blank `via` anywhere), and a new `Session` field, `challengedRelationRequirement` (a `Set<String>` of entity
names, exactly like `challengedSkips`), checked in `proposeMatchPlan` right after the existing
`requireParentConfirmationNodeForChild` check. The refusal text: `"'<entity>' has child evidence <child>: <attr1>,
<attr2>; namesakes attached to different child rows must not be confirmed as the same record on the parent's own
fields alone. Either add a node comparing the child evidence as described in the prompt, or call 'note' explaining
why it cannot help, then resubmit."` An identical second submission with still no relation field is accepted
(`challengedRelationRequirement.add` returns `false` the second time, same bookkeeping as a second `skip_entity`
call) - the model (or, in review, a person) gets exactly one nudge, never a hard block.

### 34.3 Prompt (`master.MatchPlanLlmPass#userPrompt`)

A one-line header flag, right after the entity's own name/row-count line and BEFORE its attribute list even starts
(the existing, more detailed "Relation evidence" section from §33.6 stays exactly where it was, right after the
attribute list): `"Has child evidence: <child> (<n> attribute(s)) - see 'Relation evidence' below. A matching plan
for this entity is EXPECTED to use it: either add a node comparing the child evidence as described there, or
explain in your rationale why it cannot help (e.g. no useful precise key on the child)."` - rendered only when
`EntityInfo.relationChildren` is non-empty, never for an ordinary entity. Deliberately placed at the very top of
the entity's own block so a model skimming the prompt cannot miss it the way run 112 apparently did with the
detailed section alone.

### 34.4 Findings against the task's own item 5 (checked, not changed - neither is broken)

- **`TechnicalKeyRule.isAcceptedLike`** accepts exactly `"ACCEPTED"` and `"APPLIED"` - Personnes' attributes being
  `APPLIED` are correctly treated as accepted-like everywhere this lot touches (`buildRelationChildren`'s own
  child-attribute filter included). Nothing to fix.
- **`MatchPlanLlmPass.deriveRole(null, false, Collections.<Boolean>emptyList())`** (the call `buildRelationChildren`
  makes for every child attribute) can NEVER return `ROLE_SOURCE_KEY`: that branch requires
  `!pMappingsAreOnSourceKeyColumns.isEmpty() && !pMappingsAreOnSourceKeyColumns.contains(Boolean.FALSE)`, and an
  empty list makes `!isEmpty()` false, short-circuiting straight to `ROLE_BUSINESS`. The `if
  (ROLE_SOURCE_KEY.equals(role)) continue;` guard right after it in `buildRelationChildren` is therefore dead code
  for every call site that exists today - harmless (a defensive floor that never fires, not a bug), left as-is
  rather than removed: if a future revision ever starts passing real per-mapping booleans for a child attribute
  (there is currently no source-key concept computed for a CHILD table's own attributes, only for the ENTITY the
  main pass profiles), the guard would then do real work without anyone having to remember to re-add it.

### 34.5 Tests and what remains unverified live

`tools/test_local.sh`: all green. New tests: `MatchPlanLlmSuggesterRelationEvidenceTest` (§34.1's two pure methods:
`writeRelationEvidence` omits the key when empty and writes offered/skipped correctly keyed and shaped;
`relationEvidenceLogLine` for offered-only, skipped-only, both, and neither); `MatchPlanLlmPassTest` gained
`relationEvidenceRequiredChallenge_*` (null with no relation evidence, null when the plan already uses a relation
field, the message names the entity/child/attributes and points at `'note'`/resubmit),
`relationEvidenceRequired_refusedOnceThenAcceptedOnSecondSubmission` (full `propose_match_plan` round trip: first
submission refused and nothing recorded, identical second submission accepted and recorded),
`relationEvidenceRequired_neverRefusedWhenPlanUsesARelationField`,
`relationEvidenceRequired_neverRefusedWhenNoRelationEvidence`, and `userPrompt_hasChildEvidenceHeaderLine` (the
header line renders for the entity with evidence, naming child and attribute count, and is absent from a plain
entity's own section in the same prompt).

**Never run live** (no EBX/`match-merge` write access in the session that wrote this lot, same discipline as §33.9):
whether `buildRelationChildren`'s new report actually reads as intended in a real `kernel.log`/step-detail JSON
against a live instance, and whether a real language model, given the new header line and the one-shot refusal,
actually reaches for a relation field on the resubmission rather than merely repeating the same plan unchanged (a
repeated identical submission is accepted either way, per §34.2 - this lot cannot make the model propose GOOD
evidence, only make it impossible to silently ignore that evidence exists).

### 34.6 Two more fixes from a second live failure (PersVol5, PipelineStep 472, 2026-09-26)

`MATCHING_CONFIG` FAILED for `Personne`: `generate_matching_policy` answered `INVALID_PARAMS "The outputs from
the Same Adresse.emailKey data comparison node cannot connect to the same type of relationship status"`. The
stored plan's node `N2` had exactly ONE relation field (`Adresse.City`) whose `onTrue` and `onFalse` were BOTH
`SUSPECTED`.

**Fix A - node-naming bug (`master.MatchingPolicyTranslator#buildMatchingPolicyWithRelationFields`).**
`DecisionTreePlan.labelFor(node)` auto-generates a label from the node's CURRENT fields when `Node.label` is
blank, and the substitution loop mutates `field.field` IN PLACE (the relation field's own child name becomes a
placeholder parent field name). The method used to call `labelFor` INSIDE the per-field loop, AFTER any earlier
field of the SAME node had already been substituted - so (a) a second relation field of the same node got a
different `nodeName` than the first, and (b) `buildMatchingPolicyFromPlan`'s own later call to `toNested`
recomputed the SAME auto-label a THIRD time, once every substitution in the whole plan had already run,
disagreeing with either. This is exactly how the error above happened: the node's ORIGINAL label (from its
original field, before substitution) was "Same Adresse.City", but by the time `toNested` computed the add-on's
own stored name, the field had already become the placeholder, and the auto-label read "Same Adresse.emailKey"
instead - two different strings for the same node, so `mcpgap.RelationFieldRelinker` (which looks the node up by
name) could never have found it even if the call had succeeded.

Fixed by freezing every node's `label` (via `labelFor`, from the ORIGINAL fields) in one pass, BEFORE the
substitution loop runs at all. `labelFor` already prefers a non-blank `Node.label` over recomputing, so every
later read (the spec's own `nodeName`, and `toNested`'s "name") now returns the identical, frozen string.
`master.MatchingPolicyTranslator`'s own Javadoc gained a "Node naming" paragraph documenting this.

Tests (`MatchingPolicyTranslatorTest`): `relationFields_nodeNameKeptPreSubstitution_matchesTheWrittenPolicy` (one
relation field: the spec's `nodeName` equals `decisionTree.name` in the written policy, and never mentions the
placeholder's own substituted field name), `relationFields_twoRelationFieldsInOneNode_shareOneNodeName` (two
relation fields of the same node produce two specs sharing one `nodeName`, matching the written policy).

**Fix B - generic plan guard, `SAME_OUTCOME_BOTH_BRANCHES` (`master.DecisionTreePlan#validate`).** A node whose
`onTrue` and `onFalse` name the EXACT SAME target (a leaf, e.g. both `SUSPECTED`, or the same node id) decides
nothing - the comparison never changes where a pair ends up - and `match-merge` itself refuses it with the
uninformative message quoted above. This is a plain structural defect of ANY plan, not specific to a relation
field (the field that happened to trip it here was a relation field, but the rule has nothing to do with `via`).
Added as a new per-node check inside `validateNode`, so it runs for every `validate` overload (the plain one, and
the relation-aware one used by `MatchPlanLlmPass.Session#proposeMatchPlan`) with no separate wiring needed.

Because `MatchingPolicyTranslator#buildMatchingPolicyFromPlan` ALREADY calls `DecisionTreePlan.validate(plan)`
and throws `IllegalStateException` on any structural defect - BEFORE `ebx.MatchingConfigurator#configureOne` ever
calls `generate_matching_policy`/`apply_matching_config` - the configure step already refuses a stored plan
carrying this defect with the exact same `SAME_OUTCOME_BOTH_BRANCHES` message, with no MCP call ever attempted;
`configureOne`'s own pre-existing `RuntimeException` catch turns that into a `FAILED` step with a readable
message, same discipline as every other translator-side refusal. No new call site needed in `MatchingConfigurator`
itself - only the validator gained the rule.

Tests: `DecisionTreePlanTest` gained `validate_sameOutcomeBothBranches_sameLeaf_refused` (both branches
`SUSPECTED`), `validate_sameOutcomeBothBranches_sameNodeId_refused` (both branches the same node id, not just the
same leaf), `validate_sameOutcomeBothBranches_differentLeaves_accepted` (the ordinary case is unaffected).
`MatchingPolicyTranslatorTest` gained `buildMatchingPolicy_sameOutcomeBothBranches_refusedBeforeAnyMcpCall`
(`buildMatchingPolicy` itself throws `IllegalStateException` naming the code, proving the configure step's own
pre-MCP guard catches it).

**Side effect on an existing test**: `MatchPlanLlmPassTest#parentConfirmationNode_refusedWhenOnTrueIsNotMatch`
built its confirmation node with `onTrue`/`onFalse` both `SUSPECTED` to isolate the (different)
"must route onTrue to MATCH" check - with the new rule, that input is now (correctly) caught by
`SAME_OUTCOME_BOTH_BRANCHES` first, at the base structural-validation stage, before
`checkParentConfirmationNodeShape` ever runs. Fixed by changing that test's `onFalse` to `NOT_MATCHED` (still wrong
for a confirmation node - a separate, dedicated test already covers that - but no longer identical to `onTrue`),
so the test keeps isolating exactly the check it names.

`tools/test_local.sh`: all green after both fixes.

## 35. Guard ordering and per-entity breaker (lot R4, branch `fix/matching-pass-guard-order`, 2026-09-26)

Follow-up to lot R3 (`sect;34`): a real live run exposed three more gaps in the relation-evidence/child-
confirmation feature - reported directly by the product owner from project Personnes, agent run 127, gpt-4o, PipelineStep
478, 2026-09-26 23:06. `Personne` (parent) has child `Adresse` (fk `personneRef`, 9 attributes) - `relationEvidence`
traced the offer correctly this time (lot R3's own observability), but the run still wrote ZERO plans, Personne
included.

### 35.1 `personneRef` refused inside its own parent confirmation node - the guard and the node contradicted each other

The `Adresse` plan (`N1` AVERAGE on `mailingStreet`/`mailingCity`/`mailingPostalCode`, `N2` `ALL_FIELDS` on
`personneRef` exact/100, `onTrue` MATCH/`onFalse` SUSPECTED - the exact canonical shape `sect;30`/`sect;32`
require) was refused three times in a row by `CrossSystemFieldGuard`: `"'personneRef' cannot be used as a
clustering field or with the exact algorithm: no value is shared between any two of the source systems present
here (SAP 165 filled, SALESFORCE 180 filled)..."`. This is structurally never fixable by resubmitting: a parent's
own reference values are EXPECTED to differ across systems before the parents themselves are merged - detecting
that disagreement (routing to SUSPECTED) is the entire reason the parent confirmation node exists. The guard and
the node's own contract flatly contradicted each other for the one field the node is built around.

**Fix** (`master.MatchPlanLlmPass.Session#buildAndAppendNode`): a `REFERENCE`-role field (`isReference`) is now
exempt from `CrossSystemFieldGuard` (and the dominant-value-shape conflict check right above it, already exempt)
ENTIRELY - never evaluated, not merely never refused. By the time this code runs, the structural checks earlier in
the same method already force it into the single field of its own `ALL_FIELDS` node, exact algorithm,
`minimumScore` 100, `DO_NOTHING` null handling - a "candidate confirmation node" shape - and the post-loop
`checkParentConfirmationNodeShape`/`requireParentConfirmationNodeForChild` checks still enforce the surrounding
`onTrue`/`onFalse` shape, so nothing about "is this field shared/near-unique across systems" was ever a real
question for it. The evidence-recording half of the same block (`pMatchFieldEvidence`, keyed on `matchTerminal &&
!isReference`, which used the now-inner-scoped `shared` variable) moved inside the new `if (!isReference)` guard
alongside it - `isReference` is always false there already, so behaviour is unchanged for every non-REFERENCE
field. The `systemPrompt`'s own REFERENCE-role paragraph gained a sentence stating the same exemption (never a
blocking/clustering field either - see below), so the model is told the same rule the guard now enforces, not the
opposite.

**A REFERENCE field must still never be usable as a blocking/clustering field** - previously true only as a side
effect of `CrossSystemFieldGuard` also (coincidentally) refusing it there; now made an explicit, dedicated check in
the `clusteringFields` loop (`AttributeInfo.ROLE_REFERENCE`, refused with its own message), since removing the
guard from the tier-field path could otherwise have let a REFERENCE field slip through as a clustering field on a
project where it happens to share some values across systems - blocking/pre-clustering on a parent reference would
wrongly split apart pairs the confirmation node exists to bring together, whatever its measured sharing.

Tests (`MatchPlanLlmPassTest`): a new confirmation-node case reproducing the exact Adresse shape and refusal text
above (accepted with the fix), a case proving `personneRef`-shaped exact comparison OUTSIDE a confirmation node
(an ordinary BUSINESS-role field with the same zero-shared-values shape) is still refused by
`CrossSystemFieldGuard` exactly as before, and a case proving a REFERENCE field named in `clusteringFields` is
refused by the new explicit check.

### 35.2 The repeated-refusal breaker was global - one entity's own bad plan stopped every other entity

`Personne`'s own three proposals were each refused for reasons entirely unrelated to `Adresse` (a MATCH-terminal
jarowinkler field, a phone shape conflict, a `hybridFuzzy` missing-runtime-parameter refusal) - but because
`Adresse`'s confirmation-node refusal (`sect;35.1`) tripped the SAME repeated-refusal circuit breaker first, the
whole `Session` was marked `stopped`, and every subsequent tool call - `Personne`'s included - was refused with
"the run is over" regardless of its own content. The run ended having written zero plans for any entity.

**Fix** (`master.MatchPlanLlmPass.Session#refuse`): tripping the threshold (three identical refusals in a row, on
the exact same key - unchanged) no longer sets `this.stopped`. `pKey` always starts with the entity name
(`proposeMatchPlan`/`skipEntity` both build it as `"<entityName>|..."` or the bare `entityName`) - when that name
resolves to a real, not-yet-handled entity, `refuse` now records it into `this.handled` and appends a note
(`"<entity> skipped: refused N times in a row without a genuine change (<message>)"`), exactly like an explicit
`skip_entity` call, and returns a refusal telling the model to move on to a different entity. When the key cannot
be tied to any real entity (an unresolvable/missing `entity` argument), nothing is marked handled, but the run
still never stops - the note names the raw key instead. `Session#stopped`/`#stopReason` are kept (as the seam for
a genuine future GLOBAL limit - turns/tokens - which lives outside this class, in `AgentRuntime`, not inside this
guard), but nothing in this class sets them to `true` any more.

Tests: the pre-existing `earlyStopOnRepeatedRefusal` (an unresolvable entity, `"Ghost"`, refused three times) was
rewritten for the new contract - never stops the run, a note names the raw key, and a SUBSEQUENT, valid call for a
REAL entity still succeeds (previously refused with "the run is over"). A new
`perEntityStopDoesNotStopOtherEntities` reproduces the live bug directly: a REAL entity (`Company`) refused three
times identically is recorded as skipped by name, and a DIFFERENT entity (`Vendor`) proposed right after still
gets its plan created; a later call for `Company` itself is refused as already recorded (handled), never
re-litigated.

### 35.3 `relationEvidenceRequiredChallenge` lost every race against an unrelated per-field refusal

Lot R3's challenge (`sect;34.2`) only ran AFTER the entire node-building loop succeeded - i.e., after every
per-field guard (`CrossSystemFieldGuard`, the phone/shape-conflict check, the algorithm allow-list, the
`hybridFuzzy` missing-parameter refusal, etc.) had already passed for every field in the submission. On the live
run, `Personne`'s three attempts were each refused by one of those unrelated per-field guards first, so the
relation-evidence challenge - the one guard actually relevant to what was reported as the bug - never even ran
before the (now-fixed, `sect;35.2`) breaker gave up on the entity.

**Fix**: a new overload, `MatchPlanLlmPass.relationEvidenceRequiredChallenge(EntityInfo, JsonNode)`, evaluates the
same question ("does any field carry a non-blank `via`") directly against the RAW `propose_match_plan` arguments -
scanning both the current `nodes[]` wire shape and the legacy `tiers[]` shape for a `fields[].via` - instead of an
already-built, already-validated `DecisionTreePlan.Plan` (which does not exist yet at this point in the call). The
Plan-based overload is kept (existing unit tests call it directly with a hand-built `Plan`); both now share one
private message builder, `relationEvidenceRequiredMessage`, so the challenge text is identical either way.
`Session#proposeMatchPlan` calls the new overload immediately after `legacyTiersShape` is computed - before a
single node is built or a single per-field guard runs - using the SAME one-shot `challengedRelationRequirement`
bookkeeping as before (`add(entityName)` returns `true` only the first time). The old post-node-building call site
is now unreachable dead weight and was removed (by the time execution would have reached it, the early call has
already returned the challenge, or the plan is known to use a relation field, or the entity was already
challenged) - documented in place rather than silently deleted.

Tests: a case combining a bad phone-shape-conflict field AND no relation field on the first submission - the
relation-evidence challenge fires first (not the phone refusal), naming the child and its attributes; the
resubmission (still carrying the bad phone field) then goes through the ordinary per-field guards and is refused
for the phone shape conflict instead, proving the challenge is one-shot and the ordinary guards resume normally
afterward. The three pre-existing `relationEvidenceRequired_*` round-trip tests (first-submission challenge,
already-uses-a-relation-field, no-relation-evidence-at-all) pass unchanged against the new call site.

### 35.4 What was verified vs. not

**Verified** (`tools/test_local.sh`, all green): every change above against hand-built fixtures reproducing the
live run's own shapes structurally (Personne/Adresse via `personneRef`, never any other project's field names).

**NOT verified** (no EBX/`match-merge`/LLM access this session, same discipline as every prior lot in this file):
whether a real re-run of project Personnes with these three fixes now produces a working `Adresse` plan and a
`Personne` plan that actually uses the relation evidence, and whether a real language model, given the challenge
firing before the phone/shape refusals, converges faster or simply hits a different guard on its next attempt, is
unmeasured.

## 36. Lot R5 — relinker NPE, downgrade-collision collapse, and the confirmation node's onFalse reversal (branch `fix/relink-npe-and-downgrade-collision`, 2026-09-27)

Fixes two live failures reported from project PersVol6 (2026-09-27 00:26, PipelineStep 525/526), plus a decision
the product owner made the same day that supersedes §12.7/§30's 2026-09-23 rule.

### 36.1 `RelationFieldRelinker` NPE — a doubled schema-path segment

**The bug.** `RelationFieldRelinker`'s `DN_FIELD_ADVANCED_BOTH_NULL`/`DN_FIELD_ADVANCED_ONE_NULL` constants were
declared as `Path.parse("./advancedSettings/bothValuesNull")`/`Path.parse("./advancedSettings/oneValueNull")` —
correct as an absolute-from-`fields` path, but every call site resolved them a SECOND time, relative to the
ALREADY-resolved `advancedSettings` node (`advancedNode.getNode(DN_FIELD_ADVANCED_BOTH_NULL)`), which looks for
`advancedSettings/advancedSettings/bothValuesNull` — doesn't exist, resolves to `null`, and the first
`executeRead`/`executeWrite` on it throws `NullPointerException: Cannot invoke SchemaNode.executeRead(Object)
because pAdvancedBothNode is null`. PipelineStep 525 (`Personne`, MATCHING_CONFIG) failed exactly this way, at
`RelationFieldRelinker.copyFieldOccurrence:810` ← `relinkOccurrence:779`. Confirmed against
`ebx-addon-mame-configuration.xsd` directly (RC2 and the running dev instance, both re-checked 2026-09-27):
`bothValuesNull`/`oneValueNull` are direct children of `fields/advancedSettings`, not of `fields` itself — every
OTHER `DN_FIELD_*` constant one level under `fields` (`field`, `algorithm`, `useAssociation`, `fieldParams`,
`advancedSettings` itself) was already correct; only the two nested under `advancedSettings` doubled the segment.

**The fix.** `DN_FIELD_ADVANCED_BOTH_NULL`/`DN_FIELD_ADVANCED_ONE_NULL` are now `Path.parse("./bothValuesNull")`/
`Path.parse("./oneValueNull")`, resolved relative to the ALREADY-resolved `advancedSettings` node (matching how
every call site actually uses them — `advancedNode.getNode(...)`). The plan's own "two relation fields in one
node relink correctly" requirement was already structurally exercised by the pre-existing
`relationFields_twoRelationFieldsInOneNode_shareOneNodeName`-style tests (each occurrence — including a second
relation field of the same node — goes through the exact same `copyFieldOccurrence`/`relinkOccurrence` call that
was broken): the fix is a single constant change, not a new code path, so two relation fields in one node relink
exactly like one, now that the resolution itself is correct.

**Never an NPE again, by construction.** Every `SchemaNode.getNode(Path)` lookup inside `relinkOccurrence`,
`revertOccurrence` and `findPlaceholderUuid` now goes through a new `RelationFieldRelinker.requireNode(SchemaNode
pParent, Path pPath, String pContext)` helper: null parent or null resolution both throw an `IllegalStateException`
naming the exact path and its context (e.g. `"DecisionNode.fields.advancedSettings.bothValuesNull"`), never a bare
NPE several calls downstream. This does not change behavior for the (now fixed) real paths — it only turns any
FUTURE wrong/renamed path into a clear, immediate failure instead of a repeat of this exact incident.

**New unit test, no live EBX schema needed.** `RelationFieldRelinkerPathsTest` (`mcpgap` test package) parses a
plain copy of `ebx-addon-mame-configuration.xsd` as XML (namespace-aware DOM, no EBX classes) and walks every
schema-path constant `RelationFieldRelinker` uses — exposed for this purpose only via two new package-private
accessors, `testOnlyAbsoluteChains()` (the table/record-level paths, each chain's first entry absolute from the
dataset root, every later entry relative to the previous one — mirrors `findTableConfigurationId`/
`findPolicyUuid`/`createMatchingField`'s own resolution) and `testOnlyFieldsGroupChains()` (every path resolved
relative to the `DecisionNode.fields` GROUP node itself — mirrors `relinkOccurrence`'s own chain, including the
`advancedSettings` → `bothValuesNull`/`oneValueNull` two-step that broke live). The DOM walk is a plain
"`xs:element` → its own `xs:complexType` → its own `xs:sequence` → a direct child `xs:element` by `@name`"
descent, confirmed against the real XSD nesting (including the `MatchingProcess`/`MatchingField` self-reference
STUBS the XSD also declares elsewhere with `maxOccurs="0"` — resolving each constant's FULL, multi-segment
absolute path rather than searching by name anywhere in the document is what avoids ever landing on a stub). A
regression pin spells out the exact previously-broken resolution explicitly (`advancedSettings/bothValuesNull`
must resolve; the doubled `advancedSettings/advancedSettings` must NOT), so the test still fails clearly even if
the two accessor methods are ever edited to drop that entry. The XSD path is read from the `EBX_ADDON_MAME_XSD`
environment variable, defaulting to the same server project `tools/test_local.sh` itself defaults to — a missing
file is a hard failure naming the path checked, never a silent skip. `tools/test_local.sh` runs it automatically
(every `*Test.java` under `src/test/java` is discovered and run) — no wiring needed beyond adding the file.

**Not run live this session** (task constraint: read-only against the running instance) — the fix is confirmed
correct against the XSD's own declared structure (both the RC2 and the running-dev-instance copies) and by the
new pure test, but the actual live relink call (PipelineStep 525's own `Personne` configure) was not re-executed.

### 36.2 `MatchingPolicyTranslator` — a downgrade can make two branches collide, generically

**The bug.** PipelineStep 526 (`Adresse`, MATCHING_CONFIG) failed with `generate_matching_policy`'s own
uninformative refusal: *"The outputs from the Same personneRef data comparison node cannot connect to the same
type of relationship status."* The stored plan was the canonical child parent-confirmation shape (§12.7/§30): N1
compares the entity's own identity fields, `onFalse` `NOT_MATCHED`, `onTrue` leading to N2 (the confirmation
node), N2's own `onTrue` `MATCH`, `onFalse` `SUSPECTED` (the pre-2026-09-27 rule — see §36.3). `DecisionTreePlan
.validate`'s `SAME_OUTCOME_BOTH_BRANCHES` rule (§34.6 Fix B) never caught this, because it runs on the ORIGINAL
plan — the collision only exists AFTER `MatchingPolicyTranslator.forceMatchedLeavesToSuspected` (autoMerge=false)
turns N2's own `MATCH` into `SUSPECTED`, making both of N2's branches read `SUSPECTED`. This is a plain structural
defect of ANY plan whose downgrade creates a collision — nothing about it is specific to a relation field or to
the parent-confirmation shape (the field that happened to trip it here, `personneRef`, is incidental).

**The fix — generic, bottom-up collapse, in the translator, not the plan model.** `DecisionTreePlan` stays
product-neutral (§3.4's own long-standing rule: `autoMerge` is a policy decision, kept OUT of that class).
`MatchingPolicyTranslator.buildMatchingPolicyFromPlan`, right after `forceMatchedLeavesToSuspected`, now calls a
new private `collapseSameOutcomeNodes(ObjectNode)`: post-order (children first, so a collapse CASCADES into the
node's own parent in the same pass, no second walk), a node whose `trueNode`/`falseNode` both resolved to the
SAME leaf name is replaced, in place, by that leaf itself (`ObjectNode.removeAll()` then a single `name` — the
exact shape `DecisionTreePlan.nestedLeaf` already writes) — it "decides nothing" and is never sent to the add-on
as a real node. If the ROOT itself collapses this way, `buildMatchingPolicyFromPlan` refuses the whole configure
step with a clear `IllegalStateException` naming the collapsed outcome, rather than silently sending match-merge
a policy with no real decision tree at all.

**Relation-field specs stay consistent with the collapsed tree.** `buildMatchingPolicyWithRelationFields` (the
`mcpgap` workaround's own entry point) now walks the FINAL, already-collapsed `decisionTree` with a new
`collectDecisionNodeNames` (every node name still carrying a real `function`) and drops any `RelationFieldSpec`
whose `nodeName` is not among them — a collapsed node is not written to the add-on at all, so relinking it would
target a node name that was never actually stored. Node names of every SURVIVING node are unchanged (the freeze
established by the PersVol5 node-naming fix, §33.8, is untouched by this lot — the collapse only ever removes a
node, it never renames one that remains).

**Tests** (`MatchingPolicyTranslatorTest`): `collapse_downgradeCollisionCollapsesNodeToSuspected_cascadesToParentButNotRoot`
(a 3-level chain, N3 collapses, the collapse cascades into N2 which also collapses, N1 — whose own `onFalse` is
the DIFFERENT leaf `NOT_MATCHED` — stays a real node, proving the cascade stops rather than reaching the root
unconditionally); `collapse_autoMergeTrue_leavesTreeUnchanged` (the identical chain with `autoMerge=true`: nothing
is forced to `SUSPECTED`, nothing collapses); `collapse_rootCollapse_refused` (a single root node whose two
