branches collapse to the same leaf: refused, naming the collapsed outcome); `collapse_relationNodeCollapsed_specDropped`
(a relation field's own node collapses under `autoMerge=false`: the written tree has no trace of it, and its
`RelationFieldSpec` is absent from the result). See §36.3 for `collapse_confirmationNodeShapeNotCollapsed_onFalseIsNotMatched`,
which is really a consequence of that section's own reversal, not of this fix directly.

**Not run live this session** (same constraint as §36.1) — confirmed by `tools/test_local.sh` (all green) against
hand-built fixtures reproducing the PersVol6 `Adresse` shape structurally, never against a real `generate_matching_policy`
call.

### 36.3 The parent confirmation node's `onFalse`: `NOT_MATCHED`, not `SUSPECTED` — supersedes 2026-09-23 (§12.7/§30)

**the product owner's decision, 2026-09-27**, reported directly against PersVol3 (§30's own volume test): routing a
DIFFERENT-parent (filled and different on both sides) confirmation-node outcome to `SUSPECTED` — the 2026-09-23
rule (§12.7) — produced 56,510 suspect address pairs at 5% precision (recall 2,848/3,111) on a real run. For a
child whose own identity is WEAK (street/postal code/city — exactly `Adresse`'s own shape), routing every
different-parent pair to a data steward's queue is not a "withhold the confirmation" behavior in practice, it is
"flood the review queue with noise." **New rule: the confirmation node's `onFalse` is `NOT_MATCHED`, never
`SUSPECTED` — a parent filled and DIFFERENT on both sides now disqualifies the pair outright.** `onTrue` is
unchanged (`MATCH`). A MISSING parent on either side keeps the pre-existing `DO_NOTHING` null handling on the
node's own (single) field — reasoned, not independently measured live (same discipline as §12.7's own caveat):
`DO_NOTHING`'s enum name is self-describing and every prior use of it in this codebase (§12.2/§12.7's own
"`DO_NOTHING` only covers a MISSING parent") already reads it as "this field's null does not count against the
node's own pass/fail requirement" — nothing in this lot changes that reading or exercises it against a live
instance; only the case genuinely being reasoned about here (both sides FILLED and DIFFERENT, no null involved at
all) changes, from `SUSPECTED` to `NOT_MATCHED`.

**Where this landed** (`master.MatchPlanLlmPass.java`): `Session.checkParentConfirmationNodeShape`'s own onFalse
check now requires `DecisionTreePlan.LEAF_NOT_MATCHED` (refusing `SUSPECTED` — the exact opposite of the
2026-09-23 check); `systemPrompt`, `candidateHint` (`ROLE_REFERENCE` case), `userPrompt`'s per-child-entity
annotation, `Session.skipOfChild`'s own guidance text, and `requireParentConfirmationNodeForChild`'s `shape`
message are all updated to state `onFalse NOT_MATCHED` (with a short note on why, so a language model reading the
refusal understands the reversal, not just the new rule); every code comment quoting the old contract is dated
2026-09-27 and points here. The generic "every path that can reach MATCH or SUSPECTED must cross the confirmation
node" enforcement (`requireParentConfirmationNodeForChild`/`findOutcomePathBypassingNode`) is UNCHANGED — it still
checks both leaves, since a plan can still legitimately reach `SUSPECTED` some OTHER way (a fuzzy tier elsewhere);
only the confirmation node's OWN `onFalse` changed.

**Interaction with §36.2's collapse.** With the new rule, the confirmation node's `onTrue` (`MATCH`, downgraded to
`SUSPECTED` when `autoMerge=false`) and `onFalse` (`NOT_MATCHED`, untouched) are DIFFERENT leaves — the exact
collision that caused the PersVol6 `Adresse` failure (§36.2) can no longer happen ON THIS NODE. The generic
collapse fix is kept regardless (other node shapes can still collide the same way — see §36.2's own tests), and
`MatchingPolicyTranslatorTest#collapse_confirmationNodeShapeNotCollapsed_onFalseIsNotMatched` pins exactly this:
the same two-level shape, `autoMerge=false`, asserts the confirmation node is NOT collapsed and its `onTrue` reads
`SUSPECTED` while its `onFalse` stays `NOT_MATCHED`.

**Test updates** (`MatchPlanLlmPassTest`): every fixture using the canonical confirmation-node shape (`onTrue
MATCH`/`onFalse SUSPECTED`) is updated to `onFalse NOT_MATCHED`; `parentConfirmationNode_refusedWhenOnFalseIsNotSuspected`
is REPLACED by `parentConfirmationNode_refusedWhenOnFalseIsNotNotMatched` (fixture and assertion both inverted —
it now asserts `SUSPECTED` is refused, naming "must route onFalse to NOT_MATCHED"); the relation-evidence node's
OWN `onFalse SUSPECTED` fixtures (a different feature, §33 — a relation field routing `onTrue` to `MATCH` via a
child, not a `REFERENCE`-role parent link) are left untouched, since the coordinator's own instruction and this
section both scope the reversal to the parent-CONFIRMATION node specifically, never to relation-evidence nodes in
general.

**Not run live this session** (same constraint as §36.1/§36.2): whether a real re-run of PersVol3's `Adresse`
plan under the new rule actually recovers a usable precision (rather than merely moving the noise from
"suspected" to "silently dropped") is unmeasured — only that the previously-bad shape (`onFalse SUSPECTED`) is now
refused, and the new shape (`onFalse NOT_MATCHED`) is accepted and translates without collapsing.

`tools/test_local.sh`: all green after every fix in this section (RelationFieldRelinker NPE fix + new
`RelationFieldRelinkerPathsTest`, `MatchingPolicyTranslator` collapse + five new tests, `MatchPlanLlmPass` onFalse
reversal + updated/renamed tests).

## 37. Parent-first matching order — the ordering was already there, and a note when a parent's suspects are still pending (lot R6, branch `fix/relink-shared-field`, 2026-09-27)

the product owner's decision (2026-09-27): a project's parent entity must be matched before its child so that a merged
parent group's own `relatedTables`/`alignForeignKeys: AUTOMATIC` cascade re-points the child's foreign keys
*before* the child's own parent-confirmation node (§30/§36.3) compares them. Measured live on PersVol6: `Adresse`
precision was 100% but recall only 16%, entirely attributable to per-source `Personne` records that were still
only *suspected* duplicates of each other (never merged yet) — their child `Adresse` rows pointed at *different*
(unmerged) parent records, so the confirmation node correctly, by design, routed every such pair to `NOT_MATCHED`.

**The ordering itself needed no fix.** `MatchingConfigurator.configure`/`.run` both iterate
`masterModel.builtEntities` directly, and `MasterModel.buildFromStaging` already runs every built entity list
through `orderParentsBeforeChildren` — a stable topological sort (Kahn's algorithm, ties broken by original order)
over the FK dependency graph, added 2026-09-22 for exactly this "a child's own configure/run may want its parent's
to exist first" reason (`MasterModel.java`'s own Javadoc on `builtEntities`, and `MasterModelTest`'s existing
coverage). Verified again this lot, not re-derived.

**What this lot adds: an informational note, not a behavior change.** For a CHILD entity that just ran matching in
the SAME `matching/run` call, when its promoted parent (found through the same FK graph, restricted to entities
that are both promoted/built) was ALSO run earlier in this same call (parent-first order guarantees "earlier"
whenever this note is due), and that parent still has pending suspect pairs, the run result and the child's own
`PipelineStep` end message both carry:

> `N <Parent> pair(s) await a decision: cross-source <Child> duplicates are found only once they are merged - run
> matching on <Child> again after deciding them.`

Domain-neutral wording, built only from entity names and a count — never any assumption about what the entities
represent. Split across four package-private statics in `ebx.MatchingConfigurator`, three of them pure and
unit-tested in `MatchingConfiguratorTest` with no EBX class involved:

- `parentEntitiesByChild(List<String> builtEntities, List<String[]> edges)` — the pure form: one child entity ->
  its promoted parent entities, built from `{entityName, targetEntityName}` edge pairs, both ends restricted to
  `builtEntities`, a self-reference (`entityName.equals(targetEntityName)`) excluded (same restriction
  `orderParentsBeforeChildren`'s own dependency graph already applies). The `MasterModel.Result` overload of the
  same name is a one-line adapter over it (`master.ForeignKeyInfo`'s constructor is package-private to `master`,
  so the pure logic itself cannot take that type directly from the `ebx` test package).
- `buildPendingSuspectNote(String parentEntity, String childEntity, int pendingCount)` — the exact wording above,
  null when `pendingCount <= 0`.
- `parentPendingSuspectNote(Repository, masterDataspaceKey, masterDatasetName, childEntity, parentEntities,
  ranSoFar)` — EBX-facing glue: for each parent entity that is both a declared parent of the child AND already
  present in `ran` (this call's own list of entities whose `PipelineStep` already ended successfully), reads its
  pending-suspect count and joins whatever notes result. Not unit-tested directly (needs a live metadataset), but
  it is a thin composition of the two pure statics above plus one EBX read.
- `countPendingSuspectGoldens(Repository, masterDataspaceKey, masterDatasetName, tablePath)` — a cheap proxy: GOLDEN
  `RecordMetadata` rows with `hasSuspects=true`, via `MatchingResultsBuilder.metadatasetTable`/`.scanMetadata` (both
  widened from `private` to package-visible this lot, so this reader is never a second, separately-maintained copy
  of the metadataset-lookup convention `MameMetadataset` already documents). **Not the exact pair count** — sizing
  that needs the add-on's own group scan (`MameGroups`, heavier — see `MatchStats.Kpis#pendingSuspectPairs`'s own
  Javadoc), and `MameMatchingApi.RunResult` deliberately carries no matched/suspected breakdown at all (that
  class' own Javadoc, "No public getter for the MATCHED/SUSPECTED/isolated/group counts") — so this counts flagged
  GOLDEN records instead, close enough for an informational note, never shown elsewhere as an exact pair count.
  Never throws: a missing metadataset (matching never activated on the parent) is silently 0.

**Not run live this lot** (same constraint as §36): whether the note's wording/placement reads well against a
real PersVol6 re-run, and whether the pending-suspect proxy count is a reasonable approximation of the real pair
count on that project, are both unmeasured.

`tools/test_local.sh`: all green (lot R6 — see `docs/RELATION_FIELDS_WORKAROUND.md`'s own R6 note for the
`RelationFieldKeyDedup` and pause/unpause fixes landed in the same branch).

## 38. Lot R7 — relink LAST, phase-named failures, and a null-handling key mismatch (branch `fix/relink-last-and-null-handling`, 2026-09-27)

Fixes three live findings from project PersVol7, PipelineStep 563 (2026-09-27 02:55:41): the relink procedure had
committed successfully (four relationship `MatchingField` rows confirmed live by `get_matching_config`), but a
LATER MCP write in the SAME `configureOne` call silently undid it, the failure that followed was reported as an
uninformative "matching policy translation failed ... null", and separately, the plan's `DO_NOTHING` null handling
was read back as `NOT_MATCH` by the add-on for every field of the parent policy.

### 38.1 Relink LAST — any later MCP write can re-persist the whole tree and undo an earlier relink

**The bug.** Before this lot, `ebx.MatchingConfigurator.relinkRelationFields` was called right after `generate_matching_policy`
(GENERATE_FRESH) or `apply_matching_config` (REWRITE) — i.e. BEFORE every OTHER MCP write the SAME `configureOne`
call still makes on that table: `generate_merge_policy`, the `set_merge_policy_link` patch, the cascade
related-tables `apply_matching_config`, `ensureDefaultMatchingPolicy`'s `set_table_settings`. Live evidence
(kernel.log sequence `MameTrustedSourceWriter` → `MameConfigWriter` ×2 → `MamePatchApplier` → `MameActivationWriter`):
the `set_merge_policy_link` patch re-persisted the WHOLE decision tree, and DecisionNode 75's relinked occurrence
came back with `field` reverted to the PLACEHOLDER `MatchingField`'s own id while its own `useAssociation` flag was
left at 1 — a half-relinked, internally inconsistent occurrence. Root cause (reasoned from CLAUDE.md &sect;8's own
"gap" note on `MamePatchApplier.firstMatchingField`, which resolves a decision field's target back to a
`useAssociation=NO` row by field name — exactly the placeholder row an earlier relink had replaced): ANY
`patch_matching_config`/`apply_matching_config` call on a policy the add-on re-serialises the tree for can undo a
relink, not only the ones that obviously touch the decision tree.

**The fix.** `ebx.MatchingConfigurator#configureOne` now calls `relinkRelationFields` exactly ONCE per configure
pass, at the very end — after `set_trusted_sources`, every policy-generating/rewriting call, the merge-policy link,
the cascade alignment, `ensureDefaultMatchingPolicy`, `validate_matching_config` AND `activate_matching` have all
already run, in BOTH the GENERATE_FRESH and REWRITE branches (RESUME_SAME makes no writes; the call there is a
harmless no-op whenever an existing relink already holds — idempotent by construction). `ebx.MatchingConfigurator
#applySurvivorship` — a separate REST-triggered route that also calls `patch_matching_config` on an
already-configured table, entirely outside `configureOne` — relinks the SAME way, right after its own patch, for
the SAME reason (grepped every call site of `patch_matching_config`/`apply_matching_config`/`generate_matching_policy`
in the module: `ebx.MatchingPreviewPolicy`'s own preview-policy writes never touch relation fields at all — that
class only ever calls `MatchingPolicyTranslator.buildMatchingPolicy`, the plain, non-relation translator entry
point — so it needed no relink call added).

**Idempotence/repair of a half-relinked occurrence.** `mcpgap.RelationFieldRelinker.relinkOccurrence` decided
whether one `fields[]` occurrence was "the placeholder occurrence" inline; extracted into two pure, unit-tested
functions (`RelationFieldRelinkerTest`, no EBX class needed): `isPlaceholderOccurrence(occurrenceFieldId,
placeholderFieldId)` and `isAlreadyRelinkedOccurrence(occurrenceFieldId, newFieldId)` — both keyed SOLELY on the
occurrence's own `field` id, deliberately NEVER also checking the occurrence's own `useAssociation` flag. This
matters exactly for the broken shape above: an occurrence with `useAssociation=1` but `field` reverted to the
placeholder's id is recognised as a placeholder occurrence (its `field` id matches) and gets rewritten again on the
next relink call — a decision that also checked `useAssociation` would have read "1 = already linked" and skipped
it forever, masking the corruption instead of self-healing it. The actual behaviour of `relinkOccurrence` did not
need to change (its own inline checks already happened to be field-id-only) — this lot's real contribution is
making that contract explicit, named, and pinned by a test, so a future "helpful" addition of a `useAssociation`
check cannot silently reintroduce the masking bug.

### 38.2 Failure handling — full stack trace, named phase, pause on ANY failure once a relation policy was written

**The bug.** Every `RuntimeException` reaching `configureOne`'s outermost catch was reported as "matching policy
translation failed for `<table>`: `<message>`" regardless of what actually threw — the PersVol7 failure's own
message was literally "null" (`ex.getMessage()` was null), so the recorded step detail said only "matching policy
translation failed for /root/Personne: null", naming neither the real phase (the merge-policy-link patch that
re-persisted the tree, per &sect;38.1) nor the exception's own class. Nothing in any of `configureOne`'s three
catch blocks logged to `kernel.log` either — the ONLY trace of the failure was that one string in the `PipelineStep`
detail.

**The fix.** `configureOne` now tracks `currentPhase` (a plain local `String`, reassigned at each major step:
resolving the plan, translating it, checking field capabilities, writing the policy — named per decision, e.g.
"writing the matching/merge policy via MCP (REWRITE)" — validating, activating, relinking, recording the plan
applied) and every one of the three catch blocks (`McpException`, `OperationException`, `RuntimeException`) now:
(1) logs the full exception via `LoggingCategory.getKernel().error(...)`, never only a message string; (2) records
`failedPhase` in the step detail; (3) for the `RuntimeException` catch specifically, builds the reported message as
`"<phase> failed for <table>: <message or exception class name if the message is null>"` instead of the single
hardcoded "matching policy translation failed" — a defect anywhere in the method (not only the translator) is now
named for what it actually is. `pauseIfConfigurationLeftInconsistent` (new, best-effort, reuses the R6
`pauseMatchingAfterRelinkFailure` helper) is called from all three catches: once a matching policy carrying
relation specs has actually been written (`wroteMatchingPolicyWithRelationFields`, set true right after
`generate_matching_policy`/`apply_matching_config` succeeds when `relationFieldSpecs` is non-empty, and reset back
to false once this SAME call's own relink has succeeded), ANY later failure in the same `configureOne` call — not
only a relink failure — now pauses the table's matching, since the policy could otherwise be left active
referencing a placeholder field with no relink having run at all yet. Calling the pause helper twice (once from a
relink failure inside `relinkRelationFields` itself, once from the enclosing catch) is harmless — `set_table_settings
pauseMatching=true` is idempotent.

Neither fix was exercised live this lot (same read-only-MCP-tools constraint as R1/R5/R6) — proved by
`tools/test_local.sh`'s existing coverage plus the reasoning above from the add-on's own measured behaviour
(&sect;8's `MamePatchApplier.firstMatchingField` note) and the live PersVol7 kernel.log sequence quoted at the top
of this section.

### 38.3 Null handling: a stored-plan key mismatch, not an add-on default

**The bug, confirmed by reading the source (not a live probe).** `master.DecisionTreePlan`'s own class Javadoc
states the stored-plan field-object keys are the SHORT form (`bothNull`/`oneNull`), "deliberately SHORTER than the
nested add-on shape's `bothNullValueHandling`/`oneNullValueHandling`" — and `DecisionTreePlan#fieldFromJson` (used
by `DecisionTreePlan#readFrom`'s "current, flat shape" branch, the one every `decisionTree`-shaped `MatchPlan
.requirements` goes through) only ever reads `bothNull`/`oneNull`. `master.MatchPlanLlmPass`'s own field-building
code (`Session.buildAndAppendNode`'s per-field loop and `Session.appendRelationField`) wrote the LONG add-on-shape
keys (`bothNullValueHandling`/`oneNullValueHandling`) directly into the stored plan instead — a real regression
this codebase's own `MatchPlanLlmPassTest#parentConfirmationNode_acceptedInCanonicalShape` had locked in as
"expected" (asserting `n2Field.path("bothNullValueHandling")` on the STORED requirements JSON, which is exactly
the wrong key to read there). Because `hasNonNull("bothNull")` was therefore always false on any freshly-proposed
plan, EVERY field's `bothNull`/`oneNull` parsed back as `null`, regardless of what the LLM/plan actually intended —
falling through to `DecisionTreePlan#nestedField`'s own `NOT_MATCH` default for the decision-tree copy AND to
`MatchingPolicyTranslator#nullHandlingByField`'s identical `NOT_MATCH` default for the pre-clustering
`matchingPolicy.fields[]` copy. This explains the live symptom exactly: `DO_NOTHING` visible in the stored plan
(read under the wrong key), `NOT_MATCH` on every parent decision field AND every parent `MatchingField` once
written through `generate_matching_policy`/`apply_matching_config` (not only relation/REFERENCE fields — the bug
hit every field uniformly, since the key mismatch has nothing to do with relation fields specifically). This is
UNRELATED to the "decision field `bothNullValueHandling`/`oneNullValueHandling` is a comparison override, null
falls back to the matching field's value" schema semantic the task brief flagged as a hypothesis (`matching_config_schema`,
&sect;2 top of CLAUDE.md) — that fallback never had a chance to matter here, since this codebase's own translator
always sends an explicit, non-null value at both levels; the values themselves were simply wrong before reaching
either level.

**The fix.** `MatchPlanLlmPass`'s two field-building call sites now write `bothNull`/`oneNull` (the short,
`DecisionTreePlan`-compatible keys) instead of the long add-on-shape keys — the LLM's own raw tool-call output
(`fieldNode`, read via `this.nullHandling(fieldNode, "bothNullValueHandling")`) is UNCHANGED, since that is a
different JSON entirely (what the model is asked to produce, per the tool schema at `Session
.matchPlanToolSchema`'s own long-key property names) from what gets stored. `DecisionTreePlan#nestedField`'s own
`NOT_MATCH` default is intentional and untouched — it is the correct fallback for a field genuinely never given a
null-handling value; the bug was that a `DO_NOTHING` value never reached that point in the first place, not that
the default itself was wrong. `MatchPlanLlmPassTest#parentConfirmationNode_acceptedInCanonicalShape` — the test
that had locked in the wrong key — now asserts the short keys and (new assertion) that the long key is
`isMissingNode()` on the stored plan, so a future regression back to the long-key form fails loudly here instead of
silently matching a stale expectation.

**Not run live this lot** (same constraint as &sect;38.1/&sect;38.2) — confirmed by source inspection (the exact
key strings on both the write side and `DecisionTreePlan#fieldFromJson`'s read side) and by the updated/passing
`MatchPlanLlmPassTest`; whether a live re-run of PersVol7's `Personne` plan now shows `DO_NOTHING` on
`get_matching_config` (rather than `NOT_MATCH`) is unmeasured.

**Coordinator review, same day: plans STORED before this fix still carried the long keys.** Re-proposing every
already-accepted plan is not something a code fix can force, and `MatchPlan` 16 (PersVol7's `Personne`) and every
other plan a language model wrote before this commit landed keep `bothNullValueHandling`/`oneNullValueHandling` in
their own `requirements.decisionTree.nodes[].fields[]` forever, unless someone re-proposes them by hand.
`DecisionTreePlan#fieldFromJson` now reads the SHORT key first (`bothNull`/`oneNull` — this class' own convention,
never ambiguous, since `fieldToJson` only ever writes the short one going forward) and falls back to the LONG
add-on-shape key ONLY when the short one is absent — so an old plan keeps translating to its own real value
(`DO_NOTHING`, etc.) instead of silently reading `null` and falling through to `nestedField`'s `NOT_MATCH` default
forever. Pinned end to end in `DecisionTreePlanTest#fieldFromJson_longKeyFallback_forPlansStoredBeforeTheShortKeyFix`:
a plan carrying only the long key reads the right value AND translates (`toNested`) to the right add-on payload
(`DO_NOTHING`, not `NOT_MATCH`); a plan carrying BOTH (a scenario `fieldToJson` itself never produces, checked only
for defensiveness) reads the short one; a freshly-written plan still carries only the short key.
<p>
**Does this make `MatchingPolicyComparator` flag a forever "drift" between the fixed reader and an
already-configured table?** No — checked directly: `MatchingPolicyComparator#sameCandidateFields` (the
`matchingPolicy.fields[]` pre-clustering comparison) and the decision-tree field comparison both compare the LIVE
`get_matching_config` answer (always the add-on's own long-key wire shape) against the value `MatchingPolicyTranslator`
freshly builds from the (now correctly-read) plan — which ALSO emits the long-key wire shape at both levels
(`buildMatchingPolicy`'s own `field.put("bothNullValueHandling", ...)`, `DecisionTreePlan#nestedField`). Neither
comparison ever sees the internal short-key STORAGE form at all, so this fix introduces no new key-naming mismatch
for the comparator to trip over. What changes is only the VALUE the translator now correctly derives for an
already-mis-configured entity (`DO_NOTHING` instead of the wrongly-defaulted `NOT_MATCH`) — `decideConfigureAction`
sees a real, one-time diff against the still-`NOT_MATCH` stored config, takes `REWRITE`, and after that ONE rewrite
the stored config matches the (now correct) desired one again — not a forever-drifting comparison, a one-time
self-correction exactly like any other plan-vs-stored discrepancy this comparator already exists to catch.

`tools/test_local.sh`: all green after every fix in this section (relink-last restructuring in
`ebx.MatchingConfigurator`, the `RelationFieldRelinker` placeholder-occurrence pure functions + new
`RelationFieldRelinkerTest`, the phase-named/logged/pause-on-any-failure catch blocks, the `MatchPlanLlmPass`
short-key fix + updated `MatchPlanLlmPassTest` assertion, and `DecisionTreePlan#fieldFromJson`'s long-key fallback +
new `DecisionTreePlanTest` case for plans stored before the fix) — see `docs/RELATION_FIELDS_WORKAROUND.md`'s own
R7 note for the relink-last contract and the half-relinked-occurrence repair, told from the `mcpgap` package's own
side.

## 39. Lot R8 — ownership deadlocked forever after one failed configure attempt, and duplicate decision-node names (branch `fix/config-ownership-own-publication`, 2026-09-27)

### 39.1 The live failure

Project PersVol7, `/root/Personne`, `PipelineStep` 563 (2026-09-27 02:55:41): `ebx.MatchingConfigurator#configureOne`
ran `generate_matching_policy`, `generate_merge_policy`, the `set_merge_policy_link` patch and `activate_matching`
all successfully for real — confirmed by a subsequent `get_matching_config` showing the four relationship
`MatchingField` rows live on the table — then failed LATER in the same call (the lot R7 relink-last/phase-named-
failure machinery, §38.2, paused the table's matching on that later failure). Steps 573/575, every retry after it,
were refused outright:

> "A matching configuration already exists for /root/Personne and this project's own MATCHING_CONFIG step for
> Personne has never completed (not even once): refusing to overwrite a configuration this generator did not
> create..."

**Why the guard could never self-heal.** `configureOne`'s ownership check (§19.3) read `lastConfigStepDetail` — the
detail of the SINGLE most recently recorded `MATCHING_CONFIG` step for this project/entity — and tested it with
`priorAttemptCompletedGenerationAndLink`. After the FIRST refusal, every subsequent retry's own `PipelineStep` row
records nothing but that refusal (`configureOne` throws before any tool call is even attempted, so the step detail
built so far carries no `generateMatchingPolicy`/`generateMergePolicy`/`linkMergePolicy` keys at all) — so from the
second retry onward, "the most recently recorded step detail" is always a refusal, never the original 02:55 success,
and the check could never again read `true`. A genuine, self-written configuration was refused forever, and lot R7's
own half-relinked-occurrence repair (§38.1) — which needs a `configureOne` pass to actually run past the ownership
check to reach the relink call — could never be reached either.

### 39.2 The fix — three ownership signals, `ANY` of them, recorded

`ownsExistingConfig` (and, new, `ownershipRule` in the recorded step detail — so a later read shows WHICH signal
established it, never only the boolean) is now `true` when any of:

1. **`isDoneStep`** — unchanged from §19.3: `PipelineSteps.isDone` found a genuinely `DONE` `MATCHING_CONFIG` step
   for this entity, ever.
2. **`anyPriorAttemptCompletedGenerationAndLink`** — the SAME `priorAttemptCompletedGenerationAndLink` check
   (generate+generate+link all succeeded), now applied to `allConfigStepDetails` — EVERY past `MATCHING_CONFIG`
   step detail this project/entity ever recorded (`ebx.MatchingConfigurator`'s former `lastConfigStepDetail`
   widened from "the one most recent row" to "every row"), not only the latest one. A refusal-only step still never
   satisfies the per-attempt check by itself (it carries no tool-call keys), but it no longer HIDES an earlier
   attempt's own genuine success the way reading only the latest row did.
3. **`ownsByDataModel`** — NEW, and the signal that actually breaks the PersVol7 deadlock without depending on
   `PipelineStep` history at all. Every match-merge call `configureOne` makes already goes through `MameCalls.call`,
   which sends `dataModel = urn:ebx:publication:<pModelName>` unconditionally (§28) — `pModelName` being THIS
   project's own master publication, generated exclusively for it by `MasterGenerator`/`MasterNames` and shared
   with no other project. Reading back the `dataModel` argument `MameCalls.call` actually ended up sending (it
   mutates the `ObjectNode` in place, so the value is available on the caller's own args after the call returns)
   and comparing it, exactly, against that same project-owned publication URN: a configuration FOUND while scoped
   to this project's own publication is, by construction, this project's own to manage — a publication the Factory
   itself created for a project is never shared with another one. A retry that resolved to a DIFFERENT
   `AMBIGUOUS_TABLE` candidate (a module's own schema URN, never this project's publication URN itself —
   `MameDataModelResolution`'s own `containsWholeToken` filter only lets through a candidate that literally
   contains the publication name) does not satisfy this rule; the other two signals remain the fallback there.

The three are checked in that priority order purely to report a single, deterministic `ownershipRule` when more
than one holds at once (`DONE_STEP` > `PRIOR_ATTEMPT` > `OWN_PUBLICATION` > `NONE`) — `configureOne` itself only
ever branches on `!= NONE`, never on which specific rule fired.

### 39.3 What was NOT run live

Same constraint as every write path in this class (write tools forbidden in the session that wrote this fix) — the
fix is proved by `MatchingConfiguratorTest`'s new cases (`anyPriorAttempt_refusedAfterEarlierSuccess_owned`,
`anyPriorAttempt_onlyRefusals_notOwned`, `ownsByDataModel_ownPublication_owned`,
`ownsByDataModel_otherProjectsPublication_notOwned`, `determineOwnership_*`) against hand-built fixtures matching
the exact live PersVol7 sequence above, never against a live re-run. Whether a live retry of PersVol7's `Personne`
now proceeds to `REWRITE`/relink instead of refusing is unmeasured.

`tools/test_local.sh`: all green after this fix.

### 39.4 Same lot — duplicate decision-node names, `master.DecisionTreePlan`/`MatchingPolicyTranslator`, 2026-09-27

#### 39.4.1 The live failure

Project PersVol7, step 587 (2026-09-27 11:42): `generate_matching_policy` refused outright —

> "Duplicate decision node name in the decision tree: Similar firstName and lastName and email and p..."

`DecisionTreePlan.Node#label`/`#autoLabel` (§39 above never touches this — separate files, separate bug) names a
node purely from its own `function` and `fields`, with NO regard for a SIBLING node comparing the exact same
fields: two `AVERAGE` nodes over `firstName`/`lastName`/`email`/`phone` at two different thresholds (a stricter
tier falling back to a looser one — a completely ordinary, legitimate shape a plan proposes) both auto-label to
the identical string, and the add-on refuses two decision nodes sharing one `name` outright. The same collision
can happen on two relation nodes comparing the same child (`via`) fields, and on two DIFFERENT nodes that both
happen to carry the same EXPLICIT, LLM-given label.

#### 39.4.2 The fix — freeze, then disambiguate, before either translation path ever reads a name

`DecisionTreePlan.freezeAndDisambiguateLabels(Plan)` (new, pure, package `master`) replaces the freeze-only loop
`MatchingPolicyTranslator#buildMatchingPolicyWithRelationFields` already had (Node naming fix, PersVol5,
2026-09-26, §"Node naming" above): it still computes each node's label once, up front (via `DecisionTreePlan
#labelFor`, from the node's CURRENT, un-substituted fields — unchanged from the PersVol5 fix), but now ALSO
tracks every label it has already assigned (in `Plan#nodes`' own list order — an LLM's or `fromNested`'s own
pre-order id assignment) and appends the colliding node's OWN id, `" (<id>)"`, to every REPEAT occurrence of a
label already seen — e.g. `"Similar firstName and lastName"` stays as-is on the first node, and becomes
`"Similar firstName and lastName (N2)"` on the second. A node's `id` is unique by construction (`DecisionTreePlan
#validate`'s own `DUPLICATE_ID` rule), so the suffixed result can never itself collide with a THIRD node's. An
explicit, LLM-given label that collides is disambiguated exactly the same way — the function reads whatever
`Node#label` already holds as its candidate, auto-generated or not.

Called from BOTH translation entry points, exactly where a node's name must already be final:

- `MatchingPolicyTranslator#buildMatchingPolicyWithRelationFields` — the SAME call site as the PersVol5 freeze fix,
  now calling `freezeAndDisambiguateLabels` instead of the old bare freeze loop, still BEFORE any relation-field
  substitution runs (so a captured `RelationFieldSpec#nodeName` is guaranteed unique, never built from a label
  that could still change or still collide).
- `MatchingPolicyTranslator#buildMatchingPolicyFromPlan` — the shared body EVERY translation path goes through
  (both the plain `buildMatchingPolicy` entry point, which never froze labels at all before this fix, and, a
  second time, the relation-fields path, which already froze/disambiguated them above) — called right after
  `DecisionTreePlan#validate`, before `DecisionTreePlan#toNested` ever reads a single label. `
  freezeAndDisambiguateLabels` is idempotent (a label already set is used AS IS as the next call's own candidate,
  never recomputed from `autoLabel` again), so the second call the relation-fields path triggers is a documented
  no-op — this is the ONLY place a plain, non-relation plan ever gets the treatment.

A plan with no collision at all renders byte-for-byte as it did before this fix (proved directly:
`MatchingPolicyTranslatorTest#buildMatchingPolicy_noCollision_namesUnchanged`,
`DecisionTreePlanTest#freezeAndDisambiguateLabels_noCollision_labelsUnchanged`).

#### 39.4.3 What was NOT run live

Same constraint as §39.3 (write tools forbidden in this session) — proved by `DecisionTreePlanTest`'s five new
`freezeAndDisambiguateLabels_*` cases (colliding auto-labels, colliding explicit labels, no collision, a
three-way collision, and idempotence on a second call) and `MatchingPolicyTranslatorTest`'s three new cases
(`buildMatchingPolicy_duplicateAutoLabels_distinctNamesInNestedOutput`,
`buildMatchingPolicy_noCollision_namesUnchanged`,
`buildMatchingPolicyWithRelationFields_twoNodesSameChildField_distinctSpecNodeNames` — the last one also proving
each `RelationFieldSpec#nodeName` still matches the exact name the written policy carries at its own node, per
the PersVol5 fix's own invariant). Whether a live re-run of PersVol7's colliding plan now proceeds past
`generate_matching_policy` is unmeasured.

`tools/test_local.sh`: all green after this fix.

## 40. Lot R9 - a relation node must discriminate, and the matching-run scope's key-type bug (branch `fix/relation-node-must-discriminate`, 2026-09-27)

Two live findings from project PersVol7 (agent run 169, PipelineStep 596), both about the same underlying theme:
a plan or a run scope that reads as correct can still be silently wrong once it reaches the add-on or the EBX
query layer.

### 40.1 A relation node must discriminate (`master.DecisionTreePlan`, `master.MatchPlanLlmPass`)

Reported directly against project Personnes: the LLM's only address node was `N2` (`ALL_FIELDS` on `Adresse`
`houseNumber`/`street`/`postalCode`/`city`), reached via the identity node `N1`'s own `onTrue`, with `onTrue`
`MATCH` (or `SUSPECTED` - both variants were seen) and `onFalse` `SUSPECTED`. With `autoMerge=false` (the
default, a human toggle a plan never sees) `MatchingPolicyTranslator#forceMatchedLeavesToSuspected` downgrades
every `MATCH` leaf to `SUSPECTED`, so `N2`'s two branches collapsed to the SAME outcome; `collapseSameOutcomeNodes`
(&sect;36.2) then silently dropped the whole node. The configured policy ended up with NO address evidence at
all, although the plan itself read as if it had used the child evidence, and had already passed the
relation-evidence-required challenge (&sect;34.2) on the way in.

**The fix - a new structural rule in `DecisionTreePlan.validate`/`validateNode`, `RELATION_NODE_OUTCOMES_MUST_DIFFER`.**
A node carrying at least one relation (child) field must actually discriminate: its `onTrue` and `onFalse` may
never BOTH resolve to one of {`MATCH`, `SUSPECTED`} (the same one, or not - `SAME_OUTCOME_BOTH_BRANCHES`,
&sect;34.6 Fix B, only catches the identical-string case). This is placed in `validateNode` itself, exactly like
`SAME_OUTCOME_BOTH_BRANCHES` before it, rather than as a separate `MatchPlanLlmPass`-side post-loop method: every
`validate` overload gets it for free, which means it fires BOTH at propose time (`MatchPlanLlmPass.Session
#proposeMatchPlan`'s own relation-aware `validate` call, which runs before `checkRelationMatchNodeShape` ever
gets a chance to look at the tree's shape) AND before any MCP write (`MatchingPolicyTranslator
#buildMatchingPolicyFromPlan`'s own pre-existing, unconditional `DecisionTreePlan.validate(plan)` call already
gates every configure step on it - no new call site needed, the exact "SAME_OUTCOME_BOTH_BRANCHES" precedent).
A dedicated helper, `DecisionTreePlan.isAmbiguousOutcomeLeaf` (package-visible, not `private`), is the single
source of truth for "is this leaf name MATCH or SUSPECTED" - reused (not re-derived) by `MatchPlanLlmPass
#argumentsUseAnyRelationField` (below).

**Consequence for the pre-existing "canonical shape".** &sect;33.10's own canonical example (`onTrue MATCH`,
`onFalse SUSPECTED`) is now REFUSED by this rule - it collapses exactly the same way once auto-merge is off. The
canonical shape is now `onTrue MATCH`, `onFalse NOT_MATCHED` (mirroring the parent-confirmation node's own
&sect;36.3 reversal). Every `MatchPlanLlmPassTest` fixture that used `onFalse SUSPECTED` on a MATCH-terminal
relation node was updated to `NOT_MATCHED` so each test keeps isolating the ONE rule it names (the root check, the
"node above" check, etc.) rather than tripping the new rule first; a relation field compared FUZZILY (the
"PRECISE key" test) and a node whose `onFalse` is literally `MATCH` (the "onFalse is MATCH" test) are both
refused earlier in the pipeline (inside `appendRelationField`, before the plan is even built) and needed no
change.

**Prompt alignment.** `MatchPlanLlmPass#appendRelationEvidence`'s "Relation evidence" paragraph gained a closing
sentence stating the same rule in the model's own words: a node comparing child evidence must route its `onFalse`
to `NOT_MATCHED` or to another node (a coarser child-evidence level, or an independent-identifier check) - never
to the other of MATCH/SUSPECTED, since auto-merge (off by default) makes the two equivalent.

**The relation-evidence-required challenge must not count a doomed field as "used".** `MatchPlanLlmPass
#argumentsUseAnyRelationField` (the raw-arguments scan `relationEvidenceRequiredChallenge`'s `JsonNode` overload
uses, &sect;35.3) ran BEFORE any node is built or validated - so without a fix, a plan whose ONLY relation field
sits in a node that `RELATION_NODE_OUTCOMES_MUST_DIFFER` is about to refuse would still pass the challenge (the
raw scan finds a `via`), only to be refused a few lines later anyway, telling the model contradictory things.
Fixed by applying `DecisionTreePlan.isAmbiguousOutcomeLeaf` to the SAME `nodes[]` item's own `onTrue`/`onFalse`
(read directly off the raw JSON) before counting its relation field as genuine use - a legacy `tiers[]` item is
exempt from this extra check (its own `onFalse` is always either the next tier or the final `NOT_MATCHED` by
construction, `DecisionTreePlan#fromTiers`, so it can never hit this shape).

**Tests** (`DecisionTreePlanTest`): `validate_relationNodeOutcomesMustDiffer_bothSuspected_refused` (the exact
live shape), `_matchAndSuspected_refused` (the other reported variant, different leaves that still collapse),
`_onFalseNotMatched_accepted`, `_onFalseIsAnotherNode_accepted`, `_nonRelationNode_notChecked` (the rule never
fires for an ordinary node with no relation field - that shape is legal, e.g. an ordinary MATCH-terminal identity
tier). `MatchPlanLlmPassTest`: `relationMatchNode_refusedWhenBothBranchesSuspected` and
`relationMatchNode_refusedWhenOnTrueMatchOnFalseSuspected` reproduce the live bug end to end through
`propose_match_plan`; `relationMatchNode_acceptedInCanonicalShape`/`_refusedAsRoot`/
`_refusedWhenNodeAboveHasNoOwnIdentityField` updated to `onFalse NOT_MATCHED` per the above.

**Not run live this lot** (same read-only-against-the-running-instance discipline as every prior lot in this
file): whether a real re-run of PersVol7's `Adresse`/`Personne` plans now produces a working relation node, and
whether a real language model, given the reworded prompt, actually proposes the discriminating shape rather than
looping on the refusal, are both unmeasured.

### 40.2 `MatchingRunScope` - a numeric primary key quoted as a string, and an unbounded OR list (`master.MatchingRunScope`, `ebx.MatchingConfigurator`)

`MATCHING_RUN` on `Adresse` FAILED at PipelineStep 596: `ClassCastException: class java.math.BigDecimal cannot be
cast to class java.lang.String`. `MatchingRunScope.all`'s enumerated predicate quoted every master key as an
XPath string literal (`./id='1' or ./id='2' or ...`), but `/root/Adresse/id` - like every master table's primary
key, by this factory's own design (this class' pre-existing Javadoc already said so) - is a plain auto-increment
NUMBER, so the add-on's XPath engine choked comparing a `BigDecimal` field against a string literal.

**Fix - `MatchingRunScope.KeyType`, a live-read primary-key field, and a non-enumerating whole-table predicate.**
`all` now takes a `KeyType` (`NUMERIC` unquoted, `STRING` quoted/escaped - the same doubling convention
`incremental` already uses) and the table's own `pPrimaryKeyField` (never hardcoded to `id` inside this class -
see the coordinator review below) for the ENUMERATED form, plus a `pWholeTableBelongsToProject` flag: when true
(every real caller in this codebase, since a project's master dataspace/dataset - `Project.masterDataspace`/
`masterDataset` - is created exclusively for that one project, never shared), `all` answers
`osd:is-not-null(./<pk>)` instead of enumerating at all - equivalent to "every record with an Xref row of this
project" precisely BECAUSE no other project's records can ever be in that table, and still a deliberate, explicit,
non-empty predicate (never `matching_guide`'s own warned-against "omitted scope" case). This kills the
unbounded-OR-list concern for the one path this factory actually uses, and is immune to the type bug by
construction (it never compares the key against a literal). `MatchingConfigurator#run` passes `true`/`NUMERIC`
always. The enumerated form is kept, fixed, and unit-tested (a `NUMERIC` value that does not actually look like a
number - `requireNumericLiteral` - is refused with an `IllegalStateException` naming it, rather than silently
embedded unquoted and wrong a different way) for a future table that does not satisfy the one-project-per-table
property. A composite key uses its first field only - this factory's own master tables never have one (this
class' own pre-existing Javadoc: the primary key is always the single `id` field), so this is defensive
generality, not a measured case.

**Coordinator review, same day: `true()` is not a valid EBX XPath predicate - measured live.** The first version
of this fix answered a bare `true()` for the whole-table case; re-checked against the running RC before merging:
`count_records_by_xpath` on `PersVol7_Master`/`Master`/`/root/Adresse` with filter `true()` answers `"Invalid
XPath predicate: 'true()'"`, while `osd:is-not-null(./id)` answers 4667 (every row of that table). EBX's own XPath
dialect apparently does not accept a bare boolean-function predicate with no path step at all - `all` was changed
to `osd:is-not-null(./<pk>)` instead, which both satisfies the dialect and, by naming the table's own primary key
(never null on a real row), is exactly as complete a "select everything" predicate as `true()` was meant to be.
The primary-key FIELD NAME itself is read live by `MatchingConfigurator.primaryKeyFieldOf` off
`AdaptationTable.getPrimaryKeySpec()` (CLAUDE.md &sect;9's own "answers absolute-looking paths, e.g. `/id`" note -
the leading slash is stripped here) rather than hardcoded, even though every master table this factory builds
uses the plain `id` field by design - `MatchingRunScope` itself stays pure and never assumes a field name.

**Full stack trace to `kernel.log`, `[mdm-factory]`-prefixed.** `MatchingConfigurator#run`'s own `OperationException`/
`RuntimeException` catches used to record only the exception's message in the `PipelineStep` detail - the exact
"masked kernel exception" class of bug CLAUDE.md &sect;13 already warns about, and the same gap &sect;38.2 fixed
for `configureOne`. Both catches now also call `LoggingCategory.getKernel().error("[mdm-factory] matching/run
failed for ...", ex)` before ending the step, the same convention `configureOne` already established.

**Tests** (`MatchingRunScopeTest`): `all_wholeTableBelongsToProject_isNotNullPredicate` (`osd:is-not-null(./id)`,
never a bare `true()` and never an OR list), `all_wholeTableBelongsToProject_stillRefusedWhenNoKeys` (the
empty-scope refusal survives the new path), `all_noPrimaryKeyField_refused`, `all_enumerated_numericKeysUnquoted`
(the live bug's own fix), `all_enumerated_stringKeysQuotedAndEscaped` (apostrophe doubled),
`all_enumerated_numericKeyThatDoesNotLookNumeric_refused`, `all_enumerated_nestedPrimaryKeyField` (a non-bare
field path is rendered as given, no hidden bare-name assumption). Pre-existing `all_*` tests updated to the new
4-argument signature.

**Not run live this lot beyond the one measurement quoted above**: whether a real re-run of PersVol7's `Adresse`
all-scope run now completes end to end is unmeasured; `true()`'s own invalidity and `osd:is-not-null(./id)`'s own
validity/row count were both confirmed live, against the exact table this bug was found on.

`tools/test_local.sh`: all green after every fix in this section.

## 41. Lot R11 — a stale cached decision tree after a live relink, and a numeric metadataset field crashing a best-effort note (branch `fix/tree-cache-evict-and-suspect-note`, 2026-09-27)

### 41.1 `DecisionTreeConfigCache` — the add-on caches decision trees in memory, and `RelationFieldRelinker`'s direct write never told it

Live PersVol7, 2026-09-27 21:56-21:58: Configure ended DONE, and `RelationFieldRelinker.verify` (lot R10) confirmed
in the raw EBX records that DecisionNode 102's occurrence now pointed at the real relationship `MatchingField`s
218/219/220 (`BY_FOREIGN_KEY`). But `get_matching_config`, read moments later, still showed the address node
comparing the PLACEHOLDER fields - and the 21:57 matching run matched on those same wrong fields. Root cause:
`com.orchestranetworks.addon.mame.service.decisiontree.DecisionTreeConfigCache` is a singleton keyed by matching
policy id (`getInstance().getByMatchingPolicyId(String, boolean)` / `.evict(String)` / `.evictAll()`), read by the
matching engine itself (`SimilarFinder`, `MatchingQueueProducer`, `MatchingService`) and by every
`get_matching_config` answer, populated by ANY read (this configure pass' own earlier `get_matching_config`/
`generate_matching_policy` calls). `RelationFieldRelinker.relink` writes the underlying `MatchingField`/
`DecisionNode` records directly, in a plain EBX `Procedure` - never through the `match-merge` MCP server - so
nothing ever told the cache its entry was stale.

**Evidence, `javap` on the RC2 add-on classes (`ebx-addon-mame`), 2026-09-27.** `MamePatchApplier.applyResolved`
iterates a `Set<String>` of policy ids at the end of every `patch_matching_config` call and, for each one, calls
`DecisionTreeConfigCache.getInstance().evict(id)` - but that `Set` is populated ONLY inside three helpers:
`nodeRecord` (adds the node's own `policyPk` - used by `set_threshold`, `set_field_param`, `set_algorithm`,
`set_field_preclustering`, `set_field_weight`, `set_field_null_handling`, `set_decision_node_function`, all
`policyCode`+`decisionTreeNode`-scoped), `treeRecord` (structural ops - `add_decision_node`, `remove_decision_node`,
the chain-entry ops - these re-persist the WHOLE tree via `rebuildTree`/`DecisionTreeInsertionProcedure`, exactly
the class of write lot R7 already identified as capable of reverting a relink) and `matchingFieldRecord` (adds the
field's own `policyPk` - used by the `policyCode`+`field`-only ops `set_field_preclustering`/`set_field_weight`/
`set_field_null_handling` when resolved through `findMatchingField`, not `nodeRecord`).

**The task's own first candidates do NOT evict at all - checked and rejected by `javap` before picking a
different op.** `MamePatchApplier.resolveSetShowMatchType`/`resolveSetExecutePurge` both call `matchingPolicyRecord`
with its 2-argument overload (`PatchRecords`, `MatchingPolicy` - no `Set<String>` parameter exists to pass), and
disassembling both methods end to end shows no `Set.add` call site in either. Confirmed two independent ways:
the method signatures dispatched from `resolveOperation` for `SET_SHOW_MATCH_TYPE`/`SET_EXECUTE_PURGE` never
receive the eviction `Set`, and the bytecode itself never touches one. A call to either op is accepted, mutates the
`MatchingPolicy` record, and evicts NOTHING.

**Op picked instead: `set_field_weight` on the RELATION SPEC'S OWN PLACEHOLDER FIELD, set to its current value -
a data no-op whose only purpose is the eviction side effect.** `PatchOpKind.SET_FIELD_WEIGHT`'s declared target
keys are `policyCode`+`field` only (`nodeRequired = false`) - no `decisionTreeNode` at all. `MamePatchApplier
.resolveSetFieldWeight` resolves the field through `findMatchingField` -> `firstMatchingField`, which (same
restriction `docs/RELATION_FIELDS_WORKAROUND.md`'s "the gap" section already documents for the vendor's own
`useAssociation = NO` filter) can only ever resolve to a PLAIN field's own standalone `MatchingField` row - never
to a `DecisionNode.fields[]` occurrence, and never to a relationship (`useAssociation != NO`) field either. Because
the relink NEVER deletes or rewrites the placeholder's own `MatchingField` row (`RelationFieldRelinker
.findPlaceholderUuid` only ever READS it - `docs/RELATION_FIELDS_WORKAROUND.md` lot R6's own note), that row is
always still there with its original weight, so patching it back to that SAME value is a true no-op on stored
data - it changes nothing a reader could observe except evicting the cache, and by construction it can never repeat
the R7 bug (`firstMatchingField`'s by-name resolution reverting a relinked occurrence back to the placeholder),
since it never touches a decision-node occurrence at all.

**Read-back shape, confirmed by `javap` on `MameConfig`/`MameConfigReader` (RC2, 2026-09-27).** A decision node's
own field entry (`MameConfig.DecisionFieldView.field`) is populated from a `Map<uuid, MatchingField.getField()>`
built over the policy's flat `fields[]` list, keyed by the occurrence's `fkMatchingField` (the `MatchingField`
uuid as a string) - so after a correct relink it reads back as the CHILD field path itself (e.g. `/street`), the
same value `RelationFieldSpec.childFieldPath` already carries. The top-level `MameConfig.MatchingFieldView
.useRelationships` is `UseAssociation.getMode(Integer).name()` - the Java enum name, so exactly the string
`"BY_FOREIGN_KEY"` for a relationship field, never a lower-camel-case or numeric form.

**Fix — `ebx.MatchingConfigurator.evictDecisionTreeCacheAndVerifyReadBack`**, called from `relinkRelationFields`
right after a successful `RelationFieldRelinker.relink` (still inside the same `try`/`catch` that pauses the table
on any failure - a stale cached tree is exactly as unsafe as an unrelinked occurrence, so it gets the same
pause-on-failure treatment as a relink failure itself): (1) reads `get_matching_config` once to learn the
placeholder field's current `weight`; (2) issues ONE `patch_matching_config` call, `set_field_weight` on that same
placeholder field with that same value; (3) reads `get_matching_config` a second time (now guaranteed fresh, since
the patch call's own `applyResolved` just evicted this policy's cache entry) and asserts, for EVERY
`RelationFieldSpec`, that `findDecisionNodeByName(decisionTree, spec.nodeName).fields[]` carries an entry whose
`field` equals `spec.childFieldPath`, and that the top-level matching field of that same path reads
`useRelationships = "BY_FOREIGN_KEY"`. `treeCacheEvicted` (the patch call/response) and `relinkReadBack` (the
checks array plus any errors) are both recorded in the step detail. A mismatch on EITHER assertion fails the step
and pauses the table, exactly like a relink failure - never silently accepted.

**Not measured live this lot** (same read-only-MCP-tools constraint as every other lot in
`docs/RELATION_FIELDS_WORKAROUND.md`): whether `set_field_weight`'s eviction actually makes the NEXT
`get_matching_config`/matching run see the relinked tree on a real instance. `MatchingConfiguratorTest` covers the
pure pieces (`findDecisionNodeByName` against a hand-built JSON tree); the eviction/read-back sequence itself needs
a live `match-merge` server and is the real test of this fix.

### 41.2 `MatchingResultsBuilder.safeGetString` — a numeric metadataset field crashing a best-effort note, after the matching run it decorates had already committed

Live PersVol7, step 608, `kernel.log` 21:58:03,943: `ClassCastException: BigDecimal cannot be cast to String` at
`CfContent.getString` <- `MatchingResultsBuilder.safeGetString` (`groupId`/`goldenId` are numeric on this table's
`RecordMetadata`) <- `scanMetadata` <- `MatchingConfigurator.countPendingSuspectGoldens` <-
`parentPendingSuspectNote` <- `runInternal`. The `MatchingManager` transaction that actually runs matching had
already committed at 21:58:03,457, BEFORE this crash - only the purely informational "N parent pair(s) await a
decision" note (lot R6) failed, yet the whole step was marked FAILED because nothing between the note computation
and the step's own success path caught it.

**Fix (a) - `safeGetString` never calls `Adaptation.getString(Path)` any more.** That method assumes the
underlying value is already a `String` and throws instead of formatting a number; `groupId`/`goldenId` are
`BigDecimal` at the EBX-Java boundary on this table (the same "a SQL `count()`/`xs:decimal` column is a `BigDecimal`
in Java" fact CLAUDE.md &sect;2's `db.field<T>` note already states for the scripting side of this boundary).
`safeGetString` now reads the raw value via the pre-existing `safeGet` and renders it with a new pure helper,
`MatchingResultsBuilder.renderMetadataText`: `null` stays `null`, a `BigDecimal` renders through
`toPlainString()` (never `toString()`, which can switch to scientific notation on a large id), any other value
through `String.valueOf` as before, and a blank result folds back to `null` - the same convention the old
`getString`-based implementation already applied. String values (a genuine foreign key formatted elsewhere, or a
real text field) are unaffected.

**Fix (b) - the note is best-effort, at the call site, not only at its own root cause.** `runInternal`'s call to
`parentPendingSuspectNote` is now wrapped in its own `try`/`catch (RuntimeException)`: a failure is logged with the
same `[mdm-factory]`-prefixed `LoggingCategory.getKernel().error(...)` convention every other catch in this class
already uses, and `parentSuspectNote` falls back to `MatchingConfigurator.pendingSuspectNoteOnFailure(ex.getClass())`
("pending parent pairs could not be counted: `<exception class>`") - the run step itself still ends successfully,
since `runResult` (the actual matching outcome) was already computed above this call and is unaffected. This
defends the whole call site against ANY future exception in the note's computation, not only the specific
`ClassCastException` fix (a) already closes at its root.

**Tests.** `MatchingResultsBuilderTest` (new): `renderMetadataText_bigDecimal_plainStringNeverScientificNotation`
(the live bug's own fix, plus a value that would render in scientific notation via plain `toString()`),
`renderMetadataText_otherNumber_stringValueOf`, `renderMetadataText_plainString_unchanged`,
`renderMetadataText_blankString_null`, `renderMetadataText_null_null`. `MatchingConfiguratorTest`:
`pendingSuspectNoteOnFailure_namesTheExceptionClass` (the pure fallback-message builder). The `try`/`catch` wrapping
itself at the `runInternal` call site is not unit-tested - same class of reasoning as lot R10's own
`copyAdvancedSettings` note (`SchemaNode`/`Adaptation` have no lightweight fake in this codebase's test sources);
the fix is exercised structurally by (a) making the exception it guards against no longer happen for `groupId`/
`goldenId`, and would be exercised end to end by any live run that still throws for a different metadataset field.

`tools/test_local.sh`: all green after every fix in this section.

## 42. Lot R12 — run activation self-heal, a real wait for the matching run, and a fast preflight (branch `fix/run-activation-and-wait`, 2026-09-27)

Live evidence, EBX 6.3.0-RC2, 2026-09-27, projects `ret` and `PersVol7`, after a Tomcat restart hit the "Recursive
load" boot race (CLAUDE.md &sect;8): `get_matching_activation_status` answered `{state: DISABLED, published: true,
paused: false, metadatasetExists: true}` on `/root/Personne` and `/root/Adresse` of both projects even though both
`MatchPlan`s were already `APPLIED` (a previously-successful `configure`). `runInternal` launched `matchRecords`
straight into it anyway, and the add-on refused outright: "invalid parameter: The Run match service cannot be
executed. Please check the Table activation and settings configuration" (`PipelineStep`s 670/671/673/674 on `ret`,
680/681 on `PersVol7`). `activate_matching(table, dataModel)` repaired it at once (no restart), and the run worked
right after.

### 42.1 Self-healing the activation race before `matchRecords`, and again at the end of `configureOne`

`MatchingActivationGuard.ensureActivatedBeforeSimulate` already did exactly this self-heal for the Simulate path
(&sect;29's own `activateIfNeeded`: read `get_matching_activation_status`, and only when the table is not genuinely
`isReady` - `state == ENABLED AND metadatasetExists`, never `state` alone - call `activate_matching` once and
re-read before giving up). `runInternal` had no equivalent call at all before this lot: a table whose `MatchPlan` was
`APPLIED` (a prior successful `configure`) was assumed to still be activated, which the boot race above disproves.

Fixed by a new orchestration method, `MatchingActivationGuard.ensureActivatedBeforeRun` - the SAME core
(`activateIfNeeded`, unchanged) under its own name, so a reader of `runInternal`/`configureOne` does not have to
wonder why a "simulate" method is called before a matching run or at the tail of a configure pass. Called in two
places:

1. `runInternal`, once per entity, right before `MameMatchingApi.launchScoped` - a single `get_matching_activation_status`
   read when the table is already ready (the common case, no added latency worth mentioning), the full
   status/activate/re-read cycle only when it is not. A non-null returned note means a repair actually ran: recorded
   as `detail.activationRepaired = true` + `detail.activationNote`. An `OperationException` (the table is still not
   runnable after the one repair attempt) propagates to the entity's own existing `catch (OperationException)` -
   `PipelineSteps.end(..., false, ...)` + `refused.add(...)`, exactly the same "refuse cleanly, step FAILED" path
   every other refusal in this method already takes; no new catch block was needed.
2. `configureOne`, as a SECOND, fully independent recheck at the very end of the method - the same "recheck at the
   very end, after every write this method makes" discipline lot R10 (&sect;41.1) already applies to the relation-field
   relink. `configureOne`'s own `activate_matching` call (or the skip because the table was already `ENABLED`) already
   ran earlier in the SAME method; this final check exists because the boot race is, in principle, a timing issue with
   the add-on's own async schema recompile, and a "successful" configure must never hand back a table that
   `runInternal`'s own pre-run check would immediately have to repair anyway. A repair here is recorded as
   `detail.activationRepairedAtEnd = true` + `detail.activationNoteAtEnd`; a refusal ends the step FAILED (with a
   message naming which entity/table) and re-throws, same pattern as the relink-verify-failure block just above it.

Both call sites reuse the exact same MCP calls (`get_matching_activation_status`, `activate_matching`) with no new
tool - domain-neutral, works for any table/project. Never exercised live this session (task constraint: no EBX
access) - the core (`activateIfNeeded`/`decide`/`isReady`) was already unit-tested end to end in
`MatchingActivationGuardTest` before this lot; `ensureActivatedBeforeRun` adds no new pure logic (a plain delegation),
so no new test was needed for it specifically.

### 42.2 A real end to the matching run: 15 minutes, poll until finished or stopped, retry a locked dataspace

**`DEFAULT_MAX_WAIT_MS` raised from 30s to 15 minutes** (`MatchingConfigurator.DEFAULT_MAX_WAIT_MS`). Live evidence:
Personne's own run took 34s under the old 30s bound (`PipelineStep` 676, "still RUNNING after 30000ms -
Xref.goldenKey not refreshed yet"), so `runInternal` moved on to Adresse while Personne's own process still held the
master dataspace - Adresse's own `matchRecords` call then refused ("invalid state ... this service cannot be
executed because the dataspace is locked", step 677). With a 600000ms bound the SAME sequence ran end to end
(Personne 9s, Adresse 3s, both `DONE`, no lock refusal at all). 15 minutes is a generous default; `pMaxWaitMs` stays
a real parameter (the REST route's own `maxWaitMs` query parameter) - this only changes what an unspecified call
falls back to.

**`MameMatchingApi.launchScoped` now also stops polling on a job's own requested stop**, not only the deadline - a
new overload takes a `FactoryJobs.Handle` (null for every synchronous caller, exactly as `MatchingConfigurator.run`/
`configure`'s own `pHandle` convention already works for the entity loop itself). The poll-continuation decision is
now a small pure function, `shouldKeepPolling(ProcessStatus, long nowMs, long deadlineMs, boolean cancelled)`:
continue only while the status is not terminal, the deadline has not passed, and no stop was requested. Unit-tested
against a fake clock/status sequence (`MameMatchingApiTest`): RUNNING before the deadline keeps polling; DONE/FAILED/
CANCELLED, a passed deadline, or `cancelled=true` each independently stop it; a non-terminal INITIALIZING status
still counts as "keep polling".

**A `matchRecords` refusal whose message contains "dataspace is locked" is now retried** (`ret`/`PersVol7`'s own
Adresse refusal above is the exact live shape) up to 5 times, 10 seconds apart, before it reaches the caller - two
new pure helpers: `isDataspaceLockedMessage(String)` (case-insensitive, null-safe substring match) and
`shouldRetryLock(String message, int attemptNumber, int maxAttempts)` (retry only while budget remains AND the
message is the locked shape - any other `InvalidStateException`, matching genuinely paused or a policy inactive, is
never retried regardless of budget). Both unit-tested directly. The retry sits INSIDE `launchScoped`'s own
`matchRecords` call (a plain loop with `Thread.sleep(10000)` between attempts, an `InterruptedException` during the
wait re-throws as a refusal naming the interruption rather than silently swallowing it) - the 15-minute wait above
fixes the common case (one entity's own run overrunning the OLD short bound), this retry covers what remains (an
unrelated process, or a run that still overruns even the new generous bound).

### 42.3 Never touching a finished process's report-only accessors again

`MameMatchingApi`'s own 2026-09-22 fix (this doc's earlier section on the `MatchingOperationProcess.getCurrentPhase()`
NullPointerException) made `getDetail()`/`getCompletionRate()`/`getDuration()` guarded (a throw is caught, noted,
never rethrown) but still ATTEMPTED after the process had genuinely finished - live evidence C, this lot: every
successful run's own `reportNotes` carried "getDetail(): NullPointerException ... getCurrentPhase() is null", cosmetic
pollution on every single completed run, not just the rare one this guard was written for.

Fixed by never calling those three accessors once `ProcessStatus` is terminal at all - not merely catching the
failure, avoiding the read entirely. `launchScoped`'s poll loop now calls `buildResult` (unchanged: still reads all
three, guarded) only while the status is NOT terminal, keeping the last snapshot (`lastProgress`); once terminal, a
new method, `finalResult(ProcessStatus, RunResult lastProgressOrNull)`, builds the returned `RunResult` from that
snapshot alone - its own signature carries no `MatchingProcess` parameter at all, so "never touches the process
again" is a compile-time guarantee, not a discipline to remember. `pLastProgressOrNull == null` (the process was
already terminal at the very FIRST status read, before any snapshot was ever safely observable) yields
`detail=null, completionRate=-1, durationMs=-1` - unknown, never a guess. `buildResult` itself is unchanged (it is
still exactly correct to call while the status is not terminal, and remains unit-tested that way by the pre-existing
`MameMatchingApiTest` cases) - only the CALLING DISCIPLINE in `launchScoped` changed, encoded now in the type
signature of `finalResult` rather than left to reviewer vigilance. Unit-tested directly:
`finalResult_reusesLastProgress_neverTouchesProcessAgain` (a hand-built "last progress" `RunResult`, its own detail/
completionRate/durationMs/reportNotes survive verbatim into the terminal result) and
`finalResult_noPriorProgress_returnsUnknownValuesWithGivenNotes` (`null` last progress - unknown values, no crash).

### 42.4 Preflight: a fast, explicit timeout instead of a ~79s stall

Live evidence D: a thread dump caught `POST /projects/{code}/matching/configure` stuck inside
`FactoryResource.preflight` &rarr; `McpServers.preflight` &rarr; `probe` &rarr; `McpClient.post`, roughly 79 seconds
into the call - `McpServers.probe`'s own read-timeout-retry (`PROBE_READ_TIMEOUT_MS` 30s, then
`PROBE_RETRY_READ_TIMEOUT_MS` 90s once, added 2026-09-24 for the connection-test screen's "still warming up after a
restart" case, &sect;lot "mcp-preflight-retry") is exactly the wrong patience for a REST route already mid-request,
before any side effect - the whole point of a preflight check is to fail FAST and explicitly instead of blocking the
caller.

Fixed by giving `preflight` its own, much tighter timeout, entirely separate from `test`'s (the connection-test
screen keeps the generous 30s/90s behaviour unchanged): a new `McpServers.preflightProbeTimeoutMs()` (default
5000ms, overridable with `-Debx.factory.preflightTimeoutMs=<ms>` - the "configurable" knob the task brief asks for),
read FRESH on every call (never cached in a `static final`) so a test can override the system property at runtime.
`testOne`/`probe` each gained an overload taking the read timeout and an `pAllowRetry` flag: `test` calls the
original 4-/6-arg shape (`PROBE_READ_TIMEOUT_MS`, retry allowed, unchanged behaviour), `preflight` calls the new one
with `preflightProbeTimeoutMs()` and `pAllowRetry=false` - a probe that times out at 5s is reported as a failed line
at once, never retried with a longer timeout. Each line's own `elapsedMs` (already computed by `testOne` regardless
of outcome, unchanged) is the per-server probe duration the task brief asks to be recorded - no new field was needed,
only the tighter timeout that makes it small on a healthy call and bounded on a failing one.

Unit-tested: `preflightProbeTimeoutMs_defaultsWhenPropertyUnset` (5000ms with the property cleared) and
`preflightProbeTimeoutMs_readsThePropertyAtCallTime` (a value set with `System.setProperty` is read back
immediately, proving it is not cached at class-load). The retry-suppression itself (`pAllowRetry=false`) is not
independently unit-tested beyond this - `McpServersTest`'s pre-existing `isReadTimeout*` cases already cover the
retryable-cause detection this flag now gates, and `probe`/`testOne` still require a live `McpClient` to exercise
end to end (same testing discipline as the rest of this class, `McpServersTest`'s own class Javadoc).

### 42.5 Files, never exercised live this session

`MatchingActivationGuard.java` (`ensureActivatedBeforeRun`, new), `MatchingConfigurator.java`
(`DEFAULT_MAX_WAIT_MS` raised, pre-run + end-of-configure activation checks, `pHandle` threaded into
`launchScoped`), `MameMatchingApi.java` (`isDataspaceLockedMessage`, `shouldRetryLock`, `shouldKeepPolling`,
`finalResult`, the lock-retry loop inside `launchScoped`, the new `Handle`-aware overload), `McpServers.java`
(`preflightProbeTimeoutMs`, `testOne`/`probe` timeout+retry overloads). Tests: `MameMatchingApiTest` (6 new cases),
`McpServersTest` (2 new cases). No EBX access this session (task constraint) - every fix above is reasoned from the
live evidence quoted at the top of this section and verified by `tools/test_local.sh` ("all green"), not replayed
against a running instance.

## 43. Lot R13 — null-key counting guard and a contradiction-node null-handling guard (branch `feature/null-keys-and-contradiction-guard`, 2026-09-28)

**Live measurement, PersVol7 (EBX 6.3.0-RC2, 2026-09-27 23:51, ground truth 2,996 persons = 1,594 real).** The
first address-aware plan gave Personne recall 98%/precision 72% (693 false pairs). Of the 309 false ERP-ERP pairs,
302 came from a single shape: the node "At least 2 of firstNameKey/lastNameKey/emailKey" (`AT_LEAST_N`, onTrue
`SUSPECTED`) had every field's `oneNullValueHandling` set to `DO_NOTHING` - and the add-on's own "At least N fields
match" counting function treats a `DO_NOTHING` null field as an AGREEING field, not an abstention: one filled key
(e.g. an e-mail match) plus one merely-MISSING key (e.g. a birth date never captured on one side) then counted
exactly like two genuinely equal keys. A further 4 false pairs shared two equal keys but disagreed on e-mail and
birth date by 20-40 years - the "contradiction" case: a field genuinely filled and DIFFERENT on both sides should
disqualify a pair outright, before any weaker, similarity-based `SUSPECTED` verdict downstream gets the chance to
confirm it anyway.

### 43.1 Two new structural rules, `master.DecisionTreePlan.validate`/`validateNode`

- **`IDENTITY_COUNT_FIELD_ONE_NULL_MUST_NOT_MATCH`**: a node that COUNTS agreeing fields - `AT_LEAST_N` always, or
  a MULTI-field `ALL_FIELDS` used the same way (`DecisionTreePlan.isIdentityCountingNode`, new: a single-field
  `ALL_FIELDS` node is never "counting" anything - it is a parent-confirmation or relation-match node instead, both
  with their own deliberate `DO_NOTHING` contract, §30/§33.10) - whose `onTrue` leads straight to a terminal outcome
  (`MATCH` or `SUSPECTED`, `DecisionTreePlan.isAmbiguousOutcomeLeaf` reused, §40's own predicate) must give every
  non-relation field's `oneNullValueHandling` the value `NOT_MATCH`. An omitted value is safe (`DecisionTreePlan
  #nestedField`'s own default is already `NOT_MATCH`); only an EXPLICIT other value is refused. A relation (`via`)
  field is exempt - its own `DO_NOTHING` contract (§33/§34: missing CHILD evidence withholds, never disqualifies,
  and never counts as agreement by construction of the relation-evidence guards themselves) is never re-litigated
  by this generic rule.
- **`CONTRADICTION_NODE_WRONG_SHAPE` / `CONTRADICTION_NODE_NULL_HANDLING_MUST_BE_DO_NOTHING`**: the mirror image,
  gated on a NEW, EXPLICIT `DecisionTreePlan.Node#contradiction` marker (default `false`) - **not** inferred from
  the node's shape alone. First attempt inferred it purely from shape (`onFalse` the plain `NOT_MATCHED` leaf,
  `onTrue` continuing to another node) - and immediately broke two pre-existing, perfectly ordinary tests
  (`childEntityIsProposedLikeAnyOther`, `relationMatchNode_refusedWhenNodeAboveHasNoOwnIdentityField`): an
  "identity gate above a further check" cascade node (a fuzzy `email` anchor, or an exact `lastName` identity
  field) routes `onFalse` to `NOT_MATCHED` and `onTrue` onward to a further check ALL THE TIME in this codebase's
  own idiom, with zero contradiction semantics - the shape alone cannot tell the two apart. Restricting to
  exact-algorithm-only fields helped (excluded the fuzzy `email` case) but not enough (`lastName`, exact, still a
  false positive) - so the rule now fires ONLY when the model itself marks a node `"contradiction": true`
  (`propose_match_plan`'s tool schema, new optional node property). When marked: the node must actually have the
  shape (`onFalse` `NOT_MATCHED`, `onTrue` continuing - else `CONTRADICTION_NODE_WRONG_SHAPE`), and then every
  non-relation field must resolve BOTH `bothNullValueHandling` and `oneNullValueHandling` to `DO_NOTHING` - unlike
  the counting rule above, an OMITTED value is NOT safe here (the same `nestedField` default, `NOT_MATCH`, is
  exactly the disqualifying behaviour this node must avoid), so omission is refused exactly like an explicit wrong
  value. A relation field is exempt for the same reason as above. Every plan built before this lot, and every node
  a model never marks, is entirely unaffected - the marker defaults `false`.

Both rules are purely structural (node shape, leaf names, and - for the second - the model's own explicit marker)
- neither knows a column name or a domain word, per the LLM-first discipline this whole file follows: the language
model proposes which field plays which role (and, for a contradiction node, says so explicitly), these guards only
check the shape once it does.

### 43.2 `master.MatchPlanLlmPass` - construction-time guard and two new prompt paragraphs

`Session#buildAndAppendNode` computes `identityCountingNode` once, from the node's own `function`/`onTrue`, exactly
like `average`/`matchTerminal` just above it - and refuses immediately, per field, when a counting field's own
`oneNullValueHandling` resolves to anything other than `NOT_MATCH` (the same "refuse an explicit wrong choice"
idiom the `isReference` guards already use, rather than silently defaulting it, which would hide the exact bug this
lot exists to fix). `DecisionTreePlan.validate`'s own rule (§43.1) is the structural backstop for the legacy
`tiers[]` loop and any plan built another way - `proposeMatchPlan` already calls `validate` on every submission, so
both checks fire for the same live model call, one immediately per field, one over the assembled tree.

`systemPrompt()` gained two paragraphs: **NULL HANDLING ON A COUNTING NODE**, stating the `oneNullValueHandling`
= `NOT_MATCH` contract with the add-on's own counting semantics spelled out, and **CONTRADICTION**, a domain-neutral
principle (examples from two unrelated domains - a birth date/a registration number/a package size) describing the
`onFalse NOT_MATCHED`/`onTrue continuing`/`bothNullValueHandling`+`oneNullValueHandling` `DO_NOTHING` shape and
telling the model to mark such a node `"contradiction": true` explicitly - never left to be guessed from shape.
`Session#proposeMatchPlan`'s per-node loop copies that marker straight onto the built node JSON
(`nodeArg.path("contradiction").asBoolean(false)`) right after `buildAndAppendNode` succeeds - it never influences
that method's own per-field construction, only `DecisionTreePlan.validate`'s post-loop rules.

### 43.3 `master.MatchingPolicyTranslator` - verified, not changed

Checked whether `#nullHandlingByField`'s "first appearance wins" aggregation could flatten two different nodes'
null handling for the same field name into one, as the task brief suspected. **It does not, for the decision tree
itself**: `DecisionTreePlan#toNested`/`#nestedField` write each node occurrence's own `FieldRef#bothNull`/`#oneNull`
directly, per occurrence, never consulting `nullHandlingByField` or any other cross-node aggregation - a field
compared in two different nodes with two different null-handling settings is already written correctly, per node,
today. `nullHandlingByField`'s own aggregation is scoped to the TOP-LEVEL `matchingPolicy.fields[]` pre-clustering
