## 44. Lot R14 - preflight fail-fast regression fixed, single-field null exemption narrowed, and a relink cache-evict path-normalisation bug (branch `fix/preflight-probe-and-single-field-nulls`, 2026-09-28)

### 44.1 Preflight blocked configure on a legitimately slow-but-healthy server

Live evidence, RC, 2026-09-28 10:46/10:49: `POST /projects/{code}/matching/configure` answered a bare 503 ("MCP
server(s) not usable before the step ran ... 'list_data_models' failed: ... SocketTimeoutException: Read timed
out", probe `elapsedMs` 5006) on an instance where `list_data_models` legitimately took 6-79s - lot R12's own
5-second preflight timeout (&sect;42.4) was too tight for a probe whose cost is proportional to the instance's own
DMA model count. The wizard's job path (`MatchingConfigureRun`, no preflight) configured the SAME project in 15s.

Two independent fixes, both in `ebx/McpServers.java`:

- **The `data-model` probe is no longer `list_data_models`.** `McpServers.PROBES` now calls `data_model_guide`
  (static playbook text, no repository read at all, no argument) for that server - genuinely O(1) whatever the
  instance holds, while still proving the account may call a tool of the server at all. Every other probe was
  already constant-time and is unchanged.
- **`preflight` no longer refuses outright on the first timeout.** `McpServers.probe`/`testOne` now allow ONE retry
  on a preflight probe too (previously `pAllowRetry=false` for preflight specifically, R12's own fail-fast design),
  but ONLY when the failure is a genuine `SocketTimeoutException` (`isReadTimeout`, unchanged) - a connection
  refused, an explicit HTTP 401/403/404, or a malformed answer is still refused at once, never retried. The retry
  uses the same generous budget `test`'s own connection-test screen already affords
  (`PROBE_RETRY_READ_TIMEOUT_MS`), scoped to exactly the servers the calling route asked for (never every server on
  the instance). A server that only answers on the retry is reported `ok: true, probe.slowProbe: true` - the route
  proceeds, but the fact that the server was slow is never hidden from the returned `servers` array or a `/connection/test`
  reading.

Together: the common case (a healthy, fast server) still fails in milliseconds; the FORMER live bug's own scenario
(a technically-slow-but-healthy `list_data_models` call) no longer exists (replaced by an O(1) probe); and any
OTHER probe that happens to be slow for unrelated reasons (load, a cold cache after restart) now gets one bounded
retry instead of an immediate false-positive refusal. Tests: `McpServersTest` updated for the new probe tool name;
the retry-marking logic itself is not independently unit-tested beyond that (same discipline as R12's own
`pAllowRetry` gating - `probe`/`testOne` need a live `McpClient`).

### 44.2 Single-field `ALL_FIELDS` null exemption was too broad

Live measurement, project `ret`, 2026-09-28 morning (found by another session): R13's own
`IDENTITY_COUNT_FIELD_ONE_NULL_MUST_NOT_MATCH` rule (&sect;43.1) exempted EVERY single-field `ALL_FIELDS` node from
the counting-node null-handling requirement, on the theory that a single-field node is always a parent-confirmation
or relation-match node. Disproved live: a node comparing a single ORDINARY identifier (`phoneE164`, no role at
all) with `oneNullValueHandling: DO_NOTHING` passed the guard, and a missing phone number then let a
weak "same first name, vaguely similar last name" pair through to `SUSPECTED` - most of `ret`'s 39 false positives
involved a record with no phone number.

Fixed with an EXPLICIT marker rather than an inferred one (same "explicit beats inferred" reasoning R13 already
applied to `contradiction`): `DecisionTreePlan.FieldRef` gained `referenceRole` (default `false`, round-tripped via
`fieldToJson`/`fieldFromJson` exactly like `via`/`dataType`) - `true` only for the single field of a genuine parent
confirmation node. `DecisionTreePlan.isIdentityCountingNode` now treats a single-field `ALL_FIELDS` node as
counting too, UNLESS its one field is a relation (`via`) field or is marked `referenceRole` - both keep their own
deliberate `DO_NOTHING` contract untouched. `MatchPlanLlmPass.Session#buildAndAppendNode`'s own construction-time
guard changed the same way: `identityCountingNode` is now true for a single-field `ALL_FIELDS` node too (not only
multi-field), and the per-field check is skipped when `isReference` (the field already forced to be alone in its
own node with `DO_NOTHING`/`DO_NOTHING`, exact algorithm, minimumScore 100 - the parent-confirmation contract,
&sect;30/&sect;36). The built field JSON now writes `referenceRole: true` for that field, so a LATER
re-validation of the STORED plan (`MatchingPolicyTranslator#buildMatchingPolicyFromPlan`'s own
`DecisionTreePlan.validate` call, which has no attribute-role vocabulary at all) still recognises it and does not
refuse the very node this pass just legitimately built.

Every other single-field `ALL_FIELDS` node whose `onTrue` leads straight to `MATCH`/`SUSPECTED` (no relation, no
`referenceRole` marker) must now carry `oneNullValueHandling: NOT_MATCH`, exactly like the multi-field case R13
already covered. A `contradiction`-marked node is unaffected either way - by contract its `onTrue` continues to
another node, never a leaf, so `isAmbiguousOutcomeLeaf(onTrue)` was already false for it; an explicit
`&& !pNode.contradiction` guard was added to `DecisionTreePlan.validateNode`'s call site anyway, for robustness
should that shape contract ever change.

Tests: `DecisionTreePlanTest` - the OLD blanket-exemption test was replaced with five: an ordinary single-field
node refused (the exact live bug), the same accepted with `NOT_MATCH`, a `referenceRole`-marked field still
exempt, a relation-field single-field node still exempt, and a `contradiction`-marked node never checked by this
rule even when malformed enough to also trip `CONTRADICTION_NODE_WRONG_SHAPE`. `MatchPlanLlmPassTest`: the same

with `DO_NOTHING`, used to test an unrelated translator concern) is adjusted to mark that field `referenceRole` -

### 44.3 `evictDecisionTreeCacheAndVerifyReadBack` compared a bare placeholder name against a slashed one

Live failure, RC, project PersVol7, `PipelineStep` 698, 2026-09-28 10:50: "Cannot evict the match-merge
decision-tree cache for matching policy Personne on /root/Personne: placeholder field emailKey was not found in

## 45. Lot R15 — child evidence needs BOTH roles, and a strong shared identifier must never be bundled away (branch `feature/child-evidence-both-roles`, 2026-09-28)

### 45.1 Two live measurements on the same project (PersVol7, ground truth 1,783 true `Personne` pairs)

Two consecutive plans on the same project, both structurally valid, landed at opposite ends of the precision/recall
trade-off for a completely mechanical reason - which evidence a node combined with which:

- **2026-09-27 23:51** (before lot R13's null-key guard): `N1` exact keys → `SUSPECTED`; false → `N2` name
  similarity ≥ 82 → `[N3` `AT_LEAST_N` keys → `SUSPECTED`; false → `N4` `ALL_FIELDS` address (street, houseNumber,
  postalCode) → `SUSPECTED`; false → `N5`...`]`. Recall 98%, precision 72% - the false pairs came from an empty key
  counting as agreement (fixed by R13, §43).
- **2026-09-28 11:28** (after R13): `N1` `ALL_FIELDS` exact keys (nulls `NOT_MATCH`) → `SUSPECTED`; false → `N2`
  `AVERAGE` ≥ 82 over (firstName, lastName, emailKey, phoneE164) → `N3` `AVERAGE` ≥ 70 on address fields →
  `SUSPECTED`/`NOT_MATCHED`; `N2` false → `NOT_MATCHED`. Precision 100% (only 5 false positives), recall dropped to
  81%: **340 true pairs missed, 312 of them (92%) had an IDENTICAL address on both sides that the plan never even
  looked at**, because their own identity fields (`N2`) never passed the similarity check first.

Root cause, characterised live the same day: **310 of those 312 involve one source system whose person names are
INVERTED at staging** (e.g. "ROUSSEAU Stéphane" landed with `firstName = ROUSSEAU`), so every name-similarity/
name-key node fails for them structurally - not weakly, but ALWAYS, for every record of that source. Yet
`emailKey` was IDENTICAL on both sides for the vast majority of their shared values (952 of 1,567 distinct values
shared across systems, each source individually filled 88-100%). The 2026-09-28 plan required `emailKey` together
with the (unreliable, for this source) name fields inside the SAME `N1`/`N2` nodes - bundling a highly reliable
signal with an unreliable one drags the reliable one down to the unreliable one's own failure rate.

**Conclusion, stated once for both defects (the coordinator's own framing): child evidence placed ONLY under an
own-identity-similarity node acts as a pure FILTER - on 2026-09-27 it was also used as ALTERNATIVE (independent)
evidence, on 2026-09-28 it was not. A plan needs BOTH roles whenever the entity has child evidence, and separately,
an identifier-like field measured as strongly shared and near-unique must get its OWN node, never be smoothed
into an average with fields that can be malformed, split, inverted, or unfilled in one particular source.**

### 45.2 What was built - prompt only, one new combined one-shot challenge, no new `DecisionTreePlan` rule

Per the task brief, R15 deliberately adds **no new structural rule to `DecisionTreePlan.validate`** (that file's
rule set is lot R14's own territory this cycle, on the same branch topology - `isIdentityCountingNode`/
`FieldRef#referenceRole` and the counting-node null check in `MatchPlanLlmPass#buildAndAppendNode`). Everything
below lives in `master.MatchPlanLlmPass` only: two prompt paragraphs, one new pure structural helper, two new pure
evidence-detection helpers, and one new one-shot challenge method reusing the exact mechanism `§34`'s
`relationEvidenceRequiredChallenge` already established (challenge once, accept an identical resubmission
regardless).

- **Prompt, "Relation evidence" section (`appendRelationEvidence`).** The existing "Principle" paragraph gained a
  short "TWO DIFFERENT roles" statement, domain-neutral, restating §45.1's own two roles explicitly: **(a) FILTER**
  - on the branch where the entity's own identity already looks similar, precise child evidence in common
  CONFIRMS (SUSPECTED, or MATCH under the pre-existing shape rules); none in common weakens it (NOT_MATCHED, or a
  coarser level). **(b) INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE** - on the branch where the entity's own identity is NOT similar, or
  cannot even be compared (a value missing, split, or malformed in one source), an EXACT match on PRECISE child
  evidence still deserves a data steward's review: a node there too, the same precise child key alone, onTrue
  SUSPECTED (never MATCH - own identity never agreed, nothing here confirms outright by itself), onFalse
  NOT_MATCHED. The paragraph states the consequence of building only the first role in the model's own terms and
  quotes the measured effect abstractly, as the coordinator asked: *"a plan whose ONLY child-evidence node sits
  under an own-identity-similar branch loses every pair whose own identity is dissimilar or incomparable - in one
  measured case, 312 of 340 missed pairs had identical child evidence the plan never got to look at."*
- **Prompt, system prompt.** A new "STANDALONE SHARED IDENTIFIERS" paragraph, inserted right after "CONTRADICTION"
  and before "Tools:" (`systemPrompt()`): an identifier-like field measured as widely shared across systems AND
  near-unique among its filled values deserves its OWN exact-match node, built and checked BEFORE any node that
  also requires name/description similarity - never bundled with fields that may be malformed/split/inverted/
  unfilled in one source, "judged on its OWN evidence" rather than averaged down to a weaker field's level. It
  restates the 310-of-312-inverted-names measurement abstractly (no field name, no project name) and says the
  rule is about the field's own MEASURED shareability/uniqueness, never its name - consistent with every other
  paragraph in this file (LLM-first, `mdm-factory-llm-first-suggestions.md`).
- **`MatchPlanLlmPass.reachableOnlyViaOnTrue(Plan)`** - the pure helper the task named explicitly. `true` iff the
  plan has at least one relation-bearing node AND every one of them is reached exclusively via another node's
  `onTrue` (never the plan's own `root`, which has no incoming edge, and never any node's `onFalse`) - exactly the
  "filter-only" shape of §45.1's second measurement. Checks only the DIRECT incoming edge of each relation node
  (the same convention `Session#checkRelationMatchNodeShape` already uses for the same question), not a full
  transitive closure - sufficient because every relation node is considered independently by the same loop, so an
  upstream relation node reached via `onFalse` is caught on its OWN iteration regardless of what sits below it.
  `false` (not "not applicable") when the plan has no relation-bearing node at all - the caller asks that question
  separately, via `EntityInfo#relationChildren`.
- **`MatchPlanLlmPass.isStandaloneIdentifierCandidate(EntityInfo, AttributeInfo)`** - evidence-only, no field
  names. Reuses the exact thresholds the pre-existing MATCH-terminal identifier guard already applies
  (`Session#MIN_FILL_RATE_FOR_IDENTIFIER`/`MIN_DISTINCT_RATIO_FOR_IDENTIFIER`), measured on whichever of the
  attribute itself or (when `AttributeInfo#matchKey` names one) its own derived key actually carries reliable
  fill/cardinality statistics - the key is preferred when both are reliable, since that is the field name a plan
  would actually compare. "Widely shared across systems" reads `AttributeInfo#sharedFoldGroupCount > 0` - the only
  cross-system-overlap evidence this pass already carries at prompt time (§34.3's own per-attribute rendering). A
  `SOURCE_KEY` (never comparable across sources by construction) or a `REFERENCE` (a foreign key, not an
  identifier of this entity) is never a candidate, whatever it measures.
- **`MatchPlanLlmPass.hasStandaloneIdentifierEvidence(EntityInfo)`/`planHasStandaloneIdentifierNode(EntityInfo,
  Plan)`** - the entity-level "does such a field exist at all" and plan-level "does the plan already give it its
  own single-field node, routing onTrue to MATCH or SUSPECTED" checks the challenge below composes.
- **`Session#relationAndIdentifierRolesChallenge(EntityInfo, Plan)`** - ONE combined one-shot challenge, evaluated
  over the fully-built, already-valid tree (unlike R3/R4's raw-JSON scan, this one needs the real edges), right
  after `checkRelationMatchNodeShape` in `proposeMatchPlan`. Checks BOTH gaps independently (the filter-only gap
  requires relation evidence to exist at all; the identifier gap is checked regardless of relation evidence) and
  lists whichever apply in ONE message, exactly as the coordinator asked ("one refusal total, listing both gaps") -
  never two separate refusals for the same submission. One-shot bookkeeping via a new field,
  `Session#challengedRelationAndIdentifierRoles`, the same `Set<String>`-of-entity-names mechanism as
  `challengedRelationRequirement`/`challengedSkips`.

## 46. Lot R16 — pre-clustering dominance of a standalone shared identifier (branch `feature/preclustering-dominance`, 2026-09-28)

### 46.1 The measurement (PersVol7, `/root/Personne`, 2,996 rows, ground truth 1,783 true pairs)

§45's own "STANDALONE SHARED IDENTIFIERS" node (root `N0`, "Same emailKey": `ALL_FIELDS`, single field `emailKey`,
`ebx-addon-mame@exact`, `minimumScore` 100, `onTrue` `SUSPECTED`, `onFalse` the name-similarity node) gets a node
of its own in the DECISION TREE — but the add-on's own pre-clustering (candidate search, run before the tree is
ever evaluated) does not see the tree at all: it is a SEPARATE, APPROXIMATE, WEIGHTED search over every field
`matchingPolicy.fields` declares (`MatchingPolicyTranslator`'s own `weightsByField`, the highest weight any node
gives a field, defaulting a never-weighted field to 1). With `emailKey` at its default weight (3, in this project)
against `lastName` 4 + `firstName` 3 + `lastNameKey` 2 + `firstNameKey` 2 + three relation fields 1 each = 14: 30
true pairs whose `emailKey` was IDENTICAL were never even proposed as candidates — their names were inverted or
unsplit in one source, which pulled the weighted candidate score down below the search cutoff — and 26 false pairs
("close names, no common e-mail") were candidates instead. Precision/recall: 99%/97%. Raising `emailKey`'s weight
to 20 (stricty above the sum of the rest, 14): 100%/98%, the 30 found, the 26 false gone. `matching_config_schema`
offers only `weight` (integer ≥ 0) and `searchStrategy` per field — no "mandatory"/exact-candidate rule exists at
all, so weight DOMINANCE is the only lever this add-on gives for "this field alone must be enough to make two
records comparable, whatever their other fields look like."

### 46.2 A purely structural detector, `master.DecisionTreePlan.standaloneIdentifierFieldNames(Plan)`

Domain-neutral by construction (no column name, no business word) — reads the tree's own shape, nothing else. A
node qualifies when: it is the plan's `root`, OR reached from the root exclusively through the `onFalse` branch of
every earlier QUALIFYING node in the chain (an `onTrue` edge, or the first non-qualifying node — in particular any
`AVERAGE`/similarity node — stops the walk outright; nothing past it is even visited, let alone excluded after the
fact); its function is `ALL_FIELDS` with EXACTLY ONE field; that field is neither a relation (`via`) field nor
marked `referenceRole` (a parent-confirmation node, §45.2/§14's own distinct concept, is never an identifier of
this entity); its algorithm is exact (`ebx-addon-mame@exact` or `exactFullText`, suffix match, case-insensitive —
the same convention `review.MatchSimulationBlock#isExactAlgorithm` already used for the first form, extended here
to recognise the full-text one too, factored out as `DecisionTreePlan.isExactAlgorithm`); its `minimumScore` is
null or 100 (the add-on's own documented default); and its `onTrue` is a terminal outcome (`isAmbiguousOutcomeLeaf`
— `MATCH` or `SUSPECTED`). Returns bare field names, root-to-leaf order, one per qualifying node — a plan may stack
more than one (e.g. an e-mail node above a national-id node, both before the first similarity node).

### 46.3 The guard, `master.MatchingPolicyTranslator.applyPreClusteringDominance`

Lives INSIDE `buildMatchingPolicyFromPlan`, the one shared choke point both `buildMatchingPolicy` and
`buildMatchingPolicyWithRelationFields` already funnel through — run right after `weightsByField` is computed and
before the `matchingPolicy.fields` array is written, so the raised weight (if any) is what the payload actually
carries, and so `MatchingPolicyComparator` (which always re-derives its own "desired" policy through this same
method) sees the raised value too, never the original proposal — no spurious stored-vs-desired diff on a field this
guard ever touches.

For each standalone identifier field, its weight must be STRICTLY GREATER than the sum of every OTHER field
`matchingPolicy.fields` declares (relation fields included, counted through their placeholder substitution — see
below). When the proposal already dominates, it is left untouched. When it does not, it is raised to
`sum-of-the-others + 1` — NEVER lowered, and no other field's weight is ever touched. With more than one
standalone identifier in the leading chain, EACH one only has to dominate the sum of the NON-identifier fields —
they are never required to also dominate each other (an arbitrary ordering would otherwise shrink whichever one
happens to be computed "second"; both are independently reliable signals and each deserves to anchor pre-clustering
on its own).

A relation (child) field is counted at its EFFECTIVE pre-clustering weight (lot M2, §48.1): the MCPGAP relation-fields
workaround (`buildMatchingPolicyWithRelationFields`) substitutes a relation field's `field` to a same-typed PARENT placeholder
*before* this guard runs (§33/§34), so the placeholder stands in for it in `fieldOrder`; the relationship row's own weight
(`requirements.relationClusteringWeights`, default 0) is added separately as `relationWeightSum`. (Before M2 the relation
field was counted only through the placeholder, at the plan's own node weight.)

One entry is recorded per standalone identifier field found, whether or not it needed raising (`raised: false`
when the proposal already dominated) — `{field, proposedWeight, sumOfOtherFieldsWeight, appliedWeight, raised}` —
returned as an `ArrayNode` on `MatchingPolicyTranslator.RelationTranslationResult#preClusteringDominanceNotes`
(the plain `buildMatchingPolicy` entry point drops the notes; nothing outside `ebx.MatchingConfigurator` records a
step detail today). `ebx.MatchingConfigurator#configureOne` sets it verbatim under `detail.preClusteringDominance`
of the `MATCHING_CONFIG` `PipelineStep`, alongside `sourceKeyFieldNames`/`relationFieldCount` and the rest — only
when non-empty (nothing to say for a plan with no standalone identifier).

### 46.4 Prompt, `master.MatchPlanLlmPass`

One sentence added to the end of the existing "STANDALONE SHARED IDENTIFIERS" paragraph (§45.2): give the field its
own weight ABOVE the sum of every other field's weight on the plan, because pre-clustering is an approximate,
weighted search that runs BEFORE the tree is ever evaluated — a merely-average weight lets the unreliable fields
outvote a perfectly matching identifier, and the pair is never even proposed as a candidate. States the exact
number does not matter, only that it clearly dominates, and that the system raises it further on its own if the
proposal still falls short once every field's weight is known — so the model is told the floor exists without
having to compute the exact sum itself (it may not even know every other field's final weight at propose time, all
of it being on the same tool call). No new tool round trip: the Java guard in §46.3 is the actual enforcement.

### 46.5 `MatchingPolicyComparator` — verified, not changed

Compares two ALREADY-BUILT `matchingPolicy` `ObjectNode`s field by field, including `weight` (`canonicalizeField`,

`buildMatchingPolicyFromPlan` both the "stored" and "desired" sides of any comparison are built through, a
raised weight is symmetric on both sides whenever both are computed from the guard-carrying code (i.e. always,
post this lot) — never a diff by itself.

## 47. Lot V2-B — simulating a plan that compares child-table (relation) fields (branch `fix/simulate-relation-fields`, 2026-09-30)

### 47.1 The live failure (Vol100k, `Personne`, 2026-09-29 18:00, `PipelineStep` 773 and 774)

"Simulate on 20 pivots" on the Personne plan (four tiers; P3 and P4 compare `Adresse.street`, `houseNumber`,
`postalCode`, `city` through the parent relation) failed at `generate_matching_policy` with `INVALID_PARAMS`,
"Matching field '/street' does not resolve to a field of table /root/Personne", and the wizard kept saying "Not
simulated yet" (the failure only reached the notice at the top of the page).

Root cause: `ebx.MatchingPreviewPolicy` translated the plan with `MatchingPolicyTranslator#buildMatchingPolicy`,
which knows nothing of relation fields (`DecisionTreePlan.FieldRef#via`): it declared `/street` as a field of the
parent. `Configure` never had the problem because `MatchingConfigurator.configureOne` translates with
`buildMatchingPolicyWithRelationFields` (a same-typed PLACEHOLDER parent field stands in for each child field) and
relinks last (`mcpgap.RelationFieldRelinker`, `docs/RELATION_FIELDS_WORKAROUND.md`). Two code paths, one of them
never taught about relation fields. `MatchingPreviewPolicyTest#rootCause_plainTranslationSendsTheChildFieldsAsParentFields`
pins the failing shape on the real Vol100k plan (`RelationTierStripperTest.VOL100K_PERSONNE`).

### 47.2 One translation for both paths, relation fields simulated

- `MatchingPreviewPolicy#translate` (pure, unit-tested) is now the only translation of a plan into the preview policy: a
  plan without a child field goes through `buildMatchingPolicy` exactly as before; a plan comparing child fields goes
  through `buildMatchingPolicyWithRelationFields`, the SAME call `configureOne` makes, fed by the same inputs
  (`MatchingConfigurator.parentFieldDataTypes` / `relationChildInfoByEntity`, now package-private, off the master model).
- The preview keeps every rule of §8/§25/§26: `active: true`, `matchingOnCreation`/`matchingOnUpdate` = 0 (MANUAL), never the
  table's `defaultMatchingPolicy` (cleared after generation), merge policy link by `patch_matching_config` after
  `generate_merge_policy`, and a soft miss from a generate tool is a failure.
- The relation fields are linked by `MatchingPreviewPolicy#relinkRelationFields`, called by
  `MatchPlanSimulationRunner#simulate` AFTER its activation check and BEFORE the first `simulateMatch` — relink LAST
  (`activate_matching` can re-persist the tree and revert a relink, `docs/RELATION_FIELDS_WORKAROUND.md` lot R7). It is
  the same `RelationFieldRelinker.relink` + cache eviction + read-back (`MatchingConfigurator
  .evictDecisionTreeCacheAndVerifyReadBack`) as the real policy, minus the pause/unpause of the table's matching: a preview
  that fails to link must not pause a table whose real policy runs. One `PipelineStep` (`MATCHING_SIMULATE_PREVIEW`) per
  phase, FAILED with the full detail.
- The add-on's `simulateMatch`/`executeDecisionTree` evaluate relation fields like a real run does (same engine: the real run on
  Personne, 33,374 suspect pairs, used them), so nothing in that API prevents simulating them — but the linked preview was
  NOT exercised live this lot (write tools forbidden): §47.5.

### 47.3 The fallback: simulate WITHOUT the relation tiers, and say so (`master.RelationTierStripper`)

When the relation fields cannot be written or linked — no same-typed placeholder parent field, master model unreadable, a
relink the add-on refuses — the plan is simulated on its remaining tiers and the result says which tiers were not
simulated and why, in the strip and the simulation block ("Not simulated: P3 (Adresse.street, ...) compares fields of a
related table; its pairs are reported as decided by the remaining tiers. Reason: ..."):

- Semantics: a tier that cannot be evaluated "did not fire". Every reference to a relation node is replaced by its own `onFalse`
  (the rule the legacy `tiers[]` cascade always had), a node whose two branches then reach the same target is removed
  (match-merge refuses it), unreachable nodes are dropped. Vol100k's plan becomes: same `emailKey` -> SUSPECTED, otherwise
  NOT_MATCHED — a LOWER BOUND on the suspects (the pairs only P3/P4 could suspect are missing), never an invented verdict.
- A plan whose every tier is a relation tier has nothing left to simulate: a failure, with that message.
- The fallback is automatic for a translation refusal and for a relink failure (`MatchPlanSimulationRunner` rewrites the preview
  from the stripped plan with `MatchingPreviewPolicy#ensureWithoutRelationTiers` and re-checks the activation).

### 47.4 A failed simulation is visible; the guard on a table that already carries relation fields

- The simulate action handler (`ProjectWizardUserService#simulateMatch`, `ProposalReviewUserService#simulateOne`) stores the failure
  as the plan's result (`MatchPlanView.SimulationResult#failed`); the strip and the simulation block show it as one warning line
  under the Simulate button (truncated to 400 characters; the FAILED `PipelineStep` keeps the full detail) instead of an unchanged
  "Not simulated yet". The notice at the top is unchanged.
- `apply_matching_config` replaces the whole policy list and ignores `useRelationships`/`location` on input (read-only in
  `matching_config_schema`). The old preview code copied every REAL policy back verbatim: on a table whose real policy carries relation
  fields (live Personne: four fields `BY_FOREIGN_KEY`, `location.associationTable` `/root/Adresse/personneRef`) that would rewrite them as
  plain fields of the parent. `MatchingPreviewPolicy#carriesRelationFieldsOutsidePreview` now refuses the rewrite of the preview
  (`ensureRewrite`: a clear failure, "Configure this plan to simulate it on the real policy") and makes `remove` leave the
  preview in place (`removed: false` with a note; the next configure of the entity drops it, `MatchingConfigRewriteBuilder`). Before
  this, a Simulate followed by a Configure on a relation plan ended with `remove` applying the real relinked policy verbatim, i.e. the
  case `relinkVerifiedAtEnd` was written to catch.

### 47.5 Tests, and what is not verified

Tests (all in `tools/test_local.sh`): `RelationTierStripperTest` (the real Vol100k plan: P3/P4 fall to NOT_MATCHED, P2 collapses, the
skipped tiers are named with their fields; input not mutated; root relation tier; all-relation plan; plain plan untouched; the stripped
plan translates without any child field), `MatchingPreviewPolicyTest` (root cause, the relation translation with placeholders and one
spec per child field (7 on Vol100k), the three fallbacks and the all-relation refusal, plain plan identical to the ordinary
translation, the guard on the live Personne policy / plain policy / preview-only / null mode), `MatchPlanViewTest` (the failure line in
the strip and in the block, escaping and truncation, the skipped-tiers note).

Not verified: no write tool was used. The linked preview (`relinkRelationFields` on a preview policy, then `simulateMatch` reading it)
and the fallback rewrite have never run against the add-on; the relinker itself was written for the real policy, and its cache
eviction (`set_field_weight` on the placeholder) is assumed to behave the same on a preview code. `activate_matching`'s effect on
a relinked tree was inferred from lot R7, not measured for a preview.

## 48. Pre-clustering weight of a relation field (`requirements.relationClusteringWeights`, branch `feature/relation-field-clustering-weight`, 2026-10-03)

**The need (volume experiment, 2026-10-03).** The four `Adresse` fields (street, houseNumber, postalCode, city) of the Personne decision tree
took part in the candidate search ("pre-clustering") and cost 99 % of a 78-minute matching run at 1 M rows. The weight of a RELATION matching
field (`MatchingField.preclustering.weight`, `useAssociation = 1`) was written as a literal 1 by `mcpgap.RelationFieldRelinker.createMatchingField`
and nobody could change it: `patch_matching_config` / `apply_matching_config` refuse a cross-table field ("editing the pre-processing of a
cross-table matching field is not supported yet") and the add-on's configuration dataset is "Access denied" in the data UI.

**The key.** Optional and additive, next to `clusteringFields` in `MatchPlan.requirements`:

```json
"relationClusteringWeights": { "Adresse.street": 0, "Adresse.houseNumber": 0, "Adresse.postalCode": 0, "Adresse.city": 0 }
```

Key = `<childEntity>.<field>` exactly as the tree names the relation field (`FieldRef.via` + "." + `FieldRef.field`); value = integer >= 0 (0 takes the
field out of the candidate search, it still takes part in the decision tree's comparison). Absent key, or absent entry = **0** since lot M2 (below; it was 1 when the key was introduced). A value that is not an integer >= 0, or a key that is not an object, REFUSES the translation (`IllegalStateException` naming the key) - a typo
must not run an experiment on the wrong weights. Entries naming no relation field of the plan are ignored. The key is read from `requirements` directly
(it is not part of the decision tree); since lot M2 `MatchPlanLlmPass` carries it over and may emit it (below).

**Path.** `MatchingPolicyTranslator.readRelationClusteringWeights` -> `buildMatchingPolicyWithRelationFields` builds each `RelationFieldSpec` with
`preclusteringWeight` (new 7-argument constructor; the 6-argument one keeps 1; the REST handler `mcpgap.RelationFieldsRestHandler` accepts an optional
`preclusteringWeight` per spec) -> `RelationFieldRelinker.createMatchingField` writes it on a new row; **an existing row is UPDATED** (`updateWeightIfDifferent`,
only when the stored weight differs; when several specs of one call share a row, the first spec's weight wins) -> `RelationFieldRelinker.verify` reads the
row back and fails (`expectedWeight`/`actualWeight` in the report) on a wrong weight. `MatchingConfigurator` records `relationPreclusteringWeights` in the
`MATCHING_CONFIG` step detail; the per-field relink report carries `weightUpdated`.

**Re-configure on an already configured project.** `matching/configure` calls `relinkRelationFields` at the end of EVERY branch, `RESUME_SAME` included (the
comparator does not see the relation rows' weight, so an unchanged tree still resumes), and the relinker's existing-row path now rewrites the weight: no
`delete_matching_config` needed. The add-on's per-table decision-tree cache is evicted by the existing post-relink step. Not run live: only the pure parts
(parser, spec, weight comparison) are unit-tested (`MatchingPolicyTranslatorRelationWeightTest`, `RelationFieldRelinkerTest`); the write and the `verify`
read-back need a live add-on dataset.

### 48.1 Lot M2 (2026-10-03): the default becomes 0, a relation field is compared but not searched (branch `feature/relation-weight-default-zero`)

**Decision (product owner, 2026-10-03, after a measured 1 M-row test): a relation matching field does NOT take part in the Match and Merge candidate
search by default.** Measured on 153,937 pivots against 576,692 persons (`Personne`, four `Adresse` fields: street, houseNumber, postalCode, city):

| relation fields in the candidate search | run | precision | recall |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| the four `Adresse` fields at pre-clustering weight 1 | 78 min 40 | 99.2 % | 91.9 % |
| the same four at weight 0 (still compared in the decision tree) | 8 min 54 | 99.85 % | 88.9 % |
| one relation field kept at weight 1 | 24 min | same pairs as the four | |

A positive weight makes the candidate search join the child table for every pivot (about 9x slower at 1 M rows); keeping a single relation field at 1
costs a third of that and finds exactly the same pairs, so the weight is a speed lever, not a quality one. The decision tree still compares the
relation fields (that is where the precision comes from), only the search ignores them.

**New default semantics.** `requirements.relationClusteringWeights` absent, or a relation field (`<childEntity>.<field>`) absent from it = weight **0**
(`RelationFieldSpec.DEFAULT_PRECLUSTERING_WEIGHT = 0`, also the 6-argument constructor and the REST handler's missing `preclusteringWeight`). An explicit
entry still wins: any integer >= 0, `1` or more puts that field back into the candidate search.

**An already configured project changes behaviour at its next `matching/configure`, on purpose.** The relinker rewrites the stored weight of an
existing relationship row (`updateWeightIfDifferent`) and `configure` relinks in every branch, `RESUME_SAME` included, so a project whose rows were
created with weight 1 gets 0 written the next time it is configured, with no change to the plan (`MATCHING_CONFIG` detail `relationPreclusteringWeights`
shows `0`, and the relink report `weightUpdated: true`). The next matching run is then fast and finds fewer candidates (recall -3 points in the
measurement above). A project that wants the old behaviour sets the key explicitly (`{"Adresse.street":1,...}`) before configuring.

**The language-model pass keeps the key** (`master.MatchPlanLlmPass`): (a) `propose_match_plan` has an optional `relationClusteringWeights` member (object,
integer values >= 0), described in the tool schema in two sentences - default 0 is the measured safe choice, a positive weight makes the search join the
child table for every pivot and was measured ~9x slower at 1 M rows; a key that is not a `<child entity>.<field>` of a relation field used in the proposed
tree, a negative or non-integer value, or a non-object is REFUSED with the valid keys named (a silently dropped weight would run a very different search);
(b) the plan it supersedes/rewrites (`ExistingPlan.requirements`, PROPOSED or SUPERSEDED) hands its entries over, filtered to the relation fields still in the
new tree, and the model's own entries are laid on top (an explicit entry wins, `0` included); the key is written only when non-empty. `sameStructure`
compares the key too (a changed weight is a real change).

**Screen** (`review.MatchPlanTreeDiagram`, wizard step 6, band "How candidates are found"): the search sentence lists only the fields that take part - a
relation field only when its weight is above 0 - and a one-line note follows when relation fields are compared but not searched ("The fields of related
records (Street, City) are compared below but take no part in this search." / French equivalent), bundle key `review.match.tree.clustering.relationsNotSearched`
in both `Messages_*.properties`.

**Dominance guard (§46.3) counts the effective weight.** Until now the guard counted a relation field only through its parent placeholder (the field the
translator substitutes for it), which was never the real weight of the relationship row: in particular the plan's own `FieldRef.weight` of a relation field
leaked into the placeholder's `matchingPolicy.fields[].weight`. Both are gone: `weightsByField` ignores relation fields, and
`MatchingPolicyTranslator.relationWeightSum` (distinct `<via>.<field>`, effective weights, computed before the placeholder substitution renames them) is
added to the sum an identifier must dominate. With the default 0 a relation field adds nothing; an explicit weight 9 adds 9 (`MatchingPolicyTranslatorDominanceTest`).
Not changed: `MatchingPolicyComparator` (the relation rows' weight is still invisible to it), and nothing was run against a live add-on.

Tests: `MatchingPolicyTranslatorRelationWeightTest` (default 0, explicit entries, spec constructors), `MatchingPolicyTranslatorDominanceTest` (effective weight in
the sum), `MatchPlanLlmPassTest` (schema member, emitted, refused, carried, model entry wins, `sameStructure`), `MatchPlanTreeDiagramTest` (band lists, note, French).

read-back need a live add-on dataset. The dominance guard (§46) still counts the plan's own weights, not these.

## 49. Lot M4 — four defects of the 1 M-row matching test (branch `fix/matching-run-defects`, 2026-10-03)

Found live on 2026-10-03 on project Vol1m (EBX 6.3.0-rc2, `ebx-addon-mame`, 576,692 master rows).

### 49.1 Stopping a `MATCHING_RUN` job now stops the add-on's process (`ebx.MameMatchingApi`)

**Live failure.** `POST /rest/v1/jobs/161/cancel` answered `cancelRequested: true`, the job ended `CANCELLED` ("Matching run stopped
(stopped by admin)…"), but the add-on's 8 `ebx-clustering-N` threads stayed at 100 % CPU until Tomcat was restarted: the poll loop of
`MameMatchingApi.launchScoped` only LEFT the loop on the job's flag, it never told the add-on.

**What the public API offers (`javap`, 2026-10-03, `ebx-addons.jar` and `webapps/ebx-addon-mame/WEB-INF/classes`).**
`com.orchestranetworks.addon.mame.service.matching.MatchingProcess` has `getMatchingStatus()`, `getDetail()`, `getExecutionDate()`,
`getCompletionRate()`, `getDuration()` and **`void cancel()`**. The concrete `common.process.MatchingOperationProcess extends
PhasingOperationProcess extends OperationProcess`; `OperationProcess.cancel()` (synchronized) calls `stop(new ProcessCancelException())`,
which stores the exception (the process' own `abortCheck()` rethrows it at its check points) and, in `MatchingOperationProcess.stop`,
calls `ClusterProducer.abort(message)` on the clustering producer (the `ebx-clustering` pool of `CnyCanopyProducer`) and sets the status
`CANCELLING`; `finish()` then turns `CANCELLING` into `CANCELLED` (an abort that was not a cancel becomes `FAILED`). So the stop is
cooperative: `CANCELLED` is the add-on's own confirmation that the process thread ended. No `ProcessManager` / `OperationsFactory` call is
needed (`common.process.ProcessManager` is internal).

**Behaviour now.** When the handle's stop flag is set (a person's Stop, or the watchdog's inactivity limit - both only set that flag) or the
job thread is interrupted, `launchScoped` calls `MameMatchingApi.requestStop`: `process.cancel()`, then polls `getMatchingStatus()` every
500 ms for at most `STOP_CONFIRM_WAIT_MS` (120 s) until it is terminal. The outcome (`StopOutcome`: requested, confirmed, finalStatus,
waitedMs, note) is stored in the entity's step detail under `process.stop` and a sentence is appended to the step message:
"The add-on confirmed the stop (CANCELLED after 3.2 s)." or "The add-on's process is still running: it has not confirmed the stop after
120.0 s (status CANCELLING)." or, if `cancel()` itself threw, "…it cannot be stopped from here (MatchingProcess.cancel() failed: …)".
`MatchingConfigurator.run` returns `stopUnconfirmed` (entities whose process did not confirm) and `MatchingRunRun.message` then ends the job
with "Warning: the add-on's process is still running on N entity(ies) (it did not confirm the stop)…" - "stopped" never passes for "the add-on
stopped". A synchronous caller (no handle: the REST `matching/run`, a workflow bean) is unchanged: it keeps its bounded wait and leaves the
process running, as documented.

**Not verifiable offline:** that `cancel()` really ends the 8 clustering threads on a 1 M-row run, and how long the abort takes on one (the
120 s wait is a guess to be measured). Unit tests (`MameMatchingApiTest`, `MatchingRunRunTest`) cover the wait/bound/failure logic against a
fake `MatchingProcess`.

### 49.2 `matching/configure` configures an APPLIED plan again (`ebx.MatchingConfigurator#configure`)

**Live failure (Vol1m).** After a plan reached `APPLIED` (its first successful configure, `markPlanApplied`), editing its `requirements`
and calling `POST /projects/{code}/matching/configure` answered "0 entities configured, 0 refused, 2 not accepted": the loop only
accepted `ACCEPTED`, so the plan had to be put back to `ACCEPTED` by hand.

**Now.** The loop uses `TechnicalKeyRule.isAcceptedLike` (`ACCEPTED` or `APPLIED`, the same test staging and the master generator use) through
the pure `MatchingConfigurator.isConfigurablePlanStatus`. `configureOne` is unchanged: its compare of the translated plan against what the
add-on holds already decides `RESUME_SAME` (nothing to write), `REWRITE` or `GENERATE_FRESH`. The summary sentence
(`MatchingConfigureRun.message`) now counts the `RESUME_SAME` entities - "N entities configured, U unchanged (already up to date), R refused,
X not accepted." (the `U unchanged` clause only when U > 0) - so an up-to-date APPLIED plan is neither "not accepted" nor invisible.
`PROPOSED`, `REJECTED`, `SUPERSEDED` and a missing plan are still "not accepted" (a REJECTED one still goes to `excludedByDecision`).

Verified offline: the status predicate and the sentence (`MatchingConfigureRunTest`). Only live: an APPLIED plan with changed requirements
actually REWRITEs the add-on's policy.

### 49.3 The results snapshot counts every record, and the run says what it covered (`ebx.MatchingResultsBuilder`, `matching.MatchStats`)

**Live failure (Vol1m).** After an incremental run (pivots = the last loaded batch, `./_loadId='…'`) the KPI `total` read 338,257 for a
576,692-row table, `golden` 153,937, and the source band showed one source. `queryStateSourceCounts` ran `… WHERE c."Linked_Field_State"
<> 4 GROUP BY …`: a record the add-on never touched has a NULL state, `NULL <> 4` is not true, so every untouched record was dropped.

**Now.** The statement is still ONE `GROUP BY "Linked_Field_State", "sourceSystem"` but has no `WHERE`: DELETED (state 4) comes back as a
group of its own and `MatchStats.fromStateSourceCounts` drops it (it already did, defensively); a NULL state is read as `UNSET`. `total` is
therefore the table's row count (DELETED aside), `recordsBySource` covers every source, and the new `Kpis.unmatchedRecords` (state UNSET or
NULL, stored as `kpis.unmatched` in the snapshot JSON - additive, an older snapshot reads 0, no version bump) says how many records have not
been through matching yet. The screen (`MatchResultsView.renderKpis`) states it under the KPI cards when it is not zero ("N of the M records
have not been through matching yet (an incremental run only matches the last loaded batch)…"). `golden` stays the GOLDEN state alone, and the
source band stays "where the golden records come from" (GOLDEN + MERGED groups): untouched records are not goldens, the sentence above is
what explains the gap.

**Scope of a run, said plainly.** `MatchingConfigurator.runInternal` counts, before launching (one `RequestResult.getSize()` each), the
records the run's predicate selects (the pivots) and the table's rows (`MatchingConfigurator.countRecords`; for scope ALL the predicate is the
whole table, one count only), writes `scope {mode, pivots, totalRecords, sentence}` in the entity step's detail and appends the sentence
(`MatchingRunScope.describe`) to the step message, which is what the wizard's run block ("Last run: DONE, …") and the live panel show:
"Scope: incremental - 338,257 of 576,692 records were pivots (the last loaded batch); the other 238,435 were not matched in this run." A count
that fails reads -1 and the sentence says the counts were not available - it never stops a run.

**Not verified live:** the statement itself on Vol1m (NULL group key in the aggregate, the cost of the unfiltered GROUP BY on 576,692 rows - the
same scan as before, the `WHERE` did not use an index), and that Linked_Field_State is NULL rather than 0 for never-touched records (both are
handled). **Same defect elsewhere, left alone (outside the brief):** `GoldenRecordsReader.queryEntityCounts` (step 8, the summary) still has
`WHERE c."Linked_Field_State" <> 4`, so its TOTAL also omits never-touched records.

### 49.4 The instance barely answers during a run - what the Factory controls (and what it does not)

**Live symptom (Vol1m, 2026-10-03).** During a run `GET /rest/v1/projects/Vol1m/jobs` and plain Data Services reads took 60-120 s, Tomcat
CPU ~385-510 %, the add-on's 8 `ebx-clustering-N` threads busy.

**(c) The clustering thread count - found, not configurable.** `javap -p -c` on `ebx-lib.jar`,
`com.orchestranetworks.cce.lucene.clustering.canopy.CnyCanopyProducer` (the only class holding the string `ebx-clustering`): the pool is
`Executors.newFixedThreadPool(getNbThreads(selectionSize), ThreadUtils.createNamedThreadFactory("ebx-clustering"))` and
`getNbThreads(int)` answers `Runtime.getRuntime().availableProcessors()` when the selection holds more than 1000 records, 2 when it
holds 5 to 1000, 1 otherwise (a serverless-test override `CnyCanopyProducerSpec.getNumberOfThreadsForTests()` only applies in test mode).
**No `ebx.properties` property, no add-on property** sets it: the `ebx.addon.mame.*` names in the add-on webapp (eagerMerge, grouping,
merge, matching.resultQueueCapacity, decisionTree.cache.maxSize…) and `ebx.clustering.balanceFieldScore` / `clusteringBatchFetch` /
`matchSensitivityBoost` tune other things, and `ebx.index.threads` is the Lucene indexing pool. So 8 threads = 8 logical CPUs, every core,
for a 1 M-row run: the only knob is the JVM's `-XX:ActiveProcessorCount=<n>` (which also changes GC and common-pool sizing) - an operator
decision, nothing changed here.

**(a) `GET /projects/{code}/jobs` - partly at fault, fixed.** It reads only `FactoryJob` and `PipelineStep` rows through EBX (no add-on
call, no MCP), but (1) it ran TWO full `FactoryJob` predicate scans (`active`, then "not QUEUED/RUNNING"; 6.3 ignores the module's `<index>`
so each is a pass over a table that only grows) and (2) for each of the ten "recent" finished jobs AND each active one it looked up the
parent `PipelineStep` and read its `detail` - up to 70 000 characters each (the matching-results snapshot) - to put it in `progressJson`,
which the wizard only uses for RUNNING landing/staging/master jobs. Now: one scan split by status, and `stepMessage`/`progressJson` are
read for RUNNING jobs only (`stepId` still comes from the job row). The wizard reads nothing else of those fields (`wizard.js`: `job.message`
for finished jobs, `stepMessage`/`progressJson` for RUNNING ones). The route's `./code=` Project lookup is a scan of a tiny table.

**(b) The MATCHING_RUN job's own polling - not at fault, unchanged.** `MameMatchingApi.launchScoped` polls every 500 ms: `MatchingProcess.
getMatchingStatus()` (a volatile field read), then `getDetail()`, `getCompletionRate()`, `getDuration()` (`javap -c`: the phase name, a loop over
the in-memory phase map plus `ClusterProducer.getCurrentProgress()`, `Instant.now`) - no table read, no EBX query - and `Handle.cancelled()`
(one volatile write). It does not touch EBX or the repository.

**Other Factory-side periodic reads, left as they are (facts).** The job dispatcher ticks every 2 s for the life of the module
(`FactoryJobQueue.tick`: `./status='QUEUED'` scan of `FactoryJob`, also run on every enqueue/release); the wizard's matching live panel polls
`GET .../matching/activity` every 2 s (`MatchingActivityReader`: `FactoryJob` latest + two `PipelineStep` predicate scans by project/step,
no `detail` read); the jobs banner polls `GET .../jobs` every 3 s while a job is active, 30 s otherwise. All are cheap on a quiet instance;
with every core saturated by the clustering pool they queue behind it like every other request. The CPU starvation, not these reads, is the
likely cause of the 60-120 s: not measurable offline.

## 50. Child keys on the parent — finding parents that share a child record without joining the child table (`CHILD_KEYS`, lot M3, branch `feature/child-keys-derived-attribute`, 2026-10-03)

### 50.1 The measurement that motivates it (project Vol1m, 2026-10-03)

`Personne` 576,692 rows, child `Adresse` 889,165 rows (foreign key `personneRef`). The Personne plan compares four child fields in its decision tree
(`Adresse.street`, `houseNumber`, `postalCode`, `city`).

| Candidate search on the four child fields | Run time (153,937 pivots) | Recall |
|---|---|---|
| weight 1 each (the default) | 78 min 40, 99 % in the EBX kernel's canopy clustering, a Calcite sub-query on the child table per pivot | 91.9 % |
| weight 0 each (§48) | 8 min 54 | 88.9 % (6,009 true pairs lost: no common e-mail/phone, names too far apart, only the shared address brought them together) |
| postal code alone kept in the search | 24 min | no gain |

The cost is the sub-query on the CHILD table, not the child fields as such. A field of the PARENT table in the same search costs nothing. So the fix is a
same-table attribute on the parent that holds, for each child record, one EXACT key built from the child's fields: the search compares parents on it, the
decision tree keeps comparing the real child fields.

### 50.2 The attribute

A `StagingAttribute` of the parent entity with `derivation = CHILD_KEYS`, `derivedFrom` EMPTY (the value comes from the child records, not from another
attribute of the same entity), `dataType = STRING`, `maxLength` = the cap on the value (2000 if left empty) and `derivationArgument` = a JSON object:

```json
{"child":"Adresse","fields":["postalCode","houseNumber","street"]}
```

| Key | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `child` | the child staging entity | mandatory |
| `fields` | the child attributes the key of one child record is built from, in key order | mandatory, non-empty |
| `required` | the subset of `fields` that must be non-empty for a child record to contribute a key | every field |
| `reference` | the child attribute that refers to this entity, when the child has several such attributes | the only one (several and no `reference`: the load fails, naming them) |
| `maxTokens` | a cap on the number of keys kept per parent | none (only `maxLength` caps) |
| `encoding` | `hash` (each key replaced by an opaque token of 13 letters) or `plain` (the readable key); anything else is refused at definition time (lot M7, §50.6) | `hash` |

It is a perfectly ordinary string field for `StagingModel` and `MasterModel` (generated like any other attribute, no foreign key, never mandatory); the
master load copies it like any other field, and it needs no `AttributeMapping` (every "no mapping" gate keys on "derivation is set", which is true here: the
review line, the wizard rule, the Mapping matrix row). The Mapping matrix says "Keys of the Adresse records" and "computed at load ... one key per Adresse
record, built once the Adresse records are loaded" (en/fr).

**The key of one child record** (`quality.ChildKeysDerivation`; with `encoding: plain`, the form below - the default `hash` replaces it by an opaque token, §50.6): each part goes through the house matching fold, `CleaningSteps.foldKey` (trim, collapse spaces,
strip accents, upper case) - no other normalisation - then every whitespace character is removed from inside the part (the value is a list of keys separated by
one space), then every `_` is removed from inside the part (it is the character that joins the parts, so it must not occur in one, or `(12, A_B)` and
`(12_A, B)` would build the same key). The parts are joined by `_`: `75008_12_RUEDELAPAIX`. An empty REQUIRED part gives no key for that child (a key with a hole
is a weak match, not an exact one); an empty optional part leaves an empty segment (`75008__RUEDELAPAIX`).

**The value of one parent**: the DISTINCT keys of its children, sorted (natural `String` order, so the same children always give the same value whatever order
they were read in), one space between them. The cap (`maxLength`, then `maxTokens` when set) keeps a prefix of the sorted list and drops the rest; a key that alone
is longer than `maxLength` is dropped. What the cap dropped is counted (`tokensDropped`, `parentsCapped`) in the `STAGING_LOAD` step detail and message: never silent.

### 50.3 Where and when it is computed

The children are loaded AFTER the parent row, so it is not computed row by row. `ebx.StagingLoader` runs a post-pass (`ebx.ChildKeysPass`, `staging.ChildKeysSweep`) at the
end of the staging load, after every feed and after the deferred references (so every child's parent reference is final). The definitions are read and validated
BEFORE any row is read: a definition that cannot be right (not JSON, unknown child entity, a child attribute the entity does not have, two references and no
`reference`) fails the load at once; one that is right but not yet in the generated model (entity or field not built, attribute not accepted, field not on the
published table) is SKIPPED with the reason in the step detail ("regenerate the staging model").

**When a sweep runs**: scope `all`; or a row was written in the parent entity or in the child entity this run; or the attribute never finished a computation
(`StagingAttribute.derivationLastRunAt` empty: first run after adding it, or a previous run stopped/failed halfway); or its definition (argument, `maxLength`)
changed since the last computation. A run that changed nothing in either entity skips it (`NOT_NEEDED`). The marker is emptied BEFORE the sweep and set after it,
so a failed, stopped or cancelled sweep is retried by the next load whatever that load reads (the rows already staged are not read again in scope `new`).

**Why a full sweep and not "only the children this run touched"**: a parent's value is a function of ALL its remaining children, the child table is indexed on its
primary key only (`<index>` is ignored on 6.3, CLAUDE.md §5), so the children of one parent cannot be fetched without scanning the table. A child added, changed,
moved to another parent or removed therefore means recomputing from every other child of that parent (and of the old one), which needs the scan anyway. So the
decision "is a sweep due" is made per entity pair, and a sweep recomputes every parent: the parents whose value is unchanged are read (in the parent scan) and NOT
written, the parents that no child supports any more (all their children removed, or moved) are cleared (in that same scan, §50.7).

**Cost and bounded memory** (rewritten by lot M10, §50.7; the M3 shape - tokens grouped in a map, `K = ceil(child rows / 400,000)` partitions, one child scan per
partition, one primary-key lookup per parent to read and another to write, `K` predicate scans of the parents to clear - took 728 s on Vol1m): ONE scan of the child
table builds one pair of `long`s per child row (a 64-bit hash of the parent's key, the 61-bit code of the child's key), the pairs are sorted and de-duplicated in place,
then ONE scan of the parent table computes each parent's value, compares it with the stored one it already holds and queues a write only when they differ, through the
record the scan returned. Memory is 16 bytes per child row (14 MB for Vol1m's 889,165 Adresse rows) plus a bit per pair, the fold caches (at most 50,000 distinct raw values per
part) and one write batch; the budget is 8,000,000 child rows (128 MB) with `encoding: hash`, above which the sweep splits the parents into `K = ceil(child rows / 8,000,000)`
hash partitions and repeats the two scans per partition (400,000 rows and the old shape with `encoding: plain`, whose readable keys pin a dictionary entry each). A hash
split is even, not exact, and a single parent holding most of the children cannot be split (it is capped by `maxLength` anyway).
Writes touch ONLY the attribute's own field of the parent row: `_sourceHash`, `_status`, `_loadId` are left as they are, so the landing-to-staging incremental transfer
does not see the parent as changed. A parent row REWRITTEN by its own feed keeps its keys (`NullFillRule` leaves a `CHILD_KEYS` field alone; a feed never covers it).

**Master**: the master load re-reads every staging row (docs/INCREMENTAL-TRANSFER.md §5: staging to master is still a full transfer), so a changed value is copied by
the next master load with no marker of its own - nothing in this lot makes the master transfer incremental. A master load is needed after the first computation
and after any run that updated parents.

**Reported** in the `STAGING_LOAD` step (`detail.childKeys[]`, one entry per attribute, also in the REST answer): `status` (`DONE`, `NOT_NEEDED`, `SKIPPED`, `STOPPED`) and
`reason`, then `childRows`, `childrenRead`, `passes`, `childrenWithoutParent`, `childrenWithoutKey`, `childKeysOfMissingParent`, `parentsWithKeys`, `parentsUpdated`,
`parentsCleared`, `parentsUnchanged`, `tokensDropped`, `parentsCapped`; since lot M10 also `mode`, `scans`, `parentsRead`, `writesSkippedUnchanged`, `writeBatches`,
`writeBatchSize`, `peakPairs`, `partFolds`, `partCacheHits`, `hashRestarts` and the durations `childScanMs`, `sortMs`, `parentPassMs`, `writeMs` (§50.7); and one sentence in the step message. `derivationLastRunMessage` on the attribute row keeps the last
sentence.

### 50.4 Using it in the matching plan

The attribute is an ordinary same-table field for the plan. List it in `requirements.clusteringFields` of the PARENT plan; the translator
(`MatchingPolicyTranslator`) declares every `clusteringFields` entry in `matchingPolicy.fields` with `searchStrategy @default`, a weight of 1 (the weight of the field in
the tree when it is also compared there; a clustering-only field has none), and `DO_NOTHING` null handling, and nothing refuses a field that no tier compares: the
tree is UNCHANGED (it keeps comparing the real `Adresse` fields through the relation fields, §33/§45). Take the four relation fields out of the candidate search with
§48's `relationClusteringWeights` (weight 0), so the only thing that finds parents through their address is this field:

```json
"clusteringFields": ["emailKey", "...", "adresseKeys"],
"relationClusteringWeights": {"Adresse.street": 0, "Adresse.houseNumber": 0, "Adresse.postalCode": 0, "Adresse.city": 0}
```

What the plan proposal passes do with it today: nothing, by decision of this lot (they belong to other work). `MatchPlanLlmPass` refuses a clustering field that "the decision
tree already compares, that field's own derived matching key, or the source of a matching key the tree compares" (§16 rule): a `CHILD_KEYS` attribute is none of the three,
so the LLM route would refuse it in `clusteringFields`, and the rule route never proposes it. For the volume experiment set it on the stored plan by hand (the plan row's
`requirements`), then `matching/configure`. A follow-up lot should teach the pass about `derivation = CHILD_KEYS` (accept it as a clustering field when the tree compares the
named child's fields, and describe it to the model as "a technical key of the children, never an identifier").

### 50.5 The open question, stated plainly (answered by §50.6 for `exactFullText`)

**Not measured when this lot was written; measured 2026-10-04, see §50.6.** The add-on's default search strategy (`@default`, the `@Name`-like template on a text field, §14/§26: an APPROXIMATE candidate search) must treat the value
as a SET of space-separated tokens: two parents with one identical token among several must become candidates, and a token must stay whole (`75008_12_RUEDELAPAIX` must
not be split on `_`; Lucene's standard tokenizer keeps `_` inside a token, which is why `_` was chosen, but the add-on's own analyzer has not been read or measured).
If the default strategy reads the value as one string (a similarity on the whole text), a parent with several addresses would match poorly; the alternatives to measure
then are another `searchStrategy` listed by `matching_config_schema` for the field, or one attribute per rank of address (`address1Key`, `address2Key`) instead of a list.
To measure live on Vol1m: add the attribute (§50.2), load the staging, load the master, add the field to `clusteringFields`, run, and compare the 6,009 lost pairs and the run time against the 8 min 54 /
78 min 40 above.

### 50.6 Opaque tokens and the comparator's formula (lot M7, branch `feature/child-keys-opaque-tokens`, 2026-10-04)

**The measurement** (project Vol1m, 1M rows, 2026-10-04). `adresseKeys` in readable form (`49000_8_RUEGAMBETTA 67000_113_HAUPTSTRASSE`), compared in the decision tree with
`ebx-addon-mame@exactFullText` (and used as a mandatory-field-set filter), gave recall 99.1 % but precision 87 %: 29,757 false pairs, 98.9 % of which share NO whole address key.

**The comparator's formula** (read by `javap` in the add-on, `algorithm/full_text/CompatibleFullTextComparator.compareNormalizedValues`): the value is cut into WORDS by a
Lucene analyzer (the field's search-template analyzer, not controllable from the factory) and the score is `matchedWords / max(wordsA, wordsB)`. A readable key such as
`13001_18_RUESAINTE-CATHERINE` is split into several words (at least on `-`, possibly on `_` and on letter/digit boundaries), so two different people who share only a postal
code or a street name already reach a low threshold. The cause is the key's readable shape, not the data.

**The fix: `"encoding":"hash"`, the default.** Each key is built exactly as in §50.2 (fold, whitespace and `_` removed inside a part, parts joined by `_`), then replaced by an opaque
token (`ChildKeysDerivation.opaque`): the first 8 bytes of SHA-256 of the key's UTF-8 bytes read big-endian, the top 3 bits dropped (61 bits), written in base 26 with `a`-`z` on
exactly 13 letters (26^13 = 2.48e18 > 2^61 = 2.31e18). `49000_8_RUEGAMBETTA` gives `ixmkfnujmvmbg`. No digit, no separator, no accent: no analyzer can cut it, so ONE key is ONE word. De-duplication, the
space separator, the required parts and the caps (`maxLength`, `maxTokens`) are unchanged; the tokens are sorted themselves (the order of the letters, not of the readable keys), still independent of
the reading order. Two different keys collide with a probability of about 2^-61 per pair. `"encoding":"plain"` keeps the readable form for whoever wants to read the values (not
recommended for matching). Any other value is refused when the definition is read (the load fails before any row is read) with a message naming `hash` and `plain`.

With one key = one word, the score of two parents is `sharedAddresses / max(addressesA, addressesB)`: 100 % for one address each in common, 50 % for one shared among two, 33 % among three, and
exactly 0 when no whole address is shared. Sharing a postal code or a street name no longer scores anything.

**Consequence for the plan.** Use `exactFullText` on the attribute with a `minimumScore` of `floor(100 / maxAddressesPerParent)` or lower: 20 accepts one shared address among up to 5 addresses per parent,
50 only among 2. Never tune the threshold on partial word overlap: it is the number of ADDRESSES that is being counted now, so the threshold is a statement about how many addresses a parent may have,
and a value above `floor(100 / maxAddressesPerParent)` silently rejects true pairs of parents with many addresses. `maxTokens` (§50.2) bounds `maxAddressesPerParent` from the data side: a parent
with more keys than the cap loses the rest in sorted order, which also changes what two such parents share, so pick the cap above the real maximum (the `parentsCapped` counter says whether it bites).

**Existing attributes are recomputed once.** The default changed, so values stored in readable form are stale. The marker (`derivationLastRunMessage`, ending `(def <tag>)`) now holds a tag that
starts with `h` (hash) or `p` (plain) and is computed from the argument, the length AND the effective encoding; the tags written before this lot were hexadecimal and can never start with those letters,
so the next staging load always recomputes an attribute last computed by an earlier build (`aMarkerWrittenBeforeTheEncodingExistedIsStale` in `ChildKeysPassTest`). A definition WITHOUT `encoding`
is therefore recomputed in hash form once; an attribute set explicitly to `plain` keeps its readable form (and is recomputed once too, since the tag changed - same values, no harm). The attribute's
master copy and the matching's own data follow the usual order: master load, then re-run the matching (the add-on re-indexes the changed field).

### 50.7 Lot M10 — the sweep in two scans (branch `perf/child-keys-single-pass`, 2026-10-04)

**The measurement** (project Vol1m, EBX 6.3.0-rc2, 2026-10-04): `Personne.adresseKeys` for 576,692 parents from 889,165 `Adresse` rows took 728 s, then 574 s for the
recompute that followed the encoding change (every parent rewritten) - as long as loading the whole staging (540 s for 992,479 source rows). No instance was available to the
lot: what follows is read from the code, with the operations counted, not timed.

**Where the time went (inferred) - the M3 sweep on Vol1m, `K = 3`:**

| Work | Count | Why it cost |
|---|---|---|
| child table scans | 3 x 889,165 = 2,667,495 row reads, 4 field reads each (~10.7 M) | one full scan per partition; each reads every row though a third of them matters |
| keys computed | 2,667,495 keys = 8.0 M part folds + 2.67 M SHA-256 | the key of EVERY row was computed before the row was tested against the partition, so it was computed 3 times; each fold compiled a regex (`replaceAll("\\s+")`), ran a `Normalizer`, built three strings; each hash did a `MessageDigest.getInstance` |
| parent value reads | 576,692 primary-key lookups | one per parent that has children, to read the stored value |
| parent clear scans | 3 x 576,692 = 1.73 M row reads | a predicate scan `osd:is-not-null(./adresseKeys)` per partition (no index on that field: a table scan) to find the parents that hold a value no child supports |
| writes | 576,692 `doModifyContent`, 1,154 transactions of 500, each preceded by ANOTHER primary-key lookup of the parent inside the Procedure | each write updates the Lucene index of the table; a lookup after a modification of the same table in a Procedure can force an index refresh (`installation/performance.html`); 1,154 commits |

Reading the two timings together: the recompute (574 s) rewrote every parent, like the first run (728 s), so the writes (576,692 modifications, 1.15 M lookups, 1,154
commits) are common to both and the largest share; the 154 s of difference is what the first run paid on top (the clear scans returned nothing yet, but ran in full). The
CPU of the keys (8 M folds, ~2.7 M digests) is the smaller part: the same computation on synthetic in-memory data, with the new code, takes about 1 s in total (a harness,
not EBX: the rows are Java arrays), so it is the reads and the writes that cost, and the rewrite had to cut their NUMBER.

**What changed:**

1. **One scan of each table.** Child row -> one pair `(hash64(parent key), code)`, the key computed ONCE, only for the rows of the partition (one partition below the budget).
   `ChildKeysDerivation.KeyEncoder` folds each distinct raw value of a part once (LRU map per part, 50,000 entries, values over 128 characters not cached; on the synthetic
   Vol1m shape 2,667,495 parts were served 2,481,830 times by the cache), keeps one `MessageDigest`, and gives the 61 bits of the opaque token as a `long` - two codes order
   like their tokens, so the value is the same string as before. `ChildKeysDerivation.part` is one character loop (no regex; no `Normalizer` for ASCII) and returns exactly what the old fold did
   (`ChildKeysDerivationTest.partIsTheOldFoldForAnyInput`: 200,000 random strings over 45 character classes: accents, ligatures, `ß`, Greek sigma, surrogate pairs,
   every kind of space and control character).
2. **The pairs are sorted in place** (`ChildKeysSweep.sortPairs`, three-way quicksort on two parallel `long[]`; a parent with 200,000 children costs one pass) and de-duplicated; the
   keys of a parent are a run found by binary search on its hash. No map, no per-parent object.
3. **One scan of the parent table**, in table order, `createRequestResult(null)`: each parent comes with its stored value, so there is no read by key; the new value is compared
   with it and a write is queued ONLY when they differ - including the clearing of a parent no child supports any more (value computed empty, stored value not): the extra
   predicate scan is gone. **A sweep over unchanged data costs the two scans and zero writes** (`aSecondSweepOverUnchangedDataWritesNothing`: `writeBatches = 0`).
4. **Writes by the record in hand**: the Procedure does `getContext` + `doModifyContent` on the `Adaptation` the scan returned - no lookup by key, no read of the table between two
   rows of a batch. They are made while the parent scan is open: an EBX request result is frozen when it is created (`RequestResult` Javadoc, "Query snapshot isolation"), and
   `installation/performance.html` says to "perform a single query and apply the modification when browsing the results". The price is that the superseded index files of the parent table stay
   on disk until the scan closes (the whole parent pass).
5. **Write batches of at least 5,000** (`ChildKeysPass.MIN_WRITE_BATCH`; `Settings.transferBatchSize` wins when larger): 116 transactions instead of 1,154 for Vol1m. Trade-off: a refused
   batch rolls back 5,000 parents instead of 500 and the dataset stays write-locked a little longer per batch; the sweep is idempotent and the marker stays empty, so the next run
   recomputes. Since 6.3.0 a Procedure of many changes runs in bounded memory (`ProcedureContext.setCommitThreshold` Javadoc), so the size is not a memory question.
6. **The parent key is hashed, not stored** (FNV-1a over the characters + the Murmur3 finaliser, seeded). Two parents sharing a 64-bit hash would share their children, so each run of
   pairs may be claimed by ONE parent: a second claim is a collision (~9e-9 for Vol1m), and the sweep starts again with another seed (`hashRestarts`, at most 3, then an error;
   the restart recomputes everything, so it also repairs what the first attempt wrote). Not detectable: a child that refers to a parent that does not exist, whose key hash
   equals a real parent's (a dangling reference AND a 2^-64 chance).

**After, for Vol1m (operations, `K = 1`):** 889,165 child row reads (once), 576,692 parent row reads (once), 889,165 x 3 part reads, ~185,000 folds (the rest from the cache), 889,165
digests with one `MessageDigest`, no primary-key lookup, no predicate scan. Unchanged data: 0 writes. First computation: 576,692 modifications in 116 transactions. Memory: 14 MB of
pairs + 2 MB of marks + at most 3 x 50,000 cached parts (about 25 MB) + 5,000 records = about 45 MB, against the 40-60 MB per partition of M3.

**Behaviour kept from M3/M7:** definitions are validated before any row is read; the stale-marker rule, the `h`/`p` tag, `needed()` are untouched (the values are identical, so no
attribute is recomputed because of this lot); counters, failure (a refused write throws, the marker stays empty), stop (between batches, every 50,000 parents, every 20,000 child
rows), the cap (`maxLength`, `maxTokens`, `tokensDropped`, `parentsCapped`).

**Step detail to read after the next Vol1m load** (`detail.childKeys[]` of `STAGING_LOAD`, one entry per attribute; the same sentence is in `derivationLastRunMessage`): `mode`
(`single-pass`), `passes` (1), `scans` (2), `childrenRead` (889,165), `parentsRead` (576,692), `parentsUpdated` / `parentsCleared` / `writesSkippedUnchanged`, `writeBatches`
(116 on a full write, 0 when unchanged), `writeBatchSize` (5,000), `peakPairs` (<= 889,165), `partFolds` / `partCacheHits`, `hashRestarts` (0), and the durations in ms `childScanMs`
(read + key), `sortMs`, `parentPassMs` (scan + compare, writes excluded), `writeMs`. A second load that changes nothing in either entity is `NOT_NEEDED`; to measure the unchanged cost,
launch it with scope `all`: expect `writeBatches: 0` and `writeMs: 0`.

**What only a live run can confirm:** (1) that a `RequestResult` on the parent table stays valid and complete while Procedures commit under it (documented; on PostgreSQL in mapped mode
the `RequestResult` Javadoc says cursors are invalidated at commit - then `nextAdaptation` fails after the first batch, the sweep fails loudly and the marker stays empty; the fallback
would be to collect the keys of the differing parents first and write them by lookup, as M3 did); (2) that `doModifyContent` on an `Adaptation` taken from the scan (not looked up in the
Procedure) is accepted for every row; (3) the real cost of one modification on `adresseKeys` - if `writeMs` stays large the next levers are the table's history setting and
`ProcedureContext.setTriggerActivation(false)` (not applied: they change what is recorded, a decision to take with the instance's table settings in hand); (4) the time of the two
scans on a 576,692 / 889,165-row staging (`childScanMs`, `parentPassMs`). Nothing in this lot ran on EBX.

### 50.8 Who proposes the attribute (lot M8b, branch `feature/staging-child-keys-proposal`, 2026-10-04)

§50.4 said the plan passes ignore `CHILD_KEYS` and that nothing proposed the attribute itself. The STAGING proposal now does: the language-model pass has a `propose_child_keys` tool
(`staging.StagingLlmPass`, `docs/TARGET-MAPPING.md` sec 19.1) with which the model names, on a parent entity, the child entity and the ordered child attributes that make one key (a postal code, a
house number and a street for the addresses of a person). The row is written as a `PROPOSED` `StagingAttribute` (`derivation = CHILD_KEYS`, `derivationArgument` = `{"child":...,"fields":[...]}`, default encoding
`hash`, `STRING`, `maxLength 2000`, origin `LLM`); a person accepts it like any attribute, then the staging is regenerated and loaded (the post-pass of §50.3 computes it on the first load after it was
accepted), the master regenerated and loaded. Structure only is checked in Java (`staging.ChildKeysProposalRule`: the child exists and refers to the parent through one attribute, every field is an attribute of
the child and not the link nor a technical identity attribute, the definition parses); WHICH attributes identify a child record is the model's call. Still not done, and left to the matching plan's lot: using the
attribute in `clusteringFields` / `relationClusteringWeights` (§50.4), and the comparator threshold of §50.6.


## 51. Lot M8a: plan shape for volume - exact-key paths (branch `feature/match-plan-exact-key-paths`, 2026-10-04)

The matching-plan proposal now produces, checks and explains the plan shape that was MEASURED to work at 1 M rows (project Vol1m, EBX 6.3.0-rc2 + Match and Merge add-on,
`mdm-volume-test/vol1m/FINDINGS.md`). Entity `Personne` (576,692 rows), child `Adresse`.

### 51.1 The measurement

| Variant | What the candidate search is | Run (153,937 pivots) | Precision | Recall (reachable pairs) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Reference | one weighted score over 8 fields, four of them fields of the child table | 78 min 40 | 99.2 % | 91.9 % |
| A | the same, the four child fields at weight 0 (still compared in the tree) | 8 min 54 | 99.85 % | 88.9 % |
| E | three exact-key filters (e-mail, phone, address keys), names corrupted in ECOM staging | 5 min 43 | 99.74 % | 90.8 % |
| E2 | E on correct names, readable address keys | 8 min 43 | 87.0 % | 99.1 % |
| **E3** | E2 with opaque address-key tokens (§50.6), `adresseKeys` threshold 20 | **8 min 21** | **99.84 %** | **99.15 %** |
| E3, full table | 576,692 pivots (`scope=all`) | 27 min 22 (job 32 min 39) | 99.79 % | 99.21 % of 349,141 true pairs |

E3 against the reference: 9.4 times faster, +7.2 points of recall, 323 false pairs instead of 1,524. Variants C and D showed what does NOT work: with the JVM option on but a tree in which
one path has no eligible key (names compared by an AVERAGE, addresses by child-table fields) the add-on set no filter and the run was identical to A (recall 88.9 %).

### 51.2 The rule (what the add-on does, reproduced by `matching.CandidateFilterCheck`)

With the JVM running `-Debx.addon.mame.matching.mandatoryFieldSets.enabled=true`, the add-on's `MandatoryFieldSetFinder` (read by `javap`) derives from the decision tree **one field set per path to
`MATCHED`/`SUSPECTED`**. A path's set is made of the fields of the `All fields match` (`ALL_FIELDS`) nodes the path PASSES (its `onTrue` edge - variant D showed the filters `{phoneE164}` OR `{emailKey}`,
not `{emailKey, phoneE164}`, so a node left through `onFalse` adds nothing to that path) that satisfy all of:

- the field is a field of the table itself (no `via`, not a field of a child table);
- `bothNull` and `oneNull` are both `NOT_MATCH` (absent = `NOT_MATCH`, what the translator writes for an absent one);
- `minimumScore` above 0 (absent = 100, the add-on's own default);
- algorithm `ebx-addon-mame@exact` or `ebx-addon-mame@exactFullText`.

The candidate search then keeps a pair only when it satisfies one of the sets (OR between paths, AND inside a set). **If ONE path has an empty set, the add-on sets no filter at all** and the candidate
search is one weighted score over all fields (in practice dominated by one key). The option is read at the add-on's start: it is passed to the JVM (`EBX_JAVA_OPTS` for `ebx.sh`), is NOT persistent in
EBX, and a restart is needed to change it.

The exact tree of the measurement (Factory JSON, `MatchPlan.requirements.decisionTree`; the fixture `CandidateFilterCheckTest.e3Requirements`): P1 `ALL_FIELDS [emailKey exact 100]` -> SUSPECTED, else P2
`ALL_FIELDS [phoneE164 exact 100]` -> P2B `AVERAGE >= 82 [lastName jarowinkler w5, firstName jarowinkler w4]` -> P3 `AVERAGE >= 76` on the four `Adresse` relation fields -> SUSPECTED (else NOT_MATCHED);
P2 false -> P5 `ALL_FIELDS [adresseKeys exactFullText minimumScore 20]` -> P5B `AVERAGE >= 82 [lastName, firstName]` -> SUSPECTED, else NOT_MATCHED. `clusteringFields`: emailKey, phoneE164, adresseKeys,
