lastNameKey; every null handling of a key node `NOT_MATCH` on both sides; relation fields at pre-clustering weight 0 (§48.1, the default). `adresseKeys` is the `CHILD_KEYS` attribute of §50 (opaque
tokens, §50.6); `exactFullText` scores `matched words / max(words A, words B)`, so its `minimumScore` must be at most `100 / (largest number of child records one parent has)` - 20 accepts a shared child
among up to 5.

### 51.3 `matching.CandidateFilterCheck`

Pure (Jackson only), over the stored requirements - the flat `decisionTree` or the legacy `tiers` cascade. `check(requirements)` returns a `Result`:

- `verdict`: `FILTERED` (every path to `MATCH`/`SUSPECTED` has a non-empty set), `NOT_FILTERED`, or `NOT_APPLICABLE` (no tree, or no path reaches a match - nothing to say);
- `paths`: one `PathResult` per path (`label()` = the ids of the nodes crossed, `N2 > N2B > N3`; `outcome`; `keyFields`; `rejections`). A rejection says WHY a node or field of a path gave no key:
  `NOT_ALL_FIELDS` (the node is an AVERAGE / AT_LEAST_N node), `RELATION_FIELD`, `NULL_HANDLING` (names `bothNull`/`oneNull` values), `ALGORITHM`, `MINIMUM_SCORE`, `NO_PASSED_NODE`;
- `keySets()` / `filtersPhrase()` (`emailKey OR phoneE164 OR adresseKeys`), `pathsWithoutKey()`, `explain()` (one English paragraph naming every path without a key and why), and `warning(result, jvmOption)`.

It also reads `requirements.unfilteredCandidateSearchReason` (51.4) and the JVM option (`jvmOptionEnabled()`). No guess about business meaning: it checks STRUCTURE and reports facts.

### 51.4 What the language-model pass is told and does (`master.MatchPlanLlmPass`)

The system prompt gained one paragraph, CANDIDATE FILTERS, worded as follows (a test pins its key sentences):

> CANDIDATE FILTERS (volume rule, lot M8a - measured on a 1-million-row test): on a large table the add-on finds the pairs to compare through a candidate search, and it can restrict that search to
> records that share an exact key - but only when EVERY path of your tree that ends in SUSPECTED or MATCH starts with an 'all identical' node (ALL_FIELDS) on an exact key of the record itself, with
> empty values never matching (bothNullValueHandling and oneNullValueHandling both NOT_MATCH), the exact or exactFullText algorithm, and a minimumScore above 0. Put similarity comparisons (AVERAGE
> nodes on names or descriptions) and comparisons of related records AFTER such a node, never instead of it. The keys of related records (an address, a contact) are offered as a derived child-keys
> attribute of the record itself (marked 'derived child keys' below): compare it with the exactFullText algorithm in its own ALL_FIELDS node, with NOT_MATCH on both null handlings and a minimumScore
> of at most 100 divided by the largest number of child records one record has (20 accepts a shared child among up to 5). If ONE path has no such key, the add-on sets no filter at all and the whole
> run falls back to one weighted search over every field: measured 9 times slower and 10 points of recall lower at 1 million rows (78 min 40 and 91.9 % recall, against 8 min 21 and 99.15 % recall for
> a tree whose three paths each start with an exact key). A proposal whose paths do not all start with such a key is refused, naming the path that lacks one; an entity that truly has no exact key at all
> (a child entity whose only exact field is its parent reference, say - that field keeps DO_NOTHING null handling and is never a key) may set acceptUnfilteredCandidateSearch to true together
> with a one-sentence unfilteredCandidateSearchReason.

- **Refusal.** In a session that asked for the rule (`Session.requireFilteredCandidateSearch()`, which `ebx.MatchPlanLlmSuggester` turns on for every real run; the default is off so existing callers and
  fixtures are unchanged), a proposal whose `CandidateFilterCheck` verdict is `NOT_FILTERED` is refused with the per-path explanation (`explain()`), what it costs, how to fix it and the way out. It is a
  hard refusal (not one-shot): the corrected call has a different key for the circuit breaker, a repeated identical one still ends that entity after three.
- **The way out.** Two optional members of `propose_match_plan`: `acceptUnfilteredCandidateSearch` (boolean) and `unfilteredCandidateSearchReason` (string, required with the first; a blank one is refused).
  The plan is then stored with `requirements.unfilteredCandidateSearchReason` and a warning sentence at the end of its rationale ("Candidate search NOT filtered (accepted by the model: ...)" + the
  explanation). Ignored, and nothing stored, when the plan IS filtered.
- **A `CHILD_KEYS` attribute** (`AttributeInfo.derivation`, `childKeysChild`, read by `ebx.MatchPlanLlmSuggester` from `StagingAttribute.derivation`/`derivationArgument`; the literal is pinned to
  `quality.ChildKeysDerivation.DERIVATION_CHILD_KEYS` by a test) is accepted as a tree field with `ebx-addon-mame@exactFullText` ONLY; an EXPLICIT null handling other than `NOT_MATCH` is refused, an omitted
  one is written as `NOT_MATCH` (whatever the vocabulary's first value is); in a node with a per-field `minimumScore` the value (default 100) must be at most 50, the refusal giving the formula and, when the
  relation evidence measured the largest number of child records per record, the exact ceiling (`floor(100 / max)`). A threshold between that ceiling and 50 is accepted and noted in the rationale
  ("Child keys: ... two records that share a child are found only when neither has more than N child record(s)"). As a clustering field it is accepted when a node compares it, WITHOUT the fill-rate /
  distinctness / cross-system guards (one opaque key per child record is near-unique by construction; those guards ask for the opposite); a child-keys clustering field that no node compares is refused.
  The prompt marks the attribute ("derived child keys of Adresse (at most 5 per record: minimumScore up to 20)").

### 51.5 Where the verdict is stored and shown

It is a pure function of the stored tree, so it is computed when read, never stored as a second copy that could drift: **an existing APPLIED (or any) plan gets its verdict at once, on the next screen render
and at the next `configure`/`run`, with nothing to migrate.** Only the model's explicit choice is stored (`requirements.unfilteredCandidateSearchReason`, plus the rationale sentence).

- **Plan card** (`review.MatchPlanTreeDiagram`, band "How candidates are found", both bundles `Messages_en/fr.properties`): `Candidates are filtered on: Email key OR Phone E164 OR Address keys.` or
  `Candidate search is NOT filtered: path «N2 > N2B > N3» has no exact key.` followed by `On a large table the run then compares by weighted search: measured 9 times slower and 10 points of recall lower
  at 1 million rows.` (and `Kept on purpose: <reason>` when the model gave one; at most three paths named, then `(+N)`). The M2 sentence about relation fields is unchanged.
- **Wizard step 6** (`review.MatchPlanView.renderCandidateSearchNotice`, called from `WizardPage.renderMatchPlan`): a warning paragraph when the plan is FILTERED but the JVM option is off in THIS JVM (the
  wizard runs in the EBX JVM, so `System.getProperty` is exact), and - for an ACCEPTED/APPLIED plan whose tree is folded away - the NOT FILTERED sentence.
- **`matching/configure` and `matching/run`** (`ebx.MatchingConfigurator.recordCandidateSearch`, read-only): `detail.candidateSearch` = `{verdict, jvmOption: ON|OFF, filters, pathsWithoutKey[], acceptedReason?, warning?}`
  in the step detail, and `WARNING: ...` appended to the step message when the plan is FILTERED with the option off ("the add-on's candidate filters are OFF on this server: start the JVM with
  -Debx.addon.mame.matching.mandatoryFieldSets.enabled=true") or NOT FILTERED (said instead, whatever the option). Nothing is refused, nothing is written to the add-on.
- **The rule-based `matching/suggest`** (`ebx.MatchPlanSuggester`) runs the same check on each proposal: the response carries `candidateSearch[]` (one line per entity), a plan that is NOT filtered has the
  warning at the end of its rationale. It never invents a key and never refuses its own proposal (what it produces - one exact node per validated identifier - is FILTERED).

### 51.6 Tests and what is not verified

`CandidateFilterCheckTest` (the E3 tree: FILTERED, three sets; the original tree: NOT_FILTERED with per-node reasons; null handling, algorithm, minimum score, relation, `onFalse` edge, sets of several
keys, legacy tiers, cycles, warnings), `MatchPlanLlmPassCandidateFilterTest` (contract wording, schema, E3 accepted, refusals, way out, child keys), `MatchingPolicyTranslatorCandidateFilterTest` (E3
translates; `exactFullText` + 20 + `NOT_MATCH` reach the add-on tree; relation fields at weight 0; dominance of the e-mail key), `MatchPlanCandidateSearchTest` (band, notice, French),
`MatchingCandidateSearchRecordTest` (step detail/warning, rule-based pass). Observed while writing the translator test: a relation field borrows a parent field as the placeholder `mcpgap.RelationFieldRelinker`
repoints afterwards, and the policy-field entry of a field mirrors its FIRST tree appearance - so `adresseKeys` (borrowed by node P3 before its own node P5) is declared `DO_NOTHING` in `matchingPolicy.fields`
while its P5 tree field is `NOT_MATCH`; the measured E3 run was configured this way and derived the three filters, so the add-on reads the tree node field, but this reading of the finder is the one
unverified step. Not run live: nothing here touched a server; the "a node left through onFalse adds nothing" reading is the one the measurements fit (variant D), not a documented rule.

## 52. Trigger mode, related tables, failed runs (lot MT, branch `feature/matching-trigger-mode`, 2026-10-04)

Four fixes from the 1 M-row chain on project `Vol1mF` (576,692 persons, 889,165 addresses, 6.3.0-rc2, `PLAN.md` entry "Chaîne complète à 1 M depuis zéro"). Nothing here was run against an instance:
the facts below are the ones measured that day, the code is proved by unit tests only.

### 52.1 Matching trigger mode per project (`Project.matchingTrigger`)

**Measured.** `generate_matching_policy` leaves the add-on's default execution modes on the policy: `get_matching_config` reads `matchingOnCreation: 1, matchingOnUpdate: 1`
(`MatchingPolicy$ExecutionMode`: 0 = MANUAL, 1 = AFTER_SUBMISSION, 2 = BEFORE_CREATION, 3 = INLINE_MATCHING). So every project ran an inline matching at each batch commit of a master load, although the
Factory's intended default is "matching on demand" - and, on the 1 M-row project, that inline matching left the table index behind during the mass load (the other lot of the day, `docs/MASTER-ZONE.md`).

**What is built.**
- Field `Project.matchingTrigger` (`tools/build_xsd.py`, `core/FactoryPaths.Project.MATCHING_TRIGGER`): `MANUAL` (default, also when empty) or `REALTIME`. No third mode; the add-on's 2 and 3 are never written.
- Meaning (`master/MatchingTriggerMode`, pure, `MatchingTriggerModeTest`): `MANUAL` = `matchingOnCreation` and `matchingOnUpdate` both 0 - a master load never triggers a record-by-record matching, matching
  runs when it is launched (after a load, or by hand); `REALTIME` = both 1 - each record created or changed in the master is matched at once (it slows a mass load).
- Written on the REAL policy (`processCode` = the entity name, never `<Entity>__preview`, which stays 0/0 - `MatchingPreviewPolicy`) at every configure, whichever branch ran (fresh generation, rewrite, resume):
  `MatchingConfigurator.ensureExecutionMode`, called right before `validate_matching_config`. It reads `get_matching_config`, asks `MatchingTriggerMode.patchOps` for the operations still needed, sends them in one
  `patch_matching_config`, then re-reads to prove the write stuck (it fails the configure otherwise). Idempotent: a second configure on a policy already at the wanted values sends nothing.
  The operation is the add-on's `set_execution_mode`, read by `javap` in `MamePatchApplier.resolveSetExecutionMode` (6.3.0-rc2): `{"op":"set_execution_mode","target":{"policyCode":"<entity>","paramName":"matchingOnCreation"|"matchingOnUpdate"},"value":"0"|"1"}`
  - one op per parameter, `value` a JSON STRING (it refuses a missing `policyCode`, another `paramName`, and a value other than 0..3). Recorded in the step detail as `executionMode`
  (`mode`, `wantedValue`, `foundOnCreation`/`foundOnUpdate`, `patched`, `patch`, `afterOnCreation`/`afterOnUpdate`) and in the step message ("trigger mode MANUAL: execution mode 0").
- Wizard, step 6 ("When is matching done?"): two cards, one sentence each, saved by `MATCHING_SET_TRIGGER` (`ProjectWizardUserService.setMatchingTrigger`, `WizardData.saveMatchingTrigger`, administrators only,
  a value that is neither empty nor one of the two is refused). Saving does not touch the add-on: the notice and a hint say "configure matching again to apply it" (the Factory has no drift signal for a
  project field, so it says it in words, as the brief allowed).
- Known wrinkle, deliberately not special-cased: `MatchingPolicyTranslator` writes 0/0 for a plan whose tree compares relation (child) fields (a parent is matched before its children exist). With
  `REALTIME` chosen for such a project, configure writes 1/1 anyway - the project's choice wins; the child fields are then not complete at the time of an inline match.

### 52.2 Related tables: `alignForeignKeys = NONE` (`RelatedTableAlignment.WANTED`)

**Measured.** With a related table in `alignForeignKeys = AUTOMATIC` (what the configurator set for every promoted child entity since 2026-09-23, §12.4/§22), an automatic merge at volume fails inside the add-on
with `LxiDuplicateKeyException: Duplicate key ... /root/CascadingRecords` and the whole run is rolled back (product defect, reported). With `NONE` (written by `apply_matching_config` with the re-read
`matchingPolicies` + `mergePolicies`, exactly the call the configurator already made to align) the same run completes: 180,746 groups merged, 0 false merge. The Factory re-points the child rows to the golden
itself at the next master load (`MasterLoader`, counter `referencesToGolden`: 637,795 addresses re-pointed).

**What changed.** One constant, `RelatedTableAlignment.WANTED = "NONE"`, read by `align`, `alignedPaths`, `changesAnything`, the comparator (`MatchingPolicyComparator`), the rewrite builder
(`MatchingConfigRewriteBuilder`) and the post-generation align call in `MatchingConfigurator.configureOne`. Nothing else was touched: only an entry whose `path` is a promoted child of THIS entity is rewritten, every
other entry stays exactly as stored, nothing is added or removed. A re-configure of an existing configuration whose child entry says `AUTOMATIC` or `MANUAL` now sees a difference (`related tables`) and rewrites it
to `NONE` (the REWRITE branch). The configure message reads "Related table(s) set to alignForeignKeys=NONE (the Factory re-points the children to the golden at the master load): /root/Contact." - it used to say
"aligned to AUTOMATIC". `RelatedTableAlignmentTest`, `MatchingPolicyComparatorTest`, `MatchingConfigRewriteBuilderTest` were updated (they pinned AUTOMATIC; they now also pin AUTOMATIC -> NONE).

**Going back to the add-on's cascade once the defect is fixed:** set `RelatedTableAlignment.WANTED` to `RelatedTableAlignment.AUTOMATIC` (the constant is kept for this) and re-run "Configure matching": every stored
child entry is rewritten to AUTOMATIC by the same machinery. Nothing else reads the value.

**Consequence to know.** §26/the parent-first order relied on the add-on's automatic re-pointing so that a CHILD's parent-confirmation node, run after its parent in the same call, saw the children already pointing
at the merged parent's golden. With `NONE` that re-pointing happens at the next master load instead; during a run, children of parents merged in the same run still point at their old parent. The 1 M run measured
99.71 % recall with `NONE` (with suspects), so the effect on recall is small on that data; it is not measured on a project whose child tree depends on merged parents.

**One configure is enough (fix of 2026-10-04, measured live on Vol100k, 18:40).** On `/root/Personne` (child `/root/Adresse`) the first configure after lot MT took the REWRITE branch (`differs: decisionTree, fields (candidate
gate)`) and sent the merge policy with `relatedTables: []` - the stored policy had no entry at that moment. The add-on re-adds every inverse-foreign-key table as `MANUAL` whenever a merge policy is written without it:
the read-back right after showed `[{"alignForeignKeys":"MANUAL","name":"Address","path":"/root/Adresse"}]` and the step ended DONE without `relatedTablesAligned`; only the second configure aligned it to `NONE`. The list
that was sent says nothing about the list that stands, so `MatchingConfigurator.configureOne` now converges whatever the branch (fresh, rewrite, resume, unchanged): it reads `get_matching_config` back after the branch's
writes, lists the promoted children's entries that are not `NONE` (`RelatedTableAlignment.mismatches`, which keeps the value found: step detail `relatedTablesFoundBeforeAlignment`), sends ONE `apply_matching_config` built by
the same helper the fresh branch already used (`alignRelatedTables`, `MatchingConfigRewriteBuilder.build` over the just-read policies), and, after the execution mode, validate, activate, the relation-field relink and the
preview cleanup, reads once more and FAILS the entity's configure naming the table, the value found and `NONE` if one is still different (`relatedTablesStillWrong`; `relatedTablesAlignmentVerified: true` otherwise).
Chosen over "make the builder ADD the missing entries": an entry the Factory invents carries a name the add-on did not give (and the add-on may then hold both), whereas the entry read back is the add-on's own, matched by
`path`. The write happens before the single `relinkRelationFields` call at the end, so the relation fields still end relinked (same ordering as the fresh branch's follow-up). Cost: two extra `get_matching_config` reads and,
only when something differs, one extra `apply_matching_config`. Not verified live: that the add-on keeps `NONE` after the extra write on Vol100k (the case that failed), and the cost of that second apply on a policy with 7 relation fields.

### 52.3 A failed process fails the step and the job, with the reason

**Measured.** When the add-on's process ended `FAILED` (here at `completionRate` 50.0), the per-entity step said "Matching run on Personne still FAILED after 315360000000ms - Xref.goldenKey NOT refreshed" (a job's
wait is unbounded: the number is nonsense - a terminal status is not a timeout) and the JOB ended `DONE` with "2 entities run, 0 not applied, 0 refused". The add-on gives no reason through its API
(`MatchingOperationProcess.getDetail()` throws a `NullPointerException` once finished); the reason is only an `ERROR` line of `ebx-addon-mame.log`, e.g.
`2026-10-04 15:59:48,218 CEST ERROR  log.wbp.ebx-addon-mame.com.orchestranetworks.addon.mame.auto_merge 6.3.0-rc2 [MatchingManager] The automatic merge process failed for the Marco-Luc group: Duplicate key: 418781. Index: ...,/root/CascadingRecords ...`.

**What changed** (`MatchingConfigurator.runInternal`, `matching.MatchingRunFailure`, `matching.AddonLogWindow`, `ebx.AddonLog`, `ebx.MatchingRunRun`):
- A terminal `FAILED`, or a `CANCELLED` the Factory did not ask for, is a failure (`MatchingRunFailure.isFailure`); `DONE` is not, a non-terminal status after a bounded wait (synchronous callers) is still the old "still RUNNING after Nms",
  and a `CANCELLED` caused by the person's stop is still "stopped (reason)".
- The entity's step ends `FAILED` with: "Matching run on Personne FAILED: the add-on's process failed at 50.0 % - reason from ebx-addon-mame.log: [MatchingManager] The automatic merge process failed for the Marco-Luc group: Duplicate key: 418781. Index: ...
  Xref.goldenKey NOT refreshed. <scope sentence>". When the log cannot be read or has no ERROR for the run, it says "- see <path of ebx-addon-mame.log> for the reason." instead. A completion rate the add-on does not give reads "(completion rate unknown)".
- The reason: the `ERROR`/`FATAL` lines of the log written since the instant this entity's process was launched (2 s of slack for clock rounding), message only (the date, zone, level, category and version columns are dropped;
  stack-trace lines carry no timestamp and are never taken), identical messages once, the first `ERROR` first, joined by " | ", cut at about 600 characters with "(+N more ERROR lines)" when some do not fit.
- The log directory is resolved the way EBX does it, since no API gives it (`javap` on `ebx-lib.jar`, nothing on `Repository`; nothing in this code base read it before): the JVM option `ebx.logs.directory` if set, else the
  same property read from the file named by `-Debx.properties`, with `${ebx.home}` replaced by `-Debx.home` (both set by `ebx.sh`), else `<ebx.home>/ebxLog`. Only the last 4 MB of the file are read; any failure reading it
  gives "see ebx-addon-mame.log" and never fails the run. The line selection, the cap and the directory rule are pure (`AddonLogWindowTest`, with the sample line above).
- The run returns a `failed` array (`"Personne - <reason>"`, entities whose process failed; they are NOT in `ran`), next to `ran`/`notApplied`/`refused`. The job (`MatchingRunRun`) then ends `FAILED` through
  `FactoryJobQueue.ExpectedFailure` (a routine outcome, no stack trace) with "1 of 2 entities failed: Personne - <reason>. 1 entity run, 0 not applied, 0 refused." The entities that completed keep their own results
  (golden keys refreshed, results snapshot) - the loop carries on with the next entity. A run the person stopped stays a stopped job (its sentence names the failures after it). The REST route and the workflow bean
  call the same `run` and now also receive `failed`; they were not changed otherwise.

### 52.4 Pre-clustering dominance when the root exact key leads to another node

`DecisionTreePlan.standaloneIdentifierFieldNames` (§46) used to accept a node only when its `onTrue` was directly MATCHED or SUSPECTED. On `Vol1mF` the root was `ALL_FIELDS [emailKey exact]` with `onTrue` = a confirmation
node, so `emailKey` kept weight 1 (13 when the root led directly to SUSPECTED). **Now the ROOT also counts when its `onTrue` is another node from which at least one path (either branch, any depth) reaches MATCHED or
SUSPECTED** (`leadsToPositiveOutcome`). Unchanged: a non-exact root; a root whose true side is NOT_MATCHED (a valid tree cannot have a true side with only NOT_MATCHED leaves, so that is the leaf itself); a LATER node
of the leading chain whose `onTrue` continues to another node (the measured E3 tree, `phoneE164` then a names confirmation, keeps its weight - the existing `MatchingPolicyTranslatorCandidateFilterTest` pins it).
Tests: `DecisionTreePlanTest` (root -> node -> SUSPECTED / deeper MATCHED / only NOT_MATCHED / fuzzy root / later chain node), `MatchingPolicyTranslatorDominanceTest` (the Vol1mF shape: 6 + 8 + 1 -> 16; MATCHED true side;
NOT_MATCHED true side and non-exact root: untouched, no note). A re-configure of an existing configuration rewrites the raised weight (the comparator re-derives the desired policy through the same method).

### 52.5 Not verified (needs a live instance)

`set_execution_mode` accepted by the live add-on with that exact payload, and the read-back of `matchingOnCreation`/`matchingOnUpdate` as numbers (the code also accepts them as text); a configure on a project whose
policy says 1/1 ending at 0/0 (and a second one patching nothing); a re-configure turning `AUTOMATIC`/`MANUAL` child entries into `NONE`; the log directory resolution on the real JVM options and the quoted text of a
real failure (a forced FAILED process); the wizard cards and the save action rendered by a browser; the effect of `NONE` on recall for a project whose child tree relies on merged parents.

## 53. `Xref.goldenKey` refreshed by two scans (lot V3-M3, branch `perf/golden-resolution-scans`, 2026-10-04)

§4.4 / §20 describe the refresh of `Xref.goldenKey` after a matching run, a catch-up (lot MP) and the `refresh-golden-keys` route. `GoldenKeyRefresher.refresh` (whole entity) used to read, per `Xref` row, the row, the master
record and the add-on's state: about 50 s on 576,692 rows with nothing to change (Vol1mF), and the first refresh after the merges was part of the 18 min 49 of the person run. It now reads the add-on's `RecordMetadata` once
(state and golden of every record, in memory) and the entity's `Xref` rows once, decides each row with the unchanged `GoldenKeyRefreshDecision` (`master.GoldenKeyScanPlan`; a merged record's golden is followed to the survivor through
the index, cycle-guarded) and writes only the rows whose `goldenKey` differs, in batches of 1,000. The per-record path remains for `mdm.factory.goldenRefresh.maxIndexedRows` of 0 or below the metadata row count (default
15,000,000 since lot IDX, was 5,000,000), an unreadable metadataset or add-on API, and any failed read. The refresh's JSON (`goldenKeyRefresh` of the matching run and of the catch-up, the route's per-entity node) gains `scanMs`, `readMode` (`SCAN` /
`PER_RECORD`) and `readReason`; `set` / `cleared` / `unchanged` keep their meaning. `refreshScoped` (a handful of keys, derived `Xref` lookups) is unchanged. Details, memory, the two edges where the scan could differ from the
per-record path, and what to measure live: `docs/VOLUME.md`, section "Lot V3-M3". Nothing run live.

## 54. The `scope` word is checked, not guessed (branch `fix/scope-value-and-landing-selected`, 2026-10-12)

Measured live on 2026-10-12: `POST /projects/{code}/matching/run?scope=full` (the value the end-to-end scenario `tools/itest/scenarios.py` sent) ran an INCREMENTAL run - the pivots were the last loaded batch - because `FactoryResource.runMatching` only tested `"all".equalsIgnoreCase(scope)` and read every other word as the default. A typo silently chose the lighter read.

Every route and pipeline step that takes a `scope` now accepts the words it documents (case-insensitive, surrounding blanks ignored) and refuses anything else with HTTP `400` and the usual problem JSON, `{"error": "Unknown scope 'full': accepted values are 'incremental' and 'all'."}` (a pipeline step stops with the coded refusal `engine.invalid.scope` carrying the same sentence). A missing or blank `scope` keeps its default.

| Route / step | Accepted `scope` | Blank means |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /projects/{code}/matching/run`, `MatchingRunTaskBean` | `incremental`, `all` | `incremental` |
| `POST /projects/{code}/staging/load`, `StagingLoadTaskBean` | `new`, `all` | `new` |
| `POST /projects/{code}/master/load`, `MasterLoadTaskBean` | `full`, `changed` | `-Dmdm.factory.masterLoad.defaultScope` (default `full`) |
| `POST /projects/{code}/distribution/targets/{targetId}/send`, `DistributionTaskBean` | `changed`, `all` | the target's own `scope` field |

Pure rule: `core.ScopeParam` (`ScopeParamTest`); the steps go through `workflow.BeanScope`. A workflow model that wired a free word into `scope` (for instance `full` into the matching step) now fails at that step instead of running the default: check `tools/workflow/MdmFactoryPipeline.json` variables before the next publication. Not run live.

## 55. A decision-tree field no longer accepts `DO_NOTHING` (add-on build 6.3.0.5-RC3) (branch `fix/tree-null-handling-vocabulary`, 2026-10-12)

**Measured live on 2026-10-12 20:24, project Vol100kM**, right after the Match and Merge add-on build 6.3.0.5-RC3 (of 2026-10-10) was installed:
`matching/configure` answered "1 entity configured, 1 refused" and the refusal of `Address` was

```
generate_matching_policy answered a soft miss: {"code":"INVALID_PARAMS","message":"Invalid null-value handling on a decision-tree field: DO_NOTHING","nextStep":"Use one of: MATCH, NOT_MATCH."}
```

The plan (written by the language-model pass) carried `bothNull: DO_NOTHING, oneNull: DO_NOTHING` on the parent-confirmation field `personRef` of an
ALL_FIELDS node, the parent-confirmation contract ("a missing parent only withholds"). The previous add-on build (2026-09-27) had accepted the same payload that
morning. The RC3 `matching_config_schema` now distinguishes two enums, and its description of the tree one says "DO_NOTHING is reserved for matching-policy fields":

| Where | Schema path (under `properties.matchingPolicies.items.properties`) | RC3 values |
|---|---|---|
| matching-policy field (pre-processing / candidate) | `fields.items.properties.{both,one}NullValueHandling.enum` | `DO_NOTHING, NOT_MATCH, MATCH` |
| decision-tree field | `decisionTree.properties.fields.items.properties.{both,one}NullValueHandling.enum` | `MATCH, NOT_MATCH` |

The patch op `set_field_param` says the same for the tree ("MATCH | NOT_MATCH"); `set_field_null_handling` (policy fields) still takes `DO_NOTHING`.

### 55.1 Vocabulary (`MatchPlanProfileReader`, `MatchPlanLlmPass.AllowedVocabulary`)

`readVocabulary` reads the two enums separately. `AllowedVocabulary.nullHandlings` is the policy-field list, `treeNullHandlings` the tree list; when the schema
has only one of them (builds up to 2026-09-27: only the tree path, one shared definition) it serves for both, so an older build behaves exactly as before.

The language-model pass:

- **tool schema**: the tree fields' `bothNullValueHandling` / `oneNullValueHandling` enum is the TREE list; with RC3 the property description says DO_NOTHING is reserved for matching-policy fields;
- **user prompt**: `ProjectInfo.vocabularyNote` (`AllowedVocabulary.promptNote()`, set by `MatchPlanLlmSuggester`) adds an "Add-on vocabulary note" listing the tree values and saying not to write DO_NOTHING on an ordinary tree field; nothing is added when the schema still has DO_NOTHING in the tree list;
- **validation**: an explicit value outside the tree list on a tree field is refused with the schema's own words: "`'email'` oneNullValueHandling 'DO_NOTHING' is not a null-value handling of a decision-tree field (matching_config_schema allows: MATCH, NOT_MATCH; DO_NOTHING is reserved for matching-policy fields). Use one of: MATCH, NOT_MATCH.";
- **two exemptions** keep the plan-level DO_NOTHING because the plan's own contracts need it (`DecisionTreePlan.validate`): the parent-confirmation (REFERENCE) field, whose value the pass forces itself (it must not refuse its own value), and the fields of a node marked `contradiction: true`. Both are translated when the policy is written (below);
- **default**: a tree field with no null handling gets `NOT_MATCH` when the tree list is the narrower RC3 one (the first value of that list would be `MATCH`); on an older build the default is unchanged (the first value of the single list).

### 55.2 Translation at payload time (`MatchingPolicyTranslator.translateTreeNullHandling`)

Called by `MatchingConfigurator.configureOne` right after the policy is built (before the capability check, the comparison with the stored policy and every write, so generate, resume and rewrite all work on the SAME translated policy) and by the Simulate preview policy (`MatchingPreviewPolicy`, same refusal otherwise). The live tree enum is read with one `matching_config_schema` call without a table argument.

| Plan value on a TREE field | Sent when the live tree enum has no DO_NOTHING | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `oneNull: DO_NOTHING` (ALL_FIELDS, AT_LEAST_N node) | `NOT_MATCH` | a missing value must not confirm |
| `bothNull: DO_NOTHING` | `NOT_MATCH` | two missing values no longer abstain |
| `oneNull` / `bothNull: DO_NOTHING` in an AVERAGE node ("not required": weight ignored when null) | `NOT_MATCH` | closest value of the tree enum; **the average then counts the field as 0 instead of leaving it out**, so the node's `minimumScore` may deserve lowering |

Not touched: `MATCH` and `NOT_MATCH`; every `matchingPolicy.fields[]` entry (the policy-field enum has DO_NOTHING; the pre-clustering declaration keeps mirroring the first appearance of the field in the tree); the stored plan (`MatchPlan.requirements` is not rewritten: `DecisionTreePlan`, `CrossSystemPathRule`, `CandidateFilterCheck` and the dominance rule keep reading DO_NOTHING as "not required"). Nothing is translated when the enum is not read (`treeNullHandling: not verified (...)` in the detail, payload sent as stored), when it still contains DO_NOTHING (build of 2026-09-27), or when it has no NOT_MATCH.

**What a reviewer must know about the semantics.** On RC3 the decision tree has no abstention. A parent-confirmation node (`personRef` ALL_FIELDS, onTrue MATCH, onFalse NOT_MATCHED) therefore sends a pair whose parent is MISSING on either side to NOT_MATCHED instead of withholding the confirmation; a `contradiction: true` node rejects a pair when the contradicting value is missing instead of letting it through. The translation is the closest value the add-on accepts, not an equivalent.

### 55.3 What is recorded

- step detail of `MATCHING_CONFIG` (and of the preview step): `treeNullHandlingAllowed: ["MATCH","NOT_MATCH"]` and `nullHandlingTranslated: [...]`, one line per value, e.g.
  `Address / node 'personRef' (All fields match) / field /personRef / oneNullValueHandling: DO_NOTHING -> NOT_MATCH (the add-on's decision tree accepts only MATCH, NOT_MATCH; DO_NOTHING is reserved for matching-policy fields). A missing value no longer abstains: it fails this field, so it cannot confirm the node.`
  and, for an AVERAGE node, `... The average now counts this field as 0 when a value is missing instead of leaving it out: lower the node's minimumScore if that is too strict.`;
- the entity's step message gets: ` NOTE: N decision-tree null-handling value(s) translated DO_NOTHING -> NOT_MATCH, because the add-on's decision tree accepts only MATCH, NOT_MATCH (the stored plan is unchanged; a missing value now fails the field instead of abstaining, and an AVERAGE node counts it as 0 - review its threshold). See nullHandlingTranslated in the step detail.`

### 55.4 Tests and what is not verified

`MatchPlanProfileReaderTest` (RC3 two-enum schema, older single-enum schema, policy-only schema), `MatchingPolicyTranslatorTreeNullTest` (ALL_FIELDS parent confirmation + AVERAGE field translated, stored plan unchanged and still valid, old enum untouched, unknown/empty list, idempotence, summary wording), `MatchPlanLlmPassTest` (the pass keeps its forced DO_NOTHING on a REFERENCE field and defaults others to NOT_MATCH under the RC3 vocabulary; refuses an explicit DO_NOTHING on an ordinary tree field with the schema's words; tool schema and prompt note; older vocabulary unchanged). **Not verified**: nothing ran against EBX or the add-on. The schema read in `MatchingConfigurator.translateTreeNullHandlingForLiveSchema` (MCP client call) has no unit test; the RC3 schema shape is the coordinator's description of the live document, not a captured response. Live check: reconfigure Vol100kM; `Address` is accepted and its step detail names the translation.

## 56. Lot M1 — no `constant` survivor: the golden source is `autoCreateNewGoldenSource` (branch `fix/master-source-system`, 2026-10-17)

### 56.1 The defect, measured

E2E `tools/e2e/b2c_master.sh`, variant simulate-first, project `E2EMASTER20261017212914` (6.3.0-rc3, Match and Merge 6.3.0.5-RC3): after the master build the 534 `Personne` rows
read ECOM 160 / LOYALTY 140 / STORES 234; after "run scope=all" **all 534 read `sourceSystem = MDM`** (`sourceId`, `_loadId`, e-mail… intact; the staging was right). The other
variant (project `E2EMASTER20261017212252`, `Client`) kept its sources. Evidence, in the order it was found:

1. `SELECT … "ebx-metadata"."system"."update_time"` on the master table: `creation_time` 23:33:10 (MasterLoader), `update_time` **23:34:17 on every one of the 534 rows**, updater `ebx-systemUser`;
   in the other variant `update_time` = `creation_time`. `kernel.log`: the only procedure on the master dataspace at 23:34:17 is the add-on's `ProcedureUtil` / `MatchingManager` of the run (the Factory's
   `MasterLoader` ran 1 minute earlier, once, and wrote the right values).
2. `ebx-addon-mame.log` summary of the `/root/Personne` run: `Number of MATCHED: 0`, `Number of Auto-merge groups: 534`, **`Number of merged singletons: 534`**, `Number of goldens created then
   purged: 0`, `Number of child merged groups: 300`, `Fused singleton final writes: 206`, `AUTO MERGE COSTS: singleton{groups=534 records=534 survivorMs=48 …}`. The `Client` run of the other variant:
   `Number of Auto-merge groups: 0`, `Number of merged singletons: 0`.
3. The merge policy stored on the table (`get_matching_config`): survivor `/sourceSystem` = `constant "MDM"` (what `MatchingPolicyTranslator` has written since 2026-09-22, §14), mode `ONLY_DUPLICATES`,
   `autoCreateNewGoldenSource` null. `Personne` is the MAIN table of a business object (members `Adresse`, `Transaction`; `get_business_object_activation_status`: ENABLED, every member published).
   Why the other variant escaped: its main table `Client` took the plain path (`Number of merged singletons: 0`, `DRAIN no-match fast path`; its business-object row reads `published = false`), while its
   child tables `AdresseClient`/`TelephoneClient` took the same singleton path as `Personne` (`Grouping eager-singleton PK-WALK no-match lane active`, `AUTO MERGE COSTS: singleton{groups=534 …}`) and their run
   was then ROLLED BACK by the cascade NullPointerException (the product bug of the same day, lot M2's area) - their rows kept ECOM/LOYALTY/STORES only because nothing was committed.
4. Bytecode (`javap -c`, `webapps/ebx-addon-mame/WEB-INF/classes`): `DeduplicationServiceImpl.mergesSingletons(boolean, isBusinessObject, AutoCreateNewGoldenMode)` is true for a business object in
   `ONLY_DUPLICATES`/`ANY_DUPLICATES` → `eagerSingletonGrouping` → every record without a duplicate goes through `AutoMergingService.merge` → `AutoMergingExecutor.execute` with a ONE-record list
   (`checkOnlyDuplicateModeForBO` only forbids creating a golden for it) → the survivors (`SurvivorService.getFieldSurvivors`) are written back to that record: `constant` replaces its value.

Root cause: **a constant survivor is applied by the add-on to records that are not being merged** (a table that belongs to a business object - `BusinessObjectUtil.isBusinessObject` = the table's
configuration points to the object -, mode `ONLY_DUPLICATES`, entire-table run). The simulate-first variant was a coincidence of the two plans (only its main table was tied to the object and its
run committed), not an effect of the preview policy: both merge policies (`Personne__preview`, `Personne`) carried the same constant. The preview is not involved. Editor text: `product-bugs/2026-10-17-mame-singleton-merged-in-place-constant-survivor-overwrites-records.md`.

### 56.2 The fix (Factory side, nothing to change in the add-on)

* `MatchingPolicyTranslator.buildMergePolicy`: `/sourceSystem` survivor = `no merge` (like `sourceId`); the merge policy gets `autoCreateNewGoldenSource = "MDM"`
  (`MatchingPolicyTranslator.GOLDEN_SOURCE_CODE`). By bytecode that value is read only for a golden the add-on CREATES (`AutoMergingExecutor.generateCustomSourceFieldValue`: built only when the
  policy creates goldens and the group has no golden yet; `SurvivorServiceImpl` drops the survivor rule of the source field), so a golden of a merged group is stamped MDM (as before) and a record
  merged in place keeps its source. The other survivors are identity functions on one record (`no merge`, `max`, `most trusted source`, `longest`).
* Guard: `assertMergePolicyWellFormed` refuses any `constant` survivor and a policy without golden source (`MatchingPolicyTranslatorTest`).
* The source must be REGISTERED: `TrustedSourceRanking.buildTrustedSourcesPayload` appends `MDM` last to every `tableTrustedSourceList` it writes (fresh configure, survivorship route); a REWRITE (which does not
  write the ranking) calls `MatchingConfigurator.ensureGoldenSourceRegistered` first — it sends the STORED ranking plus `MDM`, only when `MDM` is in neither the ranking nor the catalogue.
* Tables configured before the fix: `MatchingPolicyComparator` compares `autoCreateNewGoldenSource` (part of "merge policy chains") and the survivors, so a re-**Configure** is a REWRITE:
  `MatchingConfigRewriteBuilder` writes the golden source and the new survivors (`apply_matching_config`); on a business-object table `MergeConfigPatchPlanner` emits one `set_merge_policy_param`
  (`paramName autoCreateNewGoldenSource`, `value "MDM"`, a plain string) and one `set_chain_entry` replacing `constant` by `no merge` on `/sourceSystem`. **A run launched before that re-Configure
  still applies the old constant** — configure again, then run.
* The preview policy (`<Entity>__preview`, never merged) drops the key: nothing to register for it.
* Review screen (`MatchSurvivorshipBlock`): the `sourceSystem` row reads "no merge — each record keeps its own source; a golden record created by a merge carries the source MDM".

### 56.3 What is NOT done / not verified

* Not run against the live add-on (read-only lot): that `generate_merge_policy` / `apply_matching_config` / `patch_matching_config set_merge_policy_param` accept `autoCreateNewGoldenSource`, and that an
  auto-created golden then carries `MDM` while a singleton keeps its source, is read from the schema (`matching_config_schema`: `autoCreateNewGoldenSource`, `set_merge_policy_param`) and the bytecode, not measured.
  To verify after install: configure a project whose master has a published business object, run scope=all, then
  `SELECT "sourceSystem", COUNT(*) FROM <Table> GROUP BY "sourceSystem"` must show the source codes (no MDM) and, after a merge of two records, one golden with `MDM`.
* The rows already overwritten (project `E2EMASTER20261017212914`) are not repaired: rebuild the master (`master/build`) — the source of a record is only in the staging and the Xref.
* Out of scope (lots M2/M3): the NPE of the cascade on a table without business object (§ product bug of the same day), child-entity plans, the person plan's MATCH leaf.

## 57. Lot M2 - a child entity follows its parent; the Simulate preview that stays (branch `fix/matching-child-tables`, 2026-10-17)

Source: the automated master and matching test (`tools/e2e/b2c_master.sh`, report `test-master-b2c-2026-10-17/BILAN-MASTER.md`), two projects. Nothing here ran against EBX: the live
instance was only READ (data-access, `get_matching_config`, `ebx-addon-mame.log`, the add-on's bytecode with `javap`).

### 57.1 What the log and the bytecode say (it is not what the first report thought)

The first reading was: "the address plan has a MATCH leaf, the add-on auto-merges 300 groups of 2 addresses and its automatic merge throws". The log says otherwise.

- Project `E2EMASTER20261017212914`, run of `Adresse` (23:34:30-37): `End MATCHING Phase, Number of MATCH 0, No of SUSPECT 0`; `DRAIN ... readyToMergeGroupsLeft=300`; `MERGING scan: 0 group(s) skipped, 300 processed`.
  The table holds 600 records for 300 addresses (inline in two sources); the "300 groups" are the 300 single-record groups, no pair was found. The live policy (`get_matching_config`) has only `Suspect` leaves
  (the plan had `autoMerge=false`, so `MatchingPolicyTranslator` turned its MATCH leaf into SUSPECTED, section 3).
- The NullPointerException comes from `MatchingQueueConsumer.doAutoMerge` (javap, `ebx-addon-6.3.0.5-RC3`): `executeAutoMerge` runs whenever the table HAS a merge policy; when `isBusinessObject` is true
  (`BusinessObjectUtil.isBusinessObject(table)`: main table OR member) it does `table.getTableNode().getBusinessObjectModel()` and builds `CascadeMergingService(table, businessObjectModel, ...)`.
  Only the MAIN table of an object has a business object model: for a MEMBER the answer is null, hence `Cannot invoke BusinessObjectModel.getTableNode() because "businessObjectModel" is null`.
- The Factory declares one business object per parent entity that has promoted children (`BusinessObjectPlan`, section 33): `PersonneBO`, main table `/root/Personne`, member `/root/Adresse`
  (`MATCHING_CONFIG` step of `Adresse`: "trigger mode MANUAL: the matching of this table follows its business object /root/Personne"). So a child table is ALWAYS a member.

Consequences: (1) the failure does not depend on the tree - a plan of suspects only, with no pair found, fails the same way; (2) it hits every non-empty member table that has a merge policy, whatever
the pairs; (3) the product text `product-bugs/2026-10-17-mame-auto-merge-table-without-business-object-npe.md` says "no business object is declared" and "tree reaches MATCH": both are wrong, the
table IS a member and the tree had no MATCH. The text must be corrected before it goes to the editor (the reproduction: Person + Address with a business object, a policy on Address, any run).

### 57.2 Decision: a child entity has NO matching plan of its own

A child = a promoted entity whose master table holds a foreign key to ANOTHER promoted entity (`ChildEntityMatching.parentsByChild(MasterModel.Result)`, the same `foreignKeys` that build the
business objects; a self-reference is not a child; two entities that reference each other are neither's child). Its records follow the parent: the parent's plan already compares the child
values (child evidence, sections 33, 45) and the master load re-points the children to the golden record (`alignForeignKeys NONE`, section 52, then the Factory's own re-pointing).
This reverses the default of section 12 ("child entities are matched too", 2026-09-22) for the PROPOSAL; a child can still be matched on request (56.4).

| Where | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Rule pass (`MatchPlanSuggester`) | a child is not proposed; the answer lists `followsParent: ["Adresse follows Personne: no matching plan of its own (...)"]` |
| Model pass (`MatchPlanLlmSuggester`) | the sweep leaves children out (they are not in the prompt as entities to plan; the parent's relation evidence is built independently and still reads them). A request naming the child (`POST matching/suggest-llm?entity=Adresse`, "Propose another") is an explicit ask and keeps it in. `followsParent` in the answer |
| Propose job message | `... Adresse follows Personne: no matching plan of its own, its records follow the parent.` (`MatchingPlanCoverage.withFollows`) |
| Wizard step 6 | the staging order shows a card "Adresse - Follows Personne" with the reason, no button (nothing is missing); the child is not a "gap" ("No plan for X"); step 8's matching counts leave it out |
| Configure (`MatchingConfigurator.configure`) | a child without a plan, or with a PROPOSED/SUPERSEDED one: `followsParent`, not "not accepted", not a failure. A child whose own plan is APPLIED: left exactly as it is (`childKeptAsIs`, nothing deleted, nothing rewritten). Job message: `... 1 child object has no plan of its own (Adresse follows Personne): its records follow the parent's matching.` |
| Run (`MatchingConfigurator.run`) | a child without a plan is `followsParent`, not "not applied" (message: `1 child object has no plan of its own: its records follow the matching of the parent.`) |

### 57.3 When a person asks for a child plan anyway

Two guards, both before anything is written, both with the reason in words (pure: `ChildEntityMatching`, `ReviewRules.canAcceptMatchPlan`):

1. **A child plan holds no MATCH leaf.** Refused at ACCEPT (`ProposalReviews.checkAccept`, so the review screen, the wizard, the bulk accept and `POST staging/decisions` all refuse it), when switching the plan's automatic
   merge on (`setMatchPlanAutoMerge`), and at CONFIGURE (an ACCEPTED plan never configured). Rule read on the stored requirements (flat tree or legacy tiers), whatever `autoMerge` says: a pair of children is never merged on its own
   (two addresses with the same street can belong to two people).
2. **A child plan is not configured while its table is a business object member** (`ChildEntityMatching.memberRunRefusal`, switch `MEMBER_MERGE_DEFECT_PRESENT`). This one goes BEYOND the brief ("only SUSPECTED leaves"):
   56.1 shows a suspects-only plan fails too, so configuring it would buy a `DONE_WITH_FAILURES` run and a rolled-back table. In practice (the Factory declares a business object for every parent) it means a child plan
   is accepted-but-refused-at-configure today; when the add-on is fixed, flip the constant and the explicit child plan works with SUSPECTED leaves only.

These refusals are real failures of the configure (the person asked for the plan): they are listed in `refused[]`, the job ends `DONE_WITH_FAILURES` with the reason.

### 57.4 The preview that stays on the table

Live (`E2EMASTER20261017212914`, variant simulate-first): `Personne__preview` stayed after a configure that ended `DONE`. Reading the `MATCHING_CONFIG` step of `Personne`:
`previewRemovedBeforeGenerate: true` and `removedPreviewPolicy: {"removed":false, "note":"Preview policy Personne__preview left on /root/Personne: the table belongs to a business object, whose policies cannot be rewritten as a list (apply_matching_config is refused there)."}`.
So the cause is neither the answer of `apply_matching_config` nor the order with the pre-generate removal added in `d03f5edc`: **`Personne` is the main table of `PersonneBO`**, and on a business object table
no tool removes ONE policy - `apply_matching_config` is refused (section 33), `patch_matching_config` has no remove-policy op (`matching_config_schema.patchOps`), and `delete_matching_config` answers
`INVALID_PARAMS` ("the table belongs to a business object; delete it from that configuration in the UI"). The `Adresse__preview` of the same run was already gone when the post-success removal ran (the pre-generate removal had taken it: `remove` found no business object main table among its candidates).
Two defects around the cause, fixed:

- `remove` answered `removed:false` + prose for "nothing to remove" and for "exists and stays" alike, and the pre-generate removal wrote `previewRemovedBeforeGenerate: true` whatever it answered. The answer now carries
  `left: true` + `leftReason` when the preview exists and stays (`MatchingPreviewPolicy.markLeft`, `wasLeft`, `isGone`); the pre-generate record is the real boolean.
- Nothing told the person. `configureOne` now puts a preview that stays (or whose removal threw) in the step detail (`previewPolicyLeft`), in the step message (`NOTE: the Simulate preview policy X could not be removed (...)`)
  and in the configure job (`previewsLeft[]`, one sentence per table: `Personne: preview policy Personne__preview could not be removed (the table belongs to a business object and no Match and Merge tool removes one policy of such a table ...); it only runs when someone simulates (manual modes, never the default policy) and does no harm, remove it from the Match and Merge administration screen ...`).

**What is NOT fixed, because it cannot be from here:** removing the preview of a business object table. The leftover is harmless (manual execution modes, not the default policy, not the manual-merge policy since `d03f5edc`), but it is
there until someone deletes it in the add-on's administration screen. A real fix would be for the add-on to offer a policy removal on a business object table (to report with the NullPointerException). An alternative not tried (it changes what a
preview is): on a business object table, simulate under the entity's own policy code instead of `<Entity>__preview` and let the configure rewrite it in place (`BusinessObjectRewritePlan`).
The e2e check "no preview policy is left on the table" now fails only for a leftover the configure job did NOT name.

### 57.5 Existing projects

A child plan already APPLIED stays (56.2). A child plan PROPOSED stays PROPOSED (the sweeps do not touch it any more); reject it ("No matching for this entity") or accept it if it passes the two guards. Nothing is deleted
silently, no policy of the add-on is removed. No change to the XSD (`tools/build_xsd.py` output unchanged).

### 57.6 Tests

`ChildEntityMatchingTest` (who is a child, self reference, mutual reference, member to canonical, MATCH leaf in a flat and a tier plan, both refusals, `ReviewRules.canAcceptMatchPlan`, wording),
`MatchingPlanCoverageFollowersTest` (candidates without children, member -> canonical, a rejected reference makes no child, the message sentence and its French), `ChildPlanGatingSourceTest` (order of the guards before any write,
the lists in configure and run, no delete, the two accept/toggle calls), `MatchingConfigureRunTest` / `MatchingRunRunTest` (the notes), `MatchingPreviewPolicyTest` (`left` vs gone),
`b2c_master_selftest.py` (defect `mm_childplan` caught; a preview left but reported passes; the model with no child says so). **Not verified**: no run against the add-on. The business object membership of a child at
configure time comes from `MameBusinessObjects.resolve` (existing code, unchanged), the refusal text of 56.3 (2) is read from the log and the bytecode, not from a run of the new code.


## 58. Lot M3 — the person plan merges nothing and misses 40 % of the true pairs (branch `fix/matching-person-plan`, 2026-10-17/18)

Measured on the B2C master scenario of 2026-10-17 (`tools/e2e/b2c_master.sh`, ground truth `truth_b2c.json` from `tools/e2e/gen_b2c.py`): 534 person records of 212 people in three
sources (web shop `ECOM` 160, store tickets `STORES` 234, loyalty members `LOYALTY` 140), 565 true pairs (147 inside one source, 418 across). Project `E2EMASTER20261017212252`, entity
`Client`, `MatchPlan` 55 written by the language-model pass: 5 leaves (3 `SUSPECTED`, 2 `NOT_MATCHED`, no `MATCH`), `autoMerge` false. Result: 310 `Suspected` rows (341 pairs once the
add-on's rows are read as clusters), precision 1.00, **recall 0.60**, nothing merged on its own. The second project (`E2EMASTER20261017212914`, plan 56, first node `emailKey + birthDate`)
found 103 pairs: recall 0.18.

### 58.1 Why 40 % are missing — measured, not guessed

`python3 tools/e2e/b2c_missed_pairs.py <dir written by gen_b2c.py> --keys email,address` rebuilds from the three files the keys the Factory derives (e-mail key = upper-case e-mail, name key =
accent-folded lower-case tokens sorted — the `fullNameKey` of the live master, checked on five records —, phone in E.164 with +33, postal code, address key), lists every true pair with the
keys the two records share, and simulates a plan that finds a pair through the keys it uses. The simulation reproduces the live numbers: `email,address` finds **341** of 565 (the live plan:
341 pairs, 310 rows); `email+birth,address` finds **103** (the live second plan: 103 rows).

| True pairs, by the keys the two records share | pairs | found by the live plan (e-mail key OR address keys) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| e-mail, name, phone, postal code, address, birth date | 103 | 103 (ECOM with LOYALTY) |
| e-mail, name, phone, postal code | 238 | 238 |
| **name, phone, postal code only** (no e-mail key on at least one side, no address key) | **224** | **0** |

The 224 missed pairs, by applications: `STORES`-`STORES` 96 (several tickets of one person), `ECOM`-`STORES` 69, `LOYALTY`-`STORES` 59. **Every one of them involves a store ticket without an
e-mail**: the e-mail is filled on ECOM 160/160, LOYALTY 140/140 and STORES **131/234 (56 %)** — 103 tickets have none —, the address keys on ECOM and LOYALTY only (STORES 0/234, a ticket carries
a postal code, no address). The two keys the plan filters its candidates on (`emailKey` OR `addressKeys`, the add-on's own log: "Mandatory field sets: {addressKeys} {addressKeys} {emailKey}")
reach 131 of the 234 tickets; the other 103 can never be proposed as the duplicate of anything. Their name key is filled on 234/234 and is a pre-clustering field (weight 5), so these pairs are probably compared; by the tree, node N2 (average of
names, 84.6 % without the birth date) then passes and the next node demands an identical address key that a ticket does not have: `NOT_MATCHED` (inferred from the tree and the log, not read in the add-on's
per-pair results). All 224 share the name key, the E.164 phone and the postal code; none shares an e-mail key or an address key.

What the other keys would have given on this data (same script, `--keys`): the phone alone 565/565 with 0 false pair (the phone of the master is a field of the CHILD table `TelephoneClient` in this
project, `phoneNumberE164`; the plan's own rationale says "No normalized phone key exists" — a staging gap, not a plan gap); `email,name` 565 found, 129 namesakes (same name, other person);
`email,name+postal` 565 found, 16 false pairs; `email,phone` 565 found, 0 false.

Two more facts read in the live data, reported but not touched by this lot:

- The **address path found nothing live**. The tree reads `emailKey` OR `addressKeys`, so six different people sharing an address (e.g. ids 17 and 126, same `addressKeys` token, two different
  people) should have been suspects; they are not in `Suspected` (checked: `126~371`, `126~449`, `17~364` only), and the 103-row second plan equals the simulation WITHOUT address pairs. The add-on's
  candidate search did not propose the pairs although its log lists `{addressKeys}` as a mandatory set. Cause unknown (the policy gives `addressKeys` weight 1 of 29).
- Why no pair is merged: (a) the model never proposed a `MATCH` leaf — the run history shows it describing the exact shared-child-key branch as "SUSPECTED, never MATCH" —, and (b) the pass
  would have refused it: the MATCH-terminal guard of `Session#buildAndAppendNode` refuses a `MATCH_KEY` field ("a normalised copy of a business field, never a real identifier") and any field
  whose distinct-among-filled ratio is under 0.95 — a key two systems really share is by definition not near-unique (`emailKey`: 207 distinct for 391 filled). With `autoMerge` false the
  translator turns every `MATCH` into `SUSPECTED` anyway (§3.4), so a `MATCH` leaf costs nothing until a person turns automatic merge on.

### 58.2 What the pass now knows: `matching.KeyFacts`

`KeyFacts` (pure, Jackson only; `master.KeyFactsSelection` chooses the keys, `ebx.KeyFactsReader` reads them) counts, in linear time, over the master table of an entity:

- **candidate keys**: attributes of role BUSINESS or MATCH_KEY (or derived child keys), type STRING/DATE/INTEGER, not a reference, not a per-source record key, at most 255 characters (4000 for
  child keys), filled on at least 5 % when that is exactly measured, neither constant nor entirely unique; a source attribute that has its own matching key is represented by the key. Derived
  keys first, then the best filled; at most 8. Decided from role/type/length/profile, **never from a name**;
- per key and per source system: records filling it, records whose value another record also carries, distinct values, pairs of records sharing the exact value;
- per ordered pair of keys (K, J) whose **bases** differ (a key and the field it is derived from are one base): among the pairs of records carrying the same K, how many carry the same J
  (`agree`), both filled and different (`conflict`), J missing on a side (`unknown`); `rate = agree / (agree + conflict)`. A pair is **SAFE** when it has at least 10 comparable pairs, a rate of at
  least 0.99 and 0 conflict, on the complete table (`MIN_COMPARABLE_PAIRS`, `MIN_AGREEMENT`, `MAX_CONFLICTS`);
- the pattern of filled keys of every record, per source system (a bit mask): from it the number of records of a system that fill at least one key of ANY subset is exact (the "reach" of a candidate
  filter), without querying again.

Measured on the scenario (`KeyFactsTest`, numbers equal to the independent count of the Python script): `emailKey -> fullNameKey` 341 pairs, 341 agree, 0 differ (SAFE); `mobileE164 -> fullNameKey`
565/565 (SAFE); `mobileE164 -> emailKey` 341 agree, 224 unknown (SAFE on the pairs that can be compared); `fullNameKey -> emailKey` 694 pairs, 129 differ (not SAFE: namesakes);
`addressKeys -> fullNameKey` 109 pairs, 6 differ (not SAFE).

One bounded read-only EBX SQL statement per entity (`SELECT sourceSystem, <keys> FROM "<Entity>"`, streamed, closed after `MAX_ROWS` = 200,000 rows; a larger table gives facts flagged `sampled`
that relax no rule and produce no finding). Any failure gives `null` — the pass then behaves exactly as before the lot. Stored with the plan as `requirements.keyFacts` (about 2 KB): the plan card
computes its findings from the stored plan alone, a plan proposed before the lot simply has none.

### 58.3 What the model is told and what the pass accepts

- **Prompt**: after each entity's attribute list, a "Measured key facts" block — records per system; per key the fill per system (with the share), the distinct values, the records sharing a value
  per system, the pairs sharing it; per pair of independent keys the line `same emailKey -> fullNameKey: 341 pair(s), agree 341, differ 0, unknown 0, rate 100.0% [SAFE: ...]`; and "Records that fill NONE of
  the keys above, per source system". Counts only, never a value (a test pins it).
- **System prompt**, two paragraphs, no column name in either:
  - *MATCH ON TWO INDEPENDENT AGREEMENTS*: where the facts mark a pair [SAFE], build an `ALL_FIELDS` node on exactly those two keys (exact, 100, `NOT_MATCH` nulls) whose `onTrue` is `MATCH`, its
    `onFalse` continuing to the weaker paths (the strong key alone, ending in `SUSPECTED`: the pairs that share K and not J are the ones a steward should see). Anything weaker — a single key, a pair
    not marked SAFE, a similarity score — ends in `SUSPECTED`. The earlier rules stay: the same name with a different address, phone or birth date is not a match; an `AVERAGE` node never ends in
    `MATCH`; the model never sets `autoMerge` (a `MATCH` leaf merges only when a person turns it on).
  - *REACH EVERY SOURCE SYSTEM*: a candidate is found only through a key both records fill; for each source system look at the keys it fills and add a path starting with an exact key it does fill,
    even when weaker (`SUSPECTED`); say in the rationale which system each path covers.
- **Guard** (`master.MeasuredMatchPath`): an `ALL_FIELDS` node of two or more fields, `onTrue` `MATCH`, none read through a child or a reference, is accepted although none of its fields passes the
  per-field identifier checks (MATCH_KEY, fill rate, distinct ratio, never-repeats) when two of its fields K and J (after matching-key substitution) are SAFE in the entity's facts (either
  direction) on the complete table. The exact algorithm at score 100 on every field is still required; the cross-system and shape guards still run. Otherwise the old refusal stands, and when
  the facts mark pairs SAFE the refusal ends with them: "The measured key facts mark these pairs of independent keys SAFE (...): emailKey + fullNameKey (341 of 341 comparable pairs agree)". The
  accepted rationale gets, right after the model's own words, "MATCH path N1 (emailKey + fullNameKey) is justified by the measured data: 341 pair(s) of records share emailKey, 341 of the 341 that
  can be compared also share fullNameKey, 0 differ."
- **Reach challenge** (once per entity, the one-shot mechanism of §34/§45): when the plan's candidate filter is FILTERED and a source system with at least 20 records has 25 % or more of them
  outside every key of the filter, the first proposal is refused with the numbers and the keys that system does fill ("Source STORES: 103 of 234 record(s) fill none of the candidate-filter keys (emailKey,
  addressKeys), so they can never be proposed as duplicates. It fills fullNameKey (100%), mobileE164 (100%)... This is asked once"). The resubmission is accepted whatever it is, and its rationale
  keeps "Reach: ..." when the gap remains.

### 58.4 The plan card (`matching.KeyFindings`, `MatchPlanView.renderKeyFindings`)

Two findings, computed on read from the stored plan, shown under the tree title (the review screen and the wizard's step 6 share `renderTreeBlock`), EN and FR (`review.match.findings.*`):

1. **A path safe to merge automatically** — only when the plan has no `MATCH` leaf: a path ending in `SUSPECTED` whose exact key K is SAFE with an independent key J. "Path N1 is safe to merge
   automatically: 341 pair(s) of records share emailKey, and 341 of the 341 that can be compared also share fullNameKey; 0 differ. Today it ends in a review. To make it a confirmed match, require
   emailKey and fullNameKey together on that path (ask for another proposal), then turn automatic merge on." When J is already required by the path the second sentence says the `MATCH` leaf merges
   once automatic merge is on. Nothing rewrites the plan.
2. **A source out of reach**: "Source STORES: 103 of 234 record(s) fill none of the candidate-filter keys (emailKey, addressKeys), so they can never be proposed as duplicates of anything. That source
   fills fullNameKey (100%), mobileE164 (100%): a path that starts with one of them would reach it."

On the live plan 55 (rebuilt with its stored facts in `KeyFindingsTest`) both appear; the address paths get no "safe" finding (six namesakes share an address).

### 58.5 Files, tests, limits

New: `matching/KeyFacts`, `matching/KeyFindings`, `master/KeyFactsSelection`, `master/MeasuredMatchPath`, `ebx/KeyFactsReader`, `tools/e2e/b2c_missed_pairs.py`. Touched: `master/MatchPlanLlmPass` (system prompt,
`EntityInfo.keyFacts`, prompt block, MATCH guard, rationale, reach challenge, `requirements.keyFacts`), `ebx/MatchPlanLlmSuggester` (reads the facts once per eligible entity),
`review/MatchPlanView`, `Messages_en/fr.properties`, `review.css`. No XSD change (the facts live in the `requirements` JSON). Tests: `KeyFactsTest`, `KeyFindingsTest`, `MatchPlanLlmPassKeyFactsTest`,
`MatchPlanKeyFindingsViewTest`, `B2cKeyFixtureTest` over `src/test/resources/.../matching/b2c_person_keys.tsv` (the 534 records reduced to their keys; `b2c_selftest.py` checks the file is what the
generator writes and that the Python analysis gives 341 found / 224 missed).

Not verified live (nothing ran against the instance): that the language model, given the facts, proposes the `MATCH` + reach paths (the pass, the guard and the challenge are tested with scripted
proposals, including the plan the model really proposed); the SQL of `KeyFactsReader` (same shape as `CrossSystemMeasures`, not executed here); that the add-on's candidate search honours a
`fullNameKey` / phone filter (the address filter produced nothing live, see 56.1). A phone key does not exist on `Client` of project 1 (it lives in `TelephoneClient`): the facts cannot offer what
staging did not derive — the staging side (a phone key, or a child-keys attribute for the phones) would make the 224 pairs findable with a `SAFE` path.


## 59. Lot M4 — matching works end to end with Match and Merge business objects (branch `fix/matching-business-object`, 2026-10-18)

Source: the second automated run of `tools/e2e/b2c_master.sh` on 1.2.0-258 (2026-10-18 about 00:25; projects `E2EMASTER20261017222251`, variant plain, and `E2EMASTER20261017222813`, variant
simulate-first), after lots M1-M3. Nothing here ran against EBX: the instance was only READ (`data-access`, `get_business_object_config`, `get_business_object_activation_status`,
`matching_config_schema`, the MCP descriptions and the bytecode of `ebx-addon-6.3.0.5-RC3` with `javap`).

### 59.1 What the add-on requires, with the evidence

**(A) The table configuration of every table of the object must carry the business object — and only `generate_*_policy` with `businessObject` gives it.**

- Variant plain, `PipelineStep 2031`: `generate_matching_policy` on `/root/Personne` (plan with the child field `/root/Adresse/street`, weight 0) answered the soft miss `INVALID_PARAMS "businessObjectField names a field
  on a member table of a business object, and the matching-table configuration of /root/Personne carries no business object."`. The step detail shows the order of the calls: `get_matching_config` (`CONFIG_NOT_FOUND`),
  `get_business_object_config` candidates declared, **`set_trusted_sources`**, then `generate_matching_policy` with `businessObject`. `get_business_object_config /root/Personne` read afterwards:
  `businessObject.id = null, dataModel = null, published = false`, and one member, `/root/Personne`, with no policy: a configuration with no business object.
- Bytecode: `MameConfigWriter.writeFieldLocation` reads `MatchingTableConfig.getBusinessObject()`; null gives the message above. `generateMatchingPolicyForBusinessObject` /
  `generateMergePolicyForBusinessObject` call `getOrCreateBusinessObjectRecord` then `BusinessObjectUtil.createTableConfigurationIfNotExist`, which creates, **for every table of the object (main and members), a
  configuration with `businessObject` set and no policy — and skips a table that already has a configuration**. `MameServer.setTrustedSources(ctx, table, trustedSources, dataModel)` and `setTableSettings`
  have no `businessObject` argument and "create the matching-table configuration first when the table has none" (`set_trusted_sources.md`): run first, they create the BO-less configuration that
  `createTableConfigurationIfNotExist` then respects.
- No tool repairs it: `MameConfigDeleter` and `apply_matching_config` call `rejectIfBusinessObjectTable` (decided on the data model, not on the configuration). Only the administration screen can.
- The configurator did `set_trusted_sources` BEFORE the first generate since 2026-09-22 (§15); it only worked for a plan of plain fields (the object record is created by the generate) and for the
  simulate-first variant (the preview policy had been generated, with `businessObject`, earlier).

**(B) A run on the main table needs a default matching policy — and a merge policy — on EVERY member table.**

- Variant simulate-first, `PipelineStep 2079`: `matchRecords refused (invalid state ...): Table urn:ebx:publication:E2EMASTER20261017222813_Master (/root/AdresseClient): The default matching policy is not
  defined.` `get_business_object_config /root/Client` (bound, `id = "12"`, `published = true`): members `/root/Client` (policies `Client__preview`, `Client`, default `Client`) and `/root/AdresseClient`:
  `matchingPolicies: [], mergePolicies: [], tableSettings.defaultMatchingPolicy: null`. `get_business_object_activation_status`: both ENABLED with their metadataset — activation does not need a policy,
  the run does. (The merge policy: CLAUDE.md §8, "a run is refused (400) until EVERY member table has a default matching + merge policy", measured on PersonTestHan.)
- A member's configuration is created EMPTY by the first generate of the object (A above): nothing writes a member's policy by itself.

**(C) A run ON a member table ends in a NullPointerException** (`product-bugs/2026-10-17-mame-auto-merge-table-without-business-object-npe.md`): a member is configured, never run alone.

### 59.2 The design

1. **Bind first, then everything else** (`MatchingConfigurator.configureOne`, `MameBusinessObjects.checkBinding`, `master.BusinessObjectMembers.binding`). On the main table of a declared object, `get_business_object_config`
   is read before any write: `BOUND` (object record with an id), `CLEAN` (`CONFIG_NOT_FOUND`: the first generate binds), `STRAY` (id null although a table has a configuration), `NOT_DECLARED`. A `STRAY`
   object is refused before anything is written — when the plan compares a member field, the one write the add-on refuses on it — with a message that says what happened and what to do (administration screen);
   with a plan of plain fields it proceeds as before. The Factory never creates a stray any more:
2. **`set_trusted_sources` runs between `generate_matching_policy` and `generate_merge_policy` on a business object table** (`writePoliciesThroughGenerate(..., WriteStep)`), unchanged for a plain table. It still
   precedes the merge policy (the golden source it registers, lot M1, must exist when the merge policy names it).
3. **Every member gets an inert matching policy and an inert merge policy, written by the configure of the parent** (`MameBusinessObjects.ensureMemberPolicies`, after the writes of the main table in every
   branch — fresh, rewrite, resume — and before the validation and the activation; a configure that wrote member policies activates the object again).
   - `BusinessObjectMembers.inertMatchingPolicy(entity)`: `processCode` = the entity name; no `matchingOnCreation`/`matchingOnUpdate` (a member refuses them, Vol1mR step 1433; it reads back manual); one
     pre-clustering field `/id` (`@default` resolves to `@Integer` on a master table, `matching_config_schema(table)`) and one comparison `All fields match` on `/id` with `ebx-addon-mame@exact`: two distinct records never
     share an id, so the tree never leaves its false branch. `trueNode` is `SUSPECTED` (never `MATCHED`: nothing can merge on its own), `falseNode` `NOT_MATCHED` (the add-on refuses a node whose two branches reach
     the same leaf, §36).
   - `BusinessObjectMembers.inertMergePolicy(entity, mode)`: mode `DISABLED`, record selection `mostCompleted`, default field merge `longest`, identity survivors on the technical fields (`no merge`, `max`), no
     `autoCreateNewGoldenSource`, no `constant`, no trusted-source function (a member has no ranking). If the add-on refuses `DISABLED`, the same policy is written in `ONLY_DUPLICATES` (the mode of the earlier
     member policies, which the add-on accepted) and the step says which one stands.
   - `generate_matching_policy` (member as `table`, `businessObject` = the main table), `generate_merge_policy`, `patch_matching_config set_merge_policy_link`; the default is the first policy generated, checked by a
     re-read and set with `set_table_settings` otherwise (`ensureDefaultMatchingPolicy`); a final re-read must show every member with a default matching policy and a merge policy, else the configure fails.
   - A member that already holds policies is not rewritten (a child plan an earlier pass applied, `childKeptAsIs`): only what is missing is added.
   - Nothing is proposed to a person: a member has no `MatchPlan` (lot M2). The configure job says it in one sentence per member (`memberPolicies`), and the step detail carries the calls (`memberPolicies[]`).
4. **A member is never run on its own** (`ChildEntityMatching.runsAlone`, `MatchingConfigurator.runInternal`): any child entity — whatever the status of its plan, an APPLIED one included — is listed `followsParent`
   ("Adresse follows Personne"), tied to `MEMBER_MERGE_DEFECT_PRESENT`. M2 only did it for a child without a plan; an APPLIED child plan would have been run and hit the NPE.
5. **A project configured before this lot is completed before its run** (`MameBusinessObjects.ensureMembersBeforeRun`): the run of a table that is the main table of a declared object first looks at its
   members and writes the missing inert policies (then `activate_business_object_matching`). That is the state of `E2EMASTER20261017222813` — its next run needs no new configure.

### 59.3 Point C — accepted STAGING-zone constraints 333 and 351 left ACCEPTED with an empty `applyMessage`

Not "never tried": the staging load step (`PipelineStep 2024` and `2068`) says `Accepted script constraint 333 could not be applied by this load: cannot apply '333': parameter(s) [value] are still 'to be
provided' in the binding - resolve them (reject and re-propose, or edit the row) before applying.. 2 accepted script constraint(s) applied by this load.` The other accepted constraints of both projects (331, 332,
340, 341, 349, 350) were APPLIED by the same call. The two that stayed have `binding.value.toBeProvided` written by the model itself ("loyaltyPoints is an integer, no matching text attribute exists" /
"purchaseDate is a DATE, the function wants an ISO text"): a function whose parameter is text over a typed attribute.

Three defects, not one:

1. `CapabilityApplier.applyAllClaimed` caught the refusal of `prepare` (before any call), kept it in the batch result and **wrote nothing on the row** — only the failures after the first MCP call
   (`failAndEndStep`) wrote `applyMessage`. Now `recordPrepareFailure` writes it (`writeApplyMessageOnly`, the status left as it is: ACCEPTED, or APPLIED for an explicit re-apply; never a PROPOSED/REJECTED/SUPERSEDED row, another project's
   row, or a row of another nature — `recordsPrepareFailure`).
2. The notes of the auto-apply reached the job (`pListener.note`) only when a derivation had been applied by the same load (`if (autoApplied.size() > 0)`). They are forwarded whatever applied and kept in the step detail
   (`autoApplyNotes`). The note also lost its doubled full stop (`ConstraintAutoApply.failureNote`).
3. The bulk accept (`StagingBulkDecideRun`) accepts a constraint with a parameter left to be provided and says "will be applied automatically once the model is generated". **Not changed**: a derivation's
   `defaultCountry` is provided after the accept (the e2e does it at step 5), so refusing at accept would break that order; the row now says why it cannot be applied. A person rejects it or provides the parameter.

`tools/e2e/b2c_scenario.py` (`check_constraints_applied`): a constraint left ACCEPTED **with** its reason on the row passes and is printed as information; **without** it is the failure ("the load did not say why").

### 59.4 Files, tests, limits

New: `master/BusinessObjectMembers` (pure: binding, members, writes, inert policies, wording). Touched: `ebx/MameBusinessObjects` (`checkBinding`, `ensureMemberPolicies`, `ensureMembersBeforeRun`),
`ebx/MatchingConfigurator` (order of `set_trusted_sources`, binding check, member policies, run guard, pre-run completion, `memberPolicies` in the result), `ebx/MatchingConfigureRun` (job sentence),
`master/ChildEntityMatching.runsAlone`, `ebx/CapabilityApplier`, `ebx/ConstraintAutoApply`, `ebx/StagingLoader`, `tools/e2e/*` (stand-in factory answers `get_business_object_config`; the scenario checks every
member; defects `mm_nomemberpolicy`, `constraintleft`, `constraintexplained`). No XSD change, no message bundle change (the new refusals use `engine.conflict.refused` / `engine.external.toolFailed`).
Tests: `BusinessObjectMembersTest` (the live answers of both projects as fixtures), `BusinessObjectMembersSourceTest` (order of the calls), `ConstraintAutoApplyTest`, `ChildEntityMatchingTest`,
`MatchingConfigureRunTest`, and the e2e self-tests.

Not verified live (nothing was written on the instance): that the add-on accepts the inert policies as written (`validate_matching_config` is part of the configure and will say; the first live run is the test),
that it accepts the merge mode `DISABLED` on a member (the fallback is coded for the refusal), that a run of the object then ends DONE with the members as they are, and that the cascade does not copy the members'
records in `DISABLED` mode as it did in `ONLY_DUPLICATES` (project `...212914`: ids 301-600). A stray configuration (project `...222251` itself) stays: the Factory cannot delete it; the project must be rebuilt.

### 59.5 For the editor

(1) `set_trusted_sources` / `set_table_settings` create a table configuration with no business object on a table that belongs to one, and nothing can delete or repair it afterwards (`delete_matching_config`,
`apply_matching_config` are refused on any business object table); the next `generate_matching_policy` with a member field then answers "carries no business object". Suggestion: take `businessObject` on those two
