tools, or let `createTableConfigurationIfNotExist` link an existing configuration. (2) The run of an object is refused for "The default matching policy is not defined" on a member that is ENABLED with its
metadataset; `get_business_object_activation_status` should not say ENABLED for a member the run will refuse, or the first generate should create a default policy for every member.


## 60. Lot M5 - the matching model pass loops on the same refusal until the token budget ends the run (branch `fix/matching-llm-loop`, 2026-10-18)

Two live runs, same shape. **Run 433** (project `E2EMASTER20261017231233`, phase `MATCHING_SUGGEST_LLM`, 23 steps): ten `propose_match_plan` calls for `Personne`, the last four answered by the SAME refusal ("'mobileE164' is not near-unique
enough, among its filled values, for an exact, MATCH-terminal node ... measured 100.0% fill, 39.7% distinct"), then status `BUDGET` (329,919 tokens of 300,000); the wizard said "proposed nothing and gave no reason". Staging had given the
entity no name key, so no pair could be SAFE (lot M3) - yet the prompt pushed the model towards a MATCH path, and the refusal named no way out. **Run 454** (project `E2EMASTER20261017232631`, 1.2.0-260): seven refusals of `Client` -
child evidence, a minimumScore text that said "at most 100" then "never above 50", `NODE_SHARED` three times (N7, N8, N11), "candidate search NOT filtered" twice - then `skip_entity` with a sentence of the model's that read as if the Factory's
own rules contradicted each other, and the budget at step 21 (289,691 input tokens).

### 60.1 Why the old breaker never fired

It was keyed on the whole CALL (root, nodes, tiers, clustering fields): a model that varies the rest of its tree makes a new key every time, so "three identical calls" never happened while the SAME guard refused the SAME field four
times. The system prompt also promised "a refusal repeated three times in a row ends the run outright", which has been false since lot R4 (it ends one entity).

### 60.2 The breaker on the refusal itself (`MatchPlanLlmPass.Session`, a ledger per entity)

Per entity the session keeps: proposals made (`attempts`), the last refusal text, and counts per refusal SIGNATURE (the text with node ids taken out, so renaming N2 to N3 is not a new refusal). The entity's proposal ENDS - recorded as
refused, `handled`, the run goes on with the next entity, `stopped` is never set - when: the same refusal comes **twice in a row** (`SAME_REFUSAL_IN_A_ROW`), or **three times in the run** (`SAME_REFUSAL_IN_THE_RUN`), or **6 proposals**
were refused (`maxAttemptsPerEntity(int)`, default `DEFAULT_MAX_ATTEMPTS_PER_ENTITY`; settable on the session, not a Settings field - no XSD change). The old call-keyed breaker stays (it still covers `skip_entity`). The answer to the
model says "Giving up on X: <cause>. It is recorded as refused, with this reason". An entity the model skips AFTER refusals is recorded the same way (`SKIPPED_AFTER_REFUSAL`): the model's sentence stays in `notes[]` as an audit trail but is
never shown as the reason. The ledger of the entities left without a plan is written in the step detail as `attempts{entity: {count, lastRefusal (1,500 characters at most), endedBy}}`.

The wizard (`wizard.MatchingPlanCoverage.gaps(..., ModelAttempts)`) words a gap, first match wins: the pass ended it -> `MODEL_REFUSED` with the last refusal ("The language model made N proposal(s) for this object and none was accepted. Last
refusal: ..."); the model's own skip; a plan that did not fit its field; an object proposed for whose run status is `BUDGET` -> new kind `MODEL_BUDGET` ("The proposal ended on the token budget after N attempt(s), every one refused. Last
refusal: ..."); proposed for and abandoned by the model -> `MODEL_REFUSED`; only an object never proposed for stays `MODEL_SILENT`. Bundle keys `wizard.matching.gap.reason.modelRefusedAfter`, `...modelBudget`,
`review.match.tree.clustering.notFiltered.acceptedByFactory` (en and fr, end of the files). The refusal itself is the Factory's English sentence, the one the model read; only its frame is translated.

### 60.3 A refusal names the way out; the prompt says up front whether MATCH is possible

`MeasuredMatchPath.wayOut(entity, field)` ends the two MATCH-terminal refusals (a matching key; "not near-unique enough"): the field belongs to a SAFE pair -> "Pair it with <partner(s)>" and the pairs with their counts; SAFE pairs
exist but not for this field -> those pairs and "end this path in SUSPECTED"; facts complete and none SAFE -> "No SAFE pair of independent keys is measured on this entity: end this path in SUSPECTED (a MATCH is possible only on a single
field that is itself a near-unique identifier)"; no facts or a sample -> the same way out without claiming a measurement. `MeasuredMatchPath.verdictLine` adds to each entity's block of the prompt a line "MATCH paths on <entity>: ..."
(the SAFE pairs, or NO pair is SAFE, or nothing was measured), and the system prompt announces it. M3's acceptance rule (`justification`) and its thresholds are unchanged.

### 60.4 Shared nodes, the candidate filter, the child-keys ceiling (run 454)

- **`NODE_SHARED` is the Factory's constraint** (the add-on's nested `trueNode`/`falseNode` has one parent per node): `master.SharedNodeCloner` copies every node reached through a second branch, with its whole subtree, under fresh ids,
  BEFORE the tree is validated; the stored rationale says "Node N7 was reached from several branches; the Factory copied it as N12". A real cycle, a node whose two edges both lead to the same target, are left for the validation.
  `DecisionTreePlan.validate` itself still refuses a shared node (the review screens and the rule pass use it).
- **The "candidate search NOT filtered" refusal names the rewrite** with the entity's own exact keys, most filled first (measured key facts; without facts, the derived matching keys): "wrap path N1 > N3 under an ALL_FIELDS node on K (exact,
  bothNullValueHandling and oneNullValueHandling NOT_MATCH, minimumScore 100) whose onTrue is the first node of that path and whose onFalse is the other paths or NOT_MATCHED. Keys filled on this entity: K 100%, ...". **A plan with a warning
  beats none**: the SECOND unfiltered proposal of an entity - or the one the cap or the breaker was about to end the entity on - is kept as it is (every other guard passed), with `WARNING - candidate search NOT filtered (kept by the
  Factory after N proposal(s) ...)` in its rationale and `requirements.unfilteredCandidateSearchReason` + `unfilteredAcceptedBy = FACTORY`; the plan card says "Kept by the Factory so that the object has a plan ... (ask for another
  proposal to refine it)" instead of "Kept on purpose". The model's own opt-out (`acceptUnfilteredCandidateSearch`) is unchanged.
- **The child-keys ceiling is stated as it is applied**: "measured here, one record has 1 child record(s) at most, which supports 100, and this pass refuses anything above 50 whatever the count. Set minimumScore to 50 or less."

### 60.5 How tokens are counted, and what is resent

`AgentLoop` (the `on-ebx-agent` jar, read by `javap`) keeps the whole conversation and sends it again at every model round trip; `Budget.maxTotalTokens` (`AgentRuntime.DEFAULT_MAX_TOTAL_TOKENS` 300,000, setting `maxAgentTokens`) is
compared with **the sum, over the round trips, of the input tokens plus the output tokens the provider reports for each** - so the cost is cumulative and grows with the square of the number of steps (run 433: a first prompt of a few thousand
tokens, 329,919 after 23 steps). What dominates the growth is the arguments of the refused calls: each failed `propose_match_plan` carries the whole tree. `ebx.ConversationCompactor` (wrapping the client in `AgentRuntime.run`, for
every phase) drops the **arguments of the refused calls of the rounds older than the last three** (replaced by `{"omitted": ...}`; call ids and names kept, so every result still has its call), keeps the refusal (1,200 characters at most),
and touches nothing else: not the prompt, not the model's words, not an accepted call, not the last three rounds. Test: twelve refused rounds cost less than half. **Not done**: the first prompt (the entities' facts) is resent in full
at each step; trimming it would mean a summary round or a provider-side cache, which is the next step if budgets still end runs; the budget itself is unchanged. The listener's trace (`AgentStep`) still records the full original arguments.

### 60.6 Files, tests, limits

New: `master/SharedNodeCloner`, `ebx/ConversationCompactor`. Touched: `master/MatchPlanLlmPass` (ledger, `refuse`, `skipEntity`, rewrite, child-keys wording, prompt), `master/MeasuredMatchPath` (`wayOut`, `verdictLine`, `safePairs`),
`ebx/MatchPlanLlmSuggester` (`attempts{}`), `ebx/MatchingSuggestLlmRun`, `ebx/SuggestRulesRun`, `ebx/AgentRuntime`, `wizard/MatchingPlanCoverage`, `wizard/WizardPage`, `matching/CandidateFilterCheck`
(`acceptedByFactory`), `review/MatchPlanTreeDiagram`, the two bundles. **No XSD change.** Tests: `MatchPlanLlmPassLoopTest`, `ConversationCompactorTest`, `MatchingPlanCoverageTest`, and the adjusted
`MatchPlanLlmPassTest` (the call-keyed breaker now ends at the second identical refusal; the scripted sequences raise the cap), `MatchPlanLlmPassCandidateFilterTest`, `MatchPlanLlmPassKeyFactsTest`.
Not verified live: that the model, given the verdict line and the rewrite, stops trying MATCH where no pair is SAFE and converges on a filtered tree; that a compacted conversation costs the measured fraction on a real provider (the test counts
characters); a provider that rejects a tool call whose arguments no longer match the tool's schema was not seen (the history is not validated by the providers known here), but is untested.

## 61. Lot M6 — the add-on's business-object validation throws; the main table is validated alone (branch `fix/matching-validate-bo-fallback`, 2026-10-18)

Measured live 2026-10-18 02:07 (EBX 6.3.0-rc3 + Match and Merge RC3, Factory 1.2.0-263, projects `E2EMASTER20261018000216` and `E2EMASTER20261017235630`): the configure of the person entity
(main table `/root/Client` of a declared business object, member `/root/AdresseClient`) went through `generate_matching_policy(businessObject)` → `set_trusted_sources` → the member inert policies
(§59) → … and FAILED in the phase "validating the matching configuration". `validate_matching_config` called with `businessObject` (the tool takes exactly one of `table` / `businessObject`)
answered a JSON-RPC ERROR, so the MCP client threw: `tools/call: Tool invocation failed: Cannot invoke "com.orchestranetworks.addon.mame.model.config.MatchingTableConfig.getDataModel()"
because "matchingTableRecord" is null`. Add-on stack (kernel.log): `MameServer.validateMatchingConfig` → `MameConfigValidator.validateBusinessObject` → `addBusinessObjectRecordMessages` →
`BusinessObjectValidationServiceImpl.validate` → `MatchingTableValidationServiceImpl.validateInternal` (its 7th iterator, `BusinessObjectValidationIterator`) → `buildResult` →
`buildInvalidIssue`: `buildResult` takes the validation item's record, looks it up as a `MatchingTableConfig` by primary key (`MatchingTableConfigDAO.getByPrimaryKey`), the business-object
record is not one → null → NPE. A product bug of the add-on's MCP tool, triggered as soon as the business-object validation report has one item
(`product-bugs/2026-10-18-mame-validate-business-object-npe.md`). The configuration itself was fine: right after the failure `validate_matching_config {table: /root/Client, dataModel}` (no
`businessObject`) answered `valid: true` with two warnings only, `get_business_object_activation_status` answered `overallState ENABLED` with both members ENABLED and `metadatasetExists true`,
and `get_business_object_config` listed the object (id 14, published true).

### 61.1 The fallback (`ebx/MatchingValidation`)

The validate call of `MatchingConfigurator.configureOne` goes through `MatchingValidation.validate(port, table, businessObject, detail)`, pure apart from its `Port` (the same discipline as
`MatchingActivationGuard.StatusPort`). On a plain table: one call with `table`, as before. On the main table of a business object: one call with `businessObject`; when that call ends in a
THROWN error — a `McpException` (JSON-RPC error, the live case) or a tool-level `isError` answer; never a soft miss `success:false`, never `valid:false`, which are ANSWERS and keep today's
refusals — the step detail gets `validateBusinessObject = {arguments, thrown: <text>, fallback: "table"}` and the main table is validated alone (`table` + `dataModel`). The three checks that
follow (tool error, soft miss, `valid:false`) apply to THAT answer, unchanged; a fallback that throws too propagates (today's refusal: "MCP call failed" on the entity). The step detail's
`validate` entry is the call that was checked.

When the fallback validated, the configure says so, never silently: the entity step message ends with `NOTE: Match and Merge could not validate the business object /root/Client: its validation tool
failed on an error of its own (product bug, see product-bugs/2026-10-18-mame-validate-business-object-npe.md). The main table /root/Client was validated alone and the configuration went on.`; the
step detail holds the same note with its code marker (`validateBusinessObjectNote`, key `wizard.step6.configure.note.validateBusinessObjectFallback`, en/fr, `EngineMessageCodec` — the
RunTexts style); the configure job's result carries `validationNotes[]` (coded), its message the English (`MatchingConfigureRun.withNotes`, marker stripped: a job message is several sentences);
`MatchingActivityReader` reads `validationNotes` off the configure job's detail into `MatchingActivity.notes`, and the step-6 panel (`WizardPage.renderMatchingLive`) shows each note under the
job's sentence in the person's language (`RunPanelText.display`).

### 61.2 What runs after the validation on a business-object table (read in `configureOne`, not assumed)

The execution mode is written BEFORE the validation (`ensureExecutionMode`, skipped for a member table); the member inert policies (§59.3) are written before it too (`ensureMemberPolicies`,
after the writes of the main table in every branch). After the validation: `activate_business_object_matching` (`MameBusinessObjects.activate`, the object and every member must read
ENABLED + metadataset), `markApplied`, the preview-policy cleanup, the end-of-configure activation recheck, the related-table check (skipped for a business object), then the step message. None of
them reads the validate answer: with the fallback the configure reaches the activation exactly as when the object's validation answers.

### 61.3 Files, tests, limits

New: `ebx/MatchingValidation` (port, answer, outcome, note texts), `MatchingValidationTest` (the live thrown text; the fallback with the note; a tool-level error as a throw; both calls throw →
the table call's exception propagates; the fallback's `valid:false` handed back for today's refusal; a soft miss and a normal answer never fall back; a plain table makes one call; the English
of the note pinned to `Messages_en`, the French rendering; the job message without marker; the reader's extraction). Touched: `ebx/MatchingConfigurator` (the validate block; `validationNotes`
in the configure result; the step message), `ebx/MatchingConfigureRun` (`withNotes` with the notes), `ebx/MatchingActivityReader` (`validationNotes`), `matching/MatchingActivity` (`notes`,
JSON), `wizard/WizardPage` (the panel), the two bundles, `WizardMessagesTest`, `MatchingActivityTest`, `MatchingConfigureRunTest`. **No XSD change.** Not verified live: nothing was written on
the instance; the first configure of a business-object entity on 1.2.0-264+ is the test (expected: the step detail with `validateBusinessObject.thrown`, the note in the step-6 panel, the object
ENABLED). `wizard.js` repaints only the entity rows while the job is live; the notes are server-rendered when the page is rebuilt at the job's end.

## 62. Lot M8 — the member's merge policy carries the MODE of the main table's (branch `fix/member-merge-mode`, 2026-10-18)

Measured live 2026-10-18 02:57 (EBX 6.3.0-rc3 + Match and Merge RC3, Factory 1.2.0-267, project `E2EMASTER20261018005227`, DMA publication `E2EMASTER20261018005227_Master`,
business object main table `/root/Client`, member `/root/Adresse`): the configure went through (M4 + M6: the real policies on `Client`, the INERT matching and merge policies on
`Adresse`, the object ENABLED), and the matching RUN on `Client` was refused by the add-on — `PipelineStep 2311` (`MATCHING_RUN`, `FAILED`, 0.4 s): `matchRecords refused (invalid
parameter): The 'Run match' service cannot be executed. Please check if merge policies are configured for all related tables. Ensure the merge policies use the same 'Mode'.` Read back
with `get_matching_config` on both tables (`dataModel urn:ebx:publication:E2EMASTER20261018005227_Master`): `/root/Adresse` merge policy `Adresse`, `mode DISABLED`,
`autoCreateNewGoldenSource null`, identity survivors (what §59.2 wrote, `MERGE_MODE_PREFERRED`); `/root/Client` merge policy `Client`, `mode ONLY_DUPLICATES`,
`autoCreateNewGoldenSource "MDM"`. The add-on requires every member's merge policy to carry the SAME mode as the main table's; §59.4 had listed "that it accepts the merge mode `DISABLED`
on a member" among the things not verified — the add-on accepts the WRITE, and refuses the RUN.

### 62.1 What changes (`master/BusinessObjectMembers`, `ebx/MameBusinessObjects.ensureMemberPolicies`)

1. **The inert member merge policy takes the mode of the main table's merge policy, read, never a constant.** `BusinessObjectMembers.mainMergeMode(answer, mainTable)` reads it in the
   SAME `get_business_object_config` answer the configure already takes before writing the members (the main table is listed among the members with the full `MameConfig` shape, `mode`
   included): the merge policy whose code is the main table's entity name, else the first that is not a Simulate preview, else the first with a mode; null when the answer gives none.
   `memberMergeMode(mainMode, desiredMainMode)` then takes, in this order, the main table's stored mode, the mode of the policy the configure is writing on the main table
   (`desiredMergePolicy.path("mode")`, handed over by `MatchingConfigurator.configureOne`; the pre-run completion `ensureMembersBeforeRun` hands null), and the Factory's own default for a
   main table (`MERGE_MODE_DEFAULT = ONLY_DUPLICATES`, the same value as `MatchingPolicyTranslator.buildMergePolicy`'s `hints.path("mode").asText("ONLY_DUPLICATES")`). The step detail says
   which (`memberMergeMode`, `memberMergeModeSource`). `MERGE_MODE_PREFERRED` / `MERGE_MODE_FALLBACK` and the two-attempt loop are gone: there is no other mode the add-on would accept for a
   run of the object, so a refusal of `generate_merge_policy` is a failure, named with the mode.
2. **A member that already holds a merge policy in another mode is aligned, nothing else of it is touched** (`Writes.alignMergeModes`: the codes of the member's merge policies whose mode is
   known and differs; a policy whose mode the answer does not give is never aligned — unknown is not different). One `patch_matching_config` per member, one op `set_merge_mode` per policy
   (`matching_config_schema` → `patchOps`: `requiredTargetKeys [policyCode]`, value "an auto-create-new-golden mode name", a JSON STRING like every patch value), `businessObject` set, before
   `set_merge_policy_link`. The member's entry in `memberPolicies[]` carries `alignMergeMode` (arguments and answer) and `alignMergeModeCodes`; the detail carries the list
   `memberMergeModeAligned` (`/root/Adresse: merge policy Adresse DISABLED -> ONLY_DUPLICATES`); the configure message's sentence says `the mode of its merge policy Adresse (was DISABLED)
   set to ONLY_DUPLICATES, the mode of Client's merge policy (the add-on refuses a run of the object while a member's merge policy is in another mode)`. The re-read after the writes compares
   the modes too (`stillMissingRefusal` names "merge policy Adresse in mode DISABLED where /root/Client is in mode ONLY_DUPLICATES"). Idempotent: a member in the main table's mode needs
   nothing. **The pre-run completion covers the projects configured by lots M4–M7** (`E2EMASTER20261018005227` among them): their next run aligns `Adresse` and activates the object again;
   no new configure is needed.
3. **The e2e scenario checks it** (`tools/e2e/b2c_master.py check_members`: "every member merge policy carries the mode of the main table's merge policy"; stand-in defect `mm_membermode`;
   the stand-in's `get_business_object_config` now gives a `mode` on every merge policy).

### 62.2 The consequence: `ONLY_DUPLICATES` on a member that never matches

With `ONLY_DUPLICATES` on a business-object table the add-on "merges" every SINGLETON in place during a run of the object (`DeduplicationServiceImpl.mergesSingletons`: "business object
and ONLY_DUPLICATES", CLAUDE.md §8 trap (4), measured 2026-10-17 on the main table where a `constant` survivor on `/sourceSystem` overwrote the source of all 534 records — lot M1, §56).
The member's inert tree (`exact` on `/id` → `SUSPECTED`, else `NOT_MATCHED`) never groups two records, so every member row is a singleton, and the merge engine applies the member's merge
policy to each of them at every run of the object. With the inert policy as written — record selection `mostCompleted` over one record, default field chain `longest` over one record,
survivors `no merge` on `/sourceSystem`, `/sourceId`, `/_loadId` and `max` on `/_receivedAt`, **no `constant`, no `autoCreateNewGoldenSource`** — every function answers the record's own
value: nothing changes in the member table. The policy must stay that way: a `constant` survivor would overwrite that field on every member row at every run, and a golden source would
stamp them. `BusinessObjectMembersTest.theInertMergePolicyIsIdentity` and `theMemberMergeModeIsTheMainTables` pin both absences. What the engine WRITES while "merging" a singleton in place
(an `update_time` on the record, metadataset rows) is not measured on a member: the main table's run of 2026-10-17 moved `update_time` on all 534 records; a member's rows may show the same.
If the main table's mode were `DUPLICATES_AND_SINGLETONS` (not the Factory's default, §56: kept `ONLY_DUPLICATES`), the member in the same mode would get an auto-created golden per
member row — a copy of every member record; that is the §59.4 observation on project `...212914` (ids 301-600) and the reason the mode is read, not chosen: the member follows the main
table, whatever that costs, because the add-on leaves no other way to run the object.

### 62.3 Files, tests, limits

Touched: `master/BusinessObjectMembers` (`Member.mergeModes`, `mainMergeMode`, `memberMergeMode`, `MERGE_MODE_DEFAULT`, `Writes.alignMergeModes` / `mergeMode`, `writesFor(member, mode)`,
`membersToWrite(members, mode)`, `writtenSentence(entity, parent, writes, modesBefore)`, `stillMissingRefusal(main, members, mode)`), `ebx/MameBusinessObjects` (`ensureMemberPolicies(…,
desiredMainMode, detail)`: the mode read, one `generate_merge_policy`, the `set_merge_mode` patch, the detail entries), `ebx/MatchingConfigurator` (hands `desiredMergePolicy`'s mode over;
`putStrings` opened to the package), `tools/e2e/b2c_master.py`, `b2c_standin.py`, `b2c_master_selftest.py`. No XSD change, no message bundle change (the sentences are the English of the
configure job, as in lot M4). Tests: `BusinessObjectMembersTest` (the live answer of 02:57 as a fixture: the mode read, the one alignment write, idempotence in the main table's mode, an
unknown mode never aligned, the wording, the refusal), `BusinessObjectMembersSourceTest` (the mode read before any member write, one generate in that mode, the patch op and its place, the
detail entries, both callers), `MatchingConfigureRunTest` (signatures), the e2e self-test (`mm_membermode`). Not verified live: nothing was written on the instance; the first run of
`E2EMASTER20261018005227` (or the first configure of a business-object entity) on 1.2.0-268+ is the test — expected: `memberPoliciesWritten` with the alignment sentence in the run's step
detail, `get_matching_config /root/Adresse` reading `mode ONLY_DUPLICATES`, the run accepted by the add-on, and the member rows unchanged (compare a `get_record` of an `Adresse` row
before and after). Whether `set_merge_mode` is accepted on a member table with `businessObject` (the other patch ops are, §59) and whether the add-on then wants the member's
`autoCreateNewGoldenSource` too (the main table's is `MDM`; the message names only the mode) are the two open points.
## 63. Lot M9 — the model's variance must not leave an entity without a plan: structural refusals get a third chance, and the Factory proposes a fallback plan from the measured facts (branch `fix/matching-plan-fallback`, 2026-10-18)

Measured live 2026-10-18 02:59-03:04 (Factory 1.2.0-267, project `E2EMASTER20261018005904`, `AgentRun` 497, phase `MATCHING_SUGGEST_LLM`, its `AgentStep` rows read over Data Services):
the person entity `Client` ended with NO plan after five refused `propose_match_plan` calls - (1) child evidence required; (2) `fullNameKey` not near-unique for a MATCH-terminal node, with the
SAFE pairs named (`fullNameKey + firstName` 694/694, `fullNameKey + lastName` 694/694, `mobileE164 + fullNameKey` 565/565, `emailKey + fullNameKey` 341/341 - M5's wording works); (3) the `addressKeys`
ceiling; (4) and (5) `the proposed decision tree is not valid: UNKNOWN_BRANCH_TARGET: node 'N5'.onFalse = 'N7' is neither a leaf nor a known node id.` - a 12-node tree (N0-N6, N8-N11) whose
N5.onFalse named a node the model never defined, twice in a row; the second identical text tripped M5's breaker ("the same refusal came back 2 times in a row") and the entity was recorded refused.
The model then wrote the `Achat` and `PointVente` plans and ended `DONE` (7 steps, 170,766 input tokens). In the previous run (project `E2EMASTER20261018005227`, same build, same model) the same
entity got a valid 18-leaf plan at the first attempts: the failure is variance of the model, and without a plan on the person entity nothing of the master phase can be measured.

### 63.1 The refusal names the ids and the two fixes; a structural refusal gets one more chance

- `DecisionTreePlan.validateBranch` now says: `UNKNOWN_BRANCH_TARGET: node 'N5'.onFalse = 'N7' is neither a leaf nor a known node id (the tree defines N0, N1, ... and N11; the leaves are MATCH,
  SUSPECTED, NOT_MATCHED). Two fixes: define node 'N7' in nodes[], or point N5.onFalse to a leaf (SUSPECTED or NOT_MATCHED).` (an `onTrue` branch lists `MATCH, SUSPECTED or NOT_MATCHED`). Every
  caller of `validate` gets the text (the review screens, the rule pass, the translator).
- **Two classes of refusal** (`MatchPlanLlmPass.Session.isStructuralRefusal`): STRUCTURAL = the shape of the tree itself - every reason of `DecisionTreePlan.validate`, which the pass prefixes with
  `the proposed decision tree is not valid: ` (`UNKNOWN_BRANCH_TARGET`, `CYCLE_DETECTED`, a `NODE_SHARED` the cloner of M5 could not copy, `UNREACHABLE_NODE`, `MISSING_BRANCH`, `ROOT_NOT_FOUND`...),
  a duplicated node id, a node without both branches, a missing root; CONTENT = everything else (a field, an algorithm, a threshold, a challenge). The same structural refusal ends the entity on its
  **third** time in a row (`SAME_STRUCTURAL_REFUSAL_IN_A_ROW` = 3), a content refusal on its second (`SAME_REFUSAL_IN_A_ROW` = 2, unchanged); "three times in the run" and the cap on proposals apply
  to both. Reasoning: a slip of the tree's shape is corrected by a model that reads a refusal naming the ids; a field refused twice says the model does not understand the rule. The signature
  (`refusalSignature`, node ids taken out) is unchanged. The system prompt says it ("A refusal of the tree's own shape ... is tolerated three times in a row instead of two").

### 63.2 The Factory's fallback plan (`master.MatchPlanFallback`, `Session.proposeFallbacks()`)

After the model's run (`MatchPlanLlmSuggester`, whole-project pass only - "Propose another" on one entity is an explicit ask for the MODEL's plan and keeps today's revert path), every entity the
model **proposed for, was refused on, and left without an accepted plan** - whoever ended it: the breaker, the cap, a skip after refusals, or the run's budget (`endedBy` empty) - gets the Factory's
own proposal, built from its measured key facts (`KeyFacts`, lot M3) and **run through `proposeMatchPlan` exactly like a model proposal**: every guard (MATCH-terminal justification, null handling,
child-keys ceiling, cross-system guard with the live lookups, candidate filter, shape checks). The one-shot challenges (relation evidence, relation/identifier roles, reach) are marked as already
made - they ask the model to improve and accept the resubmission whatever it is; the Factory's proposal is that resubmission (a reach finding still lands in the rationale as "Reach: ..."). An
entity never proposed for, or skipped by the model without a refusal, gets no fallback (the model's opinion stands). A child entity gets none (it follows its parent, lot M2).

The shape, from the facts alone (`MatchPlanFallback.build`), never from a name:

1. **root**: an `ALL_FIELDS` node on the **strongest SAFE pair** of independent keys, exact at 100, nulls NOT_MATCH, `onTrue` MATCH - the one node M3 accepts as a MATCH on a measured justification.
   "Strongest" = the most comparable pairs (the Factory's own order, `MeasuredMatchPath.safePairs`), among the keys that may stand in a node at all; ties go to the pair whose weaker key is the more
   selective (distinct values among filled records);
2. then **one `ALL_FIELDS` node per near-unique exact key, alone** → SUSPECTED, most selective first. A key qualifies (`eligibleKeys`) when it is an attribute of the entity that is not a reference, not
   a per-source record key, not a child-keys attribute, not the source of another measured key (`base`), with no measured format conflict between source systems (the pass would refuse the exact
   comparison), shared by at least one pair, at least two distinct values, **at most 2 pairs per filled record** (`MAX_PAIRS_PER_FILLED_RECORD`: the name key of the B2C scenario, 694 pairs for 534
   records, passes; the first name, 5,660 pairs, is a grouping, not an identity) - and, when the facts mark any pair SAFE, a key whose sharing predicts another key (the `key` side of a SAFE
   agreement: the data shows it carries identity; a name key alone, 129 namesakes of 694 pairs, does not - **refined in §64.4 (lot M10a)**: the other key of that agreement must itself be selective, else the name key passed on the real facts of run 7 through its agreement with the first name). The root pair asks for the basic conditions only: its weaker key is justified by the pair;
3. then, when the entity has a derived child-keys attribute (lot M8a), an `ALL_FIELDS` node on it with `exactFullText` at the ceiling the pass computes (`childKeysScoreCeiling(maxChildrenPerParent)`,
   at most 50) → SUSPECTED;
4. NOT_MATCHED for everything else. Node ids `F1..Fn`, no `clusteringFields` (the translator declares every tree field in the policy anyway, and the pre-clustering dominance is applied from the
   tree), confidence **40**, status PROPOSED, origin **RULE**, `requirements.fallback = {afterRefusedProposals, lastRefusal (400 characters), endedBy}`. The rationale: "Factory fallback plan, not a
   proposal of the language model: the model made N proposal(s) for 'X' and none was accepted (last refusal: "..."). Built from the measured key facts alone, by the rules the Factory applies to every
   plan: records that share both K and J are the same record (SAFE pair: ...) - MATCH; then records that share one exact key alone (...) are shown to a steward - SUSPECTED; ...; anything else is
   NOT_MATCHED. Every path starts with an exact key of the record, so the candidate search is filtered. Confidence 40: a starting point for a person to review, not a recommendation. Asking for
   another proposal replaces it with the model's plan." - followed by what the pass itself appends (the measured MATCH justification, reach, evidence).

Computed on the B2C fixture of lot M3 (`b2c_person_keys.tsv`, which reproduces the two SAFE pairs run 497's refusal quoted: `mobileE164 + fullNameKey` 565/565, `emailKey + fullNameKey` 341/341;
the live facts of run 497 also held `firstName`/`lastName`, coarse, and `mobile`, whose shapes differ per system) the tree for `Client` is, and passes the pass's checks (`MatchPlanFallbackTest`):
`F1 ALL_FIELDS [mobileE164, fullNameKey] exact 100 → MATCH / F2; F2 ALL_FIELDS [emailKey] → SUSPECTED / F3; F3 ALL_FIELDS [mobileE164] → SUSPECTED / F4; F4 ALL_FIELDS [addressKeys] exactFullText
50 → SUSPECTED / NOT_MATCHED`. The name key alone gets no node (not SAFE as a key: namesakes), nor the birth date (two people born the same day: `birthDate → emailKey` has conflicts), nor the
first/last names (coarse). By M3's analysis this plan finds every pair that shares the phone or the e-mail (565 + the e-mail-only pairs), 0 false merge on the pair; the steward sees the rest.

What is recorded: the step detail gets `fallback{entity: {proposed, reason, attempts, lastRefusal, endedBy}}`, the notes a line per entity ("Client: the Factory proposed its fallback plan, built
from the measured key facts, after 5 refused proposal(s) of the model (MATCH on ...; SUSPECTED on ...)" / "Client: no Factory fallback plan - <reason>"), and when the fallback is refused too,
`attempts{entity}.fallback` holds the refusal next to the model's last one. `MatchPlanLlmSuggester.write` stores the plan with `CreatedPlan.origin` (RULE), everything else as a model plan.

### 63.3 What the person sees

- The step-6 card: badge **"Factory fallback plan"** / **"plan de repli de la fabrique"** (`wizard.step6.origin.RULE_FALLBACK`, chosen when `requirements.fallback` exists, whatever the origin) and a
  note under the header (`wizard.step6.fallback.note`: how many proposals, that the plan comes from the measured facts, that asking for another proposal replaces it, the last refusal). "Propose
  another" works as for any PROPOSED plan: the model's plan replaces it (the fallback goes SUPERSEDED, kept as `previousRequirements`).
- The job message (`MatchingSuggestLlmRun`): the fallback is counted among the plans written and named with why (`MatchingPlanCoverage.withFallbacks`, `wizard.matching.fallback.sentence`: "Client: the
  language model made 5 proposal(s) and none was accepted; the Factory proposed its fallback plan, built from the measured key facts, to review (last refusal: ...)."). Such an entity HAS a plan: it
  is never a gap. An entity whose fallback was refused too stays a gap, and its reason (`reasonText`) ends with "The Factory's fallback plan was refused too: ..." (`wizard.matching.gap.reason.fallbackRefused`).
- `MatchingPlanCoverage.rulesRan` ignores a fallback plan (origin RULE, but it comes from the language-model pass).

### 63.4 Files, tests, limits

New: `master/MatchPlanFallback`, `MatchPlanFallbackTest` (the refusal wording for both branches; the breaker: a structural refusal ends on the third time, a content one on the second, the classes; the
