## 64. Lot M10a — a path to SUSPECTED must identify a record: 16 namesake pairs in run 7, 274 in the simulate-first variant (branch `fix/matching-pair-precision`, 2026-10-18)

Measured on the 7th live run of the B2C master scenario (Factory 1.2.0-271, `tools/e2e/b2c_master.sh`, ground truth `truth_b2c.json` from `tools/e2e/gen_b2c.py`; 534 records of 212 people, 565 true
pairs). Plain variant, project `E2EMASTER20261018014728`, `/root/Personne`, MatchPlan 74 (origin LLM, confidence 80, 35 leaves: 3 MATCH turned into SUSPECTED because automatic merge is off, 24
SUSPECTED, 8 NOT_MATCHED): `Master_Personne_MDS` holds 542 `Suspected` rows, the clusters they form hold 581 pairs, 565 right and **16 two different people** (precision 0.972, recall 1.000). Simulate-first
variant, project `E2EMASTER20261018015240`, `/root/Client`, MatchPlan 75 (confidence 56, no name key staged that run): 768 rows, 839 pairs, **274 false** (precision 0.673, recall 1.000), 30 clusters
mixing 2 to 4 people. Everything below was read (Data Services `GET`, `tools/matching/pair_audit.py`), nothing was written on the instance.

### 64.1 The false pairs of run 7, characterised

Three clusters, 15 suspect edges, 16 pairs. In each, two people with the SAME NAME living in the SAME CITY (the generator draws 220 people from 28 first names, 27 last names and 10 cities):

| cluster | person A (records) | person B (records) | false pairs | they share | they differ on |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Nathan Martin, Rennes: 11 (ECOM 111, LOYALTY 265) | Nathan Martin, Rennes: 126 (ECOM 151, STORES 403, 455) | 6 (5 suspect edges) | name key, first name, last name (case aside), postal code | e-mail key, phone, birth date, street, address keys |
| 2 | Chloé Robert, Montpellier: 50 (ECOM 90, LOYALTY 258, STORES 423, 443) | Chloé Robert, Montpellier: 8 (ECOM 153) | 4 (4 edges) | the same | the same |
| 3 | Thomas Morel, Paris 11e: 18 (LOYALTY 296, STORES 335, 349) | Thomas Morel, Paris 11e: 113 (ECOM 69, LOYALTY 192) | 6 (6 edges) | the same | the same |

Characterisation (all 15 edges, counted on the stored records): same normalised full name (`nomCompletKey` 15 of 15), same first name, same last name, same postal code of the one address (15 of 15) - and
**nothing else**: the E.164 phones differ on all 15; the e-mail keys differ on the 10 edges where both records have one (the other 5 involve a store ticket without e-mail); the birth dates, the address
keys and the streets differ on the 6 edges between two ECOM / LOYALTY records and are missing on the 9 that involve a ticket (a store ticket carries a postal code and no street, no birth date). Not "postal
code only", not "surname + birth date": name AND postal code. Every one of the 565 true pairs of the scenario shares the phone; the plan's
phone/e-mail paths found all of them (527 edges, `N1` MATCH turned SUSPECTED) - the 15 edges below added nothing but the false pairs.

**Which node.** Replaying the stored tree on the 542 suspect edges (`pair_audit.py --plan 74`, Jaro-Winkler for the names, the plan's own thresholds) gives: 527 edges last pass `N1` (phone + name key,
true), **15 last pass `N9`, all false**. `N9` is `postalCode` of the related `Adresse`, exact 100 → SUSPECTED, reached by `C0` (name key, exact) > `N1` ✗ > `N4` ✗ (e-mail) > `N5` ✗ (phone) > `N6` ✗
(address keys) > `N7` ✓ (AVERAGE of `nom` + `prenom`, Jaro-Winkler ≥ 85 - trivially 100 when the name key is equal) > `N8` ✗ (street) > `N9` ✓. The rationale of the plan is honest about it ("postal code is
coarse and review-only"): the path was meant as a weak tie-breaker. Measured, it is a pair generator: the postal code takes 10 values over 534 rows (53 rows per value), so "same name + same postal code"
holds for every pair of namesakes of a city. The copy `N30` of the same path (the shared node `N4` was copied three times by lot M5's cloner) is on the branch "no key shared" and was not reached live because
the candidate search proposes pairs through a shared key; a replay over ALL pairs of the table (not only the live edges; scratch script) finds 97 false pairs through it.

### 64.2 The same defect, worse, in plan 75

The replay of plan 75 (`N6` exact first name, `N10` AVERAGE of `firstName` + `lastName` ≥ 85 → SUSPECTED) on its 768 edges: **234 false edges through `N10`**, 4 through `N11` (first name, names not similar,
same street string), 218 true through `N3` (phone), 312 true through `N1` (phone + e-mail). The 234 share the first AND last name (the first name is an exact gate, the similar-names node adds nothing the
gate does not already say) and differ on e-mail, phone, birth date: namesakes again, now across cities (the postal code is not even asked). The 4 `N11` edges are two people (Gabriel Fournier, Bordeaux;
Gabriel Vincent, Montpellier) whose single address reads the same street and number in two cities - a partial address; see 64.6.

### 64.3 The rule (`master/PathEvidenceRule`, `matching/KeyFacts`)

Structural and measured, no field name looked at. **Every path from the root to a positive leaf (MATCH or SUSPECTED) must pass, through the `onTrue` edge of an `ALL_FIELDS` node, at least one
exact condition that identifies a record.** A condition identifies a record when:

1. the field is a key of the entity's `KeyFacts` that is **predictive** (`KeyFacts.predictive`, new): complete facts (never a sample), the key is **selective** (its records share at most
   `MAX_PAIRS_PER_FILLED_RECORD` = 2 pairs each on average - the constant the fallback of lot M9 already used, moved to `KeyFacts`), and among the pairs of records that share it at least
   **90 %** (`MIN_PREDICTIVE_RATE`) of those where another **selective** key of another base is filled on both sides share that key too, over at least 10 comparable pairs. Run 7: `emailKey`
   100 %, `telephoneE164` / `telephone` 100 %, `addressKeys` 94.5 % (6 namesakes at one address), `dateNaissance` 98 %; **`nomCompletKey` 68-81 %** (79 % with `emailKey`, 81 % with `telephoneE164`: 129 of its 694 pairs are namesakes), `prenom` / `nom`
   not selective (5,660 / 2,914 pairs for 534 records). The partner must itself be selective: the name key agrees 694 of 694 with the FIRST NAME, a component of itself, which is why lot M9's
   "the key side of a SAFE agreement" let the name key through (below);
2. or it is **not among the measured keys** and, on its own profile, each distinct value is carried by at most **5** rows on average among the filled rows (`PathEvidenceRule.MAX_ROWS_PER_VALUE`;
   `AttributeInfo.rowsPerDistinctValue`, child rows estimated as parents × average per parent): `street` of the related address 1.6, `postalCode` 53.4, a city 48.5; an attribute or a related field alike (`via`);
3. or nothing is known (no reliable profile): the benefit of the doubt - the rule refuses what the data shows to be coarse, nothing else.

A condition counts only if the algorithm is `exact`, or `exactFullText` at `minimumScore` 50 or more, `bothNull` and `oneNull` are `NOT_MATCH` (a missing value must not satisfy it - the reading of
`CandidateFilterCheck`) and `minimumScore` is above 0. A similarity node (AVERAGE, AT_LEAST_N, Jaro-Winkler) never counts: a score over several fields can be reached without any one of them; it may
**refine** a path that already requires an identifying condition. The rule is **inactive** (the old behaviour) when the entity has no complete key facts, when none of its keys is predictive (nothing
could satisfy it), and when the tree has more than `CrossSystemPathRule.MAX_PATHS` positive paths.

Why this and not a threshold on the score or a SAFE bar for SUSPECTED: the 15 edges score 100 on every field the path asks for (names equal, postal code equal) - a minimum score cannot tell them apart;
SAFE (99 %, no conflict) is the bar for a certain MATCH and would also refuse the address-key path (94.5 %), which the data supports as a SUSPECTED. The 90 % bar sits between the address keys (94.5 %) and the
name key (81 %); it is a judgment, written as a constant (`KeyFacts.MIN_PREDICTIVE_RATE`) and the first number to revisit if a scenario disagrees. **Recall**: a path that requires a predictive key or a
precise field is untouched; the rule only removes paths whose every condition is shared by many unrelated records, and the data says what such a path finds: nothing a predictive key does not.

### 64.4 Where it runs

- `MatchPlanLlmPass.Session.proposeMatchPlan`, after the shape, candidate-filter and reach checks (a plan is told its structure and its filter first, its evidence last). A content refusal, so the breaker
  of lot M5 ends the entity on its second identical one and the fallback plan takes over. The text names the paths (`path C0 > N1 > ... > N9 (requires nomCompletKey exact, nom average jarowinkler, prenom average
  jarowinkler, postalCode of Adresse exact -> SUSPECTED)`), each coarse condition with its own numbers (`nomCompletKey: among the 694 pair(s) of records that share it, 79% share emailKey, 81% share
  telephoneE164 ... below 90%`; `postalCode of Adresse: each value is shared by 53.4 rows on average (10 distinct values) - a grouping, not an identity`), the identifying keys of the entity and three fixes:
  require an exact condition on one of those keys on the path; require an exact condition on a precise field; or point the `onTrue` of the named node(s) to NOT_MATCHED.
- The **system prompt** gets one paragraph ("EVERY PATH NEEDS A CONDITION THAT IDENTIFIES A RECORD", no column name) and each entity's block a line `Identifying keys on <entity>: ...` (`PathEvidenceRule.promptLine`),
  so the first proposal already ends no path on names and a postal code. Nothing is said when the rule is inactive.
- **The fallback plan of lot M9** (`MatchPlanFallback`): the SUSPECTED nodes now require `KeyFacts.safelyPredictive` (selective key, one SAFE agreement with another selective key) where the facts offer
  one, `predictive` where they offer only that, no restriction where no key predicts anything; a child-keys node is dropped when its key is measured and not predictive, and the refusal of "no usable key"
  says so. On the stored facts of run 7 the old definition produced `nomCompletKey` alone → SUSPECTED (129 namesake pairs; recomputed from the stored facts); the new one produces F1 `telephoneE164` +
  `nomCompletKey` → MATCH, F2 `emailKey` → SUSPECTED, F3 `telephoneE164` → SUSPECTED, F4 `addressKeys` (exactFullText 50) → SUSPECTED, and the tree goes through the same check as any model plan.

### 64.5 Expected effect, by replay on the two live runs

`python3 tools/matching/pair_audit.py ... --plan N --rule` replays the stored tree on the edges the add-on produced and drops the edges whose path the rule refuses (Python mirror of the Java rule; the
Java rule gives the same refused paths in `PathEvidenceRuleTest`):

| | edges | pairs found | false pairs | precision | recall |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| run 7, plan 74, before | 542 | 581 | 16 | 0.972 | 1.000 |
| run 7, after (path `N9` refused, and its copy `N30`) | 527 | 565 | 0 | 1.000 | 1.000 |
| run 8, plan 75, before | 768 | 839 | 274 | 0.673 | 1.000 |
| run 8, after (path `N10` refused) | 534 | 575 | 10 | 0.983 | 1.000 |

No true edge is dropped in either run (the dropped ones are 15 and 234, all two people). Of the 27 positive paths of plan 74 the rule refuses 2; of the 8 of plan 75, 1. It is a replay on the suspects those
plans produced: a plan the model builds under the rule will differ, and the candidate search may propose other pairs.

### 64.6 Files, tests, limits

New: `master/PathEvidenceRule`, `tools/matching/pair_audit.py` (read-only audit; credentials from `EBX_USER` / `EBX_PASSWORD`, never a file), test resources `run7_keyfacts.json`, `run7_tree.json`, `run8_keyfacts.json`,
`run8_tree.json` (the key facts and decision trees the Factory stored for plans 74 and 75: counts only). Touched: `matching/KeyFacts` (`MAX_PAIRS_PER_FILLED_RECORD`, `MIN_PREDICTIVE_RATE`, `selective`, `predictiveAgreement`,
`predictive`, `safelyPredictive`, `predictiveKeys`), `master/MatchPlanLlmPass` (the check, the prompt paragraph and line, `AttributeInfo.rowsPerDistinctValue`), `master/MatchPlanFallback`. Tests:
`PathEvidenceRuleTest` (both stored plans replayed: only the offending paths are refused, their copies included; the refusal text; the fixes; inactive without facts / on a sample / without a predictive key; fuzzy, AVERAGE,
exactFullText below 50 and missing-value handling identify nothing; unmeasured = benefit of the doubt; the street identifies and the postal code does not), `MatchPlanLlmPassPathEvidenceTest` (the pass refuses run 7's path, accepts a
street, ends the entity on the second identical refusal and accepts the fallback; without facts nothing changes; the prompt), `MatchPlanFallbackTest` (the facts of run 7 never put the name key alone; the tree passes the rule),
and two fixtures adjusted: `MatchPlanLlmPassKeyFactsTest` (its plan ended a path on the name key alone → the phone alone) and `MatchPlanLlmPassLoopTest` (the unfiltered-plan test now uses facts on which no key identifies a record,
so it stays a test of the filter). **No XSD change, no bundle change** (the refusal is an English sentence the model reads, like every other; the plan card does not show a finding for plans stored before the lot).

Limits, stated: (1) **residual 10 pairs in run 8** (4 edges through `N11`): the street is measured precise (1.6 rows per value) yet two people share "31 rue de la République" in two cities; a precise field is
judged alone, not as the part of an address it is - a rule on a related record's fields taken together would need the child's composite key. (2) The three numbers (2 pairs per record, 90 %, 5 rows per value) are
judgments on one scenario; the first two are the Factory's own existing constants or sit between measured values (94.5 % / 81 %). (3) A genuinely good "name + street" or "fuzzy name + exact date" path stays accepted only
when the street / the date is identifying by these measures; on an entity whose only predictive keys are absent (rule inactive) nothing changes. (4) The rule judges the stored facts of the entity, counted once at proposal
time; a table that grows into more namesakes keeps the plan until someone asks for another proposal. (5) **Not verified live**: nothing ran against the instance; how the model reacts to the refusal (the replay and the
Session tests use scripted proposals), and that the add-on's candidate search proposes the same pairs under a corrected plan.

## 65. Lot M12 - the group card's leftovers (branch `fix/group-card-leftovers`, 2026-10-18)

Measured on step 6 of `E2EMASTER20261018065557` (142 goldens, 180 suspect pairs, 77 groups), four defects of the group card of lot M10d:

1. **"Why these records: rule Suspect" on every card.** `executeDecisionTree().getDecisionNodes()` walks the plan's nodes and ends on the verdict's own leaf ("Suspect", the node flagged `isLastNode`); the builder stored that leaf. `matching/DecidingNode.pick` now takes the last walked name that is a node of the plan (`Spec.planNodeNames`, from `MatchPlanFacts.nodes`, which also names a repeated node `"<name> (<id>)"` as `DecisionTreePlan.freezeAndDisambiguateLabels` writes it), else the node before the leaf. The card words it from the plan ("same value on E-mail and Phone (rule N1)"); a leaf name, an unknown name or no evaluation gives "reason not available". A snapshot stored before this keeps "Suspect" and shows the same sentence. Not observed live: the exact content of `getDecisionNodes()` (leaf included or not) - both shapes are handled, the live check is the first run after the install.
2. **The opaque child-keys row and the missing address.** An attribute with derivation `CHILD_KEYS` (`PairRows.Attr.technical`) is never a row. The child summary never appeared because `childSummaries` filtered the master child table on `client`, the source's plain key (null in the master); the foreign key built by `MasterModel` is `clientRef` (`PairRows.foreignKeyFieldCandidates`, checked against the table's schema). A derived key that differs from its raw value only by case/accents/punctuation (the folded e-mail) shows the raw value first and the key under it, lighter.
3. **The run line stayed English.** The step keeps the engine's English (`.raw`); the job of the same run holds it with the codes. `MatchingActivityReader.codedMessage` takes the job's coded text when it is the same sentence, `WizardPage` words it (and an entity step message) through `RunPanelText`, and `GET .../matching/activity?lang=` words the polled answer.
4. **Golden column**: first column, header "Golden - MDM" with the source id smaller, tinted (`mdmf-match-col-golden`).

Tests: `GroupCardTest` (deciding node, technical key, child row and foreign key, golden first, raw first), `RunPanelTextTest.matchingRunLine`, `WizardPageMatchingStepTest.theRunLineIsWordedInThePersonsLanguage`. Not run against the instance (nothing installed).


## 66. Lot M13 - the model is guided with the entity's own facts, a MATCH is judged on its whole path, and every violation is told at once (branch `feat/matching-guidance`, 2026-10-18)

Measured on the 9th live run of the B2C master scenario (Factory 1.2.0-283, project `E2EMASTER20261018073824`, `AgentRun` 542, entity `Client`; the six `AgentStep` rows of the proposals read over Data Services, nothing written):
the model made six `propose_match_plan` calls, all refused, **each on a different rule** - (1) child evidence required, (2) the child-keys threshold above 50, (3) `birthDate` entirely empty for `STORES` as an exact/clustering field,
(4) a candidate search not filtered, (5) and (6) "`emailKey` ... cannot terminate a MATCH-terminal node on its own. Pair it with ... `mobileE164` ...". The model fixed each refusal faithfully; one rule was learned per turn. Proposals 5 and 6 were
RIGHT: `G1 ALL_FIELDS [mobileE164 exact] onTrue G2; G2 ALL_FIELDS [emailKey exact] onTrue MATCH` requires BOTH keys of the SAFE pair (341 of 341 comparable pairs) to reach the MATCH - exactly what the refusal recommended - and the
rule looked at the terminal node's own fields only. The second identical text tripped the breaker of lot M5, and the Factory's fallback (lot M9) took over: a false refusal ended the entity.

### 66.1 A. Rules that judge a path judge the CONJUNCTION of the exact conditions met along it

The conditions a pair must have met to reach a leaf are those of the `ALL_FIELDS` nodes the path crosses through their `onTrue` edge (`CrossSystemPathRule.PositivePath#passedNodes`); a node left through `onFalse` says nothing about the pair.
Of the rules that judge what a path requires, two already worked that way (read on the code, pinned by the tests below): the candidate filter (`CandidateFilterCheck`: "the fields of the nodes the path PASSES") with the reach challenge built on its key set, and the identifying condition of lot M10a
(`PathEvidenceRule.conditionsOf` over `passedNodes`). One did not and is fixed; the shape checks of the child evidence are kept on purpose:

- **The MATCH-terminal rule** (`MeasuredMatchPath`, `MatchPlanLlmPass.Session#matchTerminalViolations`). Before: each field of a node whose `onTrue` is MATCH had to be an identifier by itself (not a matching key, filled, near-unique, repeating) unless TWO fields of THAT SAME node formed
  a SAFE pair. Now: such a node needs no identifier of its own when the keys held by it and by the `ALL_FIELDS` nodes above it through `onTrue` (`requiredNodes`, `pathKeyNames`) contain a SAFE pair (`pathJustification`). An ancestor counts only when its field is a plain attribute (not read
  through a child, not a parent reference), compared with the exact algorithm at 100 and `NOT_MATCH` on both null handlings (a missing value would otherwise pass it: the pair would not need that key at all); an ancestor left through `onFalse` counts for nothing. The node's own fields count as before
  (the node is already required to be exact at 100). A node that is not `ALL_FIELDS`, whose `onFalse` is MATCH, or whose path holds no SAFE pair keeps the old rule, field by field. The single-node MATCH on a derived key is refused as before (`emailKey` alone: still "cannot terminate a MATCH-terminal node
  on its own"), and the refusal now says what THIS path requires ("The path to the MATCH of node 'N1' requires emailKey; keys count together when they sit on the SAME path - an ALL_FIELDS node on each ... chained through onTrue, or both in one node - and a pair needs two independent keys"), only when the facts are
  complete. The stored rationale names the path ("MATCH path G1 > G2 (mobileE164 + emailKey) is justified by the measured data: 341 pair(s) of records share ..."). A field that no SAFE pair could rescue is still refused while its node is built, before the cross-system lookups (no query is spent on it, as before);
  only the fields of SAFE pairs wait for the tree. The shape checks of the child-evidence and parent-confirmation nodes (`checkParentConfirmationNodeShape`, `checkRelationMatchNodeShape`) keep their rule "the node DIRECTLY above must compare an identity field of the record" - tried on the conjunction and put back: an existing test of the relation lot
  (`relationMatchNode_refusedWhenNodeAboveHasNoOwnIdentityField`) pins a chain "identity node > relation-only node > relation MATCH node" as refused on purpose. The child-evidence presence rule is a one-shot challenge on the tree as a whole, not a path rule.
- Test on the exact tree of run 542 (`MatchPlanLlmPassGuidanceTest`, the proposal read from `AgentStep` 10, stored as `src/test/resources/.../master/run542_step10_client_proposal.json`): **G1 and G2 (and G3 to G8) as the model wrote them are accepted** (first answer the child-evidence challenge, alone; the resubmission passes, the
  two MATCH paths G1 > G2 and G3 > G4 justified in the rationale). The whole 15-node tree is NOT accepted, and was not going to be even without the MATCH rule: the Factory copies a node reached from several branches with its whole subtree (the add-on's tree has one parent per node, lot M5) and the 15 nodes became
  **74, against the cap of 64** (`TOO_MANY_NODES`) - G3, G5, G12 and G15 are each reached from two or more branches; the path G12.onFalse > G15 (child evidence alone) would then have been refused as unfiltered. The refusal now says why ("Your proposal had 15 node(s); the Factory copied N node(s) that several branches lead to,
  each with its WHOLE subtree ... Reach each node from ONE branch only") and the system prompt says it up front.

### 66.2 B. Every violation of a proposal in ONE answer

`Session#proposeMatchPlan` no longer ends at the first refusal. While a proposal is judged (`collecting`), `refuse()` records the message and the check goes on (`judgeProposal`); the call ends with ONE answer (`combineViolations`): a single violation is told exactly as before, several are numbered -
"this proposal has N problems, all reported at once - fix every one of them in the next proposal, not one at a time: (1) ... (2) ..." - each text carrying its own fix. What is collected: every node's checks (a field that draws a violation stays in its node as the model wrote it, `appendBestEffortField`, so the tree can still be assembled and judged as a whole), the node-shape
checks (id, function, branches, AVERAGE score, `minimumMatches`), the structural validation (`DecisionTreePlan.validate`), the parent-confirmation, relation-MATCH and child-confirmation shapes, the MATCH-terminal rule, the per-path cross-system rule for fields empty in a system, `relationClusteringWeights`, every clustering-field check, the rationale,
the reach challenge, the identifying-condition rule (M10a) and the candidate filter. What ends the call at once, with what was found so far: no `root`, no `nodes`, a node without id (the tree cannot be assembled: only the checks that need no tree go on), and, as before, an entity that does not exist / is already decided.
A tree that fails its structural validation (or cannot be assembled) is not judged by the checks that need a valid tree. A set made only of structural refusals keeps the structural class of lot M9 (three chances); a mixed set is a refusal of the content.

- **The one-shot challenges stay one-shot** (relation evidence required, relation/identifier roles, reach): asked once, and now told together with the other violations of the same proposal (the resubmission is accepted whatever it is, as before). The Factory's own fallback marks them as made, as before.
- **The candidate filter is decided last.** "The second unfiltered proposal is kept, with a warning" (lot M5) applies to a proposal that has nothing else wrong with it; a proposal with other violations is told the filter every time it is not filtered (it is part of the set the breaker compares).
- **The breaker of lot M5 compares the whole set**: `refusalSignature` is computed on the combined text (node ids taken out). The same set twice in a row ends the entity; a smaller set (a violation fixed, a one-shot challenge already read) is another refusal. Consequence, measured by the tests: a model that changes an unrelated part of its tree while repeating
  the same mistakes draws a different set when a violation's text names that part (the identifying-condition rule names the offending field); the cap of six proposals and "three times in the run" still bound it.
- Replay of the live run: the first proposal of run 542 (step 2) now draws the child-evidence challenge and the child-keys ceiling in one answer (turns 1 and 2 of the run).

### 66.3 C. The entity's own facts, BEFORE the first proposal (`master/MatchPlanChecklist.entityBlock`)

After the measured key facts and the lines "MATCH paths on X" and "Identifying keys on X", a checklist built from the entity's own facts (`KeyFacts`, the attributes' per-system fill, the child-keys attribute, the relation children); a line is written only when a measure backs it, and the whole block is empty when nothing is measured (the prompt is then what it was):

1. the rule "every path to SUSPECTED or MATCH opens with an exact key of the record itself; AVERAGE nodes, similarity scores and related-record nodes only AFTER it", with the keys that can open a path (`MatchPlanFallback.eligibleKeys`, the Factory's own definition of a key that may stand in a node) and **how many records of each source system fill each** ("emailKey (ECOM 160 of 160 (100%), LOYALTY 140 of 140 (100%), STORES 131 of 234 (56%)) [identifies a record]"),
   the mark meaning `KeyFacts.predictive`; a key that a source system never fills is not in this list;
2. **the fields a source system never fills** (the facts' keys and the profile's per-system fill; the child keys are exempt, as the pass exempts them): "birthDate (empty in STORES 0 of 234)", never a clustering field, never the key that opens a path, only a refinement;
3. **the child-keys attribute with its ceiling**, as the pass applies it: "minimumScore at most 50 (measured: one record has 2 child record(s) at most, which supports 50; the pass refuses anything above 50 whatever the count)";
4. **the child evidence** the plan is expected to use, placed after an exact key.
The SAFE pairs stay in the line "MATCH paths on X" of lot M5, which now says that the two keys of a pair may sit in one node or in two nodes chained through `onTrue`. The system prompt says it once, with the "all violations at once" contract.

### 66.4 D. Rules first, the model refines (`Session#prepareStartingPlans`, `MatchPlanFallback.buildStartingPlan`)

Before the prompt is built, for every entity whose complete facts allow it, the plan `MatchPlanFallback` builds (lot M9's builder: the strongest SAFE pair at the root, each near-unique key alone, the child keys) is run through EVERY check of the pass on a scratch session (same entities, vocabulary, live lookups, candidate-filter rule; the one-shot challenges
marked as made) and, only when it passes, shown to the model as a **starting plan that passes every check** ("keep its structure, improve its leaves and thresholds, add what the facts justify (child evidence, weaker paths for the sources it does not reach), or explain in the rationale why you prefer another shape"), with its nodes in words and the `root` and `nodes` to resubmit.
- A model that resubmits its tree **unchanged** (same nodes, fields, algorithms, scores, null handling, branches; node order of fields ignored, absent defaults read as the pass reads them - `treeSignature`) has it accepted without the one-shot challenges (the Factory cannot ask the model to improve a plan it proposed itself); the rationale says "The model kept the Factory's starting plan ... unchanged".
- **A plan of the model that passes is kept as the model wrote it**: nothing replaces it by the starting plan (test: the stored plan is the model's, origin LLM). A tree changed in any detail is the model's plan, judged and challenged like any other.
- No starting plan for an entity decided by a person, a child entity, an entity without complete facts, or whose plan any check refuses; the reason is kept (`startingPlanReasons`) and written in the step detail (`startingPlans{entity: summary}`, `noStartingPlan{entity: reason}`). The fallback of lot M9 is unchanged (it also runs after the model's refusals).

### 66.5 Files, tests, limits

New: `master/MatchPlanChecklist`, `MatchPlanLlmPassGuidanceTest`, the two run-542 proposals the tests replay (steps 2 and 10 of the run) under `src/test/resources/com/on/ebx/factory/master/`. Touched: `master/MeasuredMatchPath` (path rule; the node-local `justification`/`notes` are gone), `master/MatchPlanLlmPass` (`collecting`/`refuse`/`combineViolations`, `judgeProposal`, `matchTerminalViolations`, `appendBestEffortField`,
starting plans, prompt and system prompt), `master/MatchPlanFallback` (`buildStartingPlan`), `ebx/MatchPlanLlmSuggester` (prepares the starting plans before the prompt, step detail). **No XSD, no bundle change.** Adjusted tests: `MatchPlanLlmPassTest` (the relation-evidence challenge no longer has to win a race: it arrives with the phone refusal in one answer), `MatchPlanLlmPassCandidateFilterTest`
(its helper resubmits a challenge only when it came alone), `MatchPlanLlmPassLoopTest` (the note carries the set), `MatchPlanFallbackTest` (the breaker needs the same set twice).
Not verified live (nothing was installed): how the model uses the checklist and the starting plan; the live cost of the trial of the starting plan (one extra pass of the cross-system lookups per entity, cached within a proposal); that the measured numbers of the checklist match the live facts of run 542 (the prompt there was not stored: the tests use the fixture of lot M3, the 534 records reduced to their keys).
Found on the way, not changed: (1) the copies of shared nodes (66.1) - the model's tree is a graph and the cap counts the copies; (2) **the child-keys ceiling and the identifying-condition rule contradict each other for an entity whose records have more than 2 children**: the ceiling is 100 / max children (20 for 5), the rule of lot M10a counts `exactFullText` only from 50 - a path opened by the child keys alone can never satisfy both; it needs
a predictive key beside it.

## 67. Lot M14 - child evidence never carries a path alone, and a failed comparison is not evidence (branch `fix/path-evidence-child-keys`, 2026-10-18)

Measured on the 10th live run of the B2C master scenario (Factory 1.2.0-285, project `E2EMASTER20261018090711`, `AgentRun` 562, entity `Client`; the proposals read from `AgentStep` over Data Services, nothing written): the third proposal was accepted as MatchPlan 81 (origin LLM, confidence 64). With automatic merge on, the merged pairs are perfect (341 pairs,
precision 1.000) but the SUSPECTED pairs are 1190 and 679 of them false (precision with suspects 0.429, suspect chains of up to 22 records): store tickets of one area that share only a first name or only a last name. The accepted tree, F1 to F9: `F1 [emailKey, personNameKey] -> MATCH`, `F2 [mobileE164] -> SUSPECTED`, `F3 [emailKey] -> SUSPECTED`, `F4 [addressKeys exactFullText 50] -> F5 / F7`, `F5 AVERAGE [personNameKey jarowinkler 85, birthDate]
-> F6 / SUSPECTED`, `F6 [street of Adresse] -> SUSPECTED`, `F7 [emailKey] -> F8 / F9`, `F8`, `F9 [fullAddress of Adresse exactFullText 100] -> SUSPECTED / NOT_MATCHED`. It had its starting plan from lot M13 ("... SUSPECTED on shared child keys addressKeys"), which the model copied.

### 67.1 What the data says about the false pairs (read, not assumed)

All 209 suspect edges the add-on holds now (`Master_Client_MDS`, table `Suspected`) are **STORES-STORES** pairs; none shares an e-mail key, none a phone, and **`addressKeys` is empty on every STORES record** (0 of 234 in the staging and in the master: a ticket's address is `postalCode` and `fullAddress` = the bare postal code, `street` null). So the path of the ticket
pairs is not F4 > F5.onFalse: F4 cannot be true when both `addressKeys` are empty (NOT_MATCH nulls), the pair leaves through F4.onFalse to F7 (e-mail differs) and ends on **F9: the child field `fullAddress` of Adresse, `exactFullText` 100, alone** - equal on all 209 edges ("67000" = "67000"). The run's own `MATCHING_RUN` step
had said so: "candidate search NOT filtered (1 path with no exact key): F1 > F2 > F3 > F4 > F7 > F9". F4 alone and F5.onFalse are the same defect on the pairs of the sources that fill `addressKeys` (ECOM, LOYALTY): both are refused below, but the false pairs measured are F9's. (Replay by script on the stored master and metadataset; no suspect edge of any other kind exists in the instance now.)

### 67.2 Rule A - child evidence never carries a path alone (`PathEvidenceRule.checkStructure`)

Lot M10a counted `addressKeys` (predictive, 94.5 % in run 7) and any precise `via` field as an identifying condition. A **derived child-keys attribute** (`AttributeInfo.isChildKeys`, or a multi-token key of the facts) and **any field read through a related record** (`FieldRef.via`) is evidence about the record's CHILDREN: whatever its measured rate it needs an
exact **own-identity key** of the record on the same `onTrue` chain (`PathEvidenceRule.Condition.own`): a plain attribute, not a child-keys attribute, not a related record's field, not a parent reference, compared exactly (the conditions M10a's `judge` already requires: exact, `NOT_MATCH` on both null handlings, `minimumScore` > 0), that is a measured key of the facts - predictive or not, so the name key counts - or
identifies by its own profile (at most 5 rows per value, or unmeasured). A coarse non-key attribute (the first name) is not an own-identity key. The conjunction of the path is the one of M13 (`passedNodes`): the key may sit in the same node or in any `ALL_FIELDS` ancestor left through `onTrue`; an ancestor left through `onFalse` counts for nothing. Active under complete key facts when the entity has at least one eligible
key of its own (`MatchPlanFallback.eligibleKeys`); inactive otherwise, and over `CrossSystemPathRule.MAX_PATHS` positive paths. M10a itself is unchanged (a path with no identifying condition at all is still refused there); the two rules are separate texts in the same answer. M10a's refusal now says that a related record's field "only ever accompanies an own-identity key" and the list of identifying keys marks the child keys as child evidence.

### 67.3 Rule B - a failed comparison is not evidence

`CrossSystemPathRule.PositivePath.leafViaOnFalse` records that the leaf is reached through the `onFalse` edge of the last node of the path. When that node is a **similarity node** (`AVERAGE`, `AT_LEAST_N`, `PREDICATE`, or an `ALL_FIELDS` with a non-exact field) and the exact conditions met on the path hold no own-identity key, the proposal is refused: "names not similar -> suspect" is a failed comparison used as evidence. With an own key above
it ("key equal, secondary comparison differs" - the simulate-first plan's `R6.onFalse -> SUSPECTED` under `R1` emailKey) it stays. The `onFalse` of an `ALL_FIELDS` node on exact conditions is not covered (M10a judges those paths).

### 67.4 The two refusal texts, on the exact tree of plan 81 (test `PathEvidenceChildKeysTest`)

Child evidence alone: three paths - `F1 > F2 > F3 > F4 > F5 > F6` (addressKeys, names, street of Adresse), `F1 > F2 > F3 > F4 > F5` (addressKeys), `F1 > F2 > F3 > F4 > F7 > F9` (fullAddress of Adresse) - with the fix "add one of those keys to the node that compares the child evidence (node 'F4', node 'F6', node 'F9'), or open the path with an ALL_FIELDS node on one of those keys whose onTrue leads to that node, or point the onTrue of ... to NOT_MATCHED".
Failed comparison: `node 'F5'.onFalse -> SUSPECTED`, with the fix "point node 'F5'.onFalse to NOT_MATCHED, or open the path with an own-identity key". Both are numbered in one answer with the other violations of the proposal (lot M13). The breaker's signature (`refusalSignature`) now also strips the ids of a path label (`path N1 > N2 (`), so renaming nodes is not a new refusal - the lot-M13 test that pins this.
The same fixed tree (F5.onFalse -> NOT_MATCHED, the name key added to F4 and F9) passes both rules and M10a. The **simulate-first plan of the same run** (project `E2EMASTER20261018091200`, `AgentRun` 573, step 8, entity `Personne`, 27 nodes) passes both rules.

### 67.5 The starting plan and the fallback (`MatchPlanFallback`)

The child-keys node is no longer alone: it carries a key of the record itself beside it (`partnerKey`): among the eligible keys, the ones that do not already stand alone as a SUSPECTED node first (beside an e-mail key that already suspects on its own the child keys would add nothing), then the key that reaches every source system, the most records, the most selective. On the facts of the scenario the starting plan is
`F1 [mobileE164, personNameKey] -> MATCH`, `F2 [emailKey] -> SUSPECTED`, `F3 [mobileE164] -> SUSPECTED`, **`F4 [personNameKey exact 100, addressKeys exactFullText 50] -> SUSPECTED / NOT_MATCHED`** (it passed lot M10a, both rules of this lot and the whole pass in the test). The live starting plan of run 562 was "MATCH on emailKey + personNameKey; SUSPECTED on mobileE164, emailKey (each alone); SUSPECTED on shared child keys addressKeys". With no eligible key the child node is not built and the
refusal of "no usable key" says so. The system prompt (one paragraph), the entity's checklist (`MatchPlanChecklist.openingKeys`) and the "Identifying keys" line carry both rules.

### 67.6 Files, tests, limits

Touched: `master/PathEvidenceRule` (roles on `Condition`, `checkStructure`, `structureRefusals`, wording), `master/CrossSystemPathRule` (`leafViaOnFalse`), `master/MatchPlanFallback` (`partnerKey`), `master/MatchPlanChecklist`, `master/MatchPlanLlmPass` (the check, system prompt, `refusalSignature`). New test `PathEvidenceChildKeysTest` and the two live proposals under `src/test/resources/.../master/`
(`run562_step6_client_proposal.json`, `run573_step8_personne_proposal.json`: field names and thresholds, no value). Fixtures of four existing tests were adjusted because they put child keys or a street alone on a path (`MatchPlanLlmPassPathEvidenceTest`, `MatchPlanLlmPassKeyFactsTest`, `MatchPlanLlmPassGuidanceTest`: G7 of the replayed tree of run 542 now carries the name key; `MatchPlanFallbackTest`; `PathEvidenceRuleTest` is unchanged). **No XSD, no bundle change.**
Limits: (1) **F9's real defect is also a data defect**: for a ticket the child `fullAddress` is a bare postal code, and M10a judges a related field precise from its profile over all rows of the child table; a related record's field is judged on the whole child table, not per source system. Rule A removes the path; a "name key + child address" path (the starting plan's F4) would still pair namesakes of one postal code
among tickets if `addressKeys` were filled for them (it is not: it is empty on STORES). (2) "Own-identity key" accepts the name key (the owner's reading) although M10a measured it coarse (79-81 %); the first number to revisit if a scenario disagrees. (3) Rule B looks only at the leaf edge. (4) Not verified live: nothing was installed or run; how the model reacts to the two texts and to the new starting plan.


## 68. Lot M16 - the candidate search: what the add-on measures, told to the model; the Factory sets no weight (branch `fix/candidate-search-recall`, 2026-10-18)

Measured on the 11th live run of the B2C master scenario (Factory 1.2.0-289, variant simulate-first, project `E2EMASTER20261018104106`, accepted plan 86 = `AgentRun` 595 step 6, origin LLM, confidence 65, `clusteringFields` `emailKey`, `mobileE164`;
dataspace `E2EMASTER20261018104106_Master`, table `/root/Personne`, metadataset `Master_Personne_MDS`). Automatic merge on: precision 1.000, **recall 0.735 (415 of 565 true pairs, 150 missed, 94 records left without a golden)**, while the plain
variant of the same run (project `E2EMASTER20261018103554`, plan 85) found 565 of 565 on the same data. Everything below was READ (Data Services `GET`, `get_matching_config`, `ebx-addon-mame.log`, `javap` on `ebx-lib.jar` and the add-on's classes);
nothing was written on the instance. The audit is a script: `tools/matching/candidate_gap_audit.py`.

**Direction (the product owner, mid-lot): the Factory does not find the configuration, it gives the language model the elements that let it find it.** A first version of this lot made the Factory raise the weights itself (a
`CandidateScoreShare.enforce` in the translator); it was replaced before the commit by what is described here: the arithmetic is a MEASUREMENT, told to the model (system prompt, checklist, one challenge, simulation facts), and the model
writes the weights (`clusteringWeights`). The Factory refuses only a plan that leaves a whole source system unreachable.

### 68.1 The 150 missed pairs, characterised

The 565 true pairs by what the two records fill (E = e-mail key filled) - read in the master table and the metadataset (`goldenId`), truth from `gen_b2c.py`:

| true pairs | count | found | missed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| both records fill the SAME e-mail key (ECOM-LOYALTY 103, ECOM-STORES 101, LOYALTY-STORES 86, STORES-STORES 51) | 341 | 341 | 0 |
| NEITHER record fills an e-mail (STORES-STORES) | 24 | 24 | 0 |
| ONE record fills no e-mail: ECOM-STORES | 69 | 5 | **64** |
| ONE record fills no e-mail: LOYALTY-STORES | 59 | 22 | **37** |
| ONE record fills no e-mail: STORES-STORES | 72 | 23 | **49** |

All 150 misses are pairs of which exactly ONE side lacks the e-mail key (always a store ticket); every one of them shares `mobileE164` AND `personNameKey` (the tree reaches MATCH through E3 > E5), and none shares an address key (empty on STORES and
LOYALTY in this run). No pair with both e-mails, and no pair with no e-mail on either side, was missed. The tree and the candidate filters are not the cause: the add-on's log lists, for the real policy `Personne`, the field sets `{personNameKey,
mobileE164}` (MATCHED, twice), `{personNameKey, emailKey}`, `{emailKey}`, `{addressKeys, mobileE164}`... - the phone + name pair satisfies a set.

The split that decides it, per record without an e-mail that has an e-mail-bearing partner (96 records): persons **with an ECOM record** (the only source that fills all four declared fields: e-mail, phone, name key, address key): **64 alone, 5
joined**; persons **without** an ECOM record: **0 alone, 27 joined**. (The 5 exceptions have another e-mail-bearing record that fills three fields - 444, 533, 227 - a pivot of the weaker kind.)

### 68.2 The cause: the weights, against the add-on's candidate threshold (the hypothesis of the brief, refined)

"The candidate search never proposes a pair when one side has no e-mail" is true of the outcome and wrong about the reason (it is not the filter: the sets are fine). The add-on keeps a candidate when its score is at least a fraction of the PIVOT's own score:

- `MatchingQueueProducer` (add-on, `javap`) calls `ClusterProducer.Builder.setThresholds(0.3f, 0.8f)`; `CnyTableMinScoreHelper.computeMinScoresPerTable` multiplies the center's score by the low threshold; with the mandatory field sets on
  (`computeMinScoresPerTableWithMandatoryFieldSets`) the floor is `max(0.3 x C, smallest set score)`. The center's score `C` is `sum(weight of each field the pivot FILLS)` (`computeValueScore`: a null value with `NOT_MATCH` handling is worth 0);
  a pair that satisfies a set scores `sum(weight x minScore/100)` of the set's fields (`CnyMandatoryFieldSet.computeScore`).
- The policy the Factory wrote for plan 86 (`get_matching_config`): `emailKey` **4**, `mobileE164` 1, `personNameKey` 1, `addressKeys` 1 - the dominance guard of lot R16 (section 46: an identifier's weight above the sum of the others) had raised the e-mail
  from 1 to 4 because the plan's root is a standalone e-mail node. A pivot that fills all four fields (an ECOM record) has `C = 7`; the phone + name pair scores 2: **2 / 7 = 28.6 %, under 30 %** - never a candidate. A pivot that fills three (a LOYALTY or
  STORES record with an e-mail, `C = 6`): 2 / 6 = 33 % - a candidate. That is the 27 of 27 above and the 64 of 69.
- The plain variant: every weight 1 (the root is the phone + name node, no standalone identifier): 2 / 4 = 50 % for the fullest pivot, and all 200 one-sided pairs were found (recall 1.000).

So the dominance rule, made to let an e-mail alone be enough, pushed the total weight up and put every OTHER path's keys under the add-on's 30 %. Its measured justification (section 46.1, PersVol7: 3 / 17 = 18 % before, 15 / 29 = 52 % after) was the same
threshold seen from the other side; it asked for far more than the threshold needs (an e-mail alone needs about 43 % of the sum of the others, not 100 %).

**Unexplained**: a record without an e-mail is itself a pivot with `C = 2` (phone + name, 100 % of its own score) and should have found its partner from its side; the data says it did not (64 alone). The reading that fits (canopy clustering: the
e-mail-bearing partners are consumed by an earlier center, the add-on's 0.8 "tight" threshold) is not proved by the bytecode read. Nothing here depends on it.

### 68.3 What changed: the Factory measures and tells; the model sets the weights

(a) **The model is given the facts** (`master/MatchPlanLlmPass`, `matching/KeyFacts`):
- the system prompt gained the paragraph HOW THE ADD-ON FINDS CANDIDATES: the 30 % rule, the pivot's own weight, the numbers of the live case (2 of 7 = 29 %, 150 of 565 lost, the same data at 2 of 4 = 50 % lost none), and the lever;
  the old sentence asking for a weight above the sum of the others is gone;
- `propose_match_plan` takes an optional `clusteringWeights` `{field: integer >= 1}` (the pre-clustering weight of a field of the record; it does not change how an AVERAGE node compares). Checked (unknown field, value under 1: refused with the valid
  keys), stored in `requirements.clusteringWeights`, carried over from the plan a rewrite supersedes, part of `sameStructure`, applied by the translator over the node weights;
- the entity block gives the fill rate of every key per source system (it already did) and, new, the **gaps** in numbers: `emailKey: STORES 103 of 234; addressKeys: STORES 234 of 234` (`KeyFacts.gapsText`);
- **refused** (with the numbers and the fix, counted by the circuit breaker like any refusal): a plan whose declared fields (nodes + `clusteringFields`) are filled by no record of a WHOLE source system (>= 20 records), judged on complete facts and only
  when every declared field is a measured key (`wholeSystemUnreachableRefusal`);
- **told once, then kept** (the pattern of the reach challenge): when a key set of a path that ends in MATCH holds under 31 % of the total weight under the model's own weights, the proposal is answered with the total, its weights, the failing sets with
  their share, the fill rate of their keys, the `clusteringWeights` that would hold every set (`CandidateScoreShare`, shares 40 %, 35 %, 31.5 %, MATCH sets first when not all can be served), and the two ways out; the resubmission is accepted as it is. Told LAST
  and only to a proposal with nothing else wrong, so it never changes the set of violations the breaker compares. A SUSPECTED path under 31 % costs no round trip: one sentence in the plan's rationale ("Candidate search: a pair that agrees on [...] holds
  25.0 % of the total weight 8 (kept as proposed)").

(b) **Feedback after the simulation** (`matching/CandidateCoverage`, `ebx/MatchPlanSimulationRunner`, `review/MatchSimulationBlock`): for the exact keys that open a path, the records sharing a key's value with a pivot (one bulk read per key) are compared with the
candidates the engine returned FOR THAT PIVOT (every `simulateMatch` match, before the symmetric-pair deduplication). The result is shown on the plan's simulation panel ("Candidates the add-on really evaluated": per key, `3 of 4 record(s) sharing it
with a pivot were never candidates (STORES 3)`, EN and FR), stored on the plan (`requirements.simulationFacts`, numbered statements with their cause: the failing key sets and the weights that would hold them) and handed to the model by the next "Propose another"
(`rejectionNote`: ` MEASURED by the simulation of that plan: 1) simulation: 18 pivot(s); 23 of 41 record(s) sharing mobileE164 with a pivot were never candidates (19 in STORES), for pivots of ECOM 23. Cause: ...`; a plan with facts and no reviewer comment is
told too). A failure to measure never fails the simulation. **Not done: the same measure after the RUN** (the audit script reads it; a live one needs the metadataset joined to the key shares and the SQL traps of section 8 of the knowledge base).

(c) **The dominance guard is gone** (`MatchingPolicyTranslator.applyPreClusteringDominance`, `DecisionTreePlan.standaloneIdentifierFieldNames` stays unused): the translator writes the node weights and the model's `clusteringWeights`, nothing else, and records the shares
of the key sets as facts (`detail.candidateScoreShare`, `applied: false`). It was replaced by advice (the one challenge above), not by a visible correction: a Factory-set weight is the thing that produced the miss. **The one exception is the plan the Factory builds
itself** (`MatchPlanFallback`): it carries `clusteringWeights` computed from the same arithmetic as part of the plan it proposes (stored, shown, replaceable by the model); a plan the model writes never gets one from the Factory.

### 68.4 Not changed, and what is unsure

- The filter of the add-on (`MandatoryFieldSets`) is untouched: a pair is dropped for its score, never for its e-mail (the e-mail only enters through the arithmetic above).
- Not run: nothing was written on the instance (the brief); a re-run of the scenario (variant simulate-first) is the test of the whole chain - whether the model, told the numbers, sizes the weights. The shares are raw weights x minScore: the add-on's
  `BALANCE_FIELD_SCORE` (weights balanced by token count) is off by default and not modelled; the live split (33 % passes, 29 % fails) fits the raw weights.
- More paths are proposed as candidates when weights are lifted (a single-key path such as the phone alone), so a plan whose weakly selective key opens a path costs more comparisons at volume.

### 68.5 The e2e phone check that ended SKIP (`tools/e2e/e2e_lib.py` `phone_source_systems`)

Run 11 ended `SKIP [6] phone reaches the person entity from every source whose landing holds a phone column - no landing column of a source is a filled phone column` although `STORES.TELEPHONE` is filled 234 of 234. Cause: Data Services answers a `LandingTable.id`
as a NUMBER (`{"content": 211}`; the foreign key `LandingColumn.landingTable` is the string "211"), the scenario keys the columns by that very number, and the lookup used `text(id)`: a string against int keys found nothing for any source. The stand-in factory served
string ids, so the self-test passed (the lot M15 tests on canned string ids). Fixed: ids compared as text on both sides, the column named by `sourceColumn` else `fieldName`, the columns re-read after the landing load (they were read before it, when
`fillRate` is still empty), and the stand-in now serves the `id` of the factory rows as a number like the real instance (so the good run of the scenario passes the check instead of skipping it).

### 68.6 Files, tests, limits

New: `master/CandidateScoreShare` (the arithmetic: shares, failing sets, the weights that would lift them - never applied), `matching/CandidateCoverage`, `tools/matching/candidate_gap_audit.py`, fixtures `run11_plan85_requirements.json`, `run11_plan86_requirements.json` (the two
live trees, no value). Touched: `matching/CandidateFilterCheck` (`PathResult.keyPercents`), `matching/KeyFacts` (`gapsText`, `fillText`), `master/MatchingPolicyTranslator` (`clusteringWeights`, `analyzeShares`, no dominance), `master/MatchPlanLlmPass`
(prompt, schema, checks, `rejectionNote`), `master/MatchPlanFallback`, `ebx/MatchingConfigurator`, `ebx/MatchPlanSimulationRunner`, `ebx/ProposalReviews` (`recordSimulationFacts`), `review/MatchPlanView`, `review/MatchSimulationBlock`, both message bundles, `tools/e2e/*`.
Removed: `MatchingPolicyTranslatorDominanceTest`. Tests: `CandidateScoreShareTest` (both live trees against an independent statement of the add-on's rule: the live weights fail, the suggested ones hold; the translator writes the model's weights and raises none),
`CandidateCoverageTest`, `MatchPlanLlmPassKeyFactsTest` (the contract, the challenge once with the numbers, the suggested weights accepted and stored, a SUSPECTED path only in the rationale, bad weights, the whole-system refusal, carry-over, the facts in the next
prompt), `MatchSimulationBlockTest` (the panel, EN and FR), the e2e self-test (numeric ids). Existing tests adjusted: the proposals that put a single MATCH key beside other fields now carry `clusteringWeights` (`MatchPlanLlmPassTest`); the translator tests no
longer expect the dominance raise.

## 69. Lot M17 - a table fed by one source system and sharing no key needs no plan: the model is told the facts, the Factory decides nothing (branch `feat/no-plan-for-reference-tables`, 2026-10-18)

Measured on the 12th live run of the B2C master scenario (Factory 1.2.0-291, project `E2EMASTER20261018115006`, `AgentRun` 624, status BUDGET after 10 steps / 306,833 tokens). After the person plan (`Client`, accepted at the third proposal) and the ticket plan (`Achat`),
the model spent its remaining turns proposing one-node plans with no clustering field for three REFERENCE tables fed by a single source - `VisiteMagasin`, `PaysClient`, `SuiviClient` ("Matching plan for 'VisiteMagasin' recorded: 1 node(s), 0 clustering field(s)") - until the token budget
ended the run. Nothing was lost (the real plans were recorded first), but a run that ends on BUDGET reads as a failure and those plans are useless: a table fed by ONE source system whose rows carry that source's own key cannot hold cross-system duplicates, and duplicates inside the
source are a fact to measure, not to guess.

**House rule (the product owner, 2026-10-18)**: the Factory GUIDES the language model with measured facts and explained rules; it never decides the configuration for it. Nothing here forbids a plan or skips an entity on its own.

### 69.1 The facts (`master/SingleSourceFacts`, no new read)

- **Source systems and rows**: the key facts already count the master table by `sourceSystem` (`KeyFacts.recordsBySystem`, complete facts only); an entity without key facts uses the per-system row counts of the profile (`EntityInfo.rowCountBySystem`). A sample of a larger table
  gives lower bounds and states nothing. A record whose source system is empty belongs to a source that has no name: the count is then unknown and nothing is said.
- **Intra-source key sharing**: for ONE source system every pair of rows is a pair of rows of that source, so the pairs of rows sharing an exact key (`KeyStat.pairsSharing`, already computed in linear time by `KeyFacts.compute`) ARE the within-source counts - no per-system pair
  counter was needed. The keys the selection leaves out because every filled value is unique (`KeyFactsSelection.uniqueKeys`: eligible in every other respect, `neverRepeats` true on EXACT fill and cardinality) share nothing by measurement; a table whose only keys are of that kind has no key facts at all
  (that is the reference table of run 12) and is still measured. A table with no measurable exact key is NOT marked: the checklist states the source and says that nothing is concluded.
- `noPlanNeeded()` = one source, at least one exact key measured, none shared by two rows.

### 69.2 What the model reads (`master/MatchPlanChecklist`, `MatchPlanLlmPass.userPrompt`)

First line of the entity's checklist, for every entity whose source systems are known:

- several sources: `Source systems feeding Client: 3 (ECOM 160, LOYALTY 140, STORES 234; 534 rows in all).`
- one source, no shared key: `StoreRef is fed by one source system only (STORES, 48 rows); no key is shared by two rows of that source (storeKey: 0 pair(s) of rows share it) -> no duplicate can exist: call skip_entity with that reason instead of proposing a plan; propose a plan only if a key IS shared within the source (then say which).`
- one source, a key shared: `... keys shared by two or more rows of that source: storeKey (12 pair(s) of rows) -> duplicates inside that source exist on these keys; a plan has something to find there.`
- one source, nothing measurable: `... no exact key of this entity could be measured, so nothing is concluded about duplicates inside that source.`

**Order**: the entities the facts mark are listed LAST (stable: the others keep the project's order) and named in ONE line after the fenced inventory: `Entities the facts mark as needing no plan: VisiteMagasin, PaysClient, SuiviClient (one source, no shared key) - skip them with skip_entity, after the entities above.`
The system prompt's `skip_entity` entry cites the same fact as a valid reason. **No starting plan** is built for such an entity (`prepareStartingPlans`, reason kept in `startingPlanReasons`): offering one would nudge the model to resubmit what the facts call useless.

### 69.3 A plan proposed anyway is accepted

`proposeMatchPlan` is unchanged for these entities (every check applies as before). When the facts mark the entity, the stored rationale gets one sentence after the model's words: `The facts showed one source and no shared key (STORES, 48 rows).`

### 69.4 The wizard (`wizard/MatchingPlanCoverage`, `WizardPage.renderMatchNoPlan`)

The pass stores the marked entities in its result (`noPlanNeeded{entity: "STORES, 48 rows"}`, step detail of `MATCHING_SUGGEST_LLM`). The coverage reads them: an accepted object WITHOUT a plan that is in that set is never a gap (whatever the model did: skipped it with that reason or another, said nothing, ran out of budget on it) but a `NoPlan`: a card
"No plan needed" with `No plan - one source only, no shared key (measured fact)` / `Pas de plan - une seule source, aucune cle partagee (fait mesure)` (the dash is an em dash) and the source and rows; the job message names it the same way, and "Nothing to do" with no other gap reads "Every accepted
business object that needs a matching plan already has one." followed by the facts. Bundle keys `wizard.matching.noPlan.*` and `wizard.matching.nothingToDo.noPlanOnly`, both languages, under `# reference tables need no plan (2026-10-18)`. A result stored before the lot has no `noPlanNeeded`: nothing changes for it.

### 69.5 Files, tests, limits

New: `master/SingleSourceFacts`. Touched: `master/KeyFactsSelection` (`uniqueKeys`), `master/MatchPlanChecklist` (source line, `noPlanNeeded`, `noPlanLine`), `master/MatchPlanLlmPass` (entity order and closing line, system prompt, no starting plan, rationale sentence, `Session#noPlanNeeded`), `ebx/MatchPlanLlmSuggester`
(`noPlanNeeded{}` in the result), `ebx/MatchingSuggestLlmRun`, `ebx/SuggestRulesRun`, `wizard/MatchingPlanCoverage`, `wizard/WizardPage`, both bundles. Tests: `ReferenceTablesNeedNoPlanTest` (one-source / unique-key / shared-key / several-source / sample fixtures, the order and the line, no starting plan, `skip_entity`, the rationale),
`MatchingPlanCoverageNoPlanTest` (never a gap, the wording EN and FR, the job message).
Not verified live (nothing was installed): how the model uses the sentence, and that the live facts of `VisiteMagasin`, `PaysClient`, `SuiviClient` mark them (their master tables were not read by this lot). Limits: "no duplicate can exist" is true of duplicates that share an exact key; a within-source duplicate that only a fuzzy comparison of a name
could find (two spellings in one source) is not excluded by the measure - the marking requires an exact key to have been measured and left unshared, and the model keeps its call. The Factory's fallback plan (lot M9) still runs for an entity the model proposed for and was refused on; it is not suppressed for a marked entity.
## 69. Lot M18 - the deletion removes the business object's configuration from the add-on's own dataset (branch `fix/deletion-business-object-config`, 2026-10-18)

Measured the same day: after 25 test projects were deleted with the Factory's route, `Bebx-addon-mame/ebx-addon-mame-configuration` still held 17 `BusinessObjectConfiguration` and 38 `TableConfiguration` rows (36 linked by `FKBusinessObject`) of
the deleted publications - a business-object row without its model breaks the add-on at the next start (section 8 of CLAUDE.md), and `delete_matching_config` is refused on the main table of a business object. The deletion's `matching` option now
runs, BEFORE any dataspace or model item: (a) `FKBusinessObject = null` on every table configuration of the business object, (b) delete the `BusinessObjectConfiguration` row (plan item `MATCHING_BUSINESS_OBJECT`, "Business object of Client: Client, Adresse"),
(c) `delete_matching_config` on each member table, now a plain table (item `MATCHING_CONFIG`, needs the model), then reads the add-on's dataset back (`matchingConfigRowsLeft`). `GET /matching/orphans[?publication=]` and
`POST /matching/orphans/delete` clean what earlier deletions left (rows of a vanished model: unlink and delete the business-object row, the table configurations stay); the e2e cleanup fails when the add-on still holds a row of the project's publication.
Details, exact calls and what was not verified live: `docs/PROJECT-DELETION.md`, "Match and Merge business objects: the add-on's own rows (lot M18)".

### 69.1 Second round (live 2026-10-18 15:56): the main table of the business object

After lot M18's first commit the live deletions removed the business object and the members' configurations but not the MAIN table's (`/root/Personne`, table configurations 143 and 146): `delete_matching_config` refuses a table
whose PUBLISHED model declares a business object on it (`SchemaNode.getBusinessObjectModel() != null`, `MameConfigWriter.rejectIfBusinessObjectTable`, javap), whatever the add-on's rows say. The deletion now removes the object from the model
