## 70. Lot F1 - the model gets a NUMERIC FEEDBACK after its proposal: the plan simulated, counted, told; the model revises or keeps (branch `feat/matching-simulation-feedback`, 2026-10-19)

The rule of the module (the product owner, 2026-10-18): the Factory never decides the matching configuration in place of the language model; it gives measured facts BEFORE the proposal, explained rules, and a numeric feedback AFTER it, and the model converges by itself.
Measured on the B2C scenario (`tools/e2e/b2c_master.sh`, 534 records, 565 true pairs): on identical data the model's plan varied - runs 3-5: 4 MATCH leaves of 18, every true pair merged; run 6 (2026-10-19 00:55): 1 MATCH leaf of 9 and six SUSPECTED, still no false pair and
every true pair found, but 341 pairs merged and 224 left to a steward (recall merged-only 0.60). The facts before the proposal were good (key facts, single-source facts, candidate score shares, checklist); nothing told the model, after its answer, what its plan did.

### 70.1 How the simulation reached the model before this lot (read in the code, not assumed)

- The system prompt says "The simulation of a plan reports the candidates the add-on really evaluated: read it and ask for another proposal when it shows records that share a key with a pivot and were never candidates". The model has no way to run a simulation and the pass
  never ran one: the sentence referred to the Simulate button of the plan card.
- `MatchPlanSimulationRunner.simulate` (20 pivots, `MAX_DETAIL_PAIRS` 60) measured the candidate coverage (lot M16) and stored its statements in the plan row (`requirements.simulationFacts`). They reached the model ONLY through `MatchPlanLlmPass.rejectionNote` - when a person
  had clicked Simulate, then "Propose another" (plan SUPERSEDED). The verdict counts never reached it: `review/MatchSimulationBlock` computes them for the panel (cards: pairs examined, MATCH / SUSPECT / NOT_MATCH, "same key but refused", "borderline", up to 3 example pairs
  per family, the coverage block) and nothing else reads them. The first proposal of a sweep got no feedback at all, and the scenario's two variants call the pass without or with a Simulate click: neither fed the model.

### 70.2 What the feedback is (`master/SimulationFeedback`, pure, no EBX)

Input: the stored plan (`requirements`: tree, clustering, `keyFacts`) and the pairs of ONE simulation as plain `Pair`s (origin, verdict, the values of the key fields of the two records, the add-on's visit order `enginePath`). Output: counts, never a value.

- **Sample.** The pairs the add-on evaluated for the pivots the runner drew (`ENGINE`) are the figures; the pairs the runner chose because they share a key across systems (the probes, `PROBE`) are counted apart (they are selected, not drawn). The statement says the number of pivots
  and of pairs: "measured on that sample, not on the whole table".
- **Verdicts:** how many pairs the plan sends to MATCH / SUSPECTED / NOT_MATCHED.
- **Key sets.** The exact conditions of the paths of the plan's own tree (`CandidateFilterCheck`: ALL_FIELDS nodes on an exact key of the record) and every pair of keys the entity's key facts mark SAFE when the plan uses both keys. For each set: the pairs that agree on EVERY field of it (both
  records fill it, identical value) and where the plan sends them. A set holding a multi-token key (exactFullText) is not counted - two records agree on it by a score - and the statement says so.
- **The consequence, plainly:** "With this plan, N of the M pair(s) the simulation judged identical on <keys> wait for a steward instead of merging." Then "possible misses: X of the Y NOT_MATCHED pair(s) agree on every field of at least one key set above", and
  "N of the S SUSPECTED pair(s) agree on every field of at least one key set above: with this plan they wait for a steward".
- **Leaf by leaf:** the pairs each leaf of the tree decided, from the add-on's own visit order of each pair (node names resolved through the stored labels, `DecisionTreePlan.freezeAndDisambiguateLabels`, the same the translator writes). The order is recorded for the pairs that got an `evaluatePair` call; the statement says
  "for 40 of the 87 pair(s)". A node whose two branches end in the same outcome is one entry ("either branch").
- **The candidate coverage of lot M16** is told in the same turn (its statements already existed).

Exact text produced on the fixture (`SimulationFeedbackTest`, the 534 B2C records, the plan of run 6 - e-mail alone, phone alone and address keys all end in a review; the candidates are the 703 pairs that share an e-mail key or a phone, plus a spread of pairs that share
neither, the verdicts replayed by an evaluator written independently of the class; the 341 / 224 split is the live run 6's):

```
1) sample: 20 pivot(s) drawn at random across the source systems; the add-on evaluated 703 distinct pair(s) for them. These figures are measured on that sample, not on the whole table.
2) verdicts of the 703 evaluated pair(s): 0 go to MATCH (merged automatically once automatic merge is on for the plan), 565 to SUSPECTED (a data steward decides), 138 to NOT_MATCHED.
3) leaf by leaf (the add-on's visit order was recorded for 703 of the 703 pair(s)): N1 onTrue -> SUSPECTED 341; N2 onTrue -> SUSPECTED 224; N3 onTrue -> SUSPECTED 0; N3 onFalse -> NOT_MATCHED 138.
4) of the 341 pair(s) that agree on every field of emailKey (an exact key set of the path N1 of your tree, ending in SUSPECTED): 0 go to MATCH, 341 to SUSPECTED, 0 to NOT_MATCHED. With this plan, 341 of the 341 pair(s) the simulation judged identical on emailKey wait for a steward instead of merging.
5) of the 565 pair(s) that agree on every field of mobileE164 (an exact key set of the path N1 > N2 of your tree, ending in SUSPECTED): 0 go to MATCH, 565 to SUSPECTED, 0 to NOT_MATCHED. With this plan, 565 of the 565 pair(s) the simulation judged identical on mobileE164 wait for a steward instead of merging.
6) of the 341 pair(s) that agree on every field of emailKey + mobileE164 (the entity's key facts mark these two keys SAFE: at least 99% of the comparable pairs sharing one also share the other, none differ): 0 go to MATCH, 341 to SUSPECTED, 0 to NOT_MATCHED. With this plan, 341 of the 341 pair(s) the simulation judged identical on emailKey + mobileE164 wait for a steward instead of merging.
7) 565 of the 565 SUSPECTED pair(s) agree on every field of at least one key set above: with this plan they wait for a steward.
8) not counted: addressKeys (compared by a score on a multi-token key: two records agree on it by similarity, not by an identical value).
```

The line added to the plan's rationale (step 6), in the launcher's language (bundle keys `matchfb.*`, both bundles): `Simulation: 341 pairs identical on emailKey + mobileE164 left as suspects (703 pairs evaluated, 20 pivots) - plan kept by the model.` /
`Simulation : 341 paires identiques sur emailKey + mobileE164 laissees en suspect (703 paires evaluees, 20 pivots) - plan conserve par le modele.` (accents as \uXXXX in the bundle). Variants: `plan revised by the model (these figures are those of the previous proposal)`,
`plan kept (the model gave no answer)`, and, when no waiting pair agrees on a key set, "no pair left as suspect agrees on every field of a key set of the plan". The line goes FIRST in the rationale (the 2,000-character cap cuts the end), then the model's reason when it kept the plan
(`Reason given by the model: ...`, 400 characters), then the plan's own rationale.

### 70.3 The turn (`master/MatchPlanLlmPass`, `ebx/MatchPlanFeedbackPass`)

The system prompt gained a paragraph SIMULATION FEEDBACK: what the second turn is (counts only, facts about the plan, the Factory sets no weight, threshold or leaf), the two answers and that either stands, and both costs (a MATCH merges only once a person turns automatic merge on; a pair left to a steward
costs a person's time: "weigh both"). The turn is a fresh `AgentRuntime.run` (phase `MATCHING_SUGGEST_LLM_FEEDBACK`, the same session and refusal bookkeeping, a fresh ledger per entity) whose user message holds, per entity: the model's own stored plan (fenced, without the key facts and the statements),
the numbered statements (fenced), then the facts of the entities again (`userPrompt` with another closing line - the conversation is new). Tools: `propose_match_plan` (a revised plan, judged by EVERY check of a proposal; accepted, it replaces the plan; the plan it replaced is kept in
`previousRequirements`), the new `keep_match_plan {entity, rationale}` (the plan stands, and why) and `note`; no `skip_entity`. An identical plan proposed again counts as kept; no answer counts as kept ("plan kept (the model gave no answer)"). A refused revision loses nothing: the first plan stands.
One answer per entity, one turn: the Factory re-simulates nothing, so a revised plan has no figures of its own (the line says the figures are the previous proposal's) - a person can click Simulate, and "Propose another" carries the statements.

**Where it runs.** In the whole-project proposal job (`MatchingSuggestLlmRun` -> `MatchPlanLlmSuggester.suggestClaimed`), AFTER the plans are written: the simulation needs the stored plan row (the add-on is told the plan through the `<Entity>__preview` policy, as for the Simulate button). Per entity
it is skipped, with the reason in the step detail, when: the master table is above `-Dmdm.factory.matchFeedback.maxRows` (default: `ScanBudget.current()`, 15,000,000 rows; 0 turns the turn off) - the simulation is bounded whatever the table (20 pivots, 2,000 rows read per source system,
`MatchPlanFeedbackPass.DETAIL_BUDGET` 150 detail calls) but the grouping of the probes and the coverage read are not; the 300 s bound for all the simulations of one job is spent; the plan is the Factory's own fallback (origin RULE: not the model's); the plan row does not hold the proposal
(not stored, decided by a person); the simulation fails or judges no pair. A failure of the phase never fails the proposal. A single-entity "Propose another" does not run it (it is the person's explicit ask, with the reviewer's comment, and it stays fast): the Simulate click now stores the
feedback statements on the plan (`requirements.simulationFacts`, prefix `plan simulation: `, next to the coverage ones), so the next "Propose another" gives them to the model as numbered facts with the sentence "weigh them, you may keep, rewrite or restructure the plan" - the coverage
sentence ("Rewrite clusteringWeights...") only when coverage statements are there. The two paths of the scenario keep working: both go through the proposal job (`/matching/propose?useLlm=true`); "plain" now has a preview policy left by the job's simulation, which the configure
already handles (`useForManualMerge:false`, lot of 2026-10-17; the variant "simulate-first" is exactly that state).

**Recorded.** The `AgentRun` of the turn (its steps are the model's answers), the plan row (rationale line, or the revised plan), `kernel.log` (`[mdm-factory] Matching plan feedback for <Entity> (project <P>): pivots=20 pairs=703 match=0 suspected=565 notMatched=138 suspectedOnKeys=565
notMatchedOnKeys=0 probed=0 keys=[...]` then `... the model's answer: KEPT - Simulation: ...`) and the `MATCHING_SUGGEST_LLM` step detail, key `feedback`:
`enabled`, `maxRows`, `skippedAll`, `turnError`, `error`; `agentRun.{id,status,steps,inputTokens,outputTokens,detail}`; `entities.<Entity>.{ran, reason | pivots, pairs, match, suspected, notMatched, probed, suspectedOnKeys, notMatchedOnKeys, matchOnKeys, engineWithLeaf, keySets[{fields, safe, engine{pairs,match,suspected,notMatched}, probe{...}}],
leaves[{node, branch, outcome, pairs}], outcome (REVISED | KEPT | NO_ANSWER), keptReason, stored, rationaleLine, revisedRefusal}`.

### 70.4 What the Factory still does NOT do, and what could read as a decision

No weight, threshold or leaf is set, suggested or ranked; no plan is changed by the Factory (the rationale line is a note on the model's plan; the plan itself is the model's, revised or kept). Choices that are the Factory's and can be questioned: which key sets are measured (the exact conditions of the tree's own
paths, the SAFE pairs of keys among the plan's own fields); the order of the statements and the headline of the rationale line (a SAFE pair of keys first, then the set with the most waiting pairs); the wording "wait for a steward instead of merging" (the brief's); whether the turn runs at all
(the rows bound, the time bound, no turn for the fallback plan or a single-entity proposal); that there is ONE turn and no re-simulation of the revised plan; that probed pairs are counted apart. The model's reason for keeping a plan is cut at 400 characters in the rationale (300 in the step detail).

### 70.5 Files, tests, limits

New: `master/SimulationFeedback`, `ebx/MatchPlanFeedbackPass`, `ebx/MatchPlanFeedbackText`. Touched: `master/MatchPlanLlmPass` (system prompt paragraph, `feedbackPrompt`, `Session#beginFeedback / feedbackToolGroup / keepMatchPlan / feedbackOutcomes / settleFeedback`, `rejectionNote`),
`ebx/MatchPlanSimulationRunner` (`run` + `Run`, the values of the plan's keys kept on every pair, the feedback measured and stored), `ebx/MatchPlanLlmSuggester` (the phase, `write` over a list of plans, `updateRationale`), `ebx/ProposalReviews` (`recordSimulationFacts` answers whether it stored), both bundles.
Tests (JUnit-free): `SimulationFeedbackTest` (the 534 B2C records replayed against an independent evaluator: verdicts, key sets, SAFE pair, per-leaf counts from the visit order, pairs without a path, probes apart, multi-token key not counted, counts and never a value, possible misses, gate, JSON),
`MatchPlanLlmPassFeedbackTest` (the session: revise / keep / same plan again / no answer / refused revision / one answer per entity / no turn without a plan; the tools; the prompt of the turn; the system paragraph; the statements in the next "Propose another"), `MatchPlanFeedbackTextTest` (the line EN and FR, singular, no suspect, the rationale order, the bundles).
Not verified live (nothing was installed or restarted): how the model answers the turn, the cost of the simulation inside the job on a real table (the Simulate button's own timing is the reference), the interplay of the job's preview policy with Configure on a business-object table (the leftover is harmless since d03f5edc but cannot be removed there, see section 57).
Limits: the figures are those of a sample of 20 pivots - a small sample can show 0 where a rare case exists; agreement is an identical value (a key compared by exactFullText is not counted); the leaf figures cover the pairs whose visit order was recorded (150 detail calls, probes first).

### 70.6 Lot F1b (live run 7, 2026-10-19 21:08): a date key, an Error, and a proposal that died of it

Scenario run 7 (Factory 1.2.0-332, project `E2EMASTER20261019185946`): the proposal job ended with `ExceptionInInitializerError ... Caused by: IllegalArgumentException: Invalid DATE value, 'Tue Jan 20 00:00:00 CET 2026'` at the generated `BazCte_0$1.<clinit>`, from
`MatchPlanSimulationRunner.rowsByFieldValue` <- `measureCoverage` <- `run` <- `MatchPlanFeedbackPass`. Two causes, both fixed:
1. **The literal.** The coverage read wrote every key value as a quoted string made with `String.valueOf` - for an `xs:date` key (`birthDate`, a key of the plan) that is `Date.toString`, and Calcite's generated code refused it. Values are now the field's XS string (`SchemaNode.formatToXsString`, `readField`),
   and the literal is built from the field's Java class (`getOccurrencesJavaClass`, `ebx/SqlLiterals`): a Date with an XS date -> `DATE 'yyyy-MM-dd'`, with a time -> `TIMESTAMP 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss'` (fraction and zone dropped), `HH:mm:ss` -> `TIME '...'`; Integer/Long/Short/Byte/BigInteger/BigDecimal/Double/Float
   -> the bare number; Boolean -> `TRUE`/`FALSE`; anything else, and any value that does not read as its type, the quoted string with a doubled quote (never code). The bulk reads (`rowsByFieldValue`, `rowsByFieldCombo`) select only the primary key and bucket each row by the XS string of ITS OWN value, so the buckets match the
   pivots' values whatever the engine returns for the column; the probe reads (`sharedKeyValues`, `nearMissGroups`) convert the values they read the same way. `CrossSystemMeasures` and `KeyFactsReader` were checked: they write no value literal (group-by and equality only), so they do not share the bug.
2. **The boundary.** `catch (RuntimeException)` let an `Error` through. The phase (`MatchPlanFeedbackPass.guarded`), each simulation (`simulateGuarded`), each coverage key (`measureCoverage`), the coverage block, the feedback measure and the SQL reads now catch any `Throwable` except `VirtualMachineError` and `ThreadDeath`
   (`ebx/NonFatal`), log at WARN and go on: `feedback.error` (the phase), the entity's `reason` ("the simulation failed: ..."), or a coverage statement "<field>: not measured (query failed: <reason>)" told to the model. The plans written first always stand.
Tests: `SqlLiteralsTest` (date, dateTime, time, integer, long, decimal, boolean, string with a quote, mismatched values quoted), `MatchPlanFeedbackBoundaryTest` (an Error of the phase, the live Error with its cause, a VirtualMachineError rethrown, one simulation's Error skips that entity only, no pair, the whole phase without a session).

### 70.7 Lot F1c (live run 8, 2026-10-19 20:40): the model wanted to revise and called keep_match_plan

Run 8 (AgentRun 763, 3 steps): the feedback turn ran (18 pivots, 36 pairs, 0 MATCH, 36 SUSPECTED, all 36 agreeing on the SAFE set) and the model read the figures correctly - then called `keep_match_plan` with "Revise rather than keep: ... the stored path should terminate in MATCH ... adjust weights ... I am replacing it", and a `note` saying it kept the
plan "although revision would have been preferable". Outcome KEPT, plan unchanged: the right analysis, the wrong tool, no plan emitted. Changes, none of which decides anything for the model:
1. **The contract is explicit** (feedback prompt, system prompt, tool descriptions): to change ANYTHING call `propose_match_plan` with the WHOLE revised plan (all nodes, clustering fields, `clusteringWeights`; it may rewrite the weights in the same call); `keep_match_plan` means the stored plan stays EXACTLY as it is and its rationale says why it is right as it is; a description of
   changes in a rationale changes nothing - a plan is never edited from a rationale.
2. **A consistency guard** (`Session#keepMatchPlan`, `announcedChange`): a `keep_match_plan` whose rationale contains the model's own announcement of a change (revise/revising/revised, replac..., "should terminate in", "adjust weights", "add a path", "instead of / rather than keeping") is REFUSED ONCE with
   `Your rationale says you want to change the plan ("<its sentence>"). To change it, call propose_match_plan with the full revised plan now; to keep it, call keep_match_plan with a rationale that keeps it.` The second `keep_match_plan` is accepted whatever it says (no loop); a `propose_match_plan` after the refusal is judged and stored as any revision.
   The step detail records `feedback.entities.<E>.keepRefusedOnce` next to `outcome`. The guard matches words; it never reads the plan nor chooses an outcome.
3. **What re-proposing needs** is in the turn: `feedbackPrompt` repeats the entity block of the first proposal (attributes with roles and fill rates, the add-on vocabulary note, the editor guides, the key facts, the checklist), the system prompt is the same one, and the tool schema carries the allowed enumerations - tested.
Tests: `MatchPlanLlmPassFeedbackTest` (the prompt sentences; refused once with the exact text, accepted the second time; a plain keep never refused; a propose after the refusal accepted and stored; the signals; the turn gives the facts).

## 71. Lot B7 - the matching queue pages on the server and never announces a cap as a total (branch `fix/robustesse-b7-matching-queue`, 2026-10-24)

Audit F2-106 and F2-112. `matching.MatchResultsView` cuts the queue page itself: the group cards written are those of the requested page (ten a page, `selectedTab` =
`PENDING@n`), the pager buttons are `MATCH_PAGE` actions and its total is the number of groups the stored block holds. The tabs follow one rule (`tabCount`): the real
whole-table figure when the block carries it, `cap+` when a list was cut at its cap and the figure is unknown, the count otherwise; a cut list says "N of M shown".
The lineage of a golden is read by page (`RecordLineageReader.contributorWindow`: the golden anchor first, then the window of the other contributors), with
`contributors {total, shown, nextOffset}` in the answer. Tests: `GroupCardTest` (page 3 of 25, capped tabs), `RecordLineageReaderTest` (window and N of M).
